nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Then this induces an implicit atlas $A$ (the same index set) of dimension $d-1$ on $\partial X$, simply by setting $(\partial X)_I:=\partial X_I$ and restricting the rest of the data to these subspaces.
nodes.definiendum: restriction of implicit atlas to boundary

nodes.name: Ground ring convention (VFC package)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.

nodes.name: Virtual cohomology H_vir
nodes.statement_short: Announces canonical isomorphisms from virtual cohomology $H_{vir}$ (cohomology of $C_{vir}$) to Cech cohomology with virtual orientation sheaves.
nodes.statement:
We construct canonical isomorphisms:
\begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})
\end{align}
($H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}$ denotes the cohomology of $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}$) for certain \emph{virtual orientation sheaves} $\mathfrak o_X$ and $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}$ on $X$.

nodes.name: Equation HXiso
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)
nodes.label: HXiso

nodes.name: Equation HXreliso
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow\sim\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})
nodes.label: HXreliso

nodes.name: Chain level virtual fundamental cycle
Equation sastintrotvfcsec
nodes.statement: C^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_A,E_A\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}
nodes.label: sastintrotvfcsec

nodes.name: Overview: virtual cochain complexes as pure homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement_short: Plan: virtual cochain complexes are global sections of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves with $H^0$ the virtual orientation sheaves, giving the isomorphisms to Cech cohomology.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: K&\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)\\ K&\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)&=\mathfrak o_X\\ H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&=\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}

nodes.name: Orientation module of a vector space
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb R$. We let $\mathfrak o_E$ denote the orientation module of $E$, namely $H_{\dim E}(E,E\setminus 0)$ (a free $R$-module of rank $1$).\footnote{According to the previous definition, we should really call this $(\mathfrak o_E)_0$ (the stalk at $0\in E$ of the orientation sheaf of $E$ considered as a manifold), though we do not anticipate this abuse causing any particular confusion.}

nodes.name: Locally orientable implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. We say that $A$ is \emph{locally orientable}\footnote{This is analogous to the notion of an orbifold being locally orientable.} iff for every $I\subseteq A$ and every $x\in(s_I|X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0)$, the stabilizer $(\Gamma_I)_x$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}})_x\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (this action is always by a sign $(\Gamma_I)_x\to\{\pm 1\}$). This notion is independent of the ring $R$ (due to our restriction that $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ be invertible in $R$).
differentia: the stabilizer $(\Gamma_I)_x$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}})_x\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$
nodes.label: IAlocalorient

nodes.name: Virtual orientation sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then there exists a sheaf $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ on $X$ equipped with $\Gamma_I$-equivariant isomorphisms $\psi_{\varnothing I}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X,A}\xrightarrow\sim\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ over $(s_I|X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0)$ for every $I\subseteq A$, which are compatible with the maps $\psi_{IJ}$. We call $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ the \emph{virtual orientation sheaf} of $X$ (it is unique up to unique isomorphism); it is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$. We write $\mathfrak o_X$ for $\mathfrak o_{X,A}$ when the atlas is clear from context. We let $\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}:=j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X$ where $j:X\setminus\partial X\hookrightarrow X$.
nodes.statement_short: The virtual orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$ is the sheaf on $X$ locally given by $\mathfrak o_{X_I^{reg}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$; $\mathfrak o_{X rel\partial}$ is its extension by zero off $\partial X$.
nodes.label: IAorientationsheaf

nodes.name: Deformation to the normal cone
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. For $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$, we define: \begin{equation*} X_{I,J,A}:=\left\{(e,t,x)\in E_A\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^A\times X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}t_\alpha=0\text{ for }\alpha\in A\setminus I\hfill\cr s_\alpha(x)=t_\alpha e_\alpha\text{ for }\alpha\in J\hfill\cr\psi_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\},J}(x)\in X_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\}}^{\mathrm{reg}}\hfill\end{matrix}\right\} \end{equation*} The condition $\psi_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\},J}(x)\in X_{\{\alpha\in A:t_\alpha>0\}}^{\mathrm{reg}}$ ensures that we only deform to the normal cone of those zero sets $s_{J\setminus I'}^{-1}(0)$ which are cut out transversally ($I'\subseteq I$). Clearly $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq X_{I,J,A}$ is the subset where $x\in\partial X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (the former being with respect to the restriction of $A$ to $\partial X$). There are compatible maps: \begin{equation} X_{I,J,A}\times E_{A'\setminus A}\to X_{I',J',A'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A' \end{equation} given by $t_{A'\setminus A}=0$ and $x\mapsto\psi_{J',J}(x)$. For $K\subseteq X$, we let $X_{I,J,A}^K\subseteq X_{I,J,A}$ denote the subspace where $e=0$ and $x\in\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K)$. Note that $\Gamma_A$ acts on $X_{I,J,A}$ (acting on $X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}$ via the projection $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_J$ and on $E_A$).
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Defines the deformation-to-the-normal-cone spaces $X_{I,J,A}\subseteq E_A\times\mathbb R_{\ge0}^A\times X_J^{reg}$, their maps and the subspaces $X^K_{I,J,A}$.

nodes.name: Equation pushforward
nodes.statement: X_{I,J,A}\times E_{A'\setminus A}\to X_{I',J',A'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A'
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: pushforward

nodes.name: Chains and cochains; Eilenberg--Zilber map
nodes.statement: We use $C_\bullet(X)$ (resp.\ $C^\bullet(X)$) to denote singular simplicial chains (resp.\ cochains) on a space $X$, and we use $C_\bullet(X,Y)$ to denote the cokernel of $C_\bullet(Y)\hookrightarrow C_\bullet(X)$ for $Y\subseteq X$ (``relative chains''). Let us also recall the ``Eilenberg--Zilber map'' $C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\to C_\bullet(X\times Y)$ for spaces $X$ and $Y$, corresponding to the standard subdivision of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$ into $\binom{n+m}n$ copies of $\Delta^{n+m}$. The Eilenberg--Zilber map is associative (in the sense that it gives rise to a unique map $C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(Z)\to C_\bullet(X\times Y\times Z)$) and commutative (in the sense that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(X)@>>>C_\bullet(Y\times X) \end{CD} \end{equation} for all $X$ and $Y$). We should point out that this commutativity fails for some other common models of singular chains, for example singular cubical chains (modulo degeneracies).
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Fixes singular simplicial (co)chains and relative chains, and recalls the associative, commutative Eilenberg--Zilber map.
nodes.label: chainfixing

nodes.name: Equation chainproductcommutes
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} C_\bullet(X)\otimes C_\bullet(Y)@>>>C_\bullet(X\times Y)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr C_\bullet(Y)\otimes C_\bullet(X)@>>>C_\bullet(Y\times X) \end{CD}
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: chainproductcommutes

nodes.name: Independence of chain model
nodes.statement: The particular choice of \emph{singular simplicial} chains is not particularly important. The virtual fundamental classes, etc.\ resulting from our theory should be unchanged by using any other model of singular chains. This independence would follow immediately (and all issues about finding chain models with good chain level functoriality properties would go away) if we setup the VFC package using $\infty$-categories.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.label: independenceofchainmodel

nodes.name: Fundamental cycles of vector spaces
nodes.statement: Let $I$ be a finite subset of an implicit atlas $A$. We define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(E;I):=C_{\dim E_I+\bullet}(E_I,E_I\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee)^{\Gamma_I} \end{equation} There is a canonical isomorphism $H_\bullet(E;I)=R$ (concentrated in degree zero), and we denote the canonical generator by $[E_I]\in H_\bullet(E;I)$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C_\bullet(E;I):=C_{\dim E_I+\bullet}(E_I,E_I\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee)^{\Gamma_I}
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}

nodes.name: Partial virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&:=C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\\ C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&:=\left[\begin{matrix}C_{d+\dim E_A-1-\bullet}((\partial X)_{I,J,A},(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\setminus(\partial X)_{I,J,A}^{K\cap\partial X};\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\cr\downarrow\cr C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(X_{I,J,A},X_{I,J,A}\setminus X_{I,J,A}^K;\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\end{matrix}\right] \end{align} It is clear that $K\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $K\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$. There are canonical maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A)\\ \hspace{1.5in}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J \end{align} (\eqref{Ethompushforward} is induced by the projection $X_{I,J,A}\to E_A$, and \eqref{Epushforward1} is induced by \eqref{pushforward} with $A=A'$). These are compatible with each other in that certain obvious diagrams commute.
nodes.section: 4.2 Virtual cochain complexes \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)$}{C\_vir(X;A)} and \texorpdfstring{$C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$}{C\_vir(X rel d;A)}
nodes.statement_short: Partial virtual cochain complexes: relative singular chains on the normal-cone deformations $X_{I,J,A}$ (with a boundary cone), with canonical restriction, pushforward $s_*$ and transition maps.
nodes.label: CSTcomplexdef

nodes.name: Virtual cochain complexes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} where $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}$ is the homotopy colimit (Definition \ref{homotopycolimit}) over $2^A$ with structure maps given by $(\#\Gamma_{J\setminus J'})^{-1}$ times \eqref{Epushforward1}. It is clear that $K\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)$ and $K\mapsto C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ are both complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$. There are canonical maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)\\ C^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)&\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;A) \end{align} (induced by \eqref{Erelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Ethompushforward}). More precisely, \eqref{Fpushforward} is given by \eqref{Ethompushforward} on the $p=0$ part of the $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$ and is zero on the rest.

nodes.name: Maps between virtual cochain complexes for A in A'
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite implicit atlases $A\subseteq A'$ with boundary. There are canonical maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A')_{I',J'}\text{ for }I\subseteq I'\subseteq J'\subseteq J\subseteq A\subseteq A' \end{equation} induced by \eqref{pushforward} (of which \eqref{Epushforward1} is a special case). These are compatible with each other, and thus extend to the homotopy colimit over $I\subseteq J\subseteq A$. Hence we get canonical maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)\otimes C_{-\bullet}(E;A'\setminus A)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A') \end{equation} which are compatible with \eqref{Frelpartialpullback}--\eqref{Fpushforward}.

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$. nodes.name: Proof (F100)
nodes.statement: Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. Now let us calculate $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. It follows from the submersion axiom that $X_{I,J,A}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\operatorname{vdim}_AX+\dim E_A+\#I$ with boundary (not necessarily second countable or paracompact).\footnote{In fact, it carries a natural structure of a manifold with corners, which for the present purpose is mostly irrelevant.} The boundary $\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a (not necessarily disjoint) union of two pieces, namely the locus where $x\in\partial X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (which is precisely $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}$) and the locus where $t_\alpha=0$ for some $\alpha\in I$. It is easy to see that the first piece $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a closed tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary. Hence we may apply Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality in the form of Lemma \ref{poincareduality} to see that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} (the orientation sheaf of $X_{I,J,A}$ is given by $\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_A}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes I}$). Now we apply the K\"unneth formula to conclude that: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}})^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} Since $X$ is locally orientable, we have $\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee=\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X$, so we can write: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X)^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} Now $\Gamma_A$ acts through the projection $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_J$, and $\psi_{\varnothing J}:\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\to K\cap V_I\cap V_J$ is exactly the quotient by $\Gamma_J$. Hence by Lemma \ref{cechcohomologyfinitequotient} we get isomorphisms: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_X) \end{align} Now use Lemma \ref{cptcechembeddingproperty} to write this as: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X) \end{align} Thus $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both pure, and we manifestly have the desired isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply homotopy-sheaf lemmas, then compute cohomology via Poincare--Lefschetz duality on the manifold $X_{I,J,A}$, Kunneth, local orientability and finite quotients.

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf property
nodes.statement_short: Apply the singular-chain lemmas to get homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.
nodes.statement: Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves.

nodes.statement: Now let us calculate $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$.  It follows from the submersion axiom that $X_{I,J,A}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\operatorname{vdim}_AX+\dim E_A+\#I$ with boundary (not necessarily second countable or paracompact).\footnote{In fact, it carries a natural structure of a manifold with corners, which for the present purpose is mostly irrelevant.}

nodes.name: Boundary pieces
nodes.statement_short: Describe the two boundary pieces of $X_{I,J,A}$; the first is tamely embedded.
nodes.statement: The boundary $\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a (not necessarily disjoint) union of two pieces, namely the locus where $x\in\partial X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (which is precisely $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}$) and the locus where $t_\alpha=0$ for some $\alpha\in I$.  It is easy to see that the first piece $(\partial X)_{I,J,A}\subseteq\partial(X_{I,J,A})$ is a closed tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary.

nodes.name: Poincare--Lefschetz duality
nodes.statement_short: Apply Poincare--Lefschetz duality to express $H_{vir}$ as compactly supported Cech cohomology.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H_c^{\bullet+\#I}(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J)\times\mathbb R_{>0}^I,\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes I}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}})^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.statement_short: Kunneth formula removes the $\mathbb R_{>0}^I$ factor.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\mathfrak o_{E_J}^\vee\otimes\mathfrak o_{X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}})^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.name: Use local orientability
nodes.statement_short: Local orientability identifies the coefficient sheaf with $\psi^*\mathfrak o_X$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^{\Gamma_A}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(\psi_{\varnothing J}^{-1}(K\cap V_I\cap V_J),\psi_{\varnothing J}^\ast\mathfrak o_X)^{\Gamma_A}

nodes.name: Quotient by Gamma_J
nodes.statement_short: Cech cohomology of a finite quotient removes the $\Gamma_A$ invariants.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet_c(K\cap V_I\cap V_J,\mathfrak o_X)

nodes.name: Embedding property
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite compactly supported cohomology of $K\cap V_I\cap V_J$ via $j_!j^*$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&=\check H^\bullet(K,j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_X)

nodes.name: Purity and isomorphisms
nodes.statement_short: Conclude purity and the isomorphisms EisoI--EisoII.
nodes.statement: Thus $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are both pure, and we manifestly have the desired isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII}.

nodes.name: Local description of isomorphisms H^0_vir(-;A)_II
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Consider the following maps of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $X$: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{II}&\leftarrow\left[\begin{matrix}C_{d+\dim E_A-1-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times\partial X_I^{\mathrm{reg}},E_{A\setminus I}\times(\partial X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\cr\downarrow\cr C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^{\mathrm{reg}},E_{A\setminus I}\times(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A}\hfill\end{matrix}\right]\\ C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{II}&\leftarrow C_{d+\dim E_A-\bullet}(E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^{\mathrm{reg}},E_{A\setminus I}\times(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}\setminus\psi_{\varnothing I}^{-1}(K));\mathfrak o_{E_A}^\vee)^{\Gamma_A} \end{align} (induced by the corresponding maps on spaces). These maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and the isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII} from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} coincide with the Poincar\'e duality isomorphisms for the complexes on the right above.
assumptions: $X$ be a space with finite locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary
conclusions: These maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and the isomorphisms \eqref{EisoI}--\eqref{EisoII} from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} coincide with the Poincar\'e duality isomorphisms for the complexes on the right above
nodes.statement_short: On $II$ pieces the partial complexes are quasi-isomorphic to relative chains of $E_{A\setminus I}\times X_I^{reg}$, and the $H^0$ isomorphisms are Poincare duality.

nodes.name: Proof (F111)
nodes.statement: This is a special case of Lemma \ref{gluingcechsimple}; we just need to make sure all of the hypotheses are satisfied. The open cover in question is $V_I:=\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0))$; it follows from the axioms of an implicit atlas that $V_I\cap V_K\subseteq V_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$ and $V_I\cap V_{I'}\subseteq V_{I\cup I'}$ for all $I,I'$. Now we just need to check that the system of isomorphisms from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} are compatible with the maps of the homotopy diagram. These being maps of sheaves, it suffices to check compatibility locally (on stalks) and thus is a straightforward calculation (this is where the extra normalization factor of $(\#\Gamma_{J\setminus J'})^{-1}$ in Definition \ref{Ccomplexdef} is important).
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the gluing lemma for pure homotopy sheaves; verify the cover $V_I$ and compatibility of the $H^0$ isomorphisms on stalks.

nodes.statement: Now we just need to check that the system of isomorphisms from Lemma \ref{CSTpure} are compatible with the maps of the homotopy diagram. nodes.statement_short: $C_{vir}(K;A)$ is the mapping cone of $C_{vir}(K\cap\partial X)\to C_{vir}(K rel\partial)$, giving a long exact sequence.

It follows from the definition that $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}$ is the mapping cone of the obvious map $C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\cap\partial X;A)_{IJ}\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. nodes.name: Proof (F120)
nodes.statement: By the definition of the vertical identifications, the commutativity of the first two squares of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} reduces to the commutativity of the diagram of sheaves: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofF}}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}&H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{Cpure}}}\\ \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&\mathfrak o_X\ar{r}{\eqref{sesofO}}&i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial X} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} It suffices to check commutativity on stalks, and to do this, we can work with the complexes on the right in Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}, for which the commutativity is clear. In fact, the commutativity of the last square of \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram} is also a consequence of the commutativity of \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. To see this, consider the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = small] H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial X;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}H^\bullet[C^{\bullet+1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)]\ar{r}\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}&H^{\bullet+1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{d}{\sim}&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)[1]\to H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)])\ar{r}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A))\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})&\ar{l}[swap]{\sim}\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}[1]\to\mathfrak o_X])\ar{r}&\check H^{\bullet+1}(X,\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} The middle vertical arrow is defined because of the commutativity of the left square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}. The top left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism, and thus every left horizontal arrow is a quasi-isomorphism. The bottom left square is commutative because of the commutativity of the right square in \eqref{sheafcommutativity}; the other squares are trivially commutative. Reversing the left horizontal arrows, we see that the outermost square commutes, and this is exactly the last square in \eqref{compatibilityoflesdiagram}.

nodes.name: Fiber product formula for virtual fundamental classes

nodes.name: Ground ring convention (virtual fundamental classes)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.

nodes.name: Comparison of homology theories
nodes.statement: There are (at least) three natural ``homology groups'' which one can assign to a compact Hausdorff space $X$: \begin{rlist} \item\emph{Dual of \v Cech cohomology} $\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee$ ($^\vee$ denotes dual, i.e.\ $\operatorname{Hom}(-,R)$). \item\emph{\v Cech homology} $\check H_\bullet(X)$ (the inverse limit of the homology of nerves of finite covers). \item\emph{Steenrod--Sitnikov homology} $\overline H_\bullet(X)$ (the homology of the homotopy/derived inverse limit of nerves of finite covers; see \S\ref{steenrodhomologysec}). \end{rlist} These are successively more refined, in the sense that there are natural maps: \begin{equation} \overline H_\bullet(X)\to\check H_\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee \end{equation} If $X$ is homeomorphic to a finite CW-complex, then there are natural isomorphisms: \begin{equation} \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet(X)\qquad\check H^\bullet(X)^\vee=H^\bullet(X)^\vee \end{equation} It follows that a virtual fundamental class in any of these groups can be used for all the applications we are aware of. On the other hand, there are some potential advantages to working with the more refined homology groups: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline H_\bullet$ and $\check H_\bullet$ retain torsion information. \item$\overline H_\bullet$ and $\check H_\bullet$ have a natural ``extension of scalars'' map for any map of rings $R\to S$. \item$\overline H_\bullet$ has the expected long exact sequence for pairs of spaces. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: Dual Cech cohomology, Cech homology and Steenrod--Sitnikov homology of compact spaces, successively more refined, agreeing on finite CW complexes.
nodes.label: alsogetsteenrod

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a finite subatlas (which exists by compactness). We consider the composite: \begin{equation} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\overset{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}=H^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\xrightarrow{\eqref{Fpushforward}}H_{-\bullet}(E;B)\xrightarrow{[E_B]\mapsto 1}R \end{equation} We thus get a map $\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$. Now suppose $B\subseteq B'$ are two finite subatlases. Then the following diagram commutes (it suffices to check commutativity on stalks, and to do this, we can work with the complexes on the right in Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}, for which the commutativity is clear): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}\ar[equal]{d}&H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}[swap]{\eqref{Fpushforward1}}\\ \mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;B') \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Hence the following diagram commutes (the first square following from \eqref{sheafcommforFC}, the rest being clear): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}\ar[equal]{d}&H^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}[swap]{\eqref{Fpushforward1}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;B)\ar{r}{[E_B]\mapsto 1}\ar{d}{\times[E_{B'\setminus B}]}&R\ar[equal]{d}\\ \check H^{d+\bullet}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&H^{d+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B')\ar{r}{\eqref{Fpushforward}}&H_{-\bullet}(E;B')\ar{r}{[E_{B'}]\mapsto 1}&R \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} This shows that the maps $\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ induced by $B$ and $B'$ coincide. Since any two $B_1,B_2\subseteq A$ are contained in a third $B_1\cup B_2\subseteq A$, we see that the resulting element: \begin{equation} [X]^{\mathrm{vir}}_A\in\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee \end{equation} is independent of $B$. We write $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ for $[X]_A^{\mathrm{vir}}$ when the atlas is clear from context.
nodes.statement_short: $[X]^{vir}\in\check H^d(X;\mathfrak o_{X rel\partial})^\vee$ is the composite of $H_{vir}=\check H$ with $s_*$ to $H(E;B)=R$, independent of the finite subatlas $B$.

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class of a disjoint union
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be spaces equipped with locally orientable implicit atlases with boundary, on the same index set $A$ and of the same virtual dimension. Let us also denote by $A$ the resulting implicit atlas on $X\sqcup Y$ (let $(X\sqcup Y)_I:=X_I\sqcup Y_I$). Then $A$ on $X\sqcup Y$ is locally orientable with $\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y}=(i_X)_\ast\mathfrak o_X\oplus(i_Y)_\ast\mathfrak o_Y$, and $[X\sqcup Y]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}\oplus[Y]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee=\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$.

nodes.name: Proof (F138)
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. There is a natural isomorphism: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)=C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{equation} compatible with the map to $C_{-\bullet}(E;A)$. Thus it suffices to show that the following square of isomorphisms commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} By definition of the horizontal maps, it suffices to check the commutativity of the corresponding diagram of sheaves on $X\sqcup Y$, which is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Virtual complexes split over a disjoint union compatibly with $s_*$; check the square of isomorphisms on sheaves.

nodes.name: Splitting of virtual complex
nodes.statement_short: Assume $A$ finite; the virtual complex of $X\sqcup Y$ splits compatibly with $s_*$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)=C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)

nodes.name: Reduce to square and check on sheaves
nodes.statement_short: It suffices that a square of isomorphisms commutes, which is checked on sheaves.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{d}\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X\sqcup Y;\mathfrak o_{X\sqcup Y\operatorname{rel}\partial})\ar[equal]{d}\\ H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\oplus H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(Y\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\ar[equal]{r}{\text{Thm \ref{Fsheaffundamentaliso}}}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\oplus\check H^\bullet(Y;\mathfrak o_{Y\operatorname{rel}\partial}) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Boundary of the virtual fundamental class
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. Then the dual connecting homomorphism $\delta^\vee:\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee$ sends $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ to $[\partial X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$.
assumptions: $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary
conclusions: the dual connecting homomorphism $\delta^\vee:\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee$ sends $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ to $[\partial X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$
nodes.label: boundaryfundamentalclass

nodes.name: Proof (F142)
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite. The map $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial X;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ in \eqref{sesofF} commutes with the maps from both of these groups to $C_{d-\bullet}(E;A)$. Hence the result follows from the commutativity of the last square in Proposition \ref{compatibilityoflongexactsequence}.
nodes.statement_short: The boundary map of virtual complexes commutes with $s_*$; conclude by the last square of the long exact sequence compatibility.

nodes.name: Boundary map commutes with s_*
nodes.statement_short: Assume $A$ finite; the boundary map of sesofF commutes with $s_*$.
nodes.statement: We may assume that $A$ is finite.  The map $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial X;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$ in \eqref{sesofF} commutes with the maps from both of these groups to $C_{d-\bullet}(E;A)$.

nodes.name: Apply LES compatibility
nodes.statement_short: Conclude from the last square of Proposition compatibilityoflongexactsequence.
nodes.statement: Hence the result follows from the commutativity of the last square in Proposition \ref{compatibilityoflongexactsequence}.

nodes.name: Boundary virtual class pushes forward to zero
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary. Then the pushforward map $\check H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ annihilates $[\partial X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$.
assumptions: $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas with boundary
conclusions: the pushforward map $\check H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ annihilates $[\partial X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$
nodes.label: cobordismworks

nodes.name: Proof (F144)
nodes.statement: The composition $\check H^{\bullet+1}(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(\partial X;\mathfrak o_{\partial X})^\vee\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ is zero, and $[\partial X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ is in the image of the first map by Lemma \ref{boundaryfundamentalclass}.
nodes.statement_short: Consecutive maps of the dual long exact sequence compose to zero, and $[\partial X]^{vir}$ is in the image of the first.

nodes.name: Transverse case: virtual class is the fundamental class
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary. If $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=X$ (so in particular, $X$ is a compact topological manifold with boundary of dimension $d=\operatorname{vdim}_AX$), then $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}_A$ is the usual fundamental class of $X$.
assumptions: $X$ be a space with locally orientable implicit atlas $A$ with boundary
$X^{\mathrm{reg}}=X$
conclusions: $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}_A$ is the usual fundamental class of $X$
nodes.label: fclasstransverse

nodes.name: Proof (F146)
nodes.statement: We may replace $A$ with the finite subatlas $\varnothing\subseteq A$. Now in this case, we have: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)_{\varnothing\varnothing}=C_{d-\bullet}(X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing},X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}\setminus X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}^K)=C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K) \end{equation} It follows that the identification $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=H_{d-\bullet}(X)$ is simply the usual Poincar\'e duality isomorphism, and the map $H_{-\bullet}(X)\to H_{-\bullet}(E;\varnothing)\to R$ is the usual augmentation on $H_0$. Hence the composition $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ is pairing against the usual fundamental class of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the empty subatlas, where the virtual complex is relative singular chains and the identification is Poincare duality.

nodes.name: Empty subatlas
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the empty subatlas, where the virtual complex is relative singular chains.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)_{\varnothing\varnothing}=C_{d-\bullet}(X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing},X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}\setminus X_{\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing}^K)=C_{d-\bullet}(X,X\setminus K)

nodes.name: Poincare duality
nodes.statement_short: The identification is Poincare duality and $s_*$ is the augmentation.
nodes.statement: It follows that the identification $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\varnothing)=H_{d-\bullet}(X)$ is simply the usual Poincar\'e duality isomorphism, and the map $H_{-\bullet}(X)\to H_{-\bullet}(E;\varnothing)\to R$ is the usual augmentation on $H_0$.

nodes.name: Pairing with fundamental class
nodes.statement_short: So the composite pairs against the usual fundamental class.
nodes.statement: Hence the composition $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})\to R$ is pairing against the usual fundamental class of $X$.

nodes.name: Calculating [X]^vir using perturbation
nodes.statement: The properties from this section can be used to calculate the virtual fundamental class in the following sense. Let us suppose we are given an ``explicit'' implicit atlas $A$ on a space $X$. We may always (for convenience) replace $A$ by a subatlas and/or shrink the charts of $A$ and the virtual fundamental class is preserved (Lemmas \ref{sameassubatlas} and \ref{openreduction}). Now suppose we can extend $A$ to an implicit atlas with boundary on a space $Y$ with $\partial Y=X\cup X'$ where $X'=(X')^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (if $A$ is a smooth implicit atlas, then such an extension is obtained if one can ``coherently perturb'' the Kuranishi maps $s_\alpha$ so they become transverse to zero). Then $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold, and $[X']^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']$ is the naive fundamental class (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}). Now $Y$ is a cobordism between $X$ and $X'$, so we have $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']$ as homology classes in $Y$ (Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks}). This allows us to understand the pushforward of $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ under any map $f:X\to Z$ which extends continuously to $Y$. We do not claim such perturbations always exist; an affirmative answer is provided in very similar, though not identical, contexts by Fukaya--Ono \cite{fukayaono}, Fukaya--Oh--Ohta--Ono \cite{FOOOII,foootechnicaldetails} and McDuff--Wehrheim \cite{mcduffwehrheim}.
nodes.statement_short: Shrink/subatlas invariance, cobordism and the transverse case let one compute $[X]^{vir}$ from a coherent perturbation to a transverse $X'$.
nodes.label: perturbationcalc

nodes.name: Implicit atlas on the zero set of a smooth section
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth manifold with boundary, let $p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle, and let $s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact. We define an implicit atlas of dimension $\dim B-\dim E$ with boundary on $X:=s^{-1}(0)$ as follows. The index set $A$ consists of all triples $(V_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ (called \emph{thickening datums}) where: \begin{rlist} \item$V_\alpha\subseteq B$ is an open subset. \item$E_\alpha$ is a finite-dimensional vector space. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\times V_\alpha\to p^{-1}(V_\alpha)$ is a smooth homomorphism of vector bundles. \end{rlist} The thickened spaces are defined as follows: \begin{equation} X_I:=\Bigl\{(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\bigcap_{\alpha\in I}V_\alpha\times\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\Bigm|s(x)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,e_\alpha)=0\Bigr\} \end{equation} The Kuranishi map $s_\alpha:X_I\to E_\alpha$ is the obvious projection map, the footprint $U_{IJ}$ is the locus where $x\in V_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in J$, and the footprint maps $\psi_{IJ}:(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)\to U_{IJ}$ are the obvious forgetful maps. The compatibility axioms are an easy exercise. The regular locus $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq X_I$ is the locus where $X_I$ is ``cut out transversally''; more precisely, $(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in X_I$ is in $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ iff the following map is surjective: \begin{equation} \Bigl(ds+\sum_{\alpha\in I}d\lambda_\alpha(\cdot,e_\alpha)\Bigr)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,\cdot):T_xB\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\to E_x \end{equation} The transversality axioms are an easy exercise. Thus $A$ is indeed an implicit atlas on $X$. Since everything here is in the smooth category, $A$ is in fact a smooth implicit atlas.
definiendum: implicit atlas on the zero set of a smooth section
nodes.statement_short: For a section $s$ of $E\to B$, an implicit atlas on $s^{-1}(0)$ indexed by thickening datums $(V_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ with thickened zero sets $X_I$.
nodes.label: IAonvectorbundlezeroset

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: X_I:=\Bigl\{(x,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\bigcap_{\alpha\in I}V_\alpha\times\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\Bigm|s(x)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,e_\alpha)=0\Bigr\}

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \Bigl(ds+\sum_{\alpha\in I}d\lambda_\alpha(\cdot,e_\alpha)\Bigr)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(x,\cdot):T_xB\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}E_\alpha\to E_x

nodes.name: Euler class
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a space equipped with a vector bundle $p:E\to B$ of rank $k$. This induces a canonical locally constant sheaf $\mathfrak o_E$ on $B$ whose stalk at $b\in B$ is $\mathfrak o_{E_b}$. Let $\tau_E\in H^k(E,E\setminus 0;p^\ast\mathfrak o_E)$ denote the Thom class of $E$ (characterized uniquely by the property that its restriction to any local trivialization $\mathbb R^n\times U\to U$ is the pullback of the tautological class in $H^n(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R^n\setminus 0;\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R^n})$). The \emph{Euler class} $e(E)\in H^k(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ is $s^\ast\tau_E$ where $s:B\to E$ is any section. Any two sections are homotopic, so $e(E)$ is well-defined. For any section $s:B\to E$ with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact, the \emph{Euler class with compact support} $e_c(E,s)\in H^k_c(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ is $s^\ast\tau_E$. If $s_0$ and $s_1$ are homotopic through a section $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with compact support, then $e_c(E,s_0)=e_c(E,s_1)$. The natural map $H^k_c(B;\mathfrak o_E)\to H^k(B;\mathfrak o_E)$ sends the Euler class with compact support to the Euler class.
nodes.statement_short: Euler class $e(E)=s^*\tau_E$ via the Thom class, and its compactly supported version $e_c(E,s)$ for sections with compact zero set.

nodes.name: Compactly supported Euler class of trivial bundle can be nonzero
nodes.statement: The Euler class with compact support can be nonzero even for the trivial vector bundle.

nodes.name: Virtual class of zero set of a section is the Euler class
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a smooth manifold, let $p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle, and let $s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact. Consider the implicit atlas $A$ on $X:=s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathfrak o_X=\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee$ on $X$ (in particular, $A$ is locally orientable), and the image of $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ in $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$ equals $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.
assumptions: $B$ be a smooth manifold
$p:E\to B$ be a smooth vector bundle
$s:B\to E$ be a smooth section with $s^{-1}(0)$ compact
conclusions: there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathfrak o_X=\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee$ on $X$
the image of $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ in $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$ equals $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$
nodes.statement_short: For the natural implicit atlas on the zero set of a section $s$, $[X]^{vir}$ maps to $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.
nodes.label: actuallygiveseulerclass

nodes.name: Proposition determines [X]^vir uniquely
nodes.statement: Note that $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)=\varinjlim_{X\subseteq U}H^\bullet(U;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)$ (direct limit over open neighborhoods $U\subseteq B$ of $X$), by the continuity axiom of \v Cech cohomology.  The proposition applies equally well with $U$ in place of $B$, and thus determines $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X)^\vee$ uniquely (note the use of either Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas} or \ref{openreduction}).

nodes.name: Proof (F155)
nodes.statement: The statement about orientation sheaves is a straightforward calculation which we omit. Choose some smooth family of sections $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with $\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ compact, so that $\tilde s(\cdot,0)=s$ and $s_1:=\tilde s(\cdot,1)$ is transverse to the zero section. Now $B\times[0,1]$ is a smooth manifold with boundary, so let $\tilde A$ be the implicit atlas on $\tilde X:=\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. Similarly, let $A'$ be the implicit atlas on $X':=(s')^{-1}(0)$. Now we have two implicit atlases on $X$, namely $A$ and (the restriction to the boundary of) $\tilde A$. On the other hand, we can exhibit $A$ as a subatlas of $\tilde A$ by the map on thickening datums sending $V_\alpha$ to $V_\alpha\times[0,1]$ and $\lambda_\alpha$ to its obvious extension. Hence they induce the same virtual fundamental class (Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas}), so we may just write $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ (dropping the subscript indicating which atlas we use). The same reasoning applies to $X'$. Now $\partial\tilde X=X\sqcup X'$, so we have $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']^{\mathrm{vir}}$ as homology classes on $\tilde X$ (Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks}). Hence we have: \begin{equation} [X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']^{\mathrm{vir}} \end{equation} as elements of $H^{\dim B-\dim E}(B;\mathfrak o_B\otimes\mathfrak o_E^\vee)^\vee$. We know $X'=(X')^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (it is cut out transversally), so $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold and $[X']^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']$ (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}). But now $[X']=e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$ by elementary Poincar\'e duality.
nodes.statement_short: Cobordism argument: deform $s$ to a transverse section $s_1$, use subatlas invariance and cobordism lemmas on $\tilde s^{-1}(0)$, then the transverse case.

nodes.name: Homotopy to transverse section
nodes.statement_short: Omit orientation calculation; choose a homotopy from $s$ to a transverse section.
nodes.statement:
The statement about orientation sheaves is a straightforward calculation which we omit.

Choose some smooth family of sections $\tilde s:B\times[0,1]\to E$ with $\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ compact, so that $\tilde s(\cdot,0)=s$ and $s_1:=\tilde s(\cdot,1)$ is transverse to the zero section.

nodes.name: Atlases on cobordism
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the implicit atlases $\tilde A$ and $A'$ on $\tilde X$ and $X'$.
nodes.statement: Now $B\times[0,1]$ is a smooth manifold with boundary, so let $\tilde A$ be the implicit atlas on $\tilde X:=\tilde s^{-1}(0)$ from Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}.  Similarly, let $A'$ be the implicit atlas on $X':=(s')^{-1}(0)$.

nodes.name: Subatlas invariance
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is a subatlas of the boundary restriction of $\tilde A$, so both give the same class.
nodes.statement: Now we have two implicit atlases on $X$, namely $A$ and (the restriction to the boundary of) $\tilde A$.  On the other hand, we can exhibit $A$ as a subatlas of $\tilde A$ by the map on thickening datums sending $V_\alpha$ to $V_\alpha\times[0,1]$ and $\lambda_\alpha$ to its obvious extension.  Hence they induce the same virtual fundamental class (Lemma \ref{sameassubatlas}), so we may just write $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ (dropping the subscript indicating which atlas we use).  The same reasoning applies to $X'$.

nodes.name: Cobordism
nodes.statement_short: Cobordism lemmas give $[X]^{vir}=[X']^{vir}$ in $B$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: [X]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']^{\mathrm{vir}}

nodes.name: Transverse case
nodes.statement_short: Transverse case and Poincare duality give $e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$.
nodes.statement: We know $X'=(X')^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (it is cut out transversally), so $X'$ is a closed smooth manifold and $[X']^{\mathrm{vir}}=[X']$ (Lemma \ref{fclasstransverse}).  But now $[X']=e_c(E,s)\cap[B]$ by elementary Poincar\'e duality.

nodes.name: Limitation of Proposition actuallygiveseulerclass
nodes.statement: Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} in its present form is useless in practice, because the implicit atlases which arise in interesting examples are not literally isomorphic to the one given in Definition \ref{IAonvectorbundlezeroset}. One could, though, hope to show that they are equivalent (c.f.\ Remark \ref{equivalenceofIA}) and then apply Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass}.

nodes.name: Steenrod homology versus dual Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: The natural map $\overline H_\bullet(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$ is an isomorphism if the base ring $R$ is a field (this follows from Lemma \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}), but for $R=\mathbb Z$ the kernel can be substantial (in particular, it contains all torsion).

nodes.name: Virtual fundamental class in Steenrod homology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space with localy orientable implicit atlas $A$ of dimension $d$ with boundary. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a finite subatlas. By Propositions \ref{Cpure} and \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}, there is a canonical isomorphism $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})=C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)$ in $D(R)$ (observe that the isomorphisms in the proof of Proposition \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf} all come from canonical quasi-isomorphisms on the chain level). There is also a canonical isomorphism $C_{-\bullet}(E;B)=R$ in $D(R)$. Since $C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)$ is free and bounded above, we have: \begin{equation} \operatorname{Hom}_R(C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B),C_{-\bullet}(E;B))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R) \end{equation} Thus the map $s_\ast:C_{\mathrm{vir}}^{d+\bullet}(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B)\to C_{-\bullet}(E;B)$ gives rise to an element: \begin{equation} [X]^{\mathrm{vir}}_A:=[s_\ast]\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R[-d])\overset{\text{Lem \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}}}=\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee) \end{equation} The commutativity of \eqref{sheafcommforFC} implies that this element is independent of the chosen finite subatlas $B\subseteq A$. By definition, this fundamental class \eqref{steenrodfclasseqndef} projects to the fundamental class of Definition \ref{fclassdefinition} under the map $\overline H_\bullet(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial})^\vee$. By chasing the various isomorphisms involved in its definition, it can be checked that $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$ is preserved under extension of scalars.
nodes.statement_short: Lifts $[X]^{vir}$ to Steenrod homology as the class of $s_*$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X rel\partial}),R[-d])$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \operatorname{Hom}_R(C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(X\operatorname{rel}\partial;B),C_{-\bullet}(E;B))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R)

nodes.name: Equation steenrodfclasseqndef
nodes.statement: [X]^{\mathrm{vir}}_A:=[s_\ast]\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_{X\operatorname{rel}\partial}),R[-d])\overset{\text{Lem \ref{steenrodisderiveddualofcech}}}=\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)
nodes.label: steenrodfclasseqndef

nodes.name: Properties generalize to Steenrod homology class
nodes.statement_short: The subatlas, shrinking, disjoint union, boundary, transverse and Euler class results extend to the Steenrod lift, which is determined on maps to finite CW complexes.
nodes.statement: The statements and proofs of Lemmas \ref{sameassubatlas}--\ref{fclasstransverse} and Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} generalize readily to the case of $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$.  Note that (the generalization of) Proposition \ref{actuallygiveseulerclass} does not determine $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\overline H_d(X,\partial X;\mathfrak o_X^\vee)$ uniquely since the map from the Steenrod homology of $X$ to the inverse limit of the homology of its neighborhoods is not necessarily an isomorphism (see \cite[p87, Theorem 4]{milnor}).  However, it does at least determine the image of $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ under any map from $X$ to a finite CW-complex, since any such map extends to some neighborhood of $X$.

nodes.name: Ground ring convention (stratifications)
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.

nodes.name: Stratification
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal S$ be a poset. A \emph{stratification} of $X$ by $\mathcal S$ is a lower semicontinuous function $X\to\mathcal S$. We let $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (resp. $X^{\mathfrak s}$, $X^{\geq\mathfrak s}$) denote the inverse image of $\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (resp.\ $\{\mathfrak s\}$, $\mathcal S^{\geq\mathfrak s}$); lower semicontinuity of $X\to\mathcal S$ means by definition that every $X^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is open. For a pair of spaces $(X,\partial X)$, a stratification $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ shall mean a stratification $X\to\mathcal S$ along with a downward closed (i.e.\ closed under taking smaller elements) subset $\partial\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S$ such that $X^{\partial\mathcal S}=\partial X$ (note that this implies automatically that $\partial X\subseteq X$ is closed).
nodes.label: stratificationdefinition

nodes.name: Cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: Let $(M,\partial M)$ be a topological manifold with boundary and stratification by $(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$, and fix a map $\dim:\mathcal S\to\mathbb Z$. This stratification is called \emph{cell-like} iff each pair $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})$ is a topological manifold with boundary of dimension $\dim\mathfrak s$. If $(M,\partial M)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ is cell-like, then so is $\partial M\to\partial\mathcal S$ (with empty boundary) and $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})\to(\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak s})$.
differentia: each pair $(M^{\leq\mathfrak s},M^{<\mathfrak s})$ is a topological manifold with boundary of dimension $\dim\mathfrak s$
nodes.label: celllikedef

nodes.name: Face poset stratification of a triangulated manifold is cell-like
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be a simplicial complex, and suppose that its geometric realization $M:=\left|T\right|$ is a topological manifold with boundary (then $\partial M$ necessarily corresponds to a subcomplex $\partial T\subseteq T$). Let $(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S):=(\mathcal F(T),\mathcal F(\partial T))$ be the face poset of $T$ (resp.\ $\partial T$). Then the stratification $(M,\partial M)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ is cell-like (note that $T$ need not be a PL manifold).
nodes.label: celllikeexample

nodes.name: Proof (F168)
nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t$, we have $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq M^{<\mathfrak t}=\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$, giving (\ref{inbdry}). Recall Brouwer's ``invariance of domain'', which implies that if a subset $X\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is (in the subspace topology) locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^m$, then $m\leq n$, with equality iff $X$ is open. This immediately gives (\ref{toplessdim}), (\ref{topopen}). We prove (\ref{bdrystratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^{\mathfrak s}$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}) (applied to $M^{<\mathfrak t}\to\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak t}$). A doubling argument (and invariance of domain) near $p\in\partial M$ shows that $M^s\cup M^{\mathfrak t}$ contains a neighborhood of $p$. Since we have exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^{\mathfrak s}$, it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there is no other stratum $\succ\mathfrak s$. We prove (\ref{intstratumstruct}). Fix $p\in M^{\mathfrak s}$. A neighborhood of $p$ is covered by strata $\succ\mathfrak s$, so since $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq M$ is not open, there exists a stratum $\mathfrak t\succ\mathfrak s$. Now $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq\partial M^{\leq\mathfrak t}$ is open by (\ref{topopen}), as is $M^{\mathfrak t}\subseteq M$. This gives a collar on one side of $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq M$. This still does not fill out a neighborhood of $p$, so there exists $\mathfrak t'\ne\mathfrak t$ with $\mathfrak t'\succ\mathfrak s$, giving a collar on the other side of $M^{\mathfrak s}\subseteq M$. Now by invariance of domain, we have thus exhausted a neighborhood of $p\in M^{\mathfrak s}$ inside $M$, and hence it follows using (\ref{inbdry}) that there are no more strata $\succ\mathfrak s$ other than $\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'$.
nodes.statement_short: Item by item: (i) from the definition, (ii)-(iii) from invariance of domain, (iv)-(v) by exhausting a neighborhood of a codimension-one stratum.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas with cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: Let $(X,\partial X)$ be a pair of compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a stratification $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ ($\mathcal S$ finite) along with a map $\dim:\mathcal S\to\mathbb Z$. Also fix ``orientation data'': \begin{rlist} \item For every $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S$, an orientation line $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}$ (i.e.\ a free $\mathbb Z/2$-graded $\mathbb Z$-module of rank one). \item For $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$, an odd ``coboundary'' map $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}$. \end{rlist} An \emph{implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary and cell-like stratification} on $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ consists of the same data as an implicit atlas with boundary, except that in addition we specify a $\Gamma_I$-invariant stratification $(X_I,\partial X_I)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ for all $I\subseteq A$, whose restriction to $X_\varnothing$ is the given stratification. We add the following ``compatibiltiy axiom'': \begin{rlist} \item The restriction of the stratification on $X_J$ to $(s_{J\setminus I}|X_J)^{-1}(0)$ coincides with the pullback of the stratification on $X_I$ via $\psi_{IJ}$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} and we modify one ``transversality axiom'': \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item(Submersion axiom) In the local model $\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$ (or $(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb R^{d+\dim E_I-1})\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}$), we require the stratification on the domain to be pulled back from a cell-like stratification on the first factor (for $\mathfrak s\mapsto\dim\mathfrak s+\dim E_I$). \end{rlist} We also specify isomorphisms of sheaves $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\xrightarrow\sim\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ over $(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ which are compatible with $\psi_{IJ}$ and such that the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\ar{r}\ar{d}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}\ar[equals]{d}\\ \mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}\ar{r}&\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} for $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ (the left vertical map is the tensor product of the coboundary map $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}$ and the inverse of the boundary map $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$). In other words, we identify $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}$ with the orientation line of the normal bundle of $(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$, so that the coboundary maps $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}$ coincide with the geometric coboundary maps on normal bundles. Given an implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$ on $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$, we may obtain by restriction to the corresponding strata an implicit atlas with cell-like stratification on $\partial X\to\partial\mathcal S$ (empty boundary, tensor every orientation line with $\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}$) and an implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification on $(X^{\leq\mathfrak s},X^{<\mathfrak s})\to(\mathcal S^{\leq\mathfrak s},\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak s})$ (tensor every orientation line with $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}^\vee$).
nodes.definiendum: implicit atlas of dimension $d$ with boundary and cell-like stratification
nodes.statement_short: Implicit atlas with boundary plus compatible invariant stratifications of all thickenings, locally pulled back from cell-like ones, with orientation-line data.

nodes.name: Possible weakening of cell-like condition
nodes.statement: There should be a slightly more general setting for the results of this section (and their proofs), which takes as input a weakened version of Definition \ref{celllikedef}. For example, it is probably enough to require that in a neighborhood of any $p\in M$, the closure of any (local) component of $M^{\mathfrak s}$ is a manifold with boundary whose interior is this local component (this is satisfied by both stratifications in Example \ref{celllikecornerexample}); basically this allows ``non-embedded faces''.

nodes.name: Stratified singular chains on a manifold with cell-like stratification
nodes.statement: As a first step towards understanding the main construction of this section, let us first describe a similar construction in a more familiar setting. Let $M$ be a topological manifold with cell-like stratification by $\mathcal S$. Define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C_{\bullet-(\dim M-\dim\mathfrak s)}(M^{\leq\mathfrak s};\mathfrak o_M\otimes\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak s}}^\vee) \end{equation} equipped with the differential given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ of the pushforwards $C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak s})\to C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak t})$ (covered by the dual of the boundary map $\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{M^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$) plus the internal differential. This differential squares to zero by Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} (the square of the differential is a sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=2$ of maps $C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak s})\to C_\bullet(M^{\leq\mathfrak t})$, each of which can be seen to vanish by applying Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure}(\ref{intstratumstruct}) to $M^{<\mathfrak t}\to\mathcal S^{<\mathfrak t}$). Now there is a natural map: \begin{align} C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)&\to C_\bullet(M)\\ \bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\gamma_{\mathfrak s}&\mapsto\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=\dim M\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_{\mathfrak s} \end{align} (it follows from Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} that this is a chain map) which we claim is a quasi-isomorphism. To see that \eqref{stratchainstousual} is a quasi-isomorphism, observe that it is the map on global sections of a corresponding map of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus K)$ on the one-point compactification $M_+$ of $M$. Both are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf}. Thus by Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}, it suffices to show that the map $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)\to C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $p\in M$. This holds by the following local argument. Note that $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ (to see this, consider the filtration by $\dim\mathfrak s$), so it suffices to construct a cycle in $C_\bullet(M,M\setminus p;\mathcal S)$ representing a generator of $\mathbb Z$ and show that its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)=\mathbb Z$ is a generator. Such a cycle may be constructed by induction on $\mathcal S$ (starting from the stratum containing $p$ and going up), and its image in $H_\bullet(M,M\setminus p)$ generates since its degree at $p$ coincides with its degree at any nearby point in an open stratum, which is one by construction. A similar argument appears in Barraud--Cornea \cite[p670, Lemma 2.2]{barraudcornea}. Thus we can think of $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)$ as a model for chains on $M$ (the reader should make sure they understand what this means geometrically).
nodes.statement_short: Builds $C_\bullet(M;\mathcal S)$ from chains on closed strata and shows it maps quasi-isomorphically to $C_\bullet(M)$, a model for stratified virtual cochains.
nodes.label: stratifiedchainsremark

nodes.name: Stratified virtual cochain complexes $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-,\mathcal S;A)$
nodes.statement: Let $(X,\partial X)\to(\mathcal S,\partial\mathcal S)$ be equipped with a finite implicit atlas with boundary and cell-like stratification $A$. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, we define: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K,\mathcal S;A):=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s} \end{equation} (on the right, $A$ refers to the restriction of the atlas to $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$) equipped with the differential given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t)=1$ of the pushforwards: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)\to C^{\bullet+1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak t}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A) \end{equation} tensored with the specified coboundary map $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}$ (plus the internal differential). The fact that this differential squares to zero follows from Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure} and the compatibility of the coboundary maps $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak t}$ with the geometric boundary maps $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak t}}\to\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}$. There is a natural map: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K,\mathcal S;A)&\xrightarrow\sim C^\bullet(K;A)\\ \{\gamma_{\mathfrak s}\}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}&\mapsto\biggl(\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d-1\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_{\mathfrak s},\sum_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\dim\mathfrak s=d\end{smallmatrix}}\gamma_{\mathfrak s}\biggr) \end{align} Note that for $\dim s=d$, the identification $\mathfrak o_{(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}=\mathfrak o_{X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ gives a (locally constant, but possibly not constant) isomorphism $\mathfrak o_{\mathfrak s}=\mathbb Z$ over $(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (and similarly for $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S$ with $\dim\mathfrak s=d-1$, see also Remark \ref{bdryorrmk}) which is used implicitly in \eqref{stratifiedtounformula}. This is a chain map by Lemma \ref{celllikelocalstructure}.
nodes.statement_short: Stratified virtual cochain complex: direct sum over strata of relative virtual cochains, with differential from codimension-one stratum pushforwards, plus a natural map to $C^\bullet(K;A)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.2.11
nodes.statement: Filter $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ by $\dim\mathfrak s$; the associated graded of this filtration is the direct sum of $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\cap X^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)$. Each these is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf on $X$ (pushforward from $X^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ to $X$ preserves homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves by Definition \ref{pushforwardofHsheavesworks}), and hence $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-,\mathcal S;A)$ is also a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}). Now the map \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves, so to check that it is a quasi-isomorphism, it suffices to check it is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}). For this, we may use the argument from Example \ref{stratifiedchainsremark} (adapted to the case with boundary) along with Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}. Moreover, this local construction also gives us the desired commutativity of the diagram of sheaves on $X$.
