nodes.name: Reduce to stalks
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to check the quasi-isomorphism on stalks.
nodes.statement: Now the map \eqref{stratifiedtounstratifiedpushforward} is a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves, so to check that it is a quasi-isomorphism, it suffices to check it is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (Corollary \ref{homotopysheafcheckqionstalks}).

nodes.name: Local argument
nodes.statement_short: Use the local argument of Example 6.2.9 with Lemma 4.3.13, which also gives commutativity.
nodes.statement: For this, we may use the argument from Example \ref{stratifiedchainsremark} (adapted to the case with boundary) along with Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}.  Moreover, this local construction also gives us the desired commutativity of the diagram of sheaves on $X$.

nodes.name: Product implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be spaces with implicit atlases $A_1$ and $A_2$ respectively. The \emph{product implicit atlas} $A_1\sqcup A_2$ on $X_1\times X_2$ is defined by setting $(X_1\times X_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2}:=(X_1)_{I_1}\times(X_2)_{I_2}$ and $(X_1\times Y_2)^{\mathrm{reg}}_{I_1\sqcup I_2}:=(X_1)_{I_1}^{\mathrm{reg}}\times(X_2)_{I_2}^{\mathrm{reg}}$, with the rest of the data extended in the obvious manner. Of course, this extends naturally to the setting of implicit atlases with boundary and cell-like stratification (given $X_1$ and $X_2$ stratified by $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ respectively, their product $X_1\times X_2$ is stratified by $\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2$, with $\partial(\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2):=(\partial\mathcal S_1\times\mathcal S_2)\cup(\mathcal S_1\times\partial\mathcal S_2)$).
nodes.statement_short: Product atlas $A_1\sqcup A_2$ on $X_1\times X_2$ with thickenings and regular loci taken as products; extends to boundary and cell-like stratifications.
nodes.label: productimplicitatlas

nodes.name: Product map on virtual cochain complexes for product implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be spaces with finite implicit atlases $A_1$ and $A_2$; equip $X_1\times X_2$ with the product implicit atlas $A_1\sqcup A_2$. Let us define a canonical map: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2) \end{equation} which is compatible with the maps \eqref{Fpushforward} and \eqref{Fpushforward1} and is associative. There are isomorphisms $(X_1)_{I_1,J_1,A_1}\times(X_2)_{I_2,J_2,A_2}\to(X_1\times X_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2,A_1\sqcup A_2}$ which are compatible with the maps \eqref{pushforward}. This induces maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)_{I_1,J_1}\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)_{I_2,J_2}\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2} \end{equation} These maps are compatible with the maps \eqref{Epushforward1more} (note that this compatibility uses the commutativity of \eqref{chainproductcommutes}). It follows using Definition \ref{simplicialproduct} that they induce the desired map \eqref{productatlaspushforward}. Note also that \eqref{productatlaspushforward} extends to a collection of maps: \begin{equation} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_1\times K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2) \end{equation} for compact $K_1\subseteq X_1$ and $K_2\subseteq X_2$, which are compatible with restriction, thus inducing a map of sheaves $p_1^\ast\mathfrak o_{X_1}\otimes p_2^\ast\mathfrak o_{X_2}\to\mathfrak o_{X_1\times X_2}$. It can be checked that this is the tautological such map by checking locally (i.e.\ for $K_1$ and $K_2$ single points) using Lemma \ref{localdescofISO}.
nodes.statement_short: Defines the associative product map $C_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1)\otimes C_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_2)\to C_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\times X_2)$ for the product atlas, compatible with restriction.
nodes.label: productatlasF

nodes.name: Equation productatlaspushforward
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)
nodes.label: productatlaspushforward

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)_{I_1,J_1}\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)_{I_2,J_2}\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X_1\times X_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)_{I_1\sqcup I_2,J_1\sqcup J_2}

nodes.name: Equation productatlaspushforwardonK
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_1\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_2)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K_1\times K_2\operatorname{rel}\partial;A_1\sqcup A_2)
nodes.label: productatlaspushforwardonK

nodes.name: Ground ring convention for Section 7
nodes.statement: In this section, we work over a fixed ground ring $R$, and everything takes place in the category of $R$-modules unless stated otherwise. We restrict to implicit atlases $A$ for which $\#\Gamma_\alpha$ is invertible in $R$ for all $\alpha\in A$.

nodes.name: Diagram $\mathbb H:Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ (informal)
nodes.statement_short: Informally, a diagram $\mathbb H$ assigns boundary maps, chain maps, homotopies and higher homotopies to the simplices of $Z_\bullet$.
nodes.statement:
Given a flow category diagram $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, our goal is to construct:
\begin{rlist}
\item For every $\sigma\in Z_0$, a boundary map $R[\mathcal P_{z_0}]\to R[\mathcal P_{z_0}]$.
\item For every $\sigma\in Z_1$, a chain map $R[\mathcal P_{z_0}]\to R[\mathcal P_{z_1}]$.
\item For every $\sigma\in Z_2$, a chain homotopy between the two maps $R[\mathcal P_{z_0}]\to R[\mathcal P_{z_2}]$.
\item For every $\sigma\in Z_3$, \ldots
\end{rlist}
We will refer to such data as a \emph{diagram} $\mathbb H:Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ (see Definition \ref{NdgdefII} for a precise formulation).

nodes.name: Morse--Smale case: diagram from counting flow spaces
nodes.statement: Indeed, when the flow spaces $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ are compact oriented manifolds with corners of dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ in a compatible manner (that is, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ is a \emph{Morse--Smale flow category diagram}), one may obtain such a diagram $\mathbb H$ by counting the $0$-dimensional flow spaces (one may see that the maps satisfy the required identities by considering the boundary of the $1$-dimensional flow spaces).

nodes.name: Space of coherent choices $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ (informal)
nodes.statement_short: $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is characterized by sections of $\pi$ being coherent choices of virtual fundamental cycles.
nodes.statement: Given a flow category diagram $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ with an implicit atlas, we encode the ``space'' of coherent choices via a map $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$.  Namely, $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is defined by the property that \emph{giving a section $s:Z_\bullet\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ of $\pi$ is the same as making coherent choices over all of $Z_\bullet$}.

nodes.name: Canonical diagram $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$ on $\tilde Z_\bullet$ (informal)
nodes.statement_short: $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$ on $\tilde Z_\bullet$ is the diagram whose pullback along a section $s$ is the diagram $\mathbb H$ of those coherent choices.
nodes.statement: Now, the statement that coherent choices give rise to a diagram $\mathbb H:Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ translates into a canonical diagram $\widetilde{\mathbb H}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ (defined essentially by the property that the set of coherent choices over $Z_\bullet$ corresponding to a section $s:Z_\bullet\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ gives rise to the diagram $\mathbb H:=\widetilde{\mathbb H}\circ s$).

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Z_\bullet@>\widetilde{\mathbb H}>>\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)\cr @V\pi VV\cr Z_\bullet \end{CD}

nodes.name: Restricting to the $2$-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: If one is satisfied with working in the homotopy category (i.e.\ constructing a diagram $Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$), then one needs only the $2$-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$. On the other hand, there is little simplification to be gained by using $2$-truncated semisimplicial sets instead of semisimplicial sets. Moreover, the ``higher homotopies'' which are kept track of in $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_R)$ are known to contain interesting information in certain settings (for example, they can be used to obstruct isotopies between symplectic embeddings, as in Floer--Hofer--Wysocki \cite{floerhoferwysockiSHI}).
nodes.statement_short: Working only up to homotopy needs just the 2-skeleton of $Z_\bullet$, but higher homotopies carry useful information.
nodes.label: restricttotwoskeleton

nodes.name: Simplicial set and semisimplicial set
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta$ be the category of finite nonempty totally ordered sets with morphisms weakly order-preserving maps. Let $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ be the subcategory of injective morphisms. A \emph{simplicial set} $Z_\bullet$ is a functor $Z:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Set}$, and a \emph{semisimplicial set} $Z_\bullet$ is a functor $Z:\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Set}$. In both cases, we write $Z_n$ for $Z(\{0,\ldots,n\})$. For $\sigma\in Z_n$ and $0\leq j_0<\cdots<j_m\leq n$, we denote by $\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$ the image of $\sigma$ under the map $Z_n\to Z_m$ induced by the map $\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,\ldots,n\}$ given by $i\mapsto j_i$ ($\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$ is called a facet of $\sigma$); if $m=0$ we also write $\sigma(j)$ for $\sigma|[j]$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicial and semisimplicial sets as presheaves on $\Delta$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$, with facet notation $\sigma|[j_0\ldots j_m]$.

nodes.name: Set of generators
nodes.statement: Let $Z$ be a set. A \emph{set of generators} $\mathcal P/Z$ is a collection of sets $\{\mathcal P_z\}_{z\in Z}$, each equipped with a grading $\operatorname{gr}:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb Z$ and an ``action'' $a:\mathcal P_z\to\mathbb R$. Given a set of generators $\mathcal P/Z$ and a map $f:Y\to Z$, we can form the pullback set of generators $f^\ast\mathcal P/Y$ defined by $(f^\ast\mathcal P)_y:=\mathcal P_{f(y)}$.
nodes.statement_short: A set of generators $\mathcal P/Z$: graded sets $\mathcal P_z$ with action functional, and their pullbacks.

nodes.name: Triples $(\sigma,p,q)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set, and let $\mathcal P/Z_0$ be a set of generators. The notation $(\sigma,p,q)$ \emph{always} means a triple where $\sigma\in Z_n$ is an $n$-simplex and $(p,q)\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}\times\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}$, where either $\dim\sigma>0$ or $a(p)<a(q)$. We say that $(\sigma',p',q')\prec(\sigma,p,q)$ (``strictly precedes'') iff one of the two conditions holds: \begin{rlist} \item$\sigma'\subsetneqq\sigma$ (i.e.\ $\sigma'$ is a facet of positive codimension of $\sigma$). \item$\sigma'=\sigma$ and $a(p)\leq a(p')$ and $a(q')\leq a(q)$ with at least one inequality being strict. \end{rlist} It is easy to see that $\prec$ is a partial order.
nodes.statement_short: Triples $(\sigma,p,q)$ of a simplex and generators at its ends, with the strict precedence partial order $\prec$.

nodes.name: $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set, and let $\mathcal P/Z_0$ be a set of generators. Let $\mathcal C^\otimes$ be a monoidal category with an initial object $0\in\mathcal C$ such that $X\otimes 0=0=0\otimes X$ for all $X\in\mathcal C$. An \emph{$\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module} $\mathcal W$ (often abbreviated ``$\mathsf{F}$-module'') in $\mathcal C$ is a collection of objects $\mathcal W=\{\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\in\mathcal C\}_{(\sigma,p,q)}$ equipped with: \begin{align} \text{\emph{Product maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,r)\quad\text{for }0\leq k\leq n\\ \text{\emph{Face maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\quad\text{for }0<k<n \end{align} which are compatible in a sense we will now describe. Note that for both \eqref{Wcomposition} and \eqref{Wsimplexextension}, the triples indexing the domain strictly precede the triple indexing the target (because we always restrict to triples $(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\dim\sigma>0$ or $a(p)<a(q)$). Now given any $\sigma\in Z_\bullet$ spanning vertices $0,\ldots,n$ and a choice of: \begin{align} 0&=j_0<\cdots<j_\ell=n\\ 0&=a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_m=\ell\\ p_i&\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(j_{a_i})}\quad\text{for }0\leq i\leq m \end{align} we can apply the product map $m-1$ times and the face map $n-\ell$ times in some order to obtain a map: \begin{equation} \mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p_0,p_m) \end{equation} We say that the product/face maps are \emph{compatible} iff this map is independent of the order in which they are applied (this reduces to three basic commutation identities). Given an $\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module $\mathcal W$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback $f^\ast\mathcal W$ which is an $\mathsf{F}(f^\ast\mathcal P/Y_\bullet)$-module defined by $(f^\ast\mathcal W)(\sigma,p,q):=\mathcal W(f(\sigma),p,q)$. The categories $\mathcal C$ relevant for this paper are: \begin{rlist} \item The category of spaces with the product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module space''). \item The category of posets with the product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module poset''). \item The category of chain complexes with the tensor product monoidal structure (``$\mathsf{F}$-module complex''). \end{rlist} All are in fact symmetric monoidal (noting that the relevant symmetric monoidal structure on complexes is the super tensor product).
nodes.statement_short: An $\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module: objects $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$ in a monoidal category with compatible product and face maps; spaces, posets and complexes are the cases used.
nodes.label: flowobjectdef

nodes.name: Equation Wcomposition
nodes.statement: \text{\emph{Product maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,r)\quad\text{for }0\leq k\leq n
nodes.label: Wcomposition

nodes.name: Equation Wsimplexextension
nodes.statement: \text{\emph{Face maps}:}&&\mathcal W(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\quad\text{for }0<k<n
nodes.label: Wsimplexextension

nodes.name: Equation SdataA
nodes.statement: 0&=j_0<\cdots<j_\ell=n\\ 0&=a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_m=\ell
nodes.label: SdataA

nodes.name: Equation SdataB
nodes.statement: p_i&\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(j_{a_i})}\quad\text{for }0\leq i\leq m
nodes.label: SdataB

nodes.name: Equation Wtotalcomposition
nodes.statement: \mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal W(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p_0,p_m)
nodes.label: Wtotalcomposition

nodes.name: $\mathsf{F}$-module space of broken Morse trajectories
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be any semisimplicial set, and let us take as set of generators $\mathcal P:=Z_0$ (i.e.\ a single generator over every vertex of $Z_\bullet$). We define an $\mathsf{F}(\mathcal P/Z_\bullet)$-module space $\mathcal W$ by $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q):=\mathcal F(\sigma)$, where $\mathcal F$ is the space of broken Morse trajectories from Definition \ref{simplexflows}. The reader may easily verify that this forms an $\mathsf{F}$-module space, with product/face maps given by \eqref{Fproduct}--\eqref{Fface}.
nodes.label: Fmoduleexample

nodes.name: Support of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module. We define the \emph{support} of $\mathcal W$, denoted $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$, as the smallest collection of triples containing those for which $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)\ne 0$ that is closed under product/face operations (meaning that if the triples on the left side of \eqref{Wcomposition} or \eqref{Wsimplexextension} are in the set, then so is the triple on the right). Equivalently, $(\sigma,p,q)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$ iff there is some choice of \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB} for which $p_0=p$ and $p_m=q$ and for which every factor on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} is $\ne 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Support of an $\mathsf{F}$-module: the smallest product/face-closed set of triples containing those with nonzero $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)$.

nodes.name: Strata of an $\mathsf{F}$-module
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module. We let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the set of choices of \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB} for which $p_0=p$ and $p_m=q$ and for which every factor on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} is in $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W$. We equip $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ with the partial order induced by formally applying product/face maps. The reader may easily convince themselves that $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ is itself an $\mathsf{F}$-module poset. There is an order-reversing map $\operatorname{codim}:\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$ defined by $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s:=(m-1)+(n-\ell)$ for $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$. We let $\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the unique maximal element (the only element $\mathfrak s$ with $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s=0$; it is given by $\ell=n$ and $m=1$). For $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$, we let $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ denote the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition}. The following \emph{boundary inclusion map}: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} (where $\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ denotes $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}$) will play an important role.
nodes.statement_short: Poset $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ of ways to factor a triple, its codimension function, top element, and the boundary inclusion map.

nodes.name: Equation boundaryinclusion
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: boundaryinclusion

nodes.name: Flow category diagram
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a semisimplicial set. A \emph{flow category diagram} $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ (read ``$\mathcal X$ over $Z_\bullet$'') is: \begin{rlist} \item A set of generators $\mathcal P/Z_0$. \item An $\mathsf{F}$-module space $\mathcal X$ where each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is compact Hausdorff and each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \item A stratification of each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ by $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ which is compatible with the product/face maps and so that $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\to\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a homeomorphism onto $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} with the following finiteness properties: \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \itemFor all $\sigma$, $p$, and $M<\infty$, we have $\#\{q:\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\ne\varnothing\text{ and }a(q)<a(p)+M\}<\infty$. \itemFor all $\sigma$, we have $\inf\{a(q)-a(p):\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\ne\varnothing\}>-\infty$. \setcounter{rcountsave}{\value{rcounti}} \end{rlist} Let $H$ be a group. An \emph{$H$-equivariant flow category diagram} is a flow category diagram along with: \begin{rlist} \setcounter{rcounti}{\value{rcountsave}} \item A free action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$. \item An action of $H$ on $\mathcal X$ (meaning compatible maps $h:\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathcal X(\sigma,hp,hq)$). \item Homomorphisms $\operatorname{gr}:H\to\mathbb Z$ and $a:H\to\mathbb R$ such that $\operatorname{gr}(hp)=\operatorname{gr}(h)+\operatorname{gr}(p)$ and $a(hp)=a(h)+a(p)$ for all $h\in H$ and $p\in\mathcal P$. \end{rlist} Given an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback $H$-equivariant flow category diagram $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: A flow category diagram $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$: generators plus a compact stratified $\mathsf{F}$-module space with Novikov-type finiteness; also an $H$-equivariant version.
nodes.label: semisimplicialfcdef

nodes.name: Morse--Smale flow category diagram
nodes.statement: A \emph{Morse--Smale} flow category diagram is one in which each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a (compact) topological manifold with corners of dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ (the corner structure being induced by the stratification by $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$).
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
differentia: each $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ is a (compact) topological manifold with corners of dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$
nodes.label: MSflowcatediag

nodes.name: $\infty$-category $\mathsf{FlowCat}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{FlowCat}$ be the semisimplicial set which represents the functor $Z_\bullet\mapsto\{$Flow category diagrams over $Z_\bullet\}$. The reader familiar with $\infty$-categories may wish to think of $\mathsf{FlowCat}$ as an $\infty$-category of flow categories (though only in a vague sense, since we have not given it the structure of a simplicial set, nor have we verified the weak Kan condition). All of the constructions in this section involving flow category diagrams over a semisimplicial set $Z_\bullet$ are compatible with pullback, and thus can be equivalently thought of as ``universal'' constructions over $\mathsf{FlowCat}^{\mathsf{IA}}$ (which represents the functor of flow category diagrams equipped with implicit atlases).
nodes.section: 7.2 Flow category diagrams and their implicit atlases
nodes.statement_short: $\mathsf{FlowCat}$, the semisimplicial set representing flow category diagrams, viewed loosely as an $\infty$-category; constructions are universal over $\mathsf{FlowCat}^{\mathsf{IA}}$.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas on flow category diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram. An implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ consists of the following data. We give index sets $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$, and we define:\footnote{Warning: a particular set $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma',p',q')$ may appear many times on the right hand side.} \begin{equation} \mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}:=\coprod_{\begin{smallmatrix}0\leq i_0<\cdots<i_m\leq n\cr(p',q')\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_0)}\times\mathcal P_{\sigma(i_m)}\cr\exists\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\text{ containing }([i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')\end{smallmatrix}}\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m],p',q') \end{equation} We explain the notation: recall that $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ parameterizes the ``possible left hand sides'' of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition}; the coproduct is over all $([i_0\ldots i_m],p',q')$ which appear as a factor in some $\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ with $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$. For all $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$, we give an implicit atlas with boundary with cell-like stratification $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (stratified by $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, of virtual dimension $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s$), for which the stratification conforms to the following local model. Given $\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak s$, let $G=G(\mathfrak s',\mathfrak s)$ denote the set of possible product/face operations which may be applied to $\mathfrak s'$ for which the result is still $\preceq\mathfrak s$. There is a tautological isomorphism of posets $2^G\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak s'\leq\cdot\leq\mathfrak s}$ sending a given set of product/face operations to the result of applying them to $\mathfrak s'$. Now the local model for the stratification on (regular thickened moduli spaces of) $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ near a point of type $\mathfrak s'$ is given by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^G\times\mathbb R^N$, stratified in the obvious way by $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak s'\leq\cdot\leq\mathfrak s}$. Clearly this stratification is cell-like. Moreover, the normal bundle to the $\mathfrak s'$ stratum is canonically identified with $\mathfrak o_{\mathbb R}^{\otimes G(\mathfrak s',\mathfrak s)}$, and the implicit atlas should use this as the orientation data. In addition, we give compatible identifications between these atlases as follows: \begin{rlist} \itemLet $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (the former by restriction to this substratum of $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak t}$), and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \itemLet $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on: \begin{equation*} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s} \end{equation*} and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \itemLet $\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,r)$. Then by definition: \begin{equation*} \mathcal A(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s_1}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak s_2}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,r)^{\geq(\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2)} \end{equation*} Both are implicit atlases on: \begin{equation*} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)^{\leq(\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2)} \end{equation*} and we identify the former with the subatlas of the latter corresponding to this tautological inclusion of index sets. \end{rlist} An implicit atlas on an $H$-equivariant flow category $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ is an implicit atlas along with a lift of the action of $H$ to the implicit atlas structure. Given an implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback implicit atlas $f^\ast\mathcal A$ on $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.

nodes.name: Coherent orientations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with locally orientable implicit atlas $\mathcal A$. A set of \emph{coherent orientations} $\omega$ is a choice of global sections $\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$ with the following property. Note that covering each of the product/face maps: \begin{align} \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,r)\\ \mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} is an isomorphism of orientation sheaves. We require that $\omega$ transform in the following way under this isomorphism: \begin{align} \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,r)\\ -\omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&=(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}d\omega(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} where $d\omega\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X})$ is the boundary orientation induced by $\omega$. Each of the following: \begin{gather} \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\ell],p',p'')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p'',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\ell],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')\times\omega(\sigma|[k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p',q)\\ \omega(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots\hat\ell\ldots n],p,q) \end{gather} can be expressed in terms of $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in two different ways using \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface}. One can easily check that with the choice of signs in \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface}, these two expressions coincide for each of \eqref{multiorientationI}--\eqref{multiorientationIV} (the Koszul rule of signs applies to calculating the boundary of a product of orientations, which means that this coherence condition involves $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,p')$ for both \eqref{multiorientationI} and \eqref{multiorientationIII}). Coherent orientations on an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas are coherent orientations which are invariant under the action of $H$. Given coherent orientations $\omega$ on $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ and a map $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$, we can form the pullback coherent orientations $f^\ast\omega$ on $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$.

nodes.statement: One can obtain alternative sign conventions in \eqref{coherentOproduct}--\eqref{coherentOface} by ``twisting'' $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$. For example, multiplying $\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ by $(-1)$ flips the sign of \eqref{coherentOproduct}, multiplying by $(-1)^{\dim\sigma}$ flips the sign of \eqref{coherentOface}, and multiplying by $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}$ or $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(q)}$ multiplies \eqref{coherentOproduct} by $(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(q)}$.

nodes.name: Augmented virtual cochain complexes $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]\in C_\bullet(E;\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$. We define the following complexes: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\hphantom{\Biggl\{}C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\begin{cases}\hfill C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t=\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}\cr C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{align} The structure maps of the homotopy diagrams come from the obvious pushforward maps (for increasing $\mathfrak s$) and the maps \eqref{Fpushforward1} using the fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$ (for decreasing $\mathfrak t$). These are compatible because of the commutativity of \eqref{chainproductcommutes}. Next, let us observe that we have a natural commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\ar{d}\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\ar{d}\\ C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\ar[hook]{r}{\sim}&C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The horizontal maps (inclusions of the $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t=\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}$ subcomplexes) are quasi-isomorphisms by Lemma \ref{comboretraction} (which morally says that $\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ acts as a final object in the homotopy colimits \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII}) which applies because each of the structure maps from $(\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t)$ to $(\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t')$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Note that by definition, the support of $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$ and of $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+$ are contained in the support of $\mathcal X$.
nodes.statement_short: Augmented virtual cochain complexes as homotopy colimits over pairs $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$ of stratum cochains, quasi-isomorphic to the non-augmented ones.
nodes.label: Gsheavesdef

nodes.name: Equation GmasterI
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)&:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\hphantom{\Biggl\{}C^{\bullet-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})

nodes.name: Equation GmasterII

nodes.name: Product/face maps for $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$. Let us now define face and product maps for $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$. These will be of degree $1$ and will be equipped with a canonical factorization through $C^{\bullet-1}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+$. In other words, we really are going to construct maps: \begin{align} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,r)\\ C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{align} We construct \eqref{Csimplexextension}. The corresponding face map for $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}$ is covered by a corresponding morphism of the homotopy diagrams \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII} (namely \eqref{Fpushforward1} using the fixed fundamental cycle $[E_{\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}\setminus\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,\hat k,\ldots,n],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}}]$). This gives rise to a corresponding map \eqref{Csimplexextension} on homotopy colimits. We construct \eqref{Ccomposition}. We construct a morphism of homotopy diagrams \eqref{GmasterI}--\eqref{GmasterII} covering the corresponding product map for $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}$. Using the product operation on homotopy diagrams (Definition \ref{simplicialproduct}), it suffices to construct compatible maps: \begin{multline} C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1})\otimes\\mathcal C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2})\\\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2}) \end{multline} for $\mathfrak s_1\preceq\mathfrak t_1\in\mathcal S(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)$ and $\mathfrak s_2\preceq\mathfrak t_2\in\mathcal S(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)$. By definition, the subatlas $\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1}\sqcup\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2}\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2}$ is the product implicit atlas on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}=\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\times\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}$. Thus the desired map is constructed in Definition \ref{productatlasF}.
nodes.statement_short: Constructs degree-one product and face maps on augmented virtual cochain complexes via morphisms of homotopy diagrams and the product atlas map.
nodes.label: Cproductface

nodes.name: Equation Ccomposition
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q)\otimes C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r)&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,r)

nodes.name: Equation Csimplexextension
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,q)&\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[0,\ldots,k],p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1})\otimes\\mathcal C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\leq\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma|[k,\ldots,n],q,r)^{\geq\mathfrak t_2})\\\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_1\times\mathfrak s_2}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t_1\times\mathfrak t_2})

nodes.name: Complexes $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be a flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$, where every $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite and we have fixed fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]$. We define: \begin{equation} C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q):=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A^{\geq\mathfrak t}(\sigma,p,q)) \end{equation} where the maps in the homotopy diagram are $\times[E_{A(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t')\setminus A(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak t)}]$. We equip $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$ with product/face maps just as in Definition \ref{Cproductface}. Now there are natural maps: \begin{equation} C^{\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)+\bullet}_{\mathrm{vir}}(\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q)\xrightarrow{s_\ast}C_{-\bullet}(E;\mathcal A)^+(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} (induced by \eqref{Fpushforward}), which are maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules (that is, they respect the product/face maps). Note that by definition, the support of $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)^+$ is contained in the support of $\mathcal X$.

conclusions: an injection of modules with projective cokernel automatically splits

nodes.name: Cofibrations of complexes
nodes.statement: We say a complex is \emph{cofibrant} iff it is projective (as a module). We say a map of complexes is a \emph{cofibration} iff it is injective and its cokernel is cofibrant; we use the arrow $\rightarrowtail$ to indicate that a map is a cofibration. It is easy to check that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration.

nodes.name: Composition of cofibrations is a cofibration
conclusions: a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration.

nodes.name: Cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. We say that $\mathcal W_\bullet$ is \emph{cofibrant} iff for all $(\sigma,p,q)$: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. \item The map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{equation} is a cofibration. \end{rlist}
nodes.label: Fmodulecofibrantdef

nodes.name: Equation boundaryinjective
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)
nodes.label: boundaryinjective

nodes.name: Generalized boundary maps of a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex are cofibrations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Then the map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0) \end{equation} a cofibration for all $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$.
assumptions: $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex
conclusions: a cofibration for all $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$
nodes.statement_short: In a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex, the colimit over strata strictly below any $\mathfrak s_0$ maps by a cofibration to $\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0)$.
nodes.label: cofibrantinjectivelemma

nodes.name: Equation generalizedboundaryinjective
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s_0)
nodes.label: generalizedboundaryinjective

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.22
nodes.statement: Write $\mathfrak s_0$ in the form \eqref{SdataA}--\eqref{SdataB}. Then we have: \begin{equation} \mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_0}=\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m) \end{equation} Now we consider the $m$-cubical diagram: \begin{equation} \bigotimes_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right] \end{equation} Now \eqref{generalizedboundaryinjective} is simply the map to the maximal vertex of the $m$-cube from the colimit over the $m$-cube minus the maximal vertex. This is a cofibration for any cubical diagram of the form $\bigotimes_{i=1}^m[A_i\rightarrowtail B_i]$ where each $A_i\rightarrowtail B_i$ is a cofibration. To see this, write $B_i=A_i\oplus P_i$ where $P_i$ is projective, and then the map is obviously injective with cokernel $\bigotimes_{i=1}^mP_i$. A tensor product of projective modules is projective, as can be seen using either the tensor-hom adjunction or the fact that a module is projective iff it is a direct summand of a free module.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the poset below $\mathfrak s_0$ as a product and view the map as the corner map of an $m$-cube tensor of cofibrations, whose cokernel is a tensor of projectives.

nodes.name: Product decomposition of the poset
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mathfrak s_0$ via its factors so the poset below it is a product.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s_0}=\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_0}\ldots j_{a_1}],p_0,p_1)\times\cdots\times\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_{m-1}}\ldots j_{a_m}],p_{m-1},p_m)

nodes.name: Cubical diagram
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the $m$-cubical tensor diagram of boundary cofibrations.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \bigotimes_{i=1}^m\left[\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma|[j_{a_{i-1}}\ldots j_{a_i}],p_{i-1},p_i)\right]

nodes.name: Identify the map
nodes.statement_short: The map is the corner map of the cube.
nodes.statement: Now \eqref{generalizedboundaryinjective} is simply the map to the maximal vertex of the $m$-cube from the colimit over the $m$-cube minus the maximal vertex.

nodes.name: Corner map of a cube of cofibrations
nodes.statement_short: Splitting each cofibration shows the corner map is injective with projective cokernel.
nodes.statement: This is a cofibration for any cubical diagram of the form $\bigotimes_{i=1}^m[A_i\rightarrowtail B_i]$ where each $A_i\rightarrowtail B_i$ is a cofibration.  To see this, write $B_i=A_i\oplus P_i$ where $P_i$ is projective, and then the map is obviously injective with cokernel $\bigotimes_{i=1}^mP_i$.  A tensor product of projective modules is projective, as can be seen using either the tensor-hom adjunction or the fact that a module is projective iff it is a direct summand of a free module.

nodes.name: Colimits over nested downward closed subsets give cofibrations
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ be finite downward closed subsets. Then the map: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s) \end{equation} is a cofibration. In particular, $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ is projective (take $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ above).
assumptions: $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex
$\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ be finite downward closed subsets
conclusions: is a cofibration
In particular, $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ is projective
nodes.statement_short: For finite downward closed $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T$, the induced map of colimits is a cofibration; hence such colimits are projective.
nodes.label: cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\rightarrowtail\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal T}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.23
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_{\mathfrak s}:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal T$, the case $\mathcal T=\varnothing$ being clear. Using the fact that a composition of cofibrations is again a cofibration, it suffices to consider the case $(\mathcal S,\mathcal T)=(\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0,\mathcal S)$ where $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ is a maximal element. Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_{\mathfrak s}$ is the colimit of the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] &A_{\mathfrak s_0}\\ \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}}A_{\mathfrak s}\ar[tail]{ur}\ar[tail]{rd}\\ &\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_{\mathfrak s} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where the top arrow is a cofibration by Lemma \ref{cofibrantinjectivelemma} and the bottom arrow is a cofibration by the induction hypothesis. It follows that $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_{\mathfrak s}\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_{\mathfrak s}$ is injective, with cokernel isomorphic to the cokernel of the top map above. Hence it is a cofibration as needed.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $|\mathcal T|$: add one maximal element at a time, exhibiting the colimit as a pushout of cofibrations given by Lemma 7.4.22.

nodes.name: Pushout description

Hence it is a cofibration as needed.

nodes.name: Cofibrant replacement functor $Q$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex. Suppose that $\mathcal W_\bullet$ satisfies the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item Each $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. \item Each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \end{rlist} In this case, we define (functorially) an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex $Q\mathcal W_\bullet$ (called the \emph{cofibrant replacement}) with the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$Q\mathcal W_\bullet$ is cofibrant. \item$\operatorname{supp} Q\mathcal W_\bullet=\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$. \item There is a (functorial) surjective quasi-isomorphism $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ (compatible with product/face maps). \end{rlist} We define $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ and the product/face maps with target $(\sigma,p,q)$ by induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_{\mathcal W}$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$. This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction. The inductive step for $(\sigma,p,q)$ works as follows. By the induction hypothesis, we have defined $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ for all $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$. Hence it suffices to construct (functorially) $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ fitting into the following commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}}Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{d}\ar[dashed, tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}&?\exists\,Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed, two heads]{d}{\sim}\\ \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}&\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Now we define $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ to be the mapping cylinder of the diagonal composition. Since the domain and codomain of this map are both cofibrant (for the domain, use Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}, which applies since $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ has been assumed to be finite), it follows that the top map is a cofibration and that $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is cofibrant. The product/face maps with target $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ are defined using the top horizontal map; they are compatible since by construction they factor through the colimit in the upper left corner. Certainly $\operatorname{supp} Q\mathcal W_\bullet\supseteq\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$. Conversely, suppose $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)$ is nonzero. Then either $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ne 0$ (so $(\sigma,p,q)\in\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$), or $Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ne 0$ for some $\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S(\sigma,p,q)$ (so by induction, the triples comprising $\mathfrak s$ are in $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal W_\bullet$, and hence so is $(\sigma,p,q)$).
nodes.statement_short: Inductive mapping-cylinder construction of a functorial cofibrant replacement $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\to\mathcal W_\bullet$ with the same support.
nodes.label: cofibrantreplacements

nodes.name: Equation cofibrantdefdiagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}}Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{d}\ar[dashed, tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}&?\exists\,Q\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed, two heads]{d}{\sim}\\ \displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}&\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Tensor products of cofibrant complexes preserve vanishing of negative homology
nodes.statement: Let $\{C_\bullet^k\}_{k=1}^n$ be cofibrant complexes over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_iC_\bullet^k=0$ for $i<0$. Then $H_i(\bigotimes_{k=1}^nC_\bullet^k)=0$ for $i<0$.
assumptions: $\{C_\bullet^k\}_{k=1}^n$ be cofibrant complexes over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_iC_\bullet^k=0$ for $i<0$
conclusions: $H_i(\bigotimes_{k=1}^nC_\bullet^k)=0$ for $i<0$
nodes.label: tensorproductvanishing

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.25
nodes.statement: Since the tensor product of projective modules is projective, we may use induction to reduce to the case $k=2$. Thus, we have two cofibrant complexes $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ with $H_iA_\bullet=H_iB_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$ and we would like to conclude that $H_i(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)=0$ for $i<0$. This follows from the K\"unneth theorem, specifically in the form of \cite[p301, Theorem 9.16]{osborne} or \cite[p679, Theorem 10.81]{rotman} (both of which apply because $\operatorname{Tor}^i_{\mathbb Z}(\cdot,\cdot)=0$ for $i>1$).\footnote{If we were assuming $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ to be bounded below, then we could apply the K\"unneth spectral sequence $\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_p(H_iA_\bullet,H_jB_\bullet)\Rightarrow H_{p+q}(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)$ (see \cite[p686, Theorem 10.90]{rotman}) to reach the desired conclusion without any assumptions on the ground ring.}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce by induction to two factors, then apply the Künneth theorem over $\mathbb Z$.

nodes.name: Reduce to two factors
nodes.statement_short: Induction reduces to $k=2$.
nodes.statement: Since the tensor product of projective modules is projective, we may use induction to reduce to the case $k=2$.

nodes.name: Künneth theorem
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Künneth theorem over $\mathbb Z$.
nodes.statement: Thus, we have two cofibrant complexes $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ with $H_iA_\bullet=H_iB_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$ and we would like to conclude that $H_i(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)=0$ for $i<0$.  This follows from the K\"unneth theorem, specifically in the form of \cite[p301, Theorem 9.16]{osborne} or \cite[p679, Theorem 10.81]{rotman} (both of which apply because $\operatorname{Tor}^i_{\mathbb Z}(\cdot,\cdot)=0$ for $i>1$).\footnote{If we were assuming $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ to be bounded below, then we could apply the K\"unneth spectral sequence $\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_p(H_iA_\bullet,H_jB_\bullet)\Rightarrow H_{p+q}(A_\bullet\otimes B_\bullet)$ (see \cite[p686, Theorem 10.90]{rotman}) to reach the desired conclusion without any assumptions on the ground ring.}

nodes.name: Surjectivity of homology onto colimits of a cofibrant F-module complex
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_i\mathcal W_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$. Then for any finite downward closed subset $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$, the map: \begin{equation} H_i\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\twoheadrightarrow H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s) \end{equation} is surjective for $i\leq 0$. Moreover, both sides vanish for $i<0$.
assumptions: $\mathcal W_\bullet$ be a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex over $\mathbb Z$ such that $H_i\mathcal W_\bullet=0$ for $i<0$
for any finite downward closed subset $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$
conclusions: is surjective for $i\leq 0$
Moreover, both sides vanish for $i<0$
nodes.statement_short: For a cofibrant $\mathsf{F}$-module complex with no negative homology, $H_i$ of the direct sum surjects onto $H_i$ of the colimit for $i\le 0$, and both vanish for $i<0$.
nodes.label: Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit

nodes.name: Equation tocolimitsurjective
nodes.statement: H_i\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\twoheadrightarrow H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)
nodes.label: tocolimitsurjective

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.26
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_{\mathfrak s}:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$. Since $A_{\mathfrak s}$ is a tensor product of various $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma',p',q')$, it follows (using Lemma \ref{tensorproductvanishing}) that $H_iA_{\mathfrak s}$ for $i<0$, so the left hand side of \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} vanishes for $i<0$. Hence it remains just to show that \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} is surjective for $i\leq 0$. We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal S$, the case $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ being clear. Let $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ be any maximal element. Now $\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_{\mathfrak s}$ is the colimit of \eqref{colimitdiagrambuildup}; it follows that we have the following exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s\to A_{\mathfrak s_0}\oplus\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_{\mathfrak s}\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_{\mathfrak s}\to 0 \end{equation} By the induction hypothesis, it suffices to show that the second map above is surjective on $H_i$ for $i\leq 0$. By the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{colimitSEScofibrant}, it suffices to show that $H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s=0$ for $i<0$. Now this follows from the induction hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing follows from Lemma 7.4.25; surjectivity by induction on $|\mathcal S|$ using the short exact sequence of the pushout and its long exact sequence.

nodes.name: Vanishing in negative degrees
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 7.4.25 each $A_{\mathfrak s}$ has no negative homology.
nodes.statement: Let us abbreviate $A_{\mathfrak s}:=\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$.  Since $A_{\mathfrak s}$ is a tensor product of various $\mathcal W_\bullet(\sigma',p',q')$, it follows (using Lemma \ref{tensorproductvanishing}) that $H_iA_{\mathfrak s}$ for $i<0$, so the left hand side of \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} vanishes for $i<0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to surjectivity
nodes.statement_short: It remains to show surjectivity for $i\le 0$.
nodes.statement: Hence it remains just to show that \eqref{tocolimitsurjective} is surjective for $i\leq 0$.

nodes.name: Induction on |S|
nodes.statement_short: Induct on $|\mathcal S|$ and pick a maximal element.
nodes.statement: We proceed by induction on the cardinality of $\mathcal S$, the case $\mathcal S=\varnothing$ being clear.  Let $\mathfrak s_0\in\mathcal S$ be any maximal element.

nodes.name: Short exact sequence of the pushout
nodes.statement_short: Write the short exact sequence from the pushout diagram.

nodes.name: Equation colimitSEScofibrant
nodes.statement: 0\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s\to A_{\mathfrak s_0}\oplus\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathfrak s_0}A_{\mathfrak s}\to\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}A_{\mathfrak s}\to 0
nodes.label: colimitSEScofibrant

nodes.name: Long exact sequence and induction
nodes.statement_short: The long exact sequence and the induction hypothesis give surjectivity.

By the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{colimitSEScofibrant}, it suffices to show that $H_i\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\begin{smallmatrix}\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S\cr\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak s_0\end{smallmatrix}}A_\mathfrak s=0$ for $i<0$.  Now this follows from the induction hypothesis.

nodes.name: Lifting cycles along a fibration
nodes.statement: Let $\tilde A^\bullet\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$ be surjective. Fix a cycle $a\in A^0$ and a homology class $\tilde{\mathfrak a}\in H^0\tilde A^\bullet$, whose images in $H^0A^\bullet$ coincide. Then there exists a cycle $\tilde a\in\tilde A^0$ which maps to $a$ and which represents $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$.
assumptions: $\tilde A^\bullet\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$ be surjective
Fix a cycle $a\in A^0$ and a homology class $\tilde{\mathfrak a}\in H^0\tilde A^\bullet$, whose images in $H^0A^\bullet$ coincide
conclusions: there exists a cycle $\tilde a\in\tilde A^0$ which maps to $a$ and which represents $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$
nodes.label: cycleliftinglemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.27
nodes.statement: Pick any cycle $\tilde a'\in\tilde A^0$ representing $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$. Then $\tilde a'-a\in A^0$ is a boundary $db$, and lifting $b\in A^{-1}$ to $\tilde b\in\tilde A^{-1}$, we let $\tilde a:=\tilde a'-d\tilde b$.
nodes.statement_short: Correct an arbitrary representative by the coboundary of a lift of a primitive of the difference.

nodes.name: Representing homology classes in mapping cones
nodes.statement: Fix $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ and $\omega\in H^0[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]$. Let $a\in A^0$ be a cycle representing $\delta\omega\in H^0(A^\bullet)$. Then there exists $b\in B^{-1}$ with $db=f(a)$ such that $a\oplus b$ represents $\omega$.
assumptions: Fix $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ and $\omega\in H^0[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]$
$a\in A^0$ be a cycle representing $\delta\omega\in H^0(A^\bullet)$
conclusions: there exists $b\in B^{-1}$ with $db=f(a)$ such that $a\oplus b$ represents $\omega$
nodes.label: mappingconechoiceboundary

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.28
nodes.statement: This is a special case of Lemma \ref{cycleliftinglemma} for the surjection $[A^\bullet\to B^{\bullet-1}]\twoheadrightarrow A^\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of Lemma 7.4.27 for the surjection from the mapping cone.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A_\bullet$ be a cofibrant complex over $\mathbb Z$. Then there is a natural short exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_{i-1}A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_iA_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to 0 \end{equation}
assumptions: $A_\bullet$ be a cofibrant complex over $\mathbb Z$
conclusions: there is a natural short exact sequence
nodes.label: universalcoefficient

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: 0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_{i-1}A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_iA_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\to 0

nodes.statement: Well-known.

nodes.name: Extending cocycles along a cofibration
nodes.statement: Suppose we have the following commuting diagrams (solid arrows) of complexes over $\mathbb Z$ and their homology (where $\mathbb Z$ is concentrated in degree zero): \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} A_\bullet\ar[tail]{r}\ar{d}&\tilde A_\bullet\ar[dashed]{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \overset{H_\bullet}\Longrightarrow \begin{tikzcd} H_\bullet A_\bullet\ar{r}\ar{d}&H_\bullet\tilde A_\bullet\ar{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $A_\bullet$ and $\tilde A_\bullet$ are cofibrant and $H_{-1}A_\bullet=0$. Then there exists a dashed arrow compatible with the rest of the diagram.
assumptions: $A_\bullet$ and $\tilde A_\bullet$ are cofibrant and $H_{-1}A_\bullet=0$
conclusions: there exists a dashed arrow compatible with the rest of the diagram
nodes.label: cocycleextendinglemma

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} A_\bullet\ar[tail]{r}\ar{d}&\tilde A_\bullet\ar[dashed]{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \overset{H_\bullet}\Longrightarrow \begin{tikzcd} H_\bullet A_\bullet\ar{r}\ar{d}&H_\bullet\tilde A_\bullet\ar{dl}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.4.30
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{universalcoefficient}, we have: \begin{align} H^0\operatorname{Hom}(A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow\sim\operatorname{Hom}(H_0A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)\\ H^0\operatorname{Hom}(\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z)&\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_0\tilde A_\bullet,\mathbb Z) \end{align} Let $f:A_0\to\mathbb Z$ denote the vertical map in the first diagram. Using the surjectivity of \eqref{tildesurj}, there exists a cocycle $\tilde f:\tilde A_0\to\mathbb Z$ giving the desired map on homology. Denote by $i:A_\bullet\rightarrowtail\tilde A_\bullet$ the inclusion. Now by the commutativity of the second diagram, the difference $f-\tilde fi$ acts as zero on $H_0A_\bullet$. Since \eqref{notildeiso} is an isomorphism, this difference is thus a coboundary $\delta g$ for some $g:A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$. Now extend $g$ to $\tilde g:\tilde A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$ (using the fact that $A_{-1}\rightarrowtail\tilde A_{-1}$ splits) and let the dotted arrow be $\tilde f+\delta\tilde g$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the universal coefficient theorem to lift the homology map to a cocycle on $\tilde A$, then fix the discrepancy on $A$ by extending a cochain along the split inclusion.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7.4.29 to get an isomorphism for $A$ and a surjection for $\tilde A$.

nodes.name: Lift to a cocycle on the extension
nodes.statement_short: Choose a cocycle $\tilde f$ on $\tilde A_0$ inducing the right homology map.
nodes.statement: Let $f:A_0\to\mathbb Z$ denote the vertical map in the first diagram.  Using the surjectivity of \eqref{tildesurj}, there exists a cocycle $\tilde f:\tilde A_0\to\mathbb Z$ giving the desired map on homology.

nodes.statement_short: The difference $f-\tilde fi$ vanishes on homology, hence is $\delta g$.

Since \eqref{notildeiso} is an isomorphism, this difference is thus a coboundary $\delta g$ for some $g:A_{-1}\to\mathbb Z$.
