nodes.name: System of chains
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W^\bullet$ be an $\mathsf{F}$-module complex with each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ finite. A \emph{system of chains} $\lambda\in\mathcal W^\bullet$ (of degree $d(\sigma,p,q)$) is a collection of elements $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}\in\mathcal W^{d(\sigma,p,q)}(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfying $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ where: \begin{equation} \mu_{\sigma,p,r}:=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\in\mathcal W^\bullet(\sigma,p,r) \end{equation} (using the product/face maps on the right hand side). Note that this sum is finite since $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. Also, note that the triples on the right hand side all strictly precede the triple on the left hand side. We also require that the parity (in the sense of Convention \ref{signconventions}) of $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ equals $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1\in\mathbb Z/2$. This ensures (via the Koszul rule of signs) that expanding $d\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ using the identity $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ yields zero (the signs work out correctly as a consequence of the discussion surrounding \eqref{multiorientationI}--\eqref{multiorientationIV}). In practice the degrees $d(\sigma,p,q)$ are chosen so that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ (as defined by \eqref{lambdamaster}) is formally homogeneous of the same degree as $d\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: A system of chains in an F-module complex is a family $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ with $d\lambda=\mu$, $\mu$ the signed sum of products/faces of earlier $\lambda$'s, with prescribed parity.
nodes.label: systemofcycles

nodes.name: Master equation for systems of chains
nodes.statement: \mu_{\sigma,p,r}:=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^{k+\operatorname{gr}(p)}\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\in\mathcal W^\bullet(\sigma,p,r)
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.label: lambdamaster

nodes.name: Systems of chains as F-module maps
nodes.statement: There is a natural bijection between systems of chains $\lambda\in\mathcal W^\bullet$ and maps of $\mathsf{F}$-modules $R[\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}]\to\mathcal W^\bullet$, where $R[\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}](\sigma,p,q)$ is the free $R$-module on $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ with differential $d\mathfrak s:=\sum_{\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak s)=1}\mathfrak s'$ (with appropriate signs) and equipped with the obvious product/face maps coming from the $\mathsf{F}$-module structure on $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ (more intrinsically, $R[\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}](\sigma,p,q)$ is the direct sum over $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}(\sigma,p,q)$ of the orientation lines from Definition \ref{IAonflowcategorydiagramdef}). This perspective is relevant for the key step of the proof of Proposition \ref{trivialKanfibration} below.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Systems of chains in $\mathcal W$ correspond bijectively to F-module maps $R[\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}]\to\mathcal W^\bullet$.

nodes.name: Resolution $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. We construct a \emph{resolution} $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ (which depends on $\mathcal X$, $\mathcal A$, $\omega$) as follows. A simplex $\Delta^n\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ consists of the following data: \begin{rlist} \item A map $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). \item An $H$-invariant subatlas $\mathcal B\subseteq f^\ast\mathcal A$ (meaning choices of $\bar{\mathcal B}(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar{\mathcal A}(f(\sigma),p,q)$) where each $\bar{\mathcal B}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite. \item An $H$-invariant collection of fundamental cycles $[E_\alpha]\in C_\bullet(E;\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in\bar{\mathcal B}$. \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains $\lambda\in C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(f^\ast\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+$ (degree $0$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) with the following property. Note that $(\mu,\lambda)$ is a cycle in the mapping cone $[C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(f^\ast\mathcal X\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B)^+]$, whose homology is identified with $\check H^\bullet(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. We require that the homology class of $(\mu,\lambda)$ equal $f^\ast\omega\in\check H^0(f^\ast\mathcal X;\mathfrak o_{f^\ast\mathcal X})$. \itemAn $H$-invariant system of chains $\tilde\lambda$ for $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ (degree $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ and supported inside $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal X$) whose image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ coincides with $s_\ast\lambda$ (recall \eqref{GtoCpushforward}). \itemAn $H$-invariant map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules $[[E]]:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathbb Z$ which sends the fundamental class to $1$. The left hand side $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}$ is defined over $\mathbb Z$, and the right hand side is the $\mathsf{F}$-module which for every $(\sigma,p,q)$ is $\mathbb Z$ concentrated in degree zero (with the product/face maps being multiplication/identity respectively). \end{rlist}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Simplices of $\tilde Z_\bullet$ are maps $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ with finite subatlases, fundamental cycles, systems of chains $\lambda,\tilde\lambda$ representing the orientations, and augmentations $[[E]]$.
nodes.label: Lambdadef

nodes.name: Resolution commutes with pullback
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. Let $f:Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a map, and consider $f^\ast\mathcal X/Y_\bullet$ with implicit atlas $f^\ast\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $f^\ast\omega$. Then there is a canonical fiber diagram relating the resolutions: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \tilde Y_\bullet@>>>\tilde Z_\bullet\cr @VVV@VVV\cr Y_\bullet@>>>Z_\bullet \end{CD} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.statement_short: Pulling back $\mathcal X$ along $Y_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ gives a canonical fiber square of resolutions.
nodes.label: Lambdaandpullback

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Y_\bullet@>>>\tilde Z_\bullet\cr @VVV@VVV\cr Y_\bullet@>>>Z_\bullet \end{CD}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration
nodes.statement: The map $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ has the right lifting property with respect to the boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq 0$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). In other words, given any commuting diagram of solid arrows below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \partial\Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow{d}&\tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{d}\\ \Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow[dashrightarrow]{ur}&Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} there exists a dashed arrow making the diagram commute.
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
conclusions: The map $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ has the right lifting property with respect to the boundary inclusions $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq 0$
nodes.statement_short: The resolution $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ lifts against all $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, i.e. is a trivial Kan fibration.
nodes.label: trivialKanfibration

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \partial\Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow{d}&\tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{d}\\ \Delta^n\arrow{r}\arrow[dashrightarrow]{ur}&Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}

nodes.name: Proof that the resolution is a trivial Kan fibration
nodes.statement: It is equivalent to show that given any $f:\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ along with data (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) over $\partial\Delta^n$, the data can be extended over $\Delta^n$. For ease of notation, let us rename $(f^\ast\mathcal X,f^\ast\mathcal A,f^\ast\omega)$ as $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\omega)$. We construct (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) via $H$-equivariant induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_{\mathcal X}$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$. This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction. The induction works $H$-equivariantly since the action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$ is free, and $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $(\sigma,hp,hq)$ are always incomparable for $h\in H$ (so we may henceforth ignore the action of $H$). The inductive step is as follows. \textbf{Choosing $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$.}\ We must choose a finite $\bar{\mathcal B}(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ so that the corresponding subatlas of $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}=\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfies the covering axiom (and thus is an implicit atlas). This is possible by compactness. \textbf{Choosing $[E_\alpha]$.}\ Trivial. \textbf{Choosing $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z$.}\ We need to construct $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ fitting into the following diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar[tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed]{dl}{?\exists\,[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}}\\ \mathbb Z\\ H_\bullet\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&H_\bullet QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar{dl}{[E]\mapsto 1}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}$ is cofibrant, it follows that the top horizontal map is a cofibration between cofibrant complexes (this uses Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}). Now Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} tells us that the direct sum of $H_0QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ surjects onto $H_0$ on the left, and this makes it easy to check that the second diagram commutes. Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} also tells us that $H_{-1}$ on the left vanishes. Hence we may apply Lemma \ref{cocycleextendinglemma} to conclude the existence of a suitable $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$. \textbf{Choosing $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ (the key step).}\ According to Lemma \ref{mappingconechoiceboundary}, we may choose a $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ with the required property iff the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$. Let us now prove this desired statement $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$. Let us fix $\mathfrak r_0\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ and verify equality over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$ (this is clearly enough). We consider the following diagram: \begin{align} \mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in&&&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\ &&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in&&\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}) \end{align} The differentials in \eqref{muallstrat}--\eqref{musomestrat} are given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak r\preceq\mathfrak r')=1$ of the obvious pushforward maps (plus the internal differentials of each $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$). The first vertical map is the sum over $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak r=0$ (i.e.\ over maximal elements of $\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$); clearly this is a chain map. The remaining vertical maps are clear. The easiest way to keep track of signs in the present discussion is to use the orientation lines associated to elements of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$, as in Definition \ref{stratifiedvirtualdef}, though we will supress them from the notation. Note that there is a natural diagram of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ whose diagram of global sections is \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum}. We will see below that these complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are in fact pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced diagram of sheaves (obtained by taking $H^0$) is given by the tautological maps: \begin{equation} \mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial} \end{equation} First, though, let us argue that this claim implies the desired result. The cycle $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in\eqref{mucareabout}$ lifts to a cycle $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$, where $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}$ is obtained by applying the product/face maps to the tensor product of the various $\lambda$'s corresponding to the factors on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} corresponding to $\mathfrak r$ (this is a cycle by \eqref{lambdamaster}). Obviously $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$ maps to $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$. On sections over $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the last vertical map is an isomorphism, and (the restriction to $K$ of) $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$ lifts to (the restriction to $K$ of) $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$. Finally, observe that over any $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$ coincides with the restriction of $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ to the $\mathfrak r_0$ stratum (this follows from the induction hypothesis, using the fact that the orientations are coherent and the observation at the end of Definition \ref{productatlasF}). Clearly this implies that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in homology over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$. Thus it remains only to show that \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced maps on $H^0$ coincide with the tautological maps on orientation sheaves \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry}. Note that by Proposition \ref{stratifiedispurehomotopysheaf}, the following closely related diagram satisfies all of the desired properties (i.e.\ is a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry} on $H^0$): \begin{align} &C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\ &\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\ &\qquad\uparrow\cr &C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}) \end{align} Hence it is enough to relate this diagram to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} via quasi-isomorphisms. The diagram obtained from \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} by replacing every occurence of $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}$ with $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}$ maps quasi-isomorphically to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} (by pairing with the fixed fundamental cycles), and it also maps quasi-isomorphically to the diagram above (use the obvious pushforwards on the $p=0$ level of the homotopy colimits, and zero for $p>0$), thus giving the desired result. \textbf{Choosing $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.}\ We must find $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ lifting $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and satisfying $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$. Now we know that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is a cycle (see Definition \ref{systemofcycles}); furthermore its image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ is $s_\ast\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=d(s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})$ which is null-homologous. Since $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is always a quasi-isomorphism, it follows that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is null-homologous. Hence there exists $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ with $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$; now we must modify $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ so that it lifts $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$. The difference of $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and the image of $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ is a cycle in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$. It can be lifted to a cycle in $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ using Lemma \ref{cycleliftinglemma} (again using that $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism), which is enough.

nodes.statement_short: Extend the choices over $\Delta^n$ by well-founded induction on triples $(\sigma,p,q)$. The key step shows $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega$ by comparing with a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing tautological maps on orientation sheaves.

For ease of notation, let us rename $(f^\ast\mathcal X,f^\ast\mathcal A,f^\ast\omega)$ as $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\omega)$.

nodes.name: Induction on triples
nodes.statement_short: Set up well-founded $H$-equivariant induction on triples $(\sigma,p,q)$.
nodes.statement: We construct (\ref{subatlaschoice})--(\ref{augmentationschoice}) via $H$-equivariant induction on the set of triples $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the partial order $\preceq_{\mathcal X}$ in which $(\sigma',p',q')\preceq_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ iff $(\sigma',p',q')$ appears as a ``factor'' of some element of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$.  This partial order is \emph{well-founded} (i.e.\ there is no strictly decreasing infinite sequence) since each $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ is finite, and thus it is valid for induction.  The induction works $H$-equivariantly since the action of $H$ on $\mathcal P$ is free, and $(\sigma,p,q)$ and $(\sigma,hp,hq)$ are always incomparable for $h\in H$ (so we may henceforth ignore the action of $H$).  The inductive step is as follows.

nodes.name: Choosing $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$
nodes.statement_short: Choose a finite covering subatlas by compactness.
nodes.statement: \textbf{Choosing $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)$.}\  We must choose a finite $\bar{\mathcal B}(\sigma,p,q)\subseteq\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ so that the corresponding subatlas of $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}=\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q)$ on $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ satisfies the covering axiom (and thus is an implicit atlas).  This is possible by compactness.

nodes.name: Choosing $[E_\alpha]$
nodes.statement_short: Fundamental cycles are chosen trivially.

nodes.name: Choosing $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$
nodes.statement_short: Extend the augmentation using cofibrancy and the cocycle extending lemma.
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Choosing $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}:QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\to\mathbb Z$.}\  We need to construct $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ fitting into the following diagram:
\begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge]
\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar[tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed]{dl}{?\exists\,[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}}\\
\mathbb Z\\
H_\bullet\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&H_\bullet QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar{dl}{[E]\mapsto 1}\\
\mathbb Z
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
Since $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}$ is cofibrant, it follows that the top horizontal map is a cofibration between cofibrant complexes (this uses Lemma \ref{cofibranthaslotsofcofibrations}).  Now Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} tells us that the direct sum of $H_0QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)$ surjects onto $H_0$ on the left, and this makes it easy to check that the second diagram commutes.  Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} also tells us that $H_{-1}$ on the left vanishes.  Hence we may apply Lemma \ref{cocycleextendinglemma} to conclude the existence of a suitable $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$.

nodes.name: Equation choosingEEdiagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[column sep = huge] \smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar[tail]{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar[dashed]{dl}{?\exists\,[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}}\\ \mathbb Z\\ H_\bullet\smash{\displaystyle\operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{\mathfrak s\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}}QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak s)\ar{r}{\text{product/face}}\ar{d}[swap]{[[E]]}&H_\bullet QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+_{\mathbb Z}(\sigma,p,q)\ar{dl}{[E]\mapsto 1}\\ \mathbb Z \end{tikzcd}
nodes.section: 7.5 Resolution \texorpdfstring{$\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$}{tilde Z to Z}
nodes.label: choosingEEdiagram

nodes.name: Choosing $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ (the key step)
nodes.statement_short: Show $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega$ so that $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ exists.
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Choosing $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ (the key step).}\  According to Lemma \ref{mappingconechoiceboundary}, we may choose a $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ with the required property iff the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)\in\check H^0(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)})$.  Let us now prove this desired statement $[\mu_{\sigma,p,q}]=d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$.  Let us fix $\mathfrak r_0\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$ and verify equality over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$ (this is clearly enough).

We consider the following diagram:
\begin{align} \mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in&&&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X;\mathcal B)^+(\sigma,p,q)\\
&&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\
&&&\qquad\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in&&\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})\\
&&&\qquad\uparrow\cr \mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in&&\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\prec\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t})
\end{align}
The differentials in \eqref{muallstrat}--\eqref{musomestrat} are given by the sum over $\operatorname{codim}(\mathfrak r\preceq\mathfrak r')=1$ of the obvious pushforward maps (plus the internal differentials of each $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$).  The first vertical map is the sum over $\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak r=0$ (i.e.\ over maximal elements of $\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$); clearly this is a chain map.  The remaining vertical maps are clear.  The easiest way to keep track of signs in the present discussion is to use the orientation lines associated to elements of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)$, as in Definition \ref{stratifiedvirtualdef}, though we will supress them from the notation.  Note that there is a natural diagram of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on $\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)$ whose diagram of global sections is \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum}.  We will see below that these complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are in fact pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced diagram of sheaves (obtained by taking $H^0$) is given by the tautological maps:
\begin{equation} \mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)}\to\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\leftarrow\mathfrak o_{\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial}
\end{equation}
First, though, let us argue that this claim implies the desired result.  The cycle $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}\in\eqref{mucareabout}$ lifts to a cycle $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$, where $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}$ is obtained by applying the product/face maps to the tensor product of the various $\lambda$'s corresponding to the factors on the left hand side of \eqref{Wtotalcomposition} corresponding to $\mathfrak r$ (this is a cycle by \eqref{lambdamaster}).  Obviously $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{muallstrat}$ maps to $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$.  On sections over $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the last vertical map is an isomorphism, and (the restriction to $K$ of) $\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r}\in\eqref{musomestrat}$ lifts to (the restriction to $K$ of) $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$.  Finally, observe that over any $K\subseteq\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$, the homology class of $\mu_{\sigma,p,q,\mathfrak r_0}\in\eqref{muonestratum}$ coincides with the restriction of $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ to the $\mathfrak r_0$ stratum (this follows from the induction hypothesis, using the fact that the orientations are coherent and the observation at the end of Definition \ref{productatlasF}).  Clearly this implies that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ coincides with $d\omega(\sigma,p,q)$ in homology over $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathfrak r_0}$.

Thus it remains only to show that \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves and that the induced maps on $H^0$ coincide with the tautological maps on orientation sheaves \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry}.  Note that by Proposition \ref{stratifiedispurehomotopysheaf}, the following closely related diagram satisfies all of the desired properties (i.e.\ is a diagram of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves inducing \eqref{orientationdiagramforHFbdry} on $H^0$):
\begin{align}
&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\partial\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q);\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\
&\qquad\uparrow\cr
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\
&\qquad\downarrow\cr
\bigoplus_{\mathfrak r\in\partial\mathcal S_{\mathcal X}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}}&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})\\
&\qquad\uparrow\cr
&C_{\mathrm{vir}}^\bullet(\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak r_0}\operatorname{rel}\partial;\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}})
\end{align}
Hence it is enough to relate this diagram to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} via quasi-isomorphisms.  The diagram obtained from \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} by replacing every occurence of $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak t}$ with $\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}$ maps quasi-isomorphically to \eqref{mucareabout}--\eqref{muonestratum} (by pairing with the fixed fundamental cycles), and it also maps quasi-isomorphically to the diagram above (use the obvious pushforwards on the $p=0$ level of the homotopy colimits, and zero for $p>0$), thus giving the desired result.

nodes.name: Choosing $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$
nodes.statement_short: Lift $\lambda$ to $\tilde\lambda$ using that $Q\mathcal W\to\mathcal W$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the cycle lifting lemma.
nodes.statement: \textbf{Choosing $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.}\  We must find $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ lifting $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and satisfying $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$.  Now we know that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is a cycle (see Definition \ref{systemofcycles}); furthermore its image in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ is $s_\ast\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=d(s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})$ which is null-homologous.  Since $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is always a quasi-isomorphism, it follows that $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$ is null-homologous.  Hence there exists $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ with $d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'=\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}$; now we must modify $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ so that it lifts $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$.  The difference of $s_\ast\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and the image of $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}'$ is a cycle in $C_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$.  It can be lifted to a cycle in $QC_\bullet(E;\mathcal B)^+$ using Lemma \ref{cycleliftinglemma} (again using that $Q\mathcal W_\bullet\overset\sim\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal W_\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism), which is enough.

nodes.name: Differential graded module over a graded ring
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. A \emph{differential graded $S$-module} is a graded module $A^\bullet$ over $S$ along with a map $d:A^\bullet\to A^{\bullet+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$.

nodes.name: Category $\mathsf{Ch}_S$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ denote the category whose objects are differential graded $S$-modules and whose morphisms are chain maps.
nodes.label: ChRdef

nodes.name: Category $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ denote the category whose objects are objects of $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ and whose morphisms are chain maps modulo chain homotopy.
nodes.label: HChRdef

nodes.name: Differential graded nerve
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring. We let $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ denote the differential graded nerve of $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ (see Lurie \cite[Construction 1.3.1.6]{lurieha} or Definition \ref{NdgdefII} below).
nodes.label: Ndgdef

nodes.name: Diagram in a category (nerve)
nodes.statement_short: A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ is a simplicial map to the nerve: objects on vertices, morphisms on edges, identities on degenerate edges, composition on 2-faces.

nodes.name: Diagram to the differential graded nerve
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be a graded ring and let $X_\bullet$ be a simplicial set. A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ consists of:\footnote{For the reader familiar with $\infty$-categories: the notion of a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ suffices to define $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ by Yoneda's Lemma.} \begin{rlist} \item For every $v\in X_0$, a graded $S$-module $A_v^\bullet$. \item For every $\sigma\in X_n$ spanning $v_0,\ldots,v_n\in X_0$, a map $f_\sigma:A_{v_0}\to A_{v_n}$ of degree $1-n$, such that: \begin{equation} \sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\circ f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]} \end{equation} and if $\sigma$ is degenerate, then: \begin{equation} f_\sigma=\begin{cases}\operatorname{id}&\dim\sigma=1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{equation} \end{rlist} If $X_\bullet$ is only a \emph{semi}simplicial set, then we ignore \eqref{Ndgdegenerate}.
nodes.statement_short: A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ assigns graded modules to vertices and degree $1-n$ maps $f_\sigma$ to $n$-simplices satisfying the coherence relation (Ndgmaster).
nodes.label: NdgdefII

nodes.name: Coherence relation for dg-nerve diagrams
nodes.statement: \sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}\circ f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}
nodes.label: Ndgmaster

nodes.name: Degenerate simplex condition for dg-nerve diagrams
nodes.statement: f_\sigma=\begin{cases}\operatorname{id}&\dim\sigma=1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}
nodes.label: Ndgdegenerate

nodes.name: Low-dimensional dg-nerve diagrams
nodes.statement_short: For $n=0,1,2$, (Ndgmaster) says $f_0$ is a differential, $f_{01}$ a chain map, $f_{012}$ a chain homotopy.
nodes.statement:
Let us now explain this definition by examining what \eqref{Ndgmaster} says for low-dimensional simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X_\bullet$ (following \cite[Example 1.3.1.8]{lurieha}).
\begin{rlist}
\item Let $n=0$.  Then $f_0:A_0^\bullet\to A_0^\bullet$ has degree $1$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_0\circ f_0=0$.  Thus $(A_0,f_0)$ is a chain complex.
\item Let $n=1$.  Then $f_{01}:A_0^\bullet\to A_1^\bullet$ has degree $0$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_{01}\circ f_0-f_1\circ f_{01}=0$.  Thus $f_{01}:(A^\bullet_0,f_0)\to(A^\bullet_1,f_1)$ is a chain map.  For a degenerate $1$-simplex, \eqref{Ndgdegenerate} asserts that $f_{01}:(A^\bullet_0,f_0)\to(A^\bullet_1,f_1)$ is the identity map.
\item Let $n=2$.  Then $f_{012}:A^\bullet_0\to A^\bullet_2$ has degree $-1$, and \eqref{Ndgmaster} asserts that $f_{012}f_0-f_{12}f_{01}+f_2f_{012}=-f_{02}$.  Thus $f_{012}$ is a chain homotopy between $f_{02},f_{12}f_{01}:A^\bullet_0\to A^\bullet_2$.

nodes.name: Forgetful functors Ch -> N_dg -> H^0
nodes.statement_short: Natural forgetful functors $\mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$: set higher homotopies to zero, resp. forget them.
nodes.statement:
We can now relate $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ to the more familiar categories $\mathsf{Ch}_S$ and $H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ by introducing natural forgetful functors:
\begin{equation} \mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)
\end{equation}
which should be clear given the above interpretation of diagrams to $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$.  More precisely, a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{Ch}_S$ gives rise to a diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ where the higher homotopies $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma\geq 2}$ are all zero.  A diagram $X_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ gives rise to a diagram $X_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)$ which forgets about the choice of higher homotopies $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma\geq 2}$, remembering only the existence of $\{f_\sigma\}_{\dim\sigma=2}$ satisfying \eqref{Ndgmaster}.

nodes.name: Forgetful functors between categories of complexes
nodes.statement: \mathsf{Ch}_S\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_S)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_S)
nodes.label: forgetfulonchaincomplexes

nodes.name: Schematic of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ over $\tilde Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \tilde Z_\bullet@>\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)>>\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\cr @V\pi VV\cr Z_\bullet \end{CD}

nodes.name: Refined descent to the dg nerve
nodes.statement: There should also be a (more refined) descent with target $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ (c.f.\ Remark \ref{restricttotwoskeleton}), though we have decided to omit this for sake of brevity (the correct uniqueness statement is more complicated to state).

nodes.name: Novikov rings
nodes.statement: Let $T$ be a set equipped with a ``grading'' $\operatorname{gr}:T\to\mathbb Z$ and an ``action'' $a:T\to\mathbb R$. We let $R[[T]]$ denote the graded $R$-module consisting of formal sums $\sum_{t\in T}c_t\cdot t$ with $c_t\in R$, satisfying the following two finiteness conditions: \begin{rlist} \item$\#\{n\in\mathbb Z:\exists t$ such that $c_t\ne 0$ and $\operatorname{gr}(t)=n\}<\infty$. \item$\#\{t\in T:c_t\ne 0$ and $a(t)<M\}<\infty$ for all $M<\infty$. \end{rlist} In other words, $R[[T]]$ is the graded completion of $R[T]$ with respect to the non-archimedean $a$-adic norm $\left|t\right|_a:=e^{-a(t)}$. If $T$ is a group and $\operatorname{gr}$, $a$ are group homomorphisms, then $R[[T]]$ is a graded ring.
nodes.statement_short: $R[[T]]$ consists of formal sums $\sum c_t t$ with finitely many gradings and finitely many terms below each action level; the $a$-adic completion of $R[T]$.
nodes.label: gradedcompletion

nodes.name: (Co)homology diagram $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ over $\tilde Z_\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. We define a diagram: \begin{equation} \widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]}) \end{equation} We will write $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$ when the atlas and orientations are clear from context. To a vertex of $\tilde Z_\bullet$, we associate $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$ where $z$ is the corresponding vertex in $Z_\bullet$. This is clearly a graded $R[[H]]$-module. Now for a simplex $\sigma\in\tilde Z_n$, we aim to define the map $f_\sigma:R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}]]$ by the formula: \begin{equation} f_\sigma(p):=\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(n)}}([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\cdot q \end{equation} Let us now argue that \eqref{diagramndgformula} makes sense and that the resulting maps $f_\sigma$ satisfy \eqref{Ndgmaster}. First, observe that since $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ is of degree $\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1$ and $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}$ has degree $0$, all terms on the right hand side of \eqref{diagramndgformula} are of degree $\operatorname{gr}(p)+1-\dim\sigma$. Now, we have $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ if $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\varnothing$. Hence finiteness condition Definition \ref{semisimplicialfcdef}(\ref{novikovfiniteness}) implies that \eqref{diagramndgformula} converges in the $a$-adic topology, and hence defines an $R$-linear map $f_\sigma:R[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]$. Finiteness condition (\ref{novikovfinitenessII}) implies that there exists $M<\infty$ such that $\left|f_\sigma(p)\right|_a\leq M\left|p\right|_a$. Thus $f_\sigma$ extends uniquely to a continuous (in fact, bounded) $R$-linear map $f_\sigma:R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]\to R[[\mathcal P_{\sigma(0)}]]$. Clearly $f_\sigma$ is $R[[H]]$-linear since $[[E]]$ and $\tilde\lambda$ are both $H$-invariant. Now it remains to verify that the $f_\sigma$ defined by \eqref{diagramndgformula} satisfy \eqref{Ndgmaster}. To see this, write: \begin{align*} 0&=(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}(d\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,r})\cr &=(-1)^{\operatorname{gr}(p)}\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}(\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,r})\cr &=[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}\left(\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^k\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}\cdot\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}\right)\cr &=\sum_{k=0}^n\sum_{q\in\mathcal P_{\sigma(k)}}(-1)^k[[E]]_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots k],p,q})\cdot[[E]]_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[k\ldots n],q,r})\cr&\qquad-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k[[E]]_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r}(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n],p,r})\cr &=\text{coefficient of }r\text{ in }\sum_{k=0}^n(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[k\ldots n]}(f_{\sigma|[0\ldots k]}(p))-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^kf_{\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n]}(p) \end{align*} The first equality follows because $[[E]]_{\sigma,p,r}$ is a chain map, the second equality follows from the definition of a system of chains, the third equality is \eqref{lambdamaster}, the fourth equality follows from the fact that $[[E]]$ is compatible with the product/face maps, and the fifth equality follows from the definition of $f_\sigma$ \eqref{diagramndgformula}.
nodes.statement_short: Assign $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$ to vertices and maps $f_\sigma(p)=\sum_q [[E]](\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})q$ to simplices; these converge and satisfy the dg-nerve relation.

nodes.name: Degenerate edges in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ give the identity map up to homotopy
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet=\ast$ be the semisimplicial set with a single simplex $\sigma^i$ in dimension $i$ for all $i\geq 0$ (i.e.\ the simplicial $0$-simplex). Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas and coherent orientations. Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)=\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is a single point and $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$, for all $p$. \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and all $p\ne q$. \end{rlist} Then for any $\sigma\in\tilde Z_1$ whose two vertices coincide, the associated map in $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ is homotopic to the identity map.
assumptions: Let $Z_\bullet=\ast$ be the semisimplicial set with a single simplex $\sigma^i$ in dimension $i$ for all $i\geq 0$
Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas and coherent orientations

$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and all $p\ne q$
conclusions: for any $\sigma\in\tilde Z_1$ whose two vertices coincide, the associated map in $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ is homotopic to the identity map
nodes.statement_short: Under transversality of constant trajectories, a loop edge of $\tilde Z_\bullet$ induces a map homotopic to the identity.

nodes.name: Proof that degenerate edges give the identity
nodes.statement:
Let $d:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ denote the boundary operator associated to the vertex of $\sigma$, and let $1-\epsilon:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ denote the chain map associated to $\sigma$. We must show that $\epsilon$ is chain homotopic to the zero map. Since $	ilde Z_ ullet	o Z_ ullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration (Proposition ef{trivialKanfibration}), there exists a $2$-simplex in $	ilde Z_ ullet$ all of whose edges are $\sigma$. Associated to this $2$-simplex is a chain homotopy $h:R[[\mathcal P]]	o R[[\mathcal P]]$ between $(1-\epsilon)$ and $(1-\epsilon)\circ(1-\epsilon)$; in other words:  egin{equation} \epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2 \end{equation} Now we claim that the only nonzero ``matrix coefficients'' $c_{p,q}$ of $d,\epsilon,h$ are those for which $\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)
e\varnothing$. By definition, $f_\sigma$ can have nonzero matrix coefficients $c_{p,q}$ only for $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)
e\varnothing$. Hence hypothesis (ef{highernonemptyissameaszero}) gives the desired claim as long as $p
e q$. For the diagonal matrix coefficients $c_{p,p}$, we argue separately as follows. By degree considerations, only $\epsilon$ can have nonzero $c_{p,p}$. It thus suffices to show that the matrix coefficient $c_{p,p}=[[E]]_{\sigma^1,p,p}(	ilde\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p})$ of $f_{\sigma^1}=1-\epsilon$ equals $1$. Note that no product/face maps have target $(\sigma^1,p,p)$, so $\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p}$ is a cycle representing $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$. Hence $	ilde\lambda_{\sigma^1,p,p}$ is a cycle representing $[E]$, and so $[[E]]_{\sigma^1,p,p}(	ilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,p})=1$ as needed. Hence the claim is valid. From the claim, we make the following two observations:  egin{rlist} \itemWe have $\left|d(p)ight|_a,\left|\epsilon(p)ight|_a,\left|h(p)ight|_a\leq\left|pight|_a$. \itemFor all $M<\infty$ and $p\in\mathcal P$, there exists $N<\infty$ such that any length $N$ composition of $d,\epsilon,h$ applied to $p$ has $a$-adic norm $\leq e^{-M}$. \end{rlist} (the second observation also uses Definition ef{semisimplicialfcdef}(ef{novikovfiniteness})). Now iterating the identity $\epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2$, we are led to the following infinite series: ootnote{The coefficients $ rac 1n inom{2n-2}{n-1}$ are integers (Catalan numbers $C_{n-1}$), so writing this expression does not make any implicit assumptions on the ring $R$.}  egin{equation} \epsilon=\sum_{n=1}^\infty rac 1n inom{2n-2}{n-1}(hd+dh)^n \end{equation} which by observations (ef{firstO})--(ef{secondO}) converges in the $a$-adic topology when applied to any element of $R[[\mathcal P]]$. Now we have $(hd+dh)^n=\sum_{k=0}^n(dh)^k(hd)^{n-k}=H_nd+dH_n$ where $H_n=\sum_{k=1}^nh(dh)^{k-1}(hd)^{n-k}$. This gives the desired chain homotopy between $\epsilon$ and zero (again using observations (ef{firstO})--(ef{secondO}) to justify convergence of infinite sums).
nodes.statement_short: Use a 2-simplex with all edges $\sigma$ to get $\epsilon=dh+hd+\epsilon^2$, then solve by a Catalan-number series. Matrix coefficients are controlled so the series converges $a$-adically.

nodes.name: Criterion for descent along a trivial Kan fibration
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a trivial Kan fibration of semisimplicial sets, and let $\widetilde{\mathbb H}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in some category $\mathcal C$. A \emph{descent} of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$ to $Z_\bullet$ is a diagram $\mathbb H:Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ along with an isomorphism $\widetilde{\mathbb H}\to\mathbb H\circ\pi$: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&\mathcal C\\ Z_\bullet\arrow[dashed]{ur}[swap]{\mathbb H} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$Z_\bullet$ is a simplicial set. \itemFor any edge $\sigma^1$ in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ whose endpoints coincide and which projects to a degenerate edge in $Z_\bullet$, the associated map in $\mathcal C$ is the identity map. \end{rlist} Then a descent exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism.
assumptions: Let $\pi:\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ be a trivial Kan fibration of semisimplicial sets
let $\widetilde{\mathbb H}:\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in some category $\mathcal C$
$Z_\bullet$ is a simplicial set
For any edge $\sigma^1$ in $\tilde Z_\bullet$ whose endpoints coincide and which projects to a degenerate edge in $Z_\bullet$, the associated map in $\mathcal C$ is the identity map
conclusions: a descent exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: A diagram on the total space of a trivial Kan fibration over a simplicial set descends uniquely if loop edges over degenerate edges go to identities.
nodes.label: descentofdiagram

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&\mathcal C\\ Z_\bullet\arrow[dashed]{ur}[swap]{\mathbb H} \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Proof of the descent criterion
nodes.statement: The proof below shows that we may define $\mathbb H:=\widetilde{\mathbb H}\circ s$ for any section $s:Z_\bullet\to\tilde Z_\bullet$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $0$-simplices.}\ Fix some $0$-simplex $v$ of $Z_\bullet$. For every lift $\tilde v$, we have an object $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v)$. Furthermore, for every lift $\tilde e$ of the degenerate $1$-simplex $e$ over $v$, we get a map $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_1)\xrightarrow{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e)}\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_2)$, which is the identity map if $\tilde v_1=\tilde v_2$. Finally, for every lift $\tilde f$ of the degenerate $2$-simplex $f$ over $v$, the following diagram commutes: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_2)\ar{rd}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e_{23})}&{}\cr \widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_1)\ar{ur}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e_{13})}&&{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_3)} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $\tilde e_{12},\tilde e_{23},\tilde e_{13}$ are the edges of $\tilde f$. Using that $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$ is a trivial Kan fibration to conclude that we can always find lifts with specified boundary conditions, it follows that all $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v)$ are canonically isomorphic. Thus there exists a unique choice for $\mathbb H(v)$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $1$-simplices.}\ Fix some $1$-simplex $e$ of $Z_\bullet$ with vertices $v_1,v_2$. If $\tilde e$ is any lift of $e$, then we get a map $\mathbb H(v_1)=\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_1)\xrightarrow{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e)}\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_2)=\mathbb H(v_2)$. Furthermore, this map $\mathbb H(v_1)\to\mathbb H(v_2)$ is seen to be independent of the choice of lift $\tilde e$ by lifting degenerate $2$-simplices over $e$. Thus there exists a unique choice for $\mathbb H(e)$. \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $n$-simplices for $n\geq 2$.}\ We just need to check that the following diagram commutes for all $2$-simplices $f$ in $Z_\bullet$: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = small] &\mathbb H(v_2)\ar{rd}{\mathbb H(e_{23})}&{}\cr \mathbb H(v_1)\ar{ur}{\mathbb H(e_{12})}\ar{rr}[swap]{\mathbb H(e_{13})}&&{\mathbb H(v_3)} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $e_{12},e_{23},e_{13}$ are the edges of $f$. This follows from lifting $f$ and the commutativity of \eqref{liftedF}.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\mathbb H$ simplex by simplex over 0-, 1- and 2-simplices using lifts with prescribed boundary, which exist since $\pi$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

nodes.name: Descent via a section
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb H$ will be $\widetilde{\mathbb H}\circ s$ for any section.
nodes.statement: The proof below shows that we may define $\mathbb H:=\widetilde{\mathbb H}\circ s$ for any section $s:Z_\bullet\to\tilde Z_\bullet$.

nodes.name: Over 0-simplices
nodes.statement_short: Lifts of a vertex are canonically isomorphic, fixing $\mathbb H(v)$.

nodes.name: Over 1-simplices
nodes.statement_short: Map along an edge is independent of the lift.
nodes.statement: \textbf{Defining $\mathbb H$ over $1$-simplices.}\  Fix some $1$-simplex $e$ of $Z_\bullet$ with vertices $v_1,v_2$.  If $\tilde e$ is any lift of $e$, then we get a map $\mathbb H(v_1)=\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_1)\xrightarrow{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde e)}\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\tilde v_2)=\mathbb H(v_2)$.  Furthermore, this map $\mathbb H(v_1)\to\mathbb H(v_2)$ is seen to be independent of the choice of lift $\tilde e$ by lifting degenerate $2$-simplices over $e$.  Thus there exists a unique choice for $\mathbb H(e)$.

nodes.statement_short: Commutativity over 2-simplices follows by lifting.

nodes.name: (Co)homology groups $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$ be a simplicial set. Let $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ be an $H$-equivariant flow category diagram with implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ and coherent orientations $\omega$. Suppose that for any vertex $\sigma^0$ of $Z_\bullet$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)=\mathcal X(\sigma^1,p,p)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is a single point and $\omega(\sigma^1,p,p)=1$, for all $p$. \item$\mathcal X(\sigma^0,p,q)=\varnothing\implies\mathcal X(\sigma^i,p,q)=\varnothing$ for all $i$ and $p\ne q$ \end{rlist} (where $\sigma^i$ denotes the completely degenerate $i$-simplex over $\sigma^0$). We have: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\\ Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (abusing notation and use $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X):\tilde Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ to denote the composition of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ with the forgetful functor $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}\to H^0$). The hypotheses of Lemma \ref{descentofdiagram} are satisfied by Propositions \ref{trivialKanfibration} and \ref{degenerateID}, and hence we get a canonical descent: \begin{equation} \mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]}) \end{equation} We will write $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ for $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}$ when the atlas and orientations are clear from context.
nodes.statement_short: Floer-type homology $\mathbb H(\mathcal X):Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ is the canonical descent of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ along $\tilde Z_\bullet\to Z_\bullet$.
nodes.label: defofhomologygroups

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet\arrow{r}{\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)}\arrow{d}[swap]{\pi}&H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\\ Z_\bullet \end{tikzcd}

nodes.statement: \mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{A,\omega}:Z_\bullet\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})

nodes.name: Passing to a subatlas preserves $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. If $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ is any subatlas, then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A}=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal B}$.
assumptions: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}
$\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$ is any subatlas
conclusions: there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A}=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal B}$

nodes.name: Proof of subatlas invariance
nodes.statement: Indeed, we have $\tilde Z_\bullet^{\mathcal B}\subseteq\tilde Z_\bullet^{\mathcal A}$ compatibly with $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Inclusion $\tilde Z^{\mathcal B}_\bullet\subseteq\tilde Z^{\mathcal A}_\bullet$ compatible with $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$.

nodes.name: Shrinking the charts preserves $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Let $\mathcal A'$ be obtained from $\mathcal A$ by using instead some open subsets $U_{IJ}'\subseteq U_{IJ}$, $X_I'\subseteq X_I$, $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}\prime}\subseteq X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$, and restricting $\psi_{IJ}$, $s_I$ to these subsets, so that $\mathcal A'$ is also an implicit atlas. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A}=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$.
assumptions: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}

Let $\mathcal A'$ be obtained from $\mathcal A$ by using instead some open subsets $U_{IJ}'\subseteq U_{IJ}$, $X_I'\subseteq X_I$, $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}\prime}\subseteq X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$, and restricting $\psi_{IJ}$, $s_I$ to these subsets, so that $\mathcal A'$ is also an implicit atlas
conclusions: there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A}=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$
nodes.label: homologyopenreduction

nodes.name: Proof of invariance under shrinking charts
nodes.statement: There is a natural map $\tilde Z_\bullet^{\mathcal A'}\to\tilde Z_\bullet^{\mathcal A}$ for which the pullback of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)_{\mathcal A'}$. This is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Natural map $\tilde Z^{\mathcal A'}_\bullet\to\tilde Z^{\mathcal A}_\bullet$ pulling back $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$.

nodes.name: Universal coefficients
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Let $R\to S$ a homomorphism of base rings. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$ (denoting $\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]:H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{S[[H]]})$).
assumptions: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}
Let $R\to S$ a homomorphism of base rings
conclusions: there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^S=\mathbb H(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$

nodes.name: Proof of universal coefficients
nodes.statement: There is a natural base change map $b:\tilde Z_\bullet^R\to\tilde Z_\bullet^S$ and a canonical isomorphism $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)^S\circ b=\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)^R\otimes_{R[[H]]}S[[H]]$. Now the result follows since $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)^S\circ b$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)^S$ have the same descent to $Z_\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Base change map $\tilde Z^R_\bullet\to\tilde Z^S_\bullet$ and uniqueness of descent.

nodes.name: If $\mathcal X=\mathcal X^{\mathrm{reg}}$, then $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ is given by counting $0$-dimensional flow spaces
nodes.statement: Let $Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$, $\mathcal A$, and $\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}. Suppose that $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ for all $(\sigma,p,q)$ (so, in particular, $\mathcal X/Z_\bullet$ is Morse--Smale in the sense of Remark \ref{MSflowcatediag}). Define a diagram $\mathbb H'(\mathcal X):Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ as follows. The graded $R[[H]]$-module associated to a vertex $z$ of $\tilde Z_\bullet$ is $R[[\mathcal P_z]]$. Now there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)=\mathbb H'(\mathcal X)$ (where on the right hand side we implicitly compose with the forgetful functor $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}\to H^0$).

nodes.name: Proof that transverse flow spaces give counts
nodes.statement: We will show an equality of ``matrix coefficients'': \begin{equation} ([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})=\langle\omega(\sigma,p,q),[\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)]\rangle \end{equation} for $(\sigma,p,q)\in\tilde Z_\bullet$ with $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=0$. Thus comparing \eqref{diagramndgformula} and \eqref{diagramndgformulaMS}, it follows that the two diagrams $\tilde Z_\bullet\to\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ in question, namely $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$ and $\mathbb H'(\mathcal X)\circ\pi$, coincide. The desired isomorphism thus follows from the definition of $\mathbb H(\mathcal X)$ as the descent of $\widetilde{\mathbb H}(\mathcal X)$. To prove \eqref{matrixcoeffsame}, argue as follows. Since $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$, we know that if $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)<0$ then $\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=\varnothing$ and hence $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ and $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}=0$. Now when $\operatorname{vdim}\mathcal X(\sigma,p,q)=0$, we see that $\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ and $\tilde\mu_{\sigma,p,q}=0$ (because all of the terms defining them involve a triple with negative dimension), so $\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ and $\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q}$ are cycles. nodes.name: Gysin sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a principal $S^1$-bundle. Analysis of the associated Serre spectral sequence gives the following Gysin long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(E)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet(B)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}(B)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots \end{equation} The $\cap e$ map is cap product with the Euler class $e(E)\in H^2(B)$. To see this, observe that the sequence \eqref{gysinserregeneral} coincides with the long exact sequence of the pair for (the mapping cone of) $\pi:E\to B$, and that there is a natural isomorphism $H_{\bullet+2}(B,E)\xrightarrow{\cap\tau}H_\bullet(B)$ where $\tau=\tau(E)\in H^2(B,E)$ is the Thom class (e.g.\ as argued in \cite[p444]{hatcher} for the corresponding sequence in cohomology). For any $S^1$-space $X$. there is a principal $S^1$-bundle $\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1$, and thus a long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(X)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\cap e}H_{\bullet-2}^{S^1}(X)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}\cdots \end{equation} for $e(X)\in H^2_{S^1}(X)$. The same reasoning applies for pairs of spaces, so the same exact sequence exists for relative homology as well.
assumptions: Let $\pi:E\to B$ be a principal $S^1$-bundle
conclusions: The $\cap e$ map is cap product with the Euler class $e(E)\in H^2(B)$
nodes.statement_short: A principal $S^1$-bundle has a Gysin long exact sequence with connecting map cap with the Euler class; applied to $X\times ES^1$ it gives one for equivariant homology.

nodes.name: Gysin long exact sequence

nodes.name: Proof of the trivial-action Gysin lemma
nodes.statement: The composition $H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet(X\times BS^1)\to H_\bullet(X)$ is the identity map, and so the first map is injective. On the other hand, this map is precisely $\pi_\ast:H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ since the $S^1$-action is trivial, so $\pi_\ast$ is injective which is sufficient. The same argument applies in the relative setting as well.
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_\ast$ has a left inverse via $X\times BS^1\to X$, so it is injective.

nodes.name: Left inverse
nodes.statement_short: A retraction shows the first map is injective.
nodes.statement: The composition $H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet(X\times BS^1)\to H_\bullet(X)$ is the identity map, and so the first map is injective.

nodes.name: Identify with $\pi_\ast$
nodes.statement_short: That map is $\pi_\ast$, so $\pi_\ast$ is injective and $\pi^!=0$.
nodes.statement: On the other hand, this map is precisely $\pi_\ast:H_\bullet(X)\to H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ since the $S^1$-action is trivial, so $\pi_\ast$ is injective which is sufficient.  The same argument applies in the relative setting as well.

nodes.name: Euler class vanishes near almost free orbits
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff $S^1$-space which is almost free at $p\in X$, and suppose that the order of the stabilizer $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$. Then there exists an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $S^1p\subseteq K\subseteq X$ so that the Euler class $e(K)\in H^2_{S^1}(K)$ vanishes.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff $S^1$-space which is almost free at $p\in X$
suppose that the order of the stabilizer $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$
conclusions: there exists an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $S^1p\subseteq K\subseteq X$ so that the Euler class $e(K)\in H^2_{S^1}(K)$ vanishes
nodes.label: freeactionislocallytrivial

nodes.name: Proof of local vanishing of the Euler class
nodes.statement: Apply the Tietze extension theorem to the identity map $S^1p\to S^1p$ to obtain an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $K$ of $S^1p$ and a retraction $r:K\to S^1p$. By averaging and passing to a smaller neighborhood, we may assume without loss of generality that $r$ is $S^1$-equivariant. Now by the naturality of the Euler class, we have $e(K)=r^\ast e(S^1p)$. Thus it suffices to show that $e(S^1p)\in H^2_{S^1}(S^1p)$ vanishes. Now we have $H^2_{S^1}(S^1p)=H^2_{(S^1)_p}(p)=H^2((S^1)_p)$, where the latter is the group cohomology of the finite stabilizer group $(S^1)_p$. It is a standard fact that the group cohomology of a finite group is annihilated by the order of the group. Hence our assumption that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in $R$ guarantees that this cohomology group vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: Equivariant retraction to the orbit (Tietze) reduces to group cohomology of the finite stabilizer, which is killed by its invertible order.

nodes.name: Equivariant retraction
nodes.statement_short: Tietze extension and averaging give an equivariant retraction onto the orbit.
nodes.statement: Apply the Tietze extension theorem to the identity map $S^1p\to S^1p$ to obtain an $S^1$-invariant neighborhood $K$ of $S^1p$ and a retraction $r:K\to S^1p$.  By averaging and passing to a smaller neighborhood, we may assume without loss of generality that $r$ is $S^1$-equivariant.

nodes.name: Reduce to the orbit
nodes.statement_short: By naturality, reduce to vanishing of the Euler class of the orbit.
nodes.statement: Now by the naturality of the Euler class, we have $e(K)=r^\ast e(S^1p)$.  Thus it suffices to show that $e(S^1p)\in H^2_{S^1}(S^1p)$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Finite group cohomology
nodes.statement_short: Group cohomology of the finite stabilizer vanishes after inverting its order.

It is a standard fact that the group cohomology of a finite group is annihilated by the order of the group.  Hence our assumption that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in $R$ guarantees that this cohomology group vanishes.

nodes.name: Equivariant local homology of an almost free S^1-manifold
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological $S^1$-manifold of dimension $d$ which is almost free near $p\in M$. Suppose that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\bullet\ne d-1\end{cases} \end{equation} (note also that $H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)=H^0(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M\otimes\mathfrak o_{S^1p}^\vee)$).
assumptions: Let $M$ be a topological $S^1$-manifold of dimension $d$ which is almost free near $p\in M$
Suppose that $\#(S^1)_p$ is invertible in the ground ring $R$
conclusions: H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\bullet\ne d-1\end{cases}

nodes.statement: H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\bullet\ne d-1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Proof of equivariant local homology computation
nodes.statement: By Poincar\'e duality, we have canonical isomorphisms: \begin{equation} H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)=\begin{cases}H^0(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d\cr H^1(S^1p;\mathfrak o_M)&\bullet=d-1\cr 0&\text{otherwise}\end{cases} \end{equation} By excision and Lemma \ref{freeactionislocallytrivial}, the Gysin sequence reduces to a short exact sequence: \begin{equation} 0\to H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_\bullet(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\to 0 \end{equation} Combining this with \eqref{PDforSSPD}, we see that $H_\bullet^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)=0$ for $\bullet\ne d-1$, and that the following are both isomorphisms: \begin{equation} H_{d-1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi_\ast}H_{d-1}^{S^1}(M,M\setminus S^1p)\xrightarrow{\pi^!}H_d(M,M\setminus S^1p) \end{equation} which yields the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Poincaré duality computes local homology; the Gysin sequence splits by the Euler class vanishing lemma, giving the result.

nodes.name: $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $S^1$-space. An \emph{$S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas} $A$ on $X$ is an implicit atlas $A$ along with an action of $S^1$ on each thickening $X_I$ (commuting with the $\Gamma_I$-action) such that each map $\psi_{IJ}$ is $S^1$-equivariant, each function $s_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant, and each subset $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is $S^1$-invariant. Similarly, we define an $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary and/or stratification by in addition requiring that the boundary loci $\partial X_I$ and/or stratifications $X_I\to\mathcal S$ be $S^1$-invariant.

conclusions: the $S^1$-action on $X$ lifts canonically to the orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$
nodes.statement: We begin with the trivial observation that if $X$ is equipped with a locally orientable $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas $A$, then the $S^1$-action on $X$ lifts canonically to the orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_X$.

nodes.name: Locally $S^1$-orientable implicit atlas
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $S^1$-space with $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas with boundary. We say that $A$ is \emph{locally $S^1$-orientable} iff it is locally orientable and for all $p\in X$, the stabilizer $(S^1)_p$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_X)_p$ (this action is always by a sign $(S^1)_p\to\{\pm 1\}$). This notion is independent of the ring $R$ (due to our restriction that $\#(S^1)_p$ be invertible in $R$).
differentia: for all $p\in X$, the stabilizer $(S^1)_p$ acts trivially on $(\mathfrak o_X)_p$

nodes.name: $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally constant

conclusions: $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that if $A$ is locally $S^1$-orientable, then $\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline R$ (where $\pi:X\to X/S^1$).

nodes.name: Global orientation implies locally $S^1$-orientable
nodes.statement: If $A$ is locally orientable and $\mathfrak o_X$ has a global section, then $A$ is automatically locally $S^1$-orientable ($S^1$ is connected, so the section must be $S^1$-invariant, hence the claim).

nodes.statement: The inclusion $C_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(X)\hookrightarrow C_\bullet(\pi:X\times ES^1\to(X\times ES^1)/S^1)$ is compatible with the $p$-grading on each.  Let us consider the associated morphism of spectral sequences (induced by the $p$-filtration).  The latter has $E^2_{p,q}$ term $H_p^{S^1}(X,H_q(S^1))$ by Dress.  It follows from the definition \eqref{qdegreedef} that the $E^2_{p,q}$ term of the former is the same in degrees $q\geq 1$ and zero otherwise.  Since $H_q(S^1)$ is nonzero only for $q\leq 1$, it follows that the former spectral sequence has no further differentials, and we conclude that the homology of $C_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ is indeed $H_\bullet^{S^1}(X)$ as needed.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.5.11
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{CSTpure}, we use Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf} to see that $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. More precisely, in the present context we need the statement of Lemma \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} for $C_\bullet^{S^1}$ in place of $C_\bullet$. The proof of this lemma applies equally well to $C_\bullet^{S^1}$, noting that since $C_\bullet^{S^1}$ is a model of $S^1$-equivariant chains, it in particular satisfies Mayer--Vietoris in that following (total complex) is acyclic: \begin{equation} C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cap U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U)\oplus C_\bullet^{S^1}(U')\to C_\bullet^{S^1}(U\cup U') \end{equation} Now let us show purity. By Lemma \ref{openclosedpurity}, it suffices to show that the restrictions of $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ to $(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ and to $X/S^1\setminus(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ are pure. The latter restriction is trivially pure, since both complexes are simply zero for $K\cap V_I\cap V_J=\varnothing$. Hence it suffices to show that the restrictions of both complexes to $(V_I\cap V_J)/S^1$ are pure. We consider the comparison maps: \begin{align} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&\to H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} These are Gysin maps $\pi^!$, and hence by the Gysin sequence, their kernels coincide (respectively) with the images of: \begin{align} H^{\bullet-2}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{\cap e}H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K;A)_{IJ}\\ H^{\bullet-2}_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\xrightarrow{\cap e}H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(K\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} where $e$ is (the pullback of) $e\in H^2_{S^1}(X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}/\Gamma_J)$. Pick any $p\in V_J\subseteq X$. By Lemma \ref{freeactionislocallytrivial}, this $e$ vanishes when restricted to small $S^1$-invariant compact neighborhoods of $S^1p\subseteq V_J=(s_J|X_J^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_J\subseteq X_J^{\mathrm{reg}}/\Gamma_J$. It follows that \eqref{HSTzero}--\eqref{HSTzerorel} vanish for small $S^1$-invariant compact neighborhoods $K$ of $S^1p\subseteq V_J$. Hence \eqref{HSTinjective}--\eqref{HSTinjectiverel} are injective for such $K$. Now, using this injectivity and the fact that $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves (Lemma \ref{CSTpure}), it follows that $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$ are pure on $V_J/S^1$, and hence on all of $X/S^1$. It remains to identify $H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}$ and $H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}$. Consider the comparison maps: \begin{align} H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}&\to\pi_\ast H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A)_{IJ}\\ H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ}&\to\pi_\ast H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-\operatorname{rel}\partial;A)_{IJ} \end{align} which are maps of sheaves on $X/S^1$. It suffices (by Lemma \ref{CSTpure}) to show that these are isomorphisms (which we will check on stalks, i.e.\ for $K=S^1p$). Now this is just a calculation, similar to that in the proof of Lemma \ref{CSTpure}, except using an $S^1$-equivariant version of Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality based on Lemma \ref{SSmanifoldPDbase} in place of Lemma \ref{poincareduality} (and it is in this calculation where we use the local $S^1$-orientability of $A$).
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the non-equivariant purity proof: Mayer-Vietoris gives homotopy K-sheaves; purity via the Gysin sequence, local vanishing of the Euler class and injectivity of comparison maps; H^0 by an equivariant duality calculation.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8.5.13
nodes.statement: Consider the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \begin{tikzcd} H^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)\ar{d}{\sim}\ar{rr}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}&&H^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(X;A)\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X;C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}&\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq 0}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;H^0_{S^1,\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{u}[swap]{\sim}\ar{r}{\eqref{CSStimesSS}}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}\ar{u}\ar{d}{\sim}&\check H^\bullet(X;H^0_{\mathrm{vir}}(-;A))\ar{u}[swap]{\sim}\ar{d}{\sim}\\ \check H^\bullet(X/S^1;\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\ar[equal]{r}&\check H^\bullet(X/S^1,\pi_\ast\mathfrak o_X)\ar{r}{\pi^\ast}&\check H^\bullet(X;\mathfrak o_X) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation*} where the vertical isomorphisms are by Propositions \ref{CpureSS} and \ref{Cpure} (see also \eqref{isosforpurehtpysheafcech}). Now each small square of this diagram above commutes (only the bottom left requires an argument; one shows that the corresponding diagram of sheaves commutes by checking it locally, where it is just a calculation). Now the first square in Theorem \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso} is the same as the big square above, which commutes by a diagram chase (for which one should be careful of the fact that one of the vertical arrows is not an isomorphism). An identical argument applies to the second square in Theorem \ref{Slocalfundamentaliso}.
nodes.statement_short: Build a large diagram of Cech cohomology groups using purity; small squares commute locally and a diagram chase gives the claimed square.
