nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \tilde Z_\bullet&\ar{l}\tilde Z_\bullet^a\ar{r}&\tilde Z_\bullet^b&\ar{l}\tilde Z_\bullet^c\ar{r}&\tilde Z_\bullet^0\cr \lambda&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{\eqref{relpartialSSpushforwardbigcomplex}}\lambda&&\lambda\ar[mapsto]{r}{\lambda=\lambda^0\oplus\lambda^1}&\lambda^0\cr \tilde\lambda&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!]}\tilde\lambda&&\tilde\lambda\ar[mapsto]{r}{Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus 0]}&\tilde\lambda^0\cr &{}[[E]]\ar[mapsto]{r}{\circ Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!]}&{}[[E]]&\ar[mapsto]{l}[swap]{\circ Q[\operatorname{id}\oplus 0]}\null[[E]] \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: defofZabcmaps

nodes.name: Matrix coefficients
nodes.statement_short: Define the diagrams via matrix coefficients; isomorphisms with pullbacks are evident.
nodes.statement:
Now $\widetilde{\mathbb H},\widetilde{\mathbb H}^a,\widetilde{\mathbb H}^b,\widetilde{\mathbb H}^c,\widetilde{\mathbb H}^0$ are defined via the matrix coefficients $c_{\sigma,p,q}$ defined as follows:
\begin{align*}
\text{for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\
\text{for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}^a$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\operatorname{id}\oplus\pi^!)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\
\text{for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}^b$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\
\text{for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}^c$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\operatorname{id}\oplus 0)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})\\
\text{for $\widetilde{\mathbb H}^0$:}\quad c_{\sigma,p,q}&:=([[E]]_{\sigma,p,q}\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(\tilde\lambda_{\sigma,p,q})
\end{align*}
These matrix coefficients give rise to diagrams in $\mathsf{N}_{\mathsf{dg}}(\mathsf{Ch}_{R[[H]]})$ since $[[E]]$ is a map of $\mathsf{F}$-modules.  The isomorphisms between these diagrams and their pullbacks under the maps \eqref{defofZabcmaps} are evident.

nodes.name: Trivial Kan fibrations and descent
nodes.statement_short: Each resolution is a trivial Kan fibration with degenerate-ID property; uniqueness of descent gives the isomorphisms.
nodes.statement: It now remains to show that each of the maps $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ satisfies the conclusions of Propositions \ref{trivialKanfibration} and \ref{degenerateID}.  The proof of Proposition \ref{trivialKanfibration} applies to $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ as written (for $\tilde Z_\bullet^b$, the extension of $[[E]]$ step uses the fact that $H_\bullet(E;\mathcal A)\oplus H_{\bullet-1}^{S^1}(E;\mathcal A)$ is concentrated in degrees $\geq 0$ so that Lemma \ref{Hzeroofcofibrantcolimit} still applies).  The proof of Proposition \ref{degenerateID} also applies to $\tilde Z_\bullet^a,\tilde Z_\bullet^b,\tilde Z_\bullet^c\to\tilde Z_\bullet$ as written.  Now the uniqueness of descent from Lemma \ref{descentofdiagram} shows that there are canonical isomorphisms of the descents $\mathbb H=\mathbb H^a=\mathbb H^b=\mathbb H^c=\mathbb H^0$.

nodes.name: Nodal curve of type (g,n)
nodes.statement: A \emph{nodal curve of type $(g,n)$} is a compact nodal Riemann surface $C$ of arithmetic genus $g$ along with an injective function $l:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to C$ (the ``$n$ marked points'') whose image is disjoint from the nodes of $C$. An \emph{isomorphism $(C,l)\to(C',l')$ of curves of type $(g,n)$} is an isomorphism of Riemann surfaces $\iota:C\to C'$ such that $l'=\iota\circ l$. We usually omit $l$ from the notation. Such a curve is called \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group is finite.
nodes.statement_short: Nodal genus-$g$ Riemann surface with $n$ distinct marked points off the nodes; isomorphisms and stability (finite automorphisms).

nodes.name: Deligne--Mumford moduli space and universal family
nodes.statement: We denote by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ the Deligne--Mumford moduli space of stable nodal curves of type $(g,n)$, and we denote by $\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ the universal family (which coincides with the ``forget the last marked point and stabilize'' map $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+1}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$).

nodes.name: J-holomorphic map of type (g,n)
nodes.statement: A \emph{$J$-holomorphic map of type $(g,n)$} is a pair $(C,u)$ where $C$ is a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$ and $u:C\to X$ is smooth and satisfies $\bar\partial u=0$. An \emph{isomorphism $(C,u)\to(C',u')$ of $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$} is an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(g,n)$ such that $u=u'\circ\iota$. We say a $J$-holomorphic map is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A nodal curve with a smooth map $u$ satisfying $\bar\partial u=0$; isomorphisms and stability (finite automorphism group).

nodes.name: Moduli space of stable maps
nodes.statement: Let $\beta\in H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$. We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ as the set of stable $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ for which $u_\ast[C]=\beta$. We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ with the Gromov topology, which is well-known to be compact Hausdorff.
nodes.statement_short: Set of stable $J$-holomorphic maps in class $\beta$, with the compact Hausdorff Gromov topology.

nodes.name: Gromov topology
nodes.statement_short: Neighborhood base at $(C,u)$: maps whose graphs (after stabilizing marked points) are Hausdorff-close to the graph of $u$.
nodes.statement: A neighborhood base\footnote{A \emph{neighborhood} of a point $x$ in a topological space $X$ is a subset $N\subseteq X$ such that $x\in N^\circ$ (the interior).  A \emph{neighborhood base} at a point $x\in X$ is a collection of neighborhoods $\{N_\alpha\}$ of $x$ such that for every open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$, there exists some $N_\alpha\subseteq U$.  A neighborhood base is necessarily nonempty and \emph{filtered}, i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta$, there exists $\gamma$ with $N_\gamma\subseteq N_\alpha\cap N_\beta$.  Conversely, given a set $X$ and for every $x\in X$ a nonempty filtered collection of subsets $\{N_\alpha^x\}$ each containing $x$, there is a unique topology on $X$ such that $\{N^x_\alpha\}$ is a neighborhood base at $x$ for all $x\in X$.} at a pair $(C,u)$ may be obtained as follows.  We choose some additional $\ell$ marked points on $C$ so that it has no automorphisms fixing these points, and we consider the graph $\Gamma_u\subseteq X\times\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}$ where $\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ denotes the universal curve.  A neighborhood base at $(C,u)$ is obtained taking all $J$-holomorphic maps from curves in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ whose graph is close to $\Gamma_u$ in the Hausdorff topology (and forgetting the $\ell$ extra marked points).  Choosing different $\ell'$ marked points yields an equivalent neighborhood base.

nodes.name: Gromov--Witten thickening datum / index set A^GW
nodes.statement: A \emph{(Gromov--Witten) thickening datum} $\alpha$ is a 6-tuple $(D_\alpha,r_\alpha,\Gamma_\alpha,\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$D_\alpha\to X$ is a compact smooth embedded codimension two submanifold with boundary. \item$r_\alpha\geq 0$ is an integer such that $2g+n+r_\alpha>2$. \item$\Gamma_\alpha$ is a finite group. \item$\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ is a smooth $\Gamma_\alpha$-manifold\footnote{Note that we do not assume $\Gamma_\alpha$ acts effectively on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. Indeed, $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,1}$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,0}$ are ineffective orbifolds, so we must allow ineffective actions if we want $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha$ to be isomorphic to an open subset of one of these spaces.} equipped with an isomorphism of orbifolds between $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha$ and an open subset of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ (let $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ be the pullback\footnote{Pullback here means the orbifold fiber product (see Remark \ref{orbifoldfiberproductrmk}). Note that the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ are nodal curves of type $(g,n+r_\alpha)$ (not quotiented by their automorphism group).} of the universal family; the action of $\Gamma_\alpha$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ lifts canonically to $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ by the universal property of the pullback). \item$E_\alpha$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb R[\Gamma_\alpha]$-module. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)$ is a $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariant linear map supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. \end{rlist} Let $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ denote the set\footnote{The reader concerned with set theoretic issues may wish to add ``rigidifying data'' to the definition of a thickening datum as in Remark \ref{notsetremark}.} of all thickening datums.
nodes.statement_short: A thickening datum is a divisor $D_\alpha$, count $r_\alpha$, finite group, local chart of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}$, obstruction space $E_\alpha$ and map $\lambda_\alpha$; $A^{GW}$ is the set of all of them.
nodes.label: divisorthicken

nodes.name: Transversality of smooth maps to a divisor
nodes.statement: Let $u:C\to X$ be a smooth map from a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$, and let $D\subseteq X$ be a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary. We say \emph{$u$ is transverse to $D$} (written $u\pitchfork D$) iff $u^{-1}(\partial D)=0$ and $\forall\,p\in u^{-1}(D)$, the derivative $du:T_pC\to T_{u(p)}X/T_{u(p)}D$ is surjective and $p$ is neither a node nor a marked point of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: $u\pitchfork D$: $u$ misses $\partial D$ and is transverse to $D$ at preimage points, which avoid nodes and marked points.

nodes.name: I-thickened J-holomorphic map
nodes.statement: Let $I\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ be a finite subset. An \emph{$I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic map of type $(g,n)$} is a quadruple $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(g,n)$. \item$u:C\to X$ is a smooth map such that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections for all $\alpha\in I$. \item$\phi_\alpha:C\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ an isomorphism between $C$ (with $r_\alpha$ extra marked points $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$) and some fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. \item$e_\alpha\in E_\alpha$. \item The following \emph{$I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation} is satisfied: \begin{equation} \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0 \end{equation} This equation takes place in $C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)$. Certainly $\bar\partial u$ is a smooth section of $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX$ over $\tilde C$. To interpret $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$ as such a section, consider the following composition: \begin{equation} C\xrightarrow{(\phi_\alpha,u)}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X\xrightarrow{\lambda(e_\alpha)}\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX \end{equation} This sends a point $p\in C$ to an element of $(\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha})_{\phi_\alpha(p)}\otimes T_{u(p)}X$, which we identify via $\phi_\alpha$ with $(\Omega^{0,1}_C\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)_p$. This is what we mean by $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\to(C',u',\{\phi_\alpha'\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha'\}_{\alpha\in I})$ between two $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ is an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C'$ of curves of $(g,n)$-type such that $u=u'\circ\iota$, $\phi_\alpha=\phi_\alpha'\circ\iota$, and $e_\alpha=e_\alpha'$. We say an $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic map is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A curve with map $u$ transverse to the divisors $D_\alpha$, fiber identifications $\phi_\alpha$ and $e_\alpha\in E_\alpha$ solving the perturbed $\bar\partial$-equation; isomorphisms and stability.
nodes.label: thickendefs

nodes.name: I-thickened del-bar equation
nodes.statement: \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0
nodes.label: complementeddelbar

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: C\xrightarrow{(\phi_\alpha,u)}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X\xrightarrow{\lambda(e_\alpha)}\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX

nodes.name: Atlas data for A^GW on the moduli space of stable maps
nodes.statement: We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ as the set of isomorphism classes of stable $I$-thickened $J$-holomorphic maps of type $(g,n)$ such that $u_\ast[C]=\beta$. Equip $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ with the Gromov topology\footnote{When $I\ne\varnothing$, this topology is easy to define: it is simply given by using the Hausdorff distance on the image $C\subseteq X\times\prod_{\alpha\in I}\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$.} for $(u,\phi_\alpha)$ and with the obvious topology for $e_\alpha$. It is clear by definition that $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_\varnothing$. There is an evident action $\Gamma_I$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$, namely $\{g_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}\cdot(u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})=(u,\{g_\alpha\cdot\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{g_\alpha\cdot e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ which works since $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=\lambda_\alpha(g_\alpha\cdot e_\alpha)(g_\alpha\cdot\phi_\alpha,u)$ by $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariance. There are evident maps $s_\alpha:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I\to E_\alpha$ simply picking out $e_\alpha$. For $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}$, there is an obvious forgetful map $\psi_{IJ}:(s_{J\setminus I}|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J)^{-1}(0)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Let $U_{IJ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ consist of those elements such that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections for all $\alpha\in J\setminus I$ and such that adding these extra marked points makes $C$ isomorphic to a fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$. It's not too hard to see that this is an open set (using elliptic regularity).
nodes.statement_short: Thickened moduli spaces of stable $I$-thickened maps with Gromov topology, $\Gamma_I$-action, maps $s_\alpha$, forgetful maps $\psi_{IJ}$ and open sets $U_{IJ}$.
nodes.label: GWatlasdatadef

nodes.name: Proof of the homeomorphism axiom for A^GW
nodes.statement_short: Verify the homeomorphism axiom: the induced map from the quotient of the zero locus to $U_{IJ}$ is a bijection and the topologies agree.
nodes.statement: The compatibility axioms are all immediate, though let us justify the homeomorphism axiom.  First, we claim that the map $(s_{J\setminus I}|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J)^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_{J\setminus I}\to U_{IJ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ induced by $\psi_{IJ}$ is a bijection.  This is more or less clear: fixing an element of $U_{IJ}$, an inverse image must have $e_\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$, and by definition of $U_{IJ}$, there exists a suitable $\phi_\alpha$ which is clearly unique up to the action of $\Gamma_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$.  That the topologies coincide can be checked directly from their definition.

nodes.name: Bijectivity of the forgetful map
nodes.statement_short: Claim and check that the quotient map onto $U_{IJ}$ is bijective.
nodes.statement: The compatibility axioms are all immediate, though let us justify the homeomorphism axiom.  First, we claim that the map $(s_{J\setminus I}|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J)^{-1}(0)/\Gamma_{J\setminus I}\to U_{IJ}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ induced by $\psi_{IJ}$ is a bijection.  This is more or less clear: fixing an element of $U_{IJ}$, an inverse image must have $e_\alpha=0$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$, and by definition of $U_{IJ}$, there exists a suitable $\phi_\alpha$ which is clearly unique up to the action of $\Gamma_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in J\setminus I$.

nodes.name: Topologies coincide
nodes.statement_short: Topologies agree by direct check.
nodes.statement: That the topologies coincide can be checked directly from their definition.

nodes.name: Regular locus for A^GW
nodes.statement: We define $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Let $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$. Roughly speaking, this point is contained in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ iff it has trivial automorphism group and the ``vertical'' (i.e.\ from a fixed domain curve) linearized version of the $I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation \eqref{complementeddelbar} is surjective. Let us now make this precise. Consider the smooth Banach manifold $W^{k,p}(C,X)$ for some large integer $k$ and some $p\in(1,\infty)$. Note that the condition $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections making $C$ isomorphic to a fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha$ (for all $\alpha\in I$) forms an open subset of $W^{k,p}(C,X)$ containing $u_0$. Furthermore, there is a unique continuous choice of: \begin{equation} C\times W^{k,p}(C,X)\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha \end{equation} over $C$ times a neighborhood of $u_0$ which extends $\phi_\alpha$ on $C\times\{u_0\}$ (this holds because $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ is an \'etale map of orbifolds). One can also check that this map \eqref{phiparametric} is highly differentiable (this depends on $k$ being large). Now we consider the smooth Banach bundle whose fiber over $(u,\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in W^{k,p}(C,X)\times E_I$ is $W^{k-1,p}(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)$ (where $\tilde C$ is the normalization of $C$). Now the left hand side of \eqref{complementeddelbar} (using \eqref{phiparametric} in place of $\phi_\alpha$) is a highly differentiable section of this bundle. We say that $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ iff the following two conditions hold: \begin{rlist} \item This section is transverse to the zero section at $(u_0,e_\alpha)$. \item The automorphism group of $(C,u_0,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ is trivial. \end{rlist} It is an easy exercise in elliptic regularity to show that the first condition is independent of the choice of $(k,p)$ (as long as $k$ is sufficiently large so that the condition makes sense).
nodes.statement_short: A thickened map is regular iff the vertical linearized thickened $\bar\partial$-operator is transverse to zero and its automorphism group is trivial.
nodes.label: regularsubsetdefinition

nodes.name: Equation phiparametric
nodes.statement: C\times W^{k,p}(C,X)\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha
nodes.label: phiparametric

nodes.name: Virtual dimension of the moduli space of stable maps
Equation
nodes.statement: \operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X):=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle

nodes.name: Proof of the transversality axioms for A^GW
nodes.statement_short: Freeness from trivial automorphism groups of regular points; openness and submersion from the gluing proposition.
nodes.statement: Let us now verify the transversality axioms.  Freeness of the action of $\Gamma_{J\setminus I}$ on $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})$ follows from the fact that points in $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ have trivial automorphism group.  The openness and submersion axioms follow from the following result, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingappendix}.

nodes.name: Freeness axiom
nodes.statement_short: Freeness follows from trivial automorphisms of regular points.
nodes.statement: Let us now verify the transversality axioms.  Freeness of the action of $\Gamma_{J\setminus I}$ on $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(X_I^{\mathrm{reg}})$ follows from the fact that points in $X_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ have trivial automorphism group.

nodes.name: Openness and submersion via gluing
nodes.statement_short: Openness and submersion follow from the gluing proposition.
nodes.statement: The openness and submersion axioms follow from the following result, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingappendix}.

nodes.name: Formal regularity implies topological regularity (Gromov--Witten)
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}_I\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ is an open subset. \itemThe map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}))\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J$. \itemThere is a canonical identification of the orientation local system $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}$ (by the standard reduction to the canonical orientation of a complex linear Fredholm operator as in McDuff--Salamon \cite{mcduffsalamonJholquant,mcduffsalamonJholsymp}). \end{rlist}
assumptions: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}$
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}_I\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$ is an open subset
The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ is locally modeled on the projection
There is a canonical identification of the orientation local system $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}$
nodes.statement_short: Gluing result: the regular locus is open, $s_{J\setminus I}$ is locally a submersion of the expected dimension, and orientations are canonically identified with $\mathfrak o_{E_I}$.
nodes.label: GWgluingneeded

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}

nodes.name: Content of the gluing proposition
nodes.statement: Near points of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}_I$ with smooth domain curve, the proposition follows from standard techniques (implicit function theorem, elliptic regularity, and an index theorem).  The real content of the proposition is that it holds near points with nodal domain curve.

nodes.name: Sard-type divisor lemma
nodes.statement: Let $f:N^n\to M^m$ be a smooth map of smooth manifolds with $n\leq m$. Then for every $p\in N$ with $df_p$ injective and every neighborhood $U$ of $f(p)$, there exists a codimension $n$ smooth submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq M$ contained in $U$ such that $f\pitchfork D$ and $f^{-1}(D)$ contains a point arbitrarily close to $p$.
assumptions: $f:N^n\to M^m$ be a smooth map of smooth manifolds with $n\leq m$
$p\in N$ with $df_p$ injective
every neighborhood $U$ of $f(p)$
conclusions: there exists a codimension $n$ smooth submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq M$ contained in $U$ such that $f\pitchfork D$ and $f^{-1}(D)$ contains a point arbitrarily close to $p$
nodes.statement_short: Near an immersion point one can find a small codimension-$n$ submanifold transverse to $f$ hit near $p$.
nodes.label: sortofsard

nodes.name: Proof (F434)
nodes.statement: After possibly shrinking $U$, choose a local projection $\pi:U\to T_pN$. Then let $D$ be $\pi^{-1}$ of a regular value of $\pi\circ f$ (which exists by Sard's theorem).
nodes.statement_short: Project locally to $T_pN$ and take $D$ as the preimage of a regular value of $\pi\circ f$ via Sard's theorem.

nodes.name: Domain stabilization for stable J-holomorphic maps
nodes.statement: Let $u:C\to X$ be a stable $J$-holomorphic map. Then there exists a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
assumptions: $u:C\to X$ be a stable $J$-holomorphic map
conclusions: there exists a smooth codimension two submanifold with boundary $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable
nodes.label: stabilizationlemma

nodes.name: Proof (F436)
nodes.statement: Let us observe that if $C_0\subseteq C$ is any unstable irreducible component, we must have $u:C_0\to X$ is nonconstant. Hence since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, it follows that there is a point on $C_0$ (which is not a node or marked point) where $du$ is injective. It follows using Lemma \ref{sortofsard} that there exists $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as marked points makes $C$ stable.
nodes.statement_short: Unstable components are nonconstant, so have an injectivity point of $du$; apply the Sard-type lemma to get the divisor.

nodes.name: Unstable components are nonconstant
nodes.statement_short: Unstable components must map nonconstantly.
nodes.statement: Let us observe that if $C_0\subseteq C$ is any unstable irreducible component, we must have $u:C_0\to X$ is nonconstant.

nodes.name: Injectivity point
nodes.statement_short: A nonconstant $J$-holomorphic component has a point where $du$ is injective.
nodes.statement: Hence since $u$ is $J$-holomorphic, it follows that there is a point on $C_0$ (which is not a node or marked point) where $du$ is injective.

nodes.name: Apply Sard-type lemma
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Sard-type lemma to get $D$.
nodes.statement: It follows using Lemma \ref{sortofsard} that there exists $D\subseteq X$ such that $u\pitchfork D$ and adding $u^{-1}(D)$ to $C$ as marked points makes $C$ stable.

nodes.name: Covering axiom for A^GW
nodes.statement: We have: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0)) \end{equation}
conclusions: \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0))
nodes.statement_short: Every stable map lies in the image of the regular zero locus of some thickening.
nodes.label: everythingcanbethickened

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)=\bigcup_{I\subseteq A^{\mathrm{GW}}}\psi_{\varnothing I}((s_I|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0))

nodes.name: Proof (F439)
nodes.statement: Fix a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ (that is, a curve $u:C\to X$). We will construct $\alpha\in A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ so that this point is contained in $\psi_{\varnothing\{\alpha\}}((s_\alpha|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0))$. First, pick $D_\alpha\subseteq X$ satisfying the conclusion of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}. Now let $r_\alpha=\#u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$. Adding $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$ as extra marked points to $C$ gives a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$, and we pick some local orbifold chart $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ covering this point. Now let us consider the linearized $\bar\partial$ operator: \begin{equation} D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX) \end{equation} ($\tilde C$ being the normalization of $C$) where $C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq C^\infty(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$ is the subspace of functions descending continuously to $C$. If $(k,p)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 1}\times(1,\infty)$ with $kp>2$, then we get a corresponding $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot)$ map $W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ (the restriction on $(k,p)$ comes from the need to define $W^{k,p}(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq W^{k,p}(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$). This operator is Fredholm; in particular its cokernel is finite-dimensional. Suppose we have a finite-dimensional vector space $E_0$ equipped with a linear map: \begin{equation} \tilde\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX) \end{equation} supported away from (the inverse image in $\tilde C$ of) the nodes and marked points of $C$. Then the following conditions are equivalent (exercise using elliptic regularity): \begin{rlist} \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty\to C^\infty$. \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ for some $(k,p)$. \item\eqref{lambdazero} is surjective onto the cokernel of $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ for all $(k,p)$. \end{rlist} There exists such a pair $E_0$ and $\tilde\lambda_0$ satisfying these conditions since we may choose $k=1$ and $p>2$ and then remember that $C^\infty$ functions supported away from the nodes and marked points are dense in $W^{0,p}=L^p$. Now pick any isomorphism to a fiber $\phi_\alpha:C\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ and extend $\tilde\lambda_0$ to a map $\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)$ supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers. Define $E_\alpha=E_0[\Gamma]$ and define $\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)$ by $\Gamma_\alpha$-linear extension from $\lambda_0$. It is now clear by definition that $u:C\to X$ is covered by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^{\mathrm{reg}}$, where $\alpha\in A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ is the element just constructed.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a single thickening datum covering a given stable map. Stabilize the domain with a divisor, then choose obstruction space $E_0$ surjecting onto the cokernel of the linearized $\bar\partial$ operator and extend $\Gamma_\alpha$-equivariantly.

nodes.name: Fix a stable map
nodes.statement_short: Fix a point; goal is one thickening datum covering it.
nodes.statement: Fix a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ (that is, a curve $u:C\to X$).  We will construct $\alpha\in A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ so that this point is contained in $\psi_{\varnothing\{\alpha\}}((s_\alpha|\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^{\mathrm{reg}})^{-1}(0))$.

nodes.name: Choose stabilizing divisor
nodes.statement_short: Choose $D_\alpha$ by domain stabilization.
nodes.statement: First, pick $D_\alpha\subseteq X$ satisfying the conclusion of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}.

nodes.name: Choose orbifold chart
nodes.statement_short: Set $r_\alpha$ and choose a local chart of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$.
nodes.statement: Now let $r_\alpha=\#u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$.  Adding $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$ as extra marked points to $C$ gives a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$, and we pick some local orbifold chart $\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha/\Gamma_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+r_\alpha}/S_{r_\alpha}$ covering this point.

nodes.name: Linearized operator is Fredholm
nodes.statement_short: Consider the linearized $\bar\partial$ operator in Sobolev completions; it is Fredholm.
nodes.statement:
Now let us consider the linearized $\bar\partial$ operator:
\begin{equation} D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)
\end{equation}
($\tilde C$ being the normalization of $C$) where $C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq C^\infty(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$ is the subspace of functions descending continuously to $C$.  If $(k,p)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 1}\times(1,\infty)$ with $kp>2$, then we get a corresponding $D\bar\partial(u,\cdot)$ map $W^{k,p}\to W^{k-1,p}$ (the restriction on $(k,p)$ comes from the need to define $W^{k,p}(C,u^\ast TX)\subseteq W^{k,p}(\tilde C,u^\ast TX)$).  This operator is Fredholm; in particular its cokernel is finite-dimensional.

nodes.name: Linearized del-bar operator
nodes.statement: D\bar\partial(u,\cdot):C^\infty(C,u^\ast TX)\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)
nodes.label: linearizeddelbarforthickening

nodes.name: Equivalent cokernel-surjectivity conditions
nodes.statement_short: Surjectivity of $\tilde\lambda_0$ onto the cokernel is independent of regularity class.

nodes.name: Obstruction map lambda_0
nodes.statement: \tilde\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)
nodes.label: lambdazero

nodes.name: Existence of obstruction space
nodes.statement_short: Such $E_0$ exists by density of compactly supported smooth sections in $L^p$.
nodes.statement: There exists such a pair $E_0$ and $\tilde\lambda_0$ satisfying these conditions since we may choose $k=1$ and $p>2$ and then remember that $C^\infty$ functions supported away from the nodes and marked points are dense in $W^{0,p}=L^p$.

nodes.name: Build thickening datum
nodes.statement_short: Extend $\tilde\lambda_0$ equivariantly to get $\alpha$, which covers the point.
nodes.statement: Now pick any isomorphism to a fiber $\phi_\alpha:C\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha$ and extend $\tilde\lambda_0$ to a map $\lambda_0:E_0\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)$ supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers.  Define $E_\alpha=E_0[\Gamma]$ and define $\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha/\overline{\mathcal M}_\alpha}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)$ by $\Gamma_\alpha$-linear extension from $\lambda_0$.  It is now clear by definition that $u:C\to X$ is covered by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_{\{\alpha\}}^{\mathrm{reg}}$, where $\alpha\in A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ is the element just constructed.

nodes.name: Conclusion that A^GW is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement_short: Combine the verified compatibility, transversality and covering axioms.
nodes.statement: We have now shown the following.

nodes.name: A^GW is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement: $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$.
conclusions: $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$

nodes.name: Gromov--Witten invariants
nodes.statement: Fix nonnegative integers $g$ and $n$ with $2g+n>2$, and fix $\beta\in H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$. By Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}, the virtual orientation sheaf induced by $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ is canonically trivialized. Thus the implicit atlas $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ induces a virtual fundamental class $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)]^{\mathrm{vir}}\in\check H^\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X);\mathbb Q)^\vee$. We define the \emph{Gromov--Witten invariant}: \begin{equation} \mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n;\mathbb Q) \end{equation} as the pushforward of $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ under the tautological map $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n$. This is well-defined by the next lemma.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{GW}^\beta_{g,n}(X)$ is the pushforward of the virtual fundamental class of $\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)$ to $H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n;\mathbb Q)$.

nodes.name: Gromov--Witten invariant class
nodes.statement: \mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n;\mathbb Q)

nodes.name: Independence of Gromov--Witten invariants from J
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n)$ is independent of the choice of $J$.
conclusions: $\mathrm{GW}_{g,n}^\beta(X)\in H_\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}\times X^n)$ is independent of the choice of $J$

nodes.name: Proof (F446)
nodes.statement: Let $J_0$ and $J_1$ be any two smooth $\omega$-tame almost complex structures on $X$. We denote by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ the corresponding moduli spaces of stable maps (denoted earlier by simply $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ when we considered just a fixed $J$). There exists a smooth path of $\omega$-tame almost complex structures $J_{[0,1]}=\{J_t\}_{t\in[0,1]}$ connecting $J_0$ and $J_1$. Let us consider the corresponding ``parameterized'' moduli space of stable maps $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$. The construction from \S\ref{gromovwittenimplicitatlassubsection} gives an implicit atlas with boundary $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$ whose restriction to $\partial\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}):=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)\sqcup\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ agrees with $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ on these spaces. Hence it follows using Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks} that $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ in $\check H^\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}))^\vee$, which is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Cobordism argument: a path $J_{[0,1]}$ gives an implicit atlas with boundary on the parameterized moduli space, and the disjoint union and cobordism lemmas equate the two virtual classes.

nodes.name: Two almost complex structures
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $J_0,J_1$ and their moduli spaces.
nodes.statement: Let $J_0$ and $J_1$ be any two smooth $\omega$-tame almost complex structures on $X$.  We denote by $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ the corresponding moduli spaces of stable maps (denoted earlier by simply $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)$ when we considered just a fixed $J$).

nodes.name: Parameterized moduli space
nodes.statement_short: Connect by a path and consider the parameterized moduli space.
nodes.statement: There exists a smooth path of $\omega$-tame almost complex structures $J_{[0,1]}=\{J_t\}_{t\in[0,1]}$ connecting $J_0$ and $J_1$.  Let us consider the corresponding ``parameterized'' moduli space of stable maps $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$.

nodes.name: Implicit atlas with boundary
nodes.statement_short: The construction gives an implicit atlas with boundary restricting to $A^{GW}$ on the ends.
nodes.statement: The construction from \S\ref{gromovwittenimplicitatlassubsection} gives an implicit atlas with boundary $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]})$ whose restriction to $\partial\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}):=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)\sqcup\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)$ agrees with $A^{\mathrm{GW}}$ on these spaces.

nodes.name: Cobordism invariance
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint union and cobordism lemmas equate the virtual classes.
nodes.statement: Hence it follows using Lemmas \ref{disjointunionfc} and \ref{cobordismworks} that $[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_0)]^{\mathrm{vir}}=[\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_1)]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ in $\check H^\bullet(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X,J_{[0,1]}))^\vee$, which is enough.

nodes.name: Abelian cover of free loop space
nodes.statement: Let $L_0M$ denote the space of null-homotopic smooth maps $S^1\to M$, and let $\widetilde{L_0M}$ denote the space of such loops together with a homology class of bounding $2$-disk. Then $\widetilde{L_0M}\to L_0M$ is a $\pi$-cover where $\pi=\operatorname{im}(\pi_2(M)\to H_2(M;\mathbb Z))$.\footnote{We could just as easily work on the smaller cover corresponding to the image of $\omega\oplus c_1(M):\pi_2(M)\to\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb Z$. The corresponding equivalence relation is that $f_1,f_2:D^2\to M$ with $f_1|_{S^1}=f_2|_{S^1}$ are equivalent iff $\omega$ and $c_1(M)$ both vanish on ``$f_1-f_2$''$\in\pi_2(M)$.}
nodes.statement_short: Null-homotopic loops with a homology class of bounding disk form a $\pi$-cover of $L_0M$, $\pi=\operatorname{im}(\pi_2(M)\to H_2(M))$.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian flows
nodes.statement: For a smooth function $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$, let $X_H:M\times S^1\to TM$ denote the Hamiltonian vector field induced by $H$, and let $\phi_H:M\to M$ denote the time $1$ flow map of $X_H$. A \emph{periodic orbit} of $H$ is a smooth function $\gamma:S^1\to M$ satisfying $\gamma'(t)=X_{H(t)}(\gamma(t))$. Let $C^\infty(M\times S^1)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq C^\infty(M\times S^1)$ denote those functions $H$ for which $\phi_H$ has non-degenerate fixed points.
nodes.statement_short: Hamiltonian vector field, time-1 map, periodic orbits, and Hamiltonians with non-degenerate fixed points.

nodes.name: Simplicial sets of H and J
nodes.statement: Define the simplicial set $H_\bullet(M)$ where $H_n(M)$ is the set of smooth functions $H:\Delta^n\to C^\infty(M\times S^1)$ which are constant near the vertices and send the vertices to $C^\infty(M\times S^1)^{\mathrm{reg}}$. Define the simplicial set $J_\bullet(M)$ where $J_n(M)$ is the set of smooth functions $J:\Delta^n\to J(M)$ which are constant near the vertices ($J(M)$ is the space of smooth almost complex structures tamed by $\omega$) and which send the vertices to almost complex structures which are $\omega$-compatible. It is easy to see that $H_\bullet(M)$ and $J_\bullet(M)$ are both \emph{contractible Kan complexes}. A semisimplicial set $Z_\bullet$ is a contractible Kan complex iff every map $\partial\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ can be extended to a map $\Delta^n\to Z_\bullet$ for all $n\geq 0$ (where $\Delta^n$ is the semisimplicial $n$-simplex). Let $J\!H_\bullet(M)=J_\bullet(M)\times H_\bullet(M)$, which of course is also a contractible Kan complex.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicial sets of simplex-families of Hamiltonians and almost complex structures (regular/compatible at vertices); both are contractible Kan complexes, as is their product.
nodes.label: JHdef

nodes.name: Standard Morse function on the simplex
nodes.statement:
For this definition, let us view the $n$-simplex $\Delta^n$ as:  egin{equation} \Delta^n=\{\underline x\in[0,1]^{n+1}:0=x_0\leq\cdots\leq x_n\leq 1\} \end{equation} The $i$th vertex of $\Delta^n$ is given by $x_{n-i}=0$ and $x_{n-i+1}=1$. We now consider the Morse function on $\Delta^n$ given by $f(x):=\sum_{i=1}^n\cos\pi x_i$. Its gradient:  egin{equation} 
abla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi\sin(\pi x_i) rac\partial{\partial x_i} \end{equation} is tangent to the boundary of $\Delta^n$, and its critical points are precisely the vertices of $\Delta^n$, the index at vertex $i$ being $n-i$. Note also that for any facet inclusion $\Delta^k\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, the pushforward of $
abla f$ is again $
abla f$. Let us consider the space $\mathcal F(\Delta^n)$ of broken Morse flow lines from vertex $0$ (index $n$) to vertex $n$ (index $0$). This space is homeomorphic to a cube $[0,1]^{n-1}$, the factors $[0,1]$ being naturally indexed by the ``middle vertices'' $1,\ldots,n-1$ of $\Delta^n$. A flow line is broken at a vertex $i\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ iff the corresponding coordinate in $[0,1]^{n-1}$ equals $1$. Note that for any simplex $\sigma$ there are canonical compatible product/face maps:  egin{align} \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots k])	imes\mathcal F(\sigma|[k\ldots n])&	o\mathcal F(\sigma)\ \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n])&	o\mathcal F(\sigma) \end{align} See also \Sef{simplexflowsorsec} for more details. Adams \cite{adamscobar} considered spaces of paths on $\Delta^n$ with the same key properties (though it is important that our flow lines are smooth, whereas Adams' are not).
nodes.statement_short: Morse function on $\Delta^n$ whose critical points are the vertices; the space of broken flow lines from vertex $0$ to $n$ is a cube with product/face maps.
nodes.label: simplexflows

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \Delta^n=\{\underline x\in[0,1]^{n+1}:0=x_0\leq\cdots\leq x_n\leq 1\}

nodes.name: Gradient of the standard Morse function
nodes.statement: \nabla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi\sin(\pi x_i)\frac\partial{\partial x_i}
nodes.label: simplexmorsefunctiongradient

nodes.name: Equation Fproduct
nodes.statement: \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots k])\times\mathcal F(\sigma|[k\ldots n])&\to\mathcal F(\sigma)
nodes.label: Fproduct

nodes.name: Equation Fface
nodes.statement: \mathcal F(\sigma|[0\ldots\hat k\ldots n])&\to\mathcal F(\sigma)
nodes.label: Fface

nodes.name: Capped periodic orbits P_H
nodes.statement: For $H\in C^\infty(M\times S^1)^{\mathrm{reg}}$, let $\mathcal P_H\subseteq\widetilde{L_0M}$ denote the set of null-homotopic periodic orbits equipped with a homology class of bounding $2$-disk.

nodes.name: Floer trajectory
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma\in J_n(M)\times H_n(M)$ be an $n$-simplex; we denote by $H^\sigma:\Delta^n\times M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ and $J^\sigma:\Delta^n\to J(M)$ the corresponding smooth families. Let $p\in\mathcal P_{H_0}$ and $q\in\mathcal P_{H_n}$ be periodic orbits, where $H_i=H^\sigma(i\in\Delta^n,\cdot,\cdot)$ is the Hamiltonian associated to the $i$th vertex of $\Delta^n$. A \emph{Floer trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)$} is a triple $(C,\ell,u)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(0,2)$. Let us call the two marked points $x^-,x^+\in C$, and let $k=k(C)$ be the number of vertices (irreducible components of $C$) on the unique path from $x^-$ to $x^+$ in the dual graph of $C$. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken Morse flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$ (for the Morse function in Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Let $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$ be the corresponding sequence of vertices. We allow $\ell$ to contain constant flow lines, i.e.\ we allow $v_i=v_{i+1}$. \item$u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is a smooth \emph{building} of type $(\sigma,p,q)$, by which we mean the following. Let $C^\circ$ be $C$ punctured at $\{x^-,x^+\}$ and at the nodes corresponding to the edges in the unique path in the dual graph of $C$ from $x^-$ to $x^+$. The connected components $\{C^\circ_1,\ldots,C^\circ_k\}$ are naturally ordered ($x^-$ on the $1$st component and $x^+$ on the $k$th component). There must be periodic orbits $\{\gamma_0,\ldots,\gamma_k\}$ where $\gamma_i\in\mathcal P_{H_{v_i}}$ with $\gamma_0=p$ and $\gamma_k=q$. Then the negative (resp.\ positive) end of $C^\circ_i$ must be asymptotic to $(\gamma_{i-1}(t),t)$ (resp.\ $(\gamma_i(t),t)$) (with multiplicity one). We also require that $u$ have ``finite energy''. In addition, $u|C_i^\circ$ must be in the correct homology class: the element of $\pi_2(M)$ obtained by gluing together $u|C_i^\circ$ (resolving any nodes of $C_i^\circ$) with the given disks bounding $\gamma_i$ and $\gamma_{i-1}$ must vanish in homology. \item$u$ is pseudo-holomorphic with respect to the almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ defined as follows. Use coordinates $(t,s)\in S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$. Fix the standard almost complex structure on $S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, namely $J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R}(\frac\partial{\partial s})=\frac\partial{\partial t}$. Also fix the ($s$-dependent) almost complex structure $J^\sigma(\ell(s))$ on $M$. We let $A:T[S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R]\to TM$ be defined by $A(\frac\partial{\partial s})=X_{H^\sigma(\ell(s),t,\cdot)}$ and extended anti-holomorphically. Now we use the following almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$: \begin{equation} J=\left(\begin{matrix} J^\sigma(\ell(s))&A\cr 0&J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R} \end{matrix}\right) \end{equation} Note that the projection $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is holomorphic. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(C,\ell,u)\to(C',\ell',u')$ of Floer trajectories is an isomorphism $\iota_1:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(0,2)$ and an isomorphism $\iota_2:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; note that the existence of $\iota_1$ implies that $k(C)=k(C')$) such that $u=(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\iota_2^{-1})\circ u'\circ\iota_1$ and $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota_2$. We say a Floer trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: A genus-0 two-pointed nodal curve, a broken Morse flow line on $\Delta^n$, and a finite-energy building solving Floer's equation for the $\sigma$-family of $(J,H)$; isomorphisms and stability.
nodes.label: floertrajdef

nodes.name: Almost complex structure on M x S^1 x R
nodes.statement: J=\left(\begin{matrix} J^\sigma(\ell(s))&A\cr 0&J_{S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R} \end{matrix}\right)
nodes.label: compositeJoncylinder

nodes.name: Flow category diagram of Floer trajectories
nodes.statement: We define a $\pi$-equivariant flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ as follows. \begin{rlist} \item For a vertex $(J,H)\in J_0(M)\times H_0(M)$, we let $\mathcal P_{(J,H)}=\mathcal P_H$. \item The grading $\operatorname{gr}:\mathcal P\to\mathbb Z$ is the usual Conley--Zehnder index, and $\operatorname{gr}:\pi\to\mathbb Z$ is given by $\operatorname{gr}(h)=2\langle c_1(TM),h\rangle$. \item The action $a:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R$ is the usual symplectic action, and $a:\pi\to\mathbb R$ is given by $a(h)=\langle\omega,h\rangle$. \item We let $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ be the set of stable Floer trajectories of type $(\sigma,p,q)$, equipped with the Gromov topology. It is well-known that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ is compact Hausdorff. The finiteness conditions required on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ also follow from Gromov compactness. The product/face maps on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ are evident. \item The action of $\pi$ on everything is clear. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: The $\pi$-equivariant flow category diagram with generators $\mathcal P_H$, Conley--Zehnder grading, symplectic action, and moduli spaces of stable Floer trajectories.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer thickening datum / index set A^HF
nodes.statement: A \emph{(Hamiltonian Floer) thickening datum} $\alpha$ on the simplex $\Delta^n$ is a quadruple $(D_\alpha,r_\alpha,E_\alpha,\lambda_\alpha)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$D_\alpha\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ is a compact smooth submanifold with corners locally modeled on $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'}\subseteq\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'+2}$ or $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{N+1}\times\mathbb R^{N'}\subseteq\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^N\times\mathbb R^{N'+3}$. Let us denote by $\partial^{\mathrm{ess}} D_\alpha\subseteq\partial D_\alpha$ the closure of $\partial D_\alpha\setminus[M\times S^1\times\partial\Delta^n]$ (which is precisely the set of points with local model of the second type). \item$r_\alpha\geq 1$ is an integer; let $\Gamma_\alpha=S_{r_\alpha}$. \item$E_\alpha$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb R[S_{r_\alpha}]$-module. \item$\lambda_\alpha:E_\alpha\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}\times M,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\alpha}}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM)$ is an $S_{r_\alpha}$-equivariant linear map supported away from the nodes and marked points of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$ (the universal family). \end{rlist} Let $A^{\mathrm{HF}}(\Delta^n)$ denote the set of all thickening datums on $\Delta^n$.
nodes.statement_short: A thickening datum on $\Delta^n$: a submanifold with corners $D_\alpha\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$, count $r_\alpha$, $S_{r_\alpha}$-module $E_\alpha$ and equivariant map $\lambda_\alpha$.
nodes.label: implicitatlasonFloer

nodes.name: Implicit atlas A on the Floer flow category diagram
nodes.statement: We define a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ on the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ as follows.

nodes.name: Index sets bar A(sigma,p,q)
nodes.statement: We set $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma,p,q):=A^{\mathrm{HF}}(\sigma)$.

nodes.name: I-thickened Floer trajectory (atlas data for A^HF)
nodes.statement: For $I\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, an \emph{$I$-thickened Floer trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$} is a $5$-tuple $(C,\ell,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$C$ is a nodal curve of type $(0,2)$. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$. \item$u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ is a smooth building of type $(\sigma,p,q)$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{floertrajdef}(\ref{buildingdef})), with combinatorial type of $u$ belonging to $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. Recall that by definition (see \eqref{coproductforA}), $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is a disjoint union of various $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_n],p',q'):=A^{\mathrm{HF}}(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_n])$. Hence any given $\alpha\in I$ comes from one of these, say $\bar{\mathcal A}(\sigma|[i_0^\alpha\ldots i_n^\alpha],p'_\alpha,q'_\alpha)$. Let $C_\alpha\subseteq C$ denote the union of irreducible components corresponding to this triple, which exists because the combinatorial type of $u$ belongs to $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (this $C_\alpha$ is a key notion for the present construction of an implicit atlas). \item For all $\alpha\in I$, we must have $u|_{C_\alpha}\pitchfork D_\alpha$ with exactly $r_\alpha$ intersections. By $u|_{C_\alpha}\pitchfork D_\alpha$, we mean that under the map $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u:C_\alpha\to M\times S^1\times\Delta^{\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m]}$, we have\footnote{The closure of the image $\overline{C_\alpha}$ is precisely the image of $C_{\alpha}$ union the asymptotic periodic orbits.} $\overline{C_\alpha}\cap\partial^{\mathrm{ess}} D_\alpha=\varnothing$ and for every point $p\in C_\alpha$ mapping to $D_\alpha$, the derivative $d((\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u):T_pC\to T_{u(p)}[M\times S^1\times\Delta^{\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m]}]/T_{u(p)}D_\alpha$ is surjective and $p$ is not a node or marked point of $C$. \item$\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$ is an isomorphism with a fiber (where $C_\alpha$ is considered to have two marked points $x^-,x^+$ corresponding to $p_\alpha',q_\alpha'$ plus the $r_\alpha$ marked points $(u|C_\alpha)^{-1}(D_\alpha)$). \item$e_\alpha\in E_\alpha$. \item The following \emph{$I$-thickened $\bar\partial$-equation} is satisfied: \begin{equation} \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0 \end{equation} where we use the almost complex structure on $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ defined in \eqref{compositeJoncylinder}. The term $\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)$ only makes sense over $C_\alpha$; we interpret it as zero over the rest of $C$. Note that for \eqref{approxJholforHF}, we project $\lambda_\alpha$ onto $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TM_{J^\sigma(\ell(s))}$. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} between two $I$-thickened Floer trajectories $(C,\ell,u,\{e_\alpha\},\{\phi_\alpha\})$ and $(C',\ell',u',\{e_\alpha'\},\{\phi_\alpha'\})$ is an isomorphism $\iota_1:C\to C'$ of curves of type $(0,2)$ and an isomorphism $\iota_2:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; note that the existence of $\iota_1$ implies that $k(C)=k(C')$) such that $u=(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\iota_2^{-1})\circ u'\circ\iota_1$, $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota_2$, $\phi_\alpha=\phi_\alpha'\circ\iota_1$, and $e_\alpha=e_\alpha'$ for all $\alpha\in I$. We say an $I$-thickened Floer trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite. Let $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ denote the set of stable $I$-thickened Floer trajectories of type $(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and equip it with the Gromov topology. The actions of $\Gamma_I$ on the thickened moduli spaces, the functions $s_I$, the projections $\psi_{IJ}$, and the sets $U_{IJ}$ are all defined as in Definition \ref{GWatlasdatadef} from the Gromov--Witten setting. The stratification of $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ is evident.
nodes.statement_short: Floer trajectories with transverse divisor intersections on the sub-curves $C_\alpha$, fiber identifications and $e_\alpha$ solving the thickened Floer equation; their moduli spaces and atlas maps.
nodes.label: IAonfloerthickeningsdef

nodes.name: I-thickened del-bar equation (Floer)
nodes.statement: \bar\partial u+\sum_{\alpha\in I}\lambda_\alpha(e_\alpha)(\phi_\alpha,u)=0
nodes.label: approxJholforHF

nodes.name: Compatibility and homeomorphism axioms for A(sigma,p,q)
nodes.statement_short: Compatibility axioms are immediate; homeomorphism axiom as in the Gromov--Witten case.
nodes.statement: The compatibility axioms for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ are all immediate; the homeomorphism axiom can again be verified directly as in the Gromov--Witten setting.

nodes.name: Regular loci for A(sigma,p,q)
nodes.statement: The regular loci for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ are defined following Definition \ref{regularsubsetdefinition}, meaning that a $5$-tuple $(C,\ell,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})$ is regular iff it has trival automorphism group and the linearized operator (fixing $C$ and varying $u$, $\ell$, and $\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I}$) is surjective (see \S\ref{regularlocusdef} for more details).

nodes.name: Virtual dimension of Floer moduli spaces
nodes.statement: Let $\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}:=\operatorname{gr}(q)-\operatorname{gr}(p)+\dim\sigma-1-\operatorname{codim}\mathfrak s$.

nodes.name: Transversality axioms for A(sigma,p,q)
nodes.statement_short: Openness and submersion axioms reduce to the Floer gluing proposition.
nodes.statement: Let us now discuss the (nontrivial) transversality axioms for $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$.  The openness and submersion axioms follow from the following result, whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingHF}.

nodes.name: Formal regularity implies topological regularity (Hamiltonian Floer)
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset. \item The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^{\mathrm{reg}})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$. \item There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}). \end{rlist}
assumptions: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$
conclusions: $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset
is locally modeled on the projection
There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems
nodes.statement_short: Gluing result for Floer moduli: regular loci are open, $s_{J\setminus I}$ is a stratified local submersion, and coherent orientations exist.
nodes.label: HFgluingneeded

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}

nodes.name: Covering axiom for A(sigma,p,q)
nodes.statement_short: Run the Gromov--Witten covering argument with the Floer stabilization lemma.
nodes.statement: Finally, to verify the covering axiom, we use the general strategy from Lemma \ref{everythingcanbethickened} in the Gromov--Witten case.  To apply this in the present setting, we just need the following stabilization lemma to take the place of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}.

nodes.name: Domain stabilization for stable Floer trajectories
nodes.statement: Let $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$. Then there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$ as in Definition \ref{implicitatlasonFloer}(\ref{implicitatlasFloerD}) such that $C\pitchfork D$ in the sense of Definition \ref{IAonfloerthickeningsdef}(\ref{transversalitypartIAfloer}) and so that adding the intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable.
assumptions: $\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ and $u:C\to M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ be a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$
conclusions: there exists $D\subseteq M\times S^1\times\Delta^n$
so that adding the intersections to $C$ as extra marked points makes $C$ stable
nodes.label: stabilizationlemmaforHF

nodes.name: Proof (F464)
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}, we use (an appropriate variant for manifolds with corners of) Lemma \ref{sortofsard} (which we may also use to avoid the periodic orbits in question). It thus suffices to show that for any unstable component $C_0$ of $C$, there exists a point $p\in C_0$ where $d((\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u):TC_0\to TM\times TS^1\times T\Delta^n$ injective. To find such a point, we split into two cases. First, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is constant. Then $u:C_0\to M$ is a (nonconstant!) $J$-holomorphic sphere, and thus has a point of injectivity of $du$. Second, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is not constant. Then $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is an isomorphism; let us use $(t,s)\in S^1\times\mathbb R$ as coordinates on $C_0$. Now $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\in TM\times TS^1$ has nonzero coordinate in the $TS^1$ component (everywhere), and $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}\in TM\times TS^1$ has zero coordinate in the $TS^1$ coordinate (everywhere). Hence if $du$ is everywhere noninjective, we find that $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}=0\in TM\times TS^1$ everywhere. It follows that $u:C_0\to M\times S^1$ is independent of the $\mathbb R$ coordinate, and thus is simply a trivial cylinder mapping onto a periodic orbit. Now the stability condition (the automorphism group being finite) implies that the corresponding (piece of a) flow line $\ell:\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is nontrivial. It follows that we have the desired injectivity.
nodes.statement_short: As for stable maps via the Sard-type lemma; find an injectivity point on each unstable component by cases on whether its projection to the cylinder is constant.

nodes.name: Reduce to injectivity point
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via the Sard-type lemma to finding an injectivity point on each unstable component; split into cases.
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemma}, we use (an appropriate variant for manifolds with corners of) Lemma \ref{sortofsard} (which we may also use to avoid the periodic orbits in question).  It thus suffices to show that for any unstable component $C_0$ of $C$, there exists a point $p\in C_0$ where $d((\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell)\circ u):TC_0\to TM\times TS^1\times T\Delta^n$ injective.  To find such a point, we split into two cases.

nodes.name: Case: constant projection
nodes.statement_short: Constant projection gives a nonconstant $J$-holomorphic sphere.
nodes.statement: First, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is constant.  Then $u:C_0\to M$ is a (nonconstant!) $J$-holomorphic sphere, and thus has a point of injectivity of $du$.

nodes.name: Case: nonconstant projection
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise noninjectivity forces a trivial cylinder, whose flow line must then be nontrivial by stability.
nodes.statement: Second, suppose $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is not constant.  Then $u:C_0\to S^1\times\mathbb R$ is an isomorphism; let us use $(t,s)\in S^1\times\mathbb R$ as coordinates on $C_0$.  Now $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\in TM\times TS^1$ has nonzero coordinate in the $TS^1$ component (everywhere), and $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}\in TM\times TS^1$ has zero coordinate in the $TS^1$ coordinate (everywhere).  Hence if $du$ is everywhere noninjective, we find that $\frac{\partial u}{\partial s}=0\in TM\times TS^1$ everywhere.  It follows that $u:C_0\to M\times S^1$ is independent of the $\mathbb R$ coordinate, and thus is simply a trivial cylinder mapping onto a periodic orbit.  Now the stability condition (the automorphism group being finite) implies that the corresponding (piece of a) flow line $\ell:\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is nontrivial.  It follows that we have the desired injectivity.

nodes.name: A is a pi-equivariant implicit atlas on the Floer flow category diagram
nodes.statement: $\mathcal A$ is a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$.
conclusions: $\mathcal A$ is a $\pi$-equivariant implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$
nodes.label: IAonFloerworks

nodes.name: Proof (F466)
nodes.statement: We have shown above that each individual $\mathcal A(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$ is an implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. The required compatibility isomorphisms between these implicit atlases follow directly from the definition.
nodes.statement_short: Each piece is an implicit atlas by the preceding verification; compatibility isomorphisms are immediate from the definition.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer homology
nodes.statement: We have a $\pi$-equivariant flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/J\!H_\bullet(M)$ equipped with an implicit atlas $\mathcal A$. Moreover, Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded} gives coherent orientations $\omega$. Hence according to Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups}, we get a diagram $F\mathbb H:J\!H_\bullet(M)\to H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]})$ (the hypotheses of Definition \ref{defofhomologygroups} can be easily verified). Since $J\!H_\bullet(M)$ is a contractible Kan complex, this is really just a single object $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)\in H^0(\mathsf{Ch}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]})$ which we call the \emph{Hamiltonian Floer homology of $M$}.
nodes.statement_short: The VFC package applied to the Floer flow category diagram with its implicit atlas and coherent orientations gives a single object $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ since $J\!H_\bullet(M)$ is contractible Kan.

nodes.name: Graded completion ring
nodes.statement: The ring $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$ is the \emph{graded} completion of $\mathbb Q[\pi]$, see Definition \ref{gradedcompletion}.

nodes.name: Fixed compatible almost complex structure
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth almost complex structure $J$ on $M$ compatible with $\omega$.

nodes.name: Time-independent Morse Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: Let $H:M\to\mathbb R$ be a Morse function for which the time $1$ Hamiltonian flow map of $H$ has non-degerate fixed points, all of which are critical points of $H$ (for example, $H=\epsilon\cdot H_0$ is such a function for any Morse function $H_0:M\to\mathbb R$ and sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$).

nodes.name: Inclusion of the point into JH(M)
nodes.statement: Consider the inclusion $\ast\hookrightarrow J\!H_\bullet(M)$ (where $\ast$ is the simplicial $0$-simplex, i.e.\ the simplicial set with a single $n$-simplex for all $n$) defined by mapping everything to the constant families of almost complex structures and Hamiltonians given by $J$ and $H$.

nodes.name: Pullback flow category diagram over the point
nodes.statement: We will restrict attention to the (pullback) flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$.

nodes.name: Generators for time-independent Morse Hamiltonian
conclusions: the set of generators is $\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$ canonically
assumptions: With our assumptions on $H$
nodes.statement: With our assumptions on $H$, the set of generators is $\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$ canonically, and the grading on $\mathcal P$ is given by the Morse index on $\operatorname{crit}(H)$ plus $\operatorname{gr}:\pi\to\mathbb Z$.

nodes.name: Canonical S^1-action on Floer trajectories
conclusions: there is a canonical $S^1$-action on the spaces of stable Floer trajectories in $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$
nodes.statement: Now there is a canonical $S^1$-action on the spaces of stable Floer trajectories in $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ (postcompose $u$ with a rotation of $S^1$) which is compatible with the product/face maps (this action exists since $H$ is independent of the $S^1$-coordinate).

nodes.name: S^1-fixed flow category diagram
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ is also a flow category diagram
nodes.statement: It follows that $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ is also a flow category diagram (defined using the fixed locus $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$).

nodes.name: Morse trajectory
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma\in\ast$ be the $n$-simplex, and let $p,q\in\mathcal P=\operatorname{crit}(H)\times\pi$. A \emph{Morse trajectory of type $(\sigma,p,q)$} is a triple $(k,\ell,u)$ where: \begin{rlist} \item$k\geq 1$ is a positive integer. \item$\ell:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ is a broken Morse flow line from vertex $0$ to vertex $n$ (for the Morse function in Definition \ref{simplexflows}). Let $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$ be the corresponding sequence of vertices. We allow $\ell$ to contain constant flow lines, i.e.\ we allow $v_i=v_{i+1}$. \item$u:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to M$ is a broken Morse flow line from $p$ to $q$ for the function $H$. We allow $u$ to contain constant flow lines. \item The $\pi$-components of $p$ and $q$ agree. \end{rlist} An \emph{isomorphism} $\iota:(k,\ell,u)\to(k',\ell',u')$ of Morse trajectories is an isomorphism $\iota:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\coprod_{i=1}^{k'}\mathbb R$ (acting by translation on each factor and respecting the ordering of the terms; we require $k=k'$) such that $u=u'\circ\iota$ and $\ell=\ell'\circ\iota$. We say a Morse trajectory is \emph{stable} iff its automorphism group (i.e.\ group of self-isomorphisms) is finite. Let $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ denote the space of stable Morse trajectories.
nodes.statement_short: A broken flow line on $\Delta^n$ paired with a broken Morse flow line of $H$ from $p$ to $q$; isomorphisms, stability, and the moduli space of stable ones.
nodes.label: morseTdef

nodes.name: Morse trajectory spaces are manifolds with corners
nodes.statement: Suppose $H$ is Morse--Smale. Then with the stratification by $k$, the spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ are compact topological manifolds with corners.
assumptions: Suppose $H$ is Morse--Smale
conclusions: the spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ are compact topological manifolds with corners
nodes.label: morseassumptionMS

nodes.name: Proof that Morse trajectory spaces are manifolds with corners
nodes.statement_short: Cite Wehrheim for the 0-simplex; the general case is broken Morse flow lines of $H+f$ on $M\times\Delta^n$, again by Wehrheim.
nodes.statement: For the case of the zero simplex $\sigma=\sigma^0$, this is proved by Wehrheim \cite{wehrheimMS}.  In fact, the general case also follows from \cite{wehrheimMS} since $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ is the space of broken Morse flow lines on $M\times\Delta^n$ from $p\times 0$ to $q\times n$ for the Morse function $H+f$ (and $f$ is defined and smooth on a neighborhood of $\Delta^n\subseteq\mathbb R^n$).  Alternatively, one may restrict to $H$ which have a particular normal form near each critical point in which case this result holds by more elementary arguments (see also \cite{wehrheimMS}).

nodes.name: Zero simplex case
nodes.statement_short: Cite Wehrheim for $\sigma^0$.
nodes.statement: For the case of the zero simplex $\sigma=\sigma^0$, this is proved by Wehrheim \cite{wehrheimMS}.

nodes.name: General case via H+f
nodes.statement_short: Identify with broken flow lines of $H+f$ on $M\times\Delta^n$.
nodes.statement: In fact, the general case also follows from \cite{wehrheimMS} since $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ is the space of broken Morse flow lines on $M\times\Delta^n$ from $p\times 0$ to $q\times n$ for the Morse function $H+f$ (and $f$ is defined and smooth on a neighborhood of $\Delta^n\subseteq\mathbb R^n$).

nodes.name: Alternative via normal form
nodes.statement_short: Alternative elementary argument for Hamiltonians in normal form.
nodes.statement: Alternatively, one may restrict to $H$ which have a particular normal form near each critical point in which case this result holds by more elementary arguments (see also \cite{wehrheimMS}).

nodes.name: S^1-fixed Floer trajectories are Morse trajectories
nodes.statement: There is canonical homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}=\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$.
conclusions: There is canonical homeomorphism $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}=\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$
nodes.label: fixedismorse

nodes.name: Proof (F472)
nodes.statement: Suppose a stable Floer trajectory $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant. Then each of the components $\{C_1^\circ,\ldots,C_k^\circ\}$ must be smooth (no nodes) and hence isomorphic to $S^1\times\mathbb R$. Using the holomorphic projection $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, we get holomorphic identifications $C_i^\circ=S^1\times\mathbb R$. Since $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant, the function $u:C_i^\circ\to M$ must be independent of the $S^1$-coordinate, and hence (examining the $\bar\partial$-equation) is simply a Morse flow line of $H$. Running this argument in reverse, we also see that every stable Morse trajectory gives rise to a stable Floer trajectory which is $S^1$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: An $S^1$-invariant trajectory has smooth cylindrical components on which $u$ is $t$-independent, hence a Morse flow line; conversely Morse trajectories give invariant ones.

nodes.name: Components are smooth cylinders
nodes.statement_short: An $S^1$-invariant trajectory has smooth cylindrical components.
nodes.statement: Suppose a stable Floer trajectory $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant.  Then each of the components $\{C_1^\circ,\ldots,C_k^\circ\}$ must be smooth (no nodes) and hence isomorphic to $S^1\times\mathbb R$.

nodes.name: Holomorphic identifications
nodes.statement_short: Identify components with $S^1\times\mathbb R$ via the holomorphic projection.
nodes.statement: Using the holomorphic projection $M\times S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to S^1\times\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, we get holomorphic identifications $C_i^\circ=S^1\times\mathbb R$.

nodes.name: u is a Morse flow line
nodes.statement_short: Invariance makes $u$ $t$-independent, so a Morse flow line of $H$.
nodes.statement: Since $(C,\ell,u)$ is $S^1$-invariant, the function $u:C_i^\circ\to M$ must be independent of the $S^1$-coordinate, and hence (examining the $\bar\partial$-equation) is simply a Morse flow line of $H$.

nodes.name: Converse
nodes.statement_short: Conversely every Morse trajectory gives an invariant Floer trajectory.
nodes.statement: Running this argument in reverse, we also see that every stable Morse trajectory gives rise to a stable Floer trajectory which is $S^1$-invariant.

nodes.name: H = epsilon H_0 henceforth
nodes.statement: We will also need the following deeper fact (and henceforth we assume that $H$ is defined as in Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}):

nodes.name: S^1-fixed locus is open and transversally cut out
nodes.statement: Fix a Morse function $H_0:M\to\mathbb R$ whose gradient flow is Morse--Smale and suppose $H=\epsilon\cdot H_0$ with $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small. Then $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)$ is open and cut out transversally (meaning $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$). Hence we have a partition into disjoint closed subsets: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}] \end{equation}
