nodes.name: Proof (F475)
nodes.statement: Salamon--Zehnder \cite[p1342, Theorem 7.3(1)]{salamonzehnder} show that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma^0,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma^0,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ for the $0$-simplex $\sigma^0$ and sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$. Since we only consider constant families of $J$ and $H$, the linearized operators for the higher $\sigma^i$ can be written in terms of the linearized operators for $\sigma^0$, and it follows that $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ for all $\sigma$. Now we have $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$. It remains to show that this is an open inclusion. This can likely be seen by following closely the gluing argument used to prove Propositions \ref{HFgluingneeded} and \ref{morseassumptionMS}, however we can argue directly as follows. Both $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)$ and $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ are topological manifolds with corners, and the stratification for the former is the pullback of the stratification for the latter. Their dimensions are dictated by the Morse index and the Conley--Zehnder index respectively, which in this case coincide. Hence we are done by Lemma \ref{cornersinvarianceofdomain} below.
nodes.statement_short: Transversality from Salamon--Zehnder for the 0-simplex, extended to constant families. Openness via equal dimensions and invariance of domain for manifolds with corners.

nodes.name: Salamon--Zehnder transversality

Their dimensions are dictated by the Morse index and the Conley--Zehnder index respectively, which in this case coincide.

nodes.name: Invariance of domain with corners
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold with corners and $K\subseteq M$ a closed subset. Suppose that the restriction of the corner stratification on $M$ induces a topological manifold with corners structure on $K$ of the same dimension. Then $K\subseteq M$ is open.

conclusions: $K\subseteq M$ is open

nodes.name: Proof (F477)
nodes.statement: The question is local on $M$, so we may assume that $M=\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^m$. Let $\tilde K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m$ be obtained by reflecting $K$ across the last $m$ coordinate hyperplanes. The hypotheses then imply that $\tilde K$ is a manifold of dimension $n+m$. Now we have $\tilde K\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}$ is open by Brouwer's ``invariance of domain''. This is enough.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a local model, double $K$ by reflection, and apply Brouwer's invariance of domain.

nodes.name: Naive S^1-invariant subatlas fails the covering axiom
nodes.statement_short: The subatlas of A with S^1-invariant divisors carries an S^1-action but fails the covering axiom on Morse flow lines.
nodes.statement: Let us first motivate the definition of $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ by describing a ``first attempt'' at defining an $S^1$-equivariant implicit atlas on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$.  We consider the subatlas $\mathcal A^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal A$ consisting of those thickening datums $\alpha$ for which $D_\alpha$ is $S^1$-invariant.  Now there is clearly a canonical $S^1$-action on the thickenings $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ (postcomposition of $u$ with a rotation of $S^1$) for $I\subseteq\mathcal A^{S^1}(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$.\footnote{Note that we do not need to put any restrictions on $\lambda_\alpha$.}  Now $\mathcal A^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal A$ forms an implicit atlas if and only if it satisfies the covering axiom.  However, the covering axiom for $\mathcal A^{S^1}$ fails: we cannot stabilize the domains of Morse flow lines (points of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$) using $S^1$-invariant divisors $D_\alpha$ (more generally, we cannot stabilize the domain of any broken trajectory containing a Morse flow line).

nodes.name: Implicit atlas B on M/* (unstabilized Morse components)
nodes.statement: We define an implicit atlas $\mathcal B$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ as follows. On the level of index sets, we define $\mathcal B:=\mathcal A$. However, we modify the definition of an $I$-thickened Floer trajectory as follows. We require that when $C_\alpha$ is considered with the $r_\alpha$ extra marked points $(u|C_\alpha)^{-1}(D_\alpha)$, the only unstable components are mapped by $u$ to Morse flow lines; let $C_\alpha\to C_\alpha^{\mathrm{st}}$ be the map contracting all such unstable components. Now instead of $\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$, we use $\phi_\alpha:C_\alpha^{\mathrm{st}}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\alpha}$. The rest of the atlas data is defined analogously with that of $\mathcal A$ without any serious difference. Note, however, that to verify that the locus $U_{IJ}\subseteq X_I$ is open, we must appeal to Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}.
nodes.statement_short: Modify atlas A so that Morse-flow-line components of Floer trajectories need not be stabilized; index sets unchanged.
nodes.label: modifiedatlasforMorse

nodes.name: Argument that B is an implicit atlas
nodes.statement_short: Covering axiom for B follows from that of A; the openness and submersion axioms follow from the gluing proposition.
nodes.statement: Note that the thickened moduli spaces for $\mathcal A$ are open subsets of those for $\mathcal B$, so the covering axiom for $\mathcal A$ implies the covering axiom for $\mathcal B$.  Now to verify that $\mathcal B$ is an implicit atlas, everything is the same as for $\mathcal A$ except for the openness and submersion axioms, which follow from the following result (identical to Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded}), whose proof is given in Appendix \ref{gluingHF}.

nodes.name: Formal regularity implies topological regularity
nodes.statement: For all $I\subseteq J\subseteq\mathcal B(\sigma,p,q)^{\geq\mathfrak s}$, we have: \begin{rlist} \item$(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I$ is an open subset. \item The map $s_{J\setminus I}:\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J\to E_{J\setminus I}$ over the locus $\psi_{IJ}^{-1}((\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s})^{\mathrm{reg}})\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_J$ is locally modeled on the projection: \begin{equation} \mathbb R^{\operatorname{vdim}\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}+\dim E_I}\times\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}}\to\mathbb R^{\dim E_{J\setminus I}} \end{equation} over the top stratum $\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$. More generally, the local model (compatible with stratifications) is given by replacing the first factor on the left by $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^n\times\mathbb R^{n'}$ stratified appropriately by $\mathcal S_{\overline{\mathcal M}}(\sigma,p,q)$. \item There exist $\pi$-invariant coherent trivializations of the local systems $\mathfrak o_{(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\leq\mathfrak s}_I)^{\mathrm{reg}}}\otimes\mathfrak o_{E_I}^\vee$ (in the sense of Definition \ref{cohordefabstract}), agreeing by restriction with those for $\mathcal A$, and coinciding with the usual orientations from Morse theory on $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{\mathrm{reg}}$. \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: For the atlas B, the regular locus is open, the Kuranishi maps are locally submersions, and coherent orientations exist agreeing with Morse orientations.

To complete the proof, we just need Lemma \ref{stabilizationlemmaforHFSS} below, which says that for any stable Floer trajectory, we can stabilize the domain using $S^1$-invariant divisors (except, of course, for any irreducible components mapping to Morse flow lines).

nodes.name: Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement_short: Fixed points of non-degenerate Hamiltonian symplectomorphisms are bounded below like critical points of Morse functions.
nodes.statement: Arnold conjectured that the minimal number of fixed points of a non-degenerate Hamiltonian symplectomorphism $M\to M$ enjoys a lower bound similar to the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on $M$ (known as the Morse number of $M$).

nodes.name: Proof of HF calculation via S^1-localization
nodes.statement: We use the setup of \S\ref{SSham}--\ref{SSequivariantFloeratlassec}. The homology groups associated to the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ and the implicit atlas $\mathcal A$ are by definition $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Now, as we observed previously, the thickened moduli spaces of $\mathcal A$ are open subsets of those of $\mathcal B$, so by Lemma \ref{homologyopenreduction}, $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ may also be defined using the implicit atlas $\mathcal B$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$. Now $\mathcal B^{S^1}\subseteq\mathcal B$ is a subatlas, so by Lemma \ref{homologysameassubatlas} it may also be used to define $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Thus let us restrict attention to the atlas $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$. Recall that by Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}, there is a partition into closed subsets: \begin{equation} \overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)=\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}\sqcup[\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}] \end{equation} Now we apply $S^1$-localization to $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}/\ast$ in the form of Theorem \ref{circlelocalizationhomology}, which applies since $S^1$ acts with finite stabilizers on $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,p,q)^{S^1}$ and our coefficient group is $\mathbb Q$. It follows that $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ may be defined using the flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ with the implicit atlas obtained from $\mathcal B^{S^1}$ by removing $\overline{\mathcal M}\setminus\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$ from every thickening. All the flow spaces of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ are cut out transversally by Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}, so by Proposition \ref{iftransversejustcountzero}, the homology groups of $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}/\ast$ can be defined by simply counting the $0$-dimensional flow spaces according to the orientations $\omega$. Now $\overline{\mathcal M}^{S^1}$ coincides with the Morse flow category diagram $\overline{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{morse}}/\ast$ of $H$ by Lemma \ref{fixedismorse} (with the same orientations by Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}), and this gives the desired isomorphism.

nodes.name: Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth function whose time $1$ Hamiltonian flow $\phi_H:M\to M$ has non-degenerate fixed points. Then $\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H\geq\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q)$ (in fact, we may replace $\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H$ with those fixed points whose associated periodic orbit is null-homotopic in $M$).
nodes.section: 10.7 Calculation of Hamiltonian Floer homology and the Arnold conjecture
assumptions: $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth function whose time $1$ Hamiltonian flow $\phi_H:M\to M$ has non-degenerate fixed points
conclusions: $\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H\geq\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q)$
nodes.statement_short: A non-degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism has at least dim H_*(M;Q) fixed points.

nodes.name: Proof of the Arnold conjecture
nodes.statement: Pick any $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure $J$ and consider the vertex $(J,H)\in J\!H_\bullet(M)$. Over this vertex, pick any complex $F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)$ which calculates $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$. Then $F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)$ is a free $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$-module of rank: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)\leq\#\operatorname{Fix}\phi_H \end{equation} (its rank equals the number of null-homotopic periodic orbits). By Theorem \ref{HFcalculation}, the homology $F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)$ is free of rank: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)=\dim H_\bullet(M;\mathbb Q) \end{equation} Now by definition, there is a $\mathbb Q[[\pi]]$-linear boundary map $d:F\mathbb C^\bullet(M)\to F\mathbb C^{\bullet+1}(M)$ and by definition $\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$. Now apply Lemma \ref{homologyhassmallerrank} to conclude that: \begin{equation} \operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb H^\bullet(M)\leq\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb Q[[\pi]]}F\mathbb C^\bullet(M) \end{equation} Thus we are done.

nodes.name: Rank of free homology is at most rank of module
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a free module over a commutative ring $R$, and let $d:M\to M$ satisfy $d^2=0$. If $H=\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$ is free, then $\operatorname{rk} H\leq\operatorname{rk} M$.

nodes.name: Proof of rank bound for homology
nodes.statement: Since $H$ is free, it is projective, so the surjection $\ker d\twoheadrightarrow H$ has a section $H\hookrightarrow\ker d\subseteq M$. Hence there is an injection $H\hookrightarrow M$. Now use Lemma \ref{freesubhassmallerrank}.
nodes.statement_short: Freeness gives projectivity, so H splits into ker d and injects into M; then apply the injection rank lemma.

nodes.name: Injection of free modules bounds rank
nodes.statement: Let $\phi:R^{\oplus A}\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus B}$ be an inclusion of free modules over a commutative ring $R$. Then $A\leq B$.
assumptions: $\phi:R^{\oplus A}\hookrightarrow R^{\oplus B}$ be an inclusion of free modules over a commutative ring $R$
conclusions: $A\leq B$

nodes.name: Proof that injections of free modules bound rank
nodes.statement: This is a standard yet tricky exercise. We recall one of the (many) standard proofs. The map $\phi$ is described by some matrix of $A\times B$ elements of $R$. Certainly the kernel of this matrix remains zero over the subring of $R$ generated by its entries. Thus we may assume without loss of generality that $R$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra. Now localize at a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ of height zero. Localization is exact, so again $\phi$ remains injective. Thus we may assume without loss of generality that $R$ is a local Noetherian ring of dimension zero, and thus $R$ is an Artin local ring \cite[p90, Theorem 8.5]{atiyahmacdonald}. Since $R$ is Artinian, all finitely generated modules have finite length \cite[pp76--77, Propositions 6.5 and 6.8]{atiyahmacdonald}, and hence there is a length homomorphism $K_0(R)\to\mathbb Z$ \cite[p77, Proposition 6.9]{atiyahmacdonald} (which is clearly an isomorphism since $R$ is local). It thus follows from the short exact sequence $0\to R^{\oplus A}\xrightarrow\phi R^{\oplus B}\to\operatorname{coker}\phi\to 0$ that $A\leq B$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a finitely generated Z-algebra, localize at a height-zero prime to get an Artin local ring, then use the length homomorphism on K_0.

nodes.name: Convention: space
nodes.statement: In this appendix, by \emph{space} we mean locally compact Hausdorff space.

nodes.name: Conventions on complexes
nodes.statement: By a \emph{complex} $C^\bullet$ we mean a $\mathbb Z$-graded object $\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}C^i$ (in some abelian category) along with a degree $1$ endomorphism $d$ with $d^2=0$. The \emph{homology} of a complex $C^\bullet$ is denoted $H^\bullet C^\bullet$ (defined by $H^iC^\bullet:=\ker(C^i\xrightarrow dC^{i+1})/\operatorname{im}(C^{i-1}\xrightarrow dC^i)$). A complex is called \emph{acyclic} iff its homology vanishes. A map of complexes $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ is a called a \emph{quasi-isomorphism} iff it induces an isomorphism on homology. We will often use the fact that a map of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism iff its mapping cone is acyclic. The \emph{shift} of a complex $C^\bullet[n]$ is defined by $(C^\bullet[n])^i:=C^{i+n}$. We use the \emph{truncation functors} defined by: \begin{equation*} (\tau_{\geq i}C^\bullet)^j:=\begin{cases}C^j&j>i\cr\operatorname{coker}(C^{i-1}\xrightarrow dC^i)&j=i\cr 0&j<i\end{cases}\qquad (\tau_{\leq i}C^\bullet)^j:=\begin{cases}0&j>i\cr\ker(C^i\xrightarrow dC^{i+1})&j=i\cr C^j&j<i\end{cases} \end{equation*} Given a sequence of maps of complexes $A_0^\bullet\to\cdots\to A_n^\bullet$ such that adjacent maps compose to zero, we denote by $[A_0^\bullet\to\cdots\to A_n^{\bullet-n}]$ the associated total complex of this double complex. For example, $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ denotes a map, and $[A^\bullet\xrightarrow fB^{\bullet-1}]$ denotes its mapping cone.
nodes.statement_short: Standard conventions: complexes, homology, acyclicity, quasi-isomorphisms, shifts, truncations, total complexes and mapping cones.
nodes.label: complexconventions

nodes.name: Sign conventions
nodes.statement: We fix sign conventions by making everything $\mathbb Z/2$-graded and always using the super tensor product $\otimes$ (namely, where the isomorphism $A\otimes B\xrightarrow\sim B\otimes A$ is given by $a\otimes b\mapsto(-1)^{\left|a\right|\left|b\right|}b\otimes a$ and where $(f\otimes g)(a\otimes b):=(-1)^{\left|g\right|\left|a\right|}f(a)\otimes g(b)$). We fix $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\otimes A\to B$ as given by $f\otimes a\mapsto f(a)$. Complexes are $(\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2)$-bigraded; differentials are always odd and chain maps are always even. Note that the $\mathbb Z/2$-grading of a complex is often, but not always, the reduction modulo $2$ of the $\mathbb Z$-grading.
nodes.statement_short: Koszul sign rule via Z/2-grading and super tensor product; differentials odd, chain maps even.
nodes.label: signconventions

nodes.name: Convention: directed limits
nodes.statement: Direct limits and inverse limits always take place over directed sets.

nodes.name: Presheaf and K-presheaf
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space. A \emph{presheaf} (resp.\ \emph{$\mathcal K$-presheaf}) on $X$ is a contravariant functor from the category of open (resp.\ compact) sets of $X$ to the category of abelian groups. A morphism of presheaves is simply a natural transformation of functors. The category of presheaves (resp.\ $\mathcal K$-presheaves) is denoted $\operatorname{Prshv} X$ (resp.\ $\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} X$).
nodes.origin_citation: standard; K-presheaf terminology Lurie HTT Def. 7.3.4.1
differentia: from the category of open (resp.\ compact) sets of $X$ to the category of abelian groups

nodes.name: Stalk
nodes.statement: For a presheaf $\mathcal F$, let $\mathcal F_p:=\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(U)$, and for a $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ let $\mathcal F_p:=\mathcal F(\{p\})$. In both cases we say $\mathcal F_p$ is the \emph{stalk} of $\mathcal F$ at $p$.

nodes.name: Sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{sheaf} is a presheaf $\mathcal F$ satisfying the following condition: \begin{equation*} \tag{Sh}0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\quad\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A} \end{equation*} The category of sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{Shv} X$ (a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Prshv} X$, meaning a morphism between sheaves is the same as a morphism of the corresponding presheaves).

nodes.name: Sheaf axiom (Sh)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh}0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\quad\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}
nodes.label: opensheafproperty

nodes.name: K-sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{$\mathcal K$-sheaf} is a $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ satisfying the following three conditions:\footnote{A similar set of axioms appears in Lurie \cite[Definition 7.3.4.1]{luriehtt}.} \begin{align*} \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$1}\mathcal F(\varnothing)&=0\\ \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$2}0\to\mathcal F(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F(K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1\cap K_2)&\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$3}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\to\mathcal F(K)&\text{ is an isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X \end{align*} The category of $\mathcal K$-sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} X$ (a full subcategory of $\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} X$).
nodes.statement_short: A K-presheaf vanishing on the empty set, satisfying Mayer-Vietoris exactness for pairs of compacts, and continuity under shrinking neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Axiom ShK1 (vanishing)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$1}\mathcal F(\varnothing)&=0
nodes.label: sheafvanishing

nodes.name: Axiom ShK2 (Mayer-Vietoris exactness)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$2}0\to\mathcal F(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F(K_2)\to\mathcal F(K_1\cap K_2)&\text{ is exact }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X
nodes.label: sheafproperty

nodes.name: Axiom ShK3 (continuity)
nodes.statement: \tag{Sh$_{\mathcal K}$3}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\to\mathcal F(K)&\text{ is an isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X
nodes.label: sheafcontinuity

nodes.name: Compact set is intersection of closures of its neighborhoods
nodes.statement: It is always the case that $K=\bigcap_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\overline U$ for compact $K\subseteq X$.
nodes.label: nbhdintersectiongood

nodes.name: Proof of sheaf/K-sheaf equivalence
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf, and let us verify $\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Axiom \eqref{sheafvanishing} is clear (take $A=\varnothing$ in \eqref{opensheafproperty}). Axiom \eqref{sheafproperty} follows from \eqref{opensheafproperty} and Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} since direct limits are exact. Axiom \eqref{sheafcontinuity} is clear from the definition also. Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf, and let us verify that $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. Let us first observe that (by induction using \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}) if $\{K_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is any collection of compact sets, all but finitely many of which are empty, then the following is exact: \begin{equation} 0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha\cap K_\beta) \end{equation} Let us now verify axiom \eqref{opensheafproperty} for $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ for open sets $\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$. Certainly \eqref{opensheafproperty} is the inverse limit of \eqref{compactfiniteexact} over all collections of compact subsets $\{K_\alpha\subseteq U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ for which $K_\alpha=\varnothing$ except for finitely many $\alpha\in A$. This is sufficient since inverse limit is left exact. Now to see that the adjoint pair $\alpha^\ast\dashv\alpha_\ast$ is actually an equivalence of categories, it suffices to show that the natural morphisms $\mathcal F\to\alpha_\ast\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ and $\alpha^\ast\alpha_\ast\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ are isomorphisms. In other words, we must show that following natural maps are isomorphisms: \begin{align} \mathcal F(U)&\to\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U'\cr U'\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U')\\ \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K'\subseteq U\cr K'\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal G(K')&\to\mathcal G(K) \end{align} The right hand side of \eqref{Funit} can be thought of as the inverse limit of $\mathcal F(U')$ over all open $U'\subseteq U$ with $\overline{U'}\subseteq U$ and $\overline{U'}$ compact. It is easy to see that the map from $\mathcal F(U)$ to this inverse limit is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. The left hand side of \eqref{Gunit} can be identified with the left hand side of \eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and thus the map to $\mathcal G(K)$ is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.statement_short: Check alpha^* preserves sheaf axioms via exactness of direct limits, alpha_* via left exactness of inverse limits, then show unit and counit are isomorphisms.

nodes.name: alpha^* of a sheaf is a K-sheaf
nodes.statement_short: Verify the K-sheaf axioms for alpha^* F.
nodes.statement: Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf, and let us verify $\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.  Axiom \eqref{sheafvanishing} is clear (take $A=\varnothing$ in \eqref{opensheafproperty}).  Axiom \eqref{sheafproperty} follows from \eqref{opensheafproperty} and Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} since direct limits are exact.  Axiom \eqref{sheafcontinuity} is clear from the definition also.

nodes.name: alpha_* of a K-sheaf is a sheaf
nodes.statement_short: Finite exactness for compacts, then inverse limit.
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf, and let us verify that $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ is a sheaf.  Let us first observe that (by induction using \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}) if $\{K_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is any collection of compact sets, all but finitely many of which are empty, then the following is exact:
\begin{equation} 0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha\cap K_\beta)
\end{equation}
Let us now verify axiom \eqref{opensheafproperty} for $\alpha_\ast\mathcal F$ for open sets $\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}$.  Certainly \eqref{opensheafproperty} is the inverse limit of \eqref{compactfiniteexact} over all collections of compact subsets $\{K_\alpha\subseteq U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ for which $K_\alpha=\varnothing$ except for finitely many $\alpha\in A$.  This is sufficient since inverse limit is left exact.

nodes.name: Finite compact Mayer-Vietoris exactness
nodes.statement: 0\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha\cap K_\beta)
nodes.label: compactfiniteexact

nodes.name: Unit and counit are isomorphisms
nodes.statement_short: Check unit and counit maps are isomorphisms.
nodes.statement:
Now to see that the adjoint pair $\alpha^\ast\dashv\alpha_\ast$ is actually an equivalence of categories, it suffices to show that the natural morphisms $\mathcal F\to\alpha_\ast\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ and $\alpha^\ast\alpha_\ast\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ are isomorphisms.  In other words, we must show that following natural maps are isomorphisms:
\begin{align} \mathcal F(U)&\to\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U'\cr U'\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U')\\ \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K'\subseteq U\cr K'\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal G(K')&\to\mathcal G(K)
\end{align}
The right hand side of \eqref{Funit} can be thought of as the inverse limit of $\mathcal F(U')$ over all open $U'\subseteq U$ with $\overline{U'}\subseteq U$ and $\overline{U'}$ compact.  It is easy to see that the map from $\mathcal F(U)$ to this inverse limit is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf.  The left hand side of \eqref{Gunit} can be identified with the left hand side of \eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and thus the map to $\mathcal G(K)$ is an isomorphism if $\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.

nodes.name: Unit map F -> alpha_* alpha^* F
nodes.statement: \mathcal F(U)&\to\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr K\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U'\cr U'\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(U')
nodes.label: Funit

nodes.name: Counit map alpha^* alpha_* G -> G
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\varprojlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K'\subseteq U\cr K'\textrm{ compact}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal G(K')&\to\mathcal G(K)
nodes.label: Gunit

nodes.name: Convention: sheaf means either
nodes.statement: In view of the canonical equivalence of categories $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} X$ from Lemma \ref{opencptshvequivalence}, we use the single word ``sheaf'' for an object of either category.

nodes.name: Continuity of K-presheaf along filtered intersections
nodes.statement: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$ (i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta\in A$ there exists $\gamma\in A$ with $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$). Then for any $\mathcal F$ satisfying \eqref{sheafcontinuity}, the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr) \end{equation}
assumptions: $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$
for any $\mathcal F$ satisfying \eqref{sheafcontinuity}
conclusions: the following is an isomorphism
nodes.label: anycompactintersectionworksSH

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)

nodes.name: Proof of continuity along filtered intersections
nodes.statement: Write $K:=\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha$. Now consider the diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}\ar{d}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}\exists\alpha\in A:K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{d}\\ \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\ar{rr}&&\mathcal F(K) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The vertical maps are both isomorphisms by \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. The first horizontal map is an isomorphism since $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is filtered. It thus remains to show that if $K\subseteq U$ and $U$ is open, then there exists $\alpha\in A$ such that $K_\alpha\subseteq U$. Since $K\subseteq U$, we have $(X\setminus U)\cap K=\varnothing$, so $\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha=\varnothing$. This is a filtered directed system of compact sets, and so the intersection being empty implies that one of the terms $(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha$ is empty, so $K_\alpha\subseteq U$ as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Compare via a diagram with neighborhood limits; vertical maps are isomorphisms by continuity, and compactness shows each neighborhood of K contains some K_alpha.

nodes.name: Comparison diagram
nodes.statement_short: Set K as the intersection and compare via a diagram.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}\ar{d}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}\exists\alpha\in A:K_\alpha\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{r}& \varinjlim\limits_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F(\overline U)\ar{d}\\ \varinjlim\limits_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F(K_\alpha)\ar{rr}&&\mathcal F(K) \end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Reduce to a neighborhood statement
nodes.statement_short: Vertical and first horizontal maps are isomorphisms; remains to find K_alpha inside U.
nodes.statement: The vertical maps are both isomorphisms by \eqref{sheafcontinuity}.  The first horizontal map is an isomorphism since $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is filtered.  It thus remains to show that if $K\subseteq U$ and $U$ is open, then there exists $\alpha\in A$ such that $K_\alpha\subseteq U$.

nodes.name: Compactness argument
nodes.statement_short: Filtered intersection of compacts empty implies one term empty.
nodes.statement: Since $K\subseteq U$, we have $(X\setminus U)\cap K=\varnothing$, so $\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha=\varnothing$.  This is a filtered directed system of compact sets, and so the intersection being empty implies that one of the terms $(X\setminus U)\cap K_\alpha$ is empty, so $K_\alpha\subseteq U$ as desired.

nodes.name: Objectwise notions for complexes of presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves. The notions from Convention \ref{complexconventions} are applied ``objectwise'', that is, to each complex $\mathcal F^\bullet(U)$ (resp.\ $F^\bullet(K)$) individually. For example, the homology $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is again a ($\mathcal K$-)presheaf, and a map of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $f:\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff it induces an isomorphism of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet\to H^i\mathcal G^\bullet$ for all $i$. The homology ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ should not be confused with the various flavors of \v Cech (hyper)cohomology $\check H^i(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ we introduce in \S\ref{cechsection}.

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{homotopy sheaf} is a complex of presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying the following condition: \begin{equation*} \tag{hSh}\hspace{-20pt}\biggl[\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\to\cdots\biggr]\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A} \end{equation*} The category of homotopy sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{hShv} X$ (morphisms are morphisms of complexes of presheaves).

nodes.name: Homotopy sheaf axiom (hSh)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh}\hspace{-20pt}\biggl[\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\Bigr)\to\prod_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(U_\alpha)\to\prod_{\alpha,\beta\in A}\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\to\cdots\biggr]\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }\{U_\alpha\subseteq X\}_{\alpha\in A}
nodes.label: openhomotopysheafproperty

nodes.name: Remark A.2.17
nodes.statement: The definition above is given for illustrative purposes only. It is probably only a good definition for $\mathcal F^\bullet$ which is bounded below, and it would perhaps be better to impose \eqref{openhomotopysheafproperty} for all \emph{hypercovers} of open subsets $U\subseteq X$.

nodes.name: Flasque sheaves and singular cochains give homotopy sheaves
nodes.statement: A sheaf $\mathcal F$ is \emph{flasque} iff all restriction maps $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U')$ are surjective. It is easy to see that any bounded below complex of flasque sheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy sheaf. For example, let $\mathcal F^\bullet(U):=C^\bullet(U)$ be the presheaf of singular cochain complexes. Then the sheafification of $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a complex of flasque sheaves, and thus is a homotopy sheaf. One can show (using barycentric subdivision) that the map from $\mathcal F^\bullet$ to its sheafification is a quasi-isomorphism, and hence $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy sheaf as well.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded below complexes of flasque sheaves, and the singular cochain presheaf, are homotopy sheaves.
nodes.label: flasquehomotopysheafresolution

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf
nodes.statement: A \emph{homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf} is a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying the following three conditions: \begin{align*} \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$1}\mathcal F^\bullet(\varnothing)&\text{ is acyclic}\\ \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$2}\hspace{-10pt}\bigl[\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K_1\cap K_2)\bigr]&\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X\\ \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$3}\smash{\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}}\mathcal F^\bullet(\overline U)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K)&\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X \end{align*} The category of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on a space $X$ is denoted $\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X$ (morphisms are morphisms of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves).
nodes.statement_short: Complex of K-presheaves: acyclic on empty set, homotopy Mayer-Vietoris for pairs of compacts, continuity up to quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.label: homotopyKsheaf

nodes.name: Axiom hShK1 (acyclic on empty set)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$1}\mathcal F^\bullet(\varnothing)&\text{ is acyclic}
nodes.label: homotopysheafacyclic

nodes.name: Axiom hShK2 (homotopy Mayer-Vietoris)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$2}\hspace{-10pt}\bigl[\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cup K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K_1\cap K_2)\bigr]&\text{ is acyclic }\forall\text{ }K_1,K_2\subseteq X
nodes.label: homotopysheafproperty

nodes.name: Axiom hShK3 (homotopy continuity)
nodes.statement: \tag{hSh$_{\mathcal K}$3}\smash{\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}K\subseteq U\cr U\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}}\mathcal F^\bullet(\overline U)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K)&\text{ is a quasi-isomorphism }\forall\text{ }K\subseteq X
nodes.label: homotopysheafcontinuity

nodes.name: Remark A.2.20
nodes.statement: Note that \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} gives rise to a ``Mayer--Vietoris'' long exact sequence in cohomology.

nodes.name: Soft K-sheaves give homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: A $\mathcal K$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ is \emph{soft} iff all restriction maps $\mathcal F(K)\to\mathcal F(K')$ are surjective. It is easy to see that any complex of soft $\mathcal K$-sheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
nodes.label: softhomotopysheafresolution

nodes.name: Expected equivalence of homotopy sheaves and homotopy K-sheaves
nodes.statement: In analogy with Definition \ref{opencptrelationfunctors}, we expect there are functors: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{R\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{hShv} X\end{tikzcd} \end{equation} where $\alpha^\ast$ is the direct limit \eqref{alphaast} and $R\alpha_\ast$ is the \emph{homotopy} (or \emph{derived}) version $R\varprojlim$ of the inverse limit \eqref{alphaupperast} (the naive inverse limit functor $\alpha_\ast$ is the ``wrong'' functor since inverse limit is not exact). In analogy with Lemma \ref{opencptshvequivalence}, it seems likely\footnote{A similar result appears in Lurie \cite[Corollary 7.3.4.10]{luriehtt}.} that there is an adjunction $\alpha^\ast\dashv R\alpha_\ast$ which is an equivalence (in the sense of model categories or $\infty$-categories), though perhaps only after restricting to the (possibly better-behaved) subcategory of homotopy ($\mathcal K$-)sheaves which are bounded below.
nodes.statement_short: Expected: alpha^* and R alpha_* give an equivalence between homotopy K-sheaves and homotopy sheaves (perhaps bounded below).
nodes.label: homotopyKnotsheavesequivalencermk

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{R\alpha_\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{\alpha^\ast}\operatorname{hShv} X\end{tikzcd}

nodes.name: Homotopy K-sheaf axioms are quasi-isomorphism invariant
nodes.statement: Properties \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} are preserved by quasi-isomorphisms.
conclusions: Properties \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} are preserved by quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.label: qihomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Proof of quasi-isomorphism invariance
nodes.statement: For \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} this is trivial. For \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, suppose $\mathcal F^\bullet\xrightarrow\sim\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Now the sequence \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} applied to the mapping cone $[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}]$ is certainly acyclic (since it has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic). Thus \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} holds for $\mathcal F^\bullet$ iff it holds for $\mathcal G^\bullet$.
nodes.statement_short: Two axioms are immediate; for Mayer-Vietoris, apply it to the mapping cone, acyclic by a finite filtration.

nodes.name: Axioms 1 and 3
nodes.statement_short: Trivial for acyclicity and continuity.
nodes.statement: For \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} this is trivial.

nodes.name: Axiom 2 via mapping cone
nodes.statement_short: Apply the sequence to the mapping cone.
nodes.statement: For \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, suppose $\mathcal F^\bullet\xrightarrow\sim\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.  Now the sequence \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} applied to the mapping cone $[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}]$ is certainly acyclic (since it has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic).  Thus \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} holds for $\mathcal F^\bullet$ iff it holds for $\mathcal G^\bullet$.

nodes.name: Extensions of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves are homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves. If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf, then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.label: associatedgradedhomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Proof via filtrations of acyclic complexes
nodes.statement: This follows from the fact that if a complex $C^\bullet$ has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic then $C^\bullet$ is itself acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: A complex with finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic is acyclic.

nodes.name: Lowest nonzero homology $\mathcal K$-presheaf of a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and $H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$, then $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
$H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$
conclusions: $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.label: lowervanishingimpliessheaf

nodes.name: Proof that lowest homology is a K-sheaf
nodes.statement: Properties \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafcontinuity} follow directly from \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}. To show \eqref{sheafproperty} for $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$, use the long exact sequence induced by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} and the vanishing of $H^{-1}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_1\cap K_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing and continuity are inherited directly; exactness follows from the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence and vanishing of H^{-1}.

nodes.name: Homotopy continuity along filtered intersections
nodes.statement: Let $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$ (i.e.\ for all $\alpha,\beta\in A$ there exists $\gamma\in A$ with $K_\gamma\subseteq K_\alpha\cap K_\beta$). Then for any $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, the following is a quasi-isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr) \end{equation}
assumptions: $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be a filtered directed system of compact subsets of $X$
for any $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfying \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}
conclusions: the following is a quasi-isomorphism
nodes.label: anycompactintersectionworks

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}\mathcal F^\bullet(K_\alpha)\to\mathcal F^\bullet\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha\Bigr)

nodes.name: Proof of homotopy continuity
nodes.statement: Same as for Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworksSH}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as for K-sheaves.

nodes.name: Pushforward of ($\mathcal K$-)presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. We define functors: \begin{rlist} \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Prshv} X\to\operatorname{Prshv} Y$ by $(f_\ast\mathcal F)(U):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(U))$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} X\to\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} Y$ by $(f_\ast\mathcal F)(K):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(K))$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist} (the action of $f_\ast$ on morphism spaces is obvious).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.label: presheafpushforward

nodes.name: Preimages of neighborhoods are cofinal under proper maps
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper. Then $\{f^{-1}(U)\}_{K\subseteq U}$ is a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $f^{-1}(K)$ for any compact $K\subseteq X$.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
assumptions: $f:X\to Y$ be proper
conclusions: $\{f^{-1}(U)\}_{K\subseteq U}$ is a cofinal system of neighborhoods of $f^{-1}(K)$ for any compact $K\subseteq X$
nodes.label: properpullbackfinalneighborhood

nodes.name: Proof of cofinality under proper maps
nodes.statement: Exercise (use the fact that a compact Hausdorff space is normal).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.statement_short: Exercise using normality of compact Hausdorff spaces.

nodes.name: Pushforward preserves sheaf axioms
nodes.statement: $f_\ast$ preserves \eqref{opensheafproperty}, \eqref{openhomotopysheafproperty}, \eqref{sheafvanishing}--\eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
conclusions: $f_\ast$ preserves \eqref{opensheafproperty}, \eqref{openhomotopysheafproperty}, \eqref{sheafvanishing}--\eqref{sheafcontinuity}, and \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}--\eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}
nodes.label: pushforwardandsheafproperties

nodes.name: Proof that pushforward preserves axioms
nodes.statement: These are trivial except for \eqref{sheafcontinuity} and \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, which use Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.statement_short: Trivial except continuity, which uses cofinality of preimages under proper maps.

nodes.name: Pushforward of ($\mathcal K$-)sheaves and homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. By Lemma \ref{pushforwardandsheafproperties}, Definition \ref{presheafpushforward} gives rise to functors: \begin{rlist} \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Shv} X\to\operatorname{Shv} Y$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{hShv} X\to\operatorname{hShv} Y$. \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} X\to\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} Y$ (if $f$ is proper). \item$f_\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X\to\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} Y$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist} (the action on morphism spaces is induced from the $f_\ast$ at the level of (complexes of) \mbox{($\mathcal K$-)presheaves}). It is easy to see that $f_\ast$ commutes with the equivalence $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} X$ (if $f$ is proper).
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback
nodes.definiendum: pushforward $f_\ast$ of sheaves and homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.label: pushforwardofHsheavesworks

nodes.name: Pullback and exceptional pushforward of sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. We define: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\operatorname{Shv} Y\to\operatorname{Shv} X$ the standard sheaf pullback (namely $f^\ast\mathcal F$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal F(V)$). \item$f_!:\operatorname{Shv} X\to\operatorname{Shv} Y$ by $(f_!\mathcal F)(U)\subseteq(f_\ast\mathcal F)(U)$ being the subspace of sections which vanish in a neighborhood of $Y\setminus X$ (if $f$ is the inclusion of an open set). \end{rlist}
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback

nodes.name: Pullback of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an injective map of spaces. We define: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} Y\to\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X$ by $(f^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)(K):=\mathcal F^\bullet(f(K))$. \end{rlist} We check the properties: \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} is clear, and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} follows since $f$ is injective. For \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity}, use Remark \ref{nbhdintersectiongood}, the injectivity of $f$, and Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworks}.
nodes.section: A.3 Pushforward, exceptional pushforward, and pullback

nodes.name: Refinement of a cover
nodes.statement: A \emph{refinement} of a cover $\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is a cover $\{U_\beta\}_{\beta\in B}$ along with a map $f:B\to A$ such that $U_\beta\subseteq U_{f(\alpha)}$. Refinements are the morphisms used in the directed systems used to define (all flavors of) \v Cech cohomology. Different refinements $\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}\to\{U_\beta\}_{\beta\in B}$ induce different maps on \v Cech complexes, but they all agree after passing to cohomology (more precisely, the ``space'' of such refinements is contractible or empty). In particular, it follows that the directed systems used in defining \v Cech cohomology are \emph{filtered}.
differentia: along with a map $f:B\to A$ such that $U_\beta\subseteq U_{f(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement_short: Refinements are the morphisms of the (filtered) directed systems defining Cech cohomology; induced maps agree on cohomology.
nodes.label: coveringscategoryrmk

nodes.name: Cech cohomology of the empty space vanishes
nodes.statement: The empty covering is a final object in the category of coverings of $\varnothing$, so we always have $\check H^\bullet(\varnothing;-)=0$.

nodes.name: Cech cohomology of sheaves (with supports, compact supports)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a space $X$. We define the \v Cech cohomology: \begin{equation} \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq A\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in S}U_\alpha\Bigr)[-p]\biggr] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential.\footnote{Technically speaking, so that the signs in the differential can be defined canonically, we should really tensor each term of the direct product with $(\mathbb Zo_1\oplus\mathbb Zo_2)/(o_1+o_2)\cong\mathbb Z$ where $o_1,o_2$ denote the two orientations of the $p$-simplex on vertex set $S$.} For any compact $K\subseteq X$, define $\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cohomology with supports in $K$) via \eqref{cechcomplexI} except replacing every instance of $\mathcal F(U)$ with $\ker[\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U\setminus K)]$. We let $\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cohomology with compact supports).
nodes.statement_short: Cech cohomology as a direct limit over open covers, with supports in K and compact supports.
nodes.label: cechdefnI

nodes.name: Cech complex for open covers
nodes.statement: \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq A\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{\alpha\in S}U_\alpha\Bigr)[-p]\biggr]
nodes.label: cechcomplexI

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ on a compact space needs only finite open covers
nodes.statement: If $X$ is compact, then the natural map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{fin}(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, where the left hand side is defined as in \eqref{cechcomplexI} except using only finite open covers.
assumptions: $X$ is compact
conclusions: the natural map $\check H^\bullet_\mathrm{fin}(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism

nodes.name: Proof: finite covers cofinal
nodes.statement: Since $X$ is compact, it follows that finite open covers are cofinal (every open cover has a finite refinement).
nodes.statement_short: Finite open covers are cofinal on a compact space.

nodes.name: $\check H_c^\bullet=\check H^\bullet$ on compact space
nodes.statement: If $X$ is compact, then the natural map $\check H_c^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: $X$ is compact
conclusions: the natural map $\check H_c^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism

nodes.name: Proof that compact supports agree on compact space
nodes.statement: Trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial.

nodes.name: Pullback on $\check H^\bullet$ and $\check H^\bullet_c$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. An open cover of $Y$ pulls back to give an open cover of $X$, and this gives an identification of the \v Cech complex for the cover of $Y$ with coefficients in $f_\ast\mathcal F$ with the \v Cech complex for the cover of $X$ with coefficients in $\mathcal F$. Hence we get natural maps: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$. \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$ (if $f$ is proper). \end{rlist}
nodes.label: pullbackdefn

nodes.name: $\check H_c^\bullet$ commutes with $f_!$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the inclusion of an open subset. Then there is a natural isomorphism $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$.
assumptions: $f:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the inclusion of an open subset
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: cptcechembeddingproperty

nodes.name: Proof that compactly supported Cech cohomology commutes with f_!
nodes.statement: For $K\subseteq X$, there are natural maps: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} \check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{f^\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{f_!}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} (for $f^\ast$: pull back the open cover) (for $f_!$: add $Y\setminus K$ to the open cover and extend by zero). It is easy to see that $f_!$ and $f^\ast$ are inverses. The desired map $f_!:\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_!\mathcal F)$ is defined as the composition: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)\overset{\eqref{trivialKequivalence}}=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\varinjlim_{K\subseteq Y}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F) \end{equation} We must show that the second map is an isomorphism; to see this, it suffices to show that the following is an isomorphism for all $K\subseteq Y$: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{K'\subseteq X\cap K}\check H^\bullet_{K'}(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F) \end{equation} We claim that for any \v Cech cochain $\beta$ for $f_!\mathcal F$ with supports in $K$ subordinate to an open cover of $Y$, there is a refinement on which the restriction of $\beta$ has supports in some $K'\subseteq X\cap K$. It follows from the claim (using a cofinality argument) that \eqref{supportcompactinXorY} is an isomorphism. To prove the claim, argue as follows. First, choose a refinement for which only finitely many open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ intersect $K$ and for which the remaining open sets cover $Y\setminus K$. Pick open sets $V_i\subseteq U_i$ which cover $K$ and for which $\overline{V_i}$ is compact and $\overline{V_i}\subseteq U_i$ (this is always possible). Now $\beta$ is a finite collection $\{\beta_I\in(f_!\mathcal F)(\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i)\}_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}$. We have: \begin{equation} \operatorname{supp}\Bigl(\beta_I|\bigcap_{i\in I}V_i\Bigr)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i} \end{equation} Since $\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ is (relatively) closed and $\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i}\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ is compact, it follows that the right hand side is compact. Also, we have $\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\subseteq X$ (by definition of $f_!\mathcal F$). Hence the right hand side of \eqref{restrictionsupport} is a compact subset of $X$. It follows that the restriction of $\beta$ to the refinement obtained by replacing $U_i$ with $V_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ has support in a compact subset of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify supports-in-K cohomology of X and Y, then show by refining covers that cochains supported in K are supported in a compact subset of X. The key step shrinks the finitely many cover sets meeting K to relatively compact ones.

nodes.name: Supports-in-K maps f^* and f_!
nodes.statement_short: Define inverse maps on cohomology with supports in K.

nodes.name: Supports-in-K identification f^*, f_!
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd} \check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{f^\ast}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{f_!}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F) \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: trivialKequivalence

nodes.name: Define the desired map
nodes.statement_short: Define f_! as a composition of direct limits.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)\overset{\eqref{trivialKequivalence}}=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\varinjlim_{K\subseteq Y}\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)

nodes.name: Reduce to supports compact in X or Y
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to show the comparison map for each compact K is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Compact supports in X versus Y
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{K'\subseteq X\cap K}\check H^\bullet_{K'}(Y;f_!\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_K(Y;f_!\mathcal F)
nodes.label: supportcompactinXorY

nodes.name: Claim: refinement with supports in X
nodes.statement_short: Claim: cochains admit refinements with support compact in X; this gives the isomorphism.
