It follows from the claim (using a cofinality argument) that \eqref{supportcompactinXorY} is an isomorphism.  To prove the claim, argue as follows.

nodes.name: Claim implies isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: Cofinality yields the isomorphism from the claim.
nodes.statement: It follows from the claim (using a cofinality argument) that \eqref{supportcompactinXorY} is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Announce proof of claim
nodes.statement_short: Meta: start proof of claim.
nodes.statement: To prove the claim, argue as follows.

nodes.name: Choose refinement and shrinkings
nodes.statement_short: Choose a refinement with finitely many sets meeting K and shrinkings V_i.
nodes.statement: First, choose a refinement for which only finitely many open sets $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ intersect $K$ and for which the remaining open sets cover $Y\setminus K$.  Pick open sets $V_i\subseteq U_i$ which cover $K$ and for which $\overline{V_i}$ is compact and $\overline{V_i}\subseteq U_i$ (this is always possible).

nodes.name: Supports become compact in X
nodes.statement_short: Restricted cochains have support in a compact subset of X.

nodes.name: Support of restricted cochain
nodes.statement: \operatorname{supp}\Bigl(\beta_I|\bigcap_{i\in I}V_i\Bigr)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\beta_I\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\overline{V_i}
nodes.label: restrictionsupport

nodes.name: $f^\ast$ is an isomorphism if $f$ has finite fibers
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper with finite fibers. Then $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism, as is $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$.
assumptions: $f:X\to Y$ be proper with finite fibers
conclusions: $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism
as is $f^\ast:\check H^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: finitemap

nodes.name: Proof via partitions of covers
nodes.statement: Given an open cover containing $U=U_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup U_n$ (finite disjoint union), we get a refinement by replacing $U$ with $\{U_1,\ldots,U_n\}$. A \emph{partition} of an open cover is a refinement obtained by doing such a replacement on some (possibly infinitely many) open sets of the cover. Note that a partition induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cochains since $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf. We claim that partitions of pullbacks of open covers of $Y$ form a cofinal system of open covers of $X$. This is clear using Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood} and the fact that $f$ has finite fibers. It follows from this cofinality that $f^\ast$ is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Partitions of covers induce isomorphisms on Cech cochains; partitions of pulled-back covers are cofinal by properness and finite fibers.

nodes.name: Partitions of covers
nodes.statement_short: Define partitions; they induce isomorphisms on Cech cochains.
nodes.statement: Given an open cover containing $U=U_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup U_n$ (finite disjoint union), we get a refinement by replacing $U$ with $\{U_1,\ldots,U_n\}$.  A \emph{partition} of an open cover is a refinement obtained by doing such a replacement on some (possibly infinitely many) open sets of the cover.  Note that a partition induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cochains since $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf.

nodes.name: Claim: partitions of pullbacks are cofinal
nodes.statement_short: Partitions of pulled-back covers are cofinal; hence f^* is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement: We claim that partitions of pullbacks of open covers of $Y$ form a cofinal system of open covers of $X$.  This is clear using Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood} and the fact that $f$ has finite fibers.  It follows from this cofinality that $f^\ast$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Cofinality via proper map lemma
nodes.statement_short: Use the proper-map cofinality lemma and finite fibers.
nodes.statement: This is clear using Lemma \ref{properpullbackfinalneighborhood} and the fact that $f$ has finite fibers.

nodes.name: Conclude isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: Cofinality gives the isomorphism.
nodes.statement: It follows from this cofinality that $f^\ast$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ and $\check H^\bullet_c$ commute with finite quotients
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a space and let $\pi:X\to X/\Gamma$ be the quotient map under a finite group action. Let $\mathcal F$ be any sheaf of $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules on $X/\Gamma$. Then the following maps are all isomorphisms: \begin{align*} \check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma)\to\check H^\bullet(X/\Gamma;\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\to\check H^\bullet(X;\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\\ \check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma)\to\check H^\bullet_c(X/\Gamma;\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma\to\check H^\bullet_c(X;\pi^\ast\mathcal F)^\Gamma \end{align*} (here we note that by functoriality, $\pi^\ast\mathcal F$ is $\Gamma$-equivariant, and thus $\Gamma$ acts on $\pi_\ast\pi^\ast\mathcal F$).
assumptions: $\pi:X\to X/\Gamma$ be the quotient map under a finite group action
$\mathcal F$ be any sheaf of $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules on $X/\Gamma$
conclusions: the following maps are all isomorphisms
nodes.label: cechcohomologyfinitequotient

nodes.name: Proof of commutation with finite quotients
nodes.statement: Isomorphism one: the natural map $\mathcal F\to(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast)^\Gamma$ is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves (check on stalks). Isomorphism two: obvious since taking $\Gamma$-invariants is exact on $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules. Isomorphism three: use Lemma \ref{finitemap}, which applies since $\pi$ is automatically proper.
nodes.statement_short: Check the three maps one at a time: isomorphism on stalks, exactness of invariants with |Γ| inverted, and the finite-fiber lemma.

nodes.name: Isomorphisms one and two
nodes.statement_short: Stalk check and exactness of invariants.
nodes.statement: Isomorphism one: the natural map $\mathcal F\to(\pi_\ast\pi^\ast)^\Gamma$ is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves (check on stalks).  Isomorphism two: obvious since taking $\Gamma$-invariants is exact on $\mathbb Z[\frac 1{\#\Gamma}]$-modules.

nodes.name: Isomorphism three
nodes.statement_short: Finite-fiber lemma for the proper quotient map.
nodes.statement: Isomorphism three: use Lemma \ref{finitemap}, which applies since $\pi$ is automatically proper.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on a compact space $X$. We define: \begin{equation} \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i\cr\text{finite compact cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{j=0}^pK_{i_j}\Bigr)\biggr] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential (plus the internal differential of $\mathcal F^\bullet$). We also define $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for any $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ by viewing it as a complex concentrated in degree zero.
nodes.statement_short: Cech hypercohomology of a complex of K-presheaves on a compact space via finite compact covers.
nodes.label: cechdefnII

nodes.name: Cech complex for finite compact covers
nodes.statement: \check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i\cr\text{finite compact cover}\end{smallmatrix}}H^\bullet\biggl[\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{j=0}^pK_{i_j}\Bigr)\biggr]
nodes.label: cechcomplexII

nodes.name: Two definitions of $\check H^\bullet$ on $\operatorname{Shv} X=\operatorname{Shv}_{\mathcal K} X$ agree
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a compact space $X$. Then there is a natural isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$ ($\alpha^\ast\mathcal F$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf; c.f.\ Definition \ref{opencptrelationfunctors}).
assumptions: $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on a compact space $X$
conclusions: there is a natural isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$
nodes.label: cHsameforopencompactcovers

nodes.name: Proof that open and compact Cech cohomology agree
nodes.statement: Let us denote by $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})$ (resp.\ $\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)$) the argument of the direct limit \eqref{cechcomplexI} (resp.\ \eqref{cechcomplexII}). Since $X$ is compact, every open cover has a finite compact refinement. This gives a map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F)$. To show that this map is an isomorphism, it suffices to show that for any fixed finite compact cover $\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n$, the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover refined by }\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n\end{smallmatrix}}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n) \end{equation} By a cofinality argument, we can change the directed system on the left side to be open covers $\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n$ with $U_i\supseteq K_i$. Hence it suffices to show that the following is an isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\{U_i\supseteq K_i\}_{i=1}^n}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n) \end{equation} This is clear from the definition of $\alpha^\ast$ and from Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal}.
nodes.statement_short: Map via finite compact refinements; by cofinality reduce to open covers U_i containing K_i, then use the definition of alpha^* and cofinality of intersections.

nodes.name: Notation for fixed covers
nodes.statement_short: Name the cohomology for a fixed cover.
nodes.statement: Let us denote by $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})$ (resp.\ $\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)$) the argument of the direct limit \eqref{cechcomplexI} (resp.\ \eqref{cechcomplexII}).

nodes.name: Reduce to a fixed compact cover
nodes.statement_short: Finite compact refinements give the map; reduce to a fixed cover.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigcup_{\alpha\in A}U_\alpha\cr\text{open cover refined by }\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n\end{smallmatrix}}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A})\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)

nodes.name: Cofinality reduction
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to open covers U_i containing K_i.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_{\{U_i\supseteq K_i\}_{i=1}^n}\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F;\{U_i\}_{i=1}^n)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\alpha^\ast\mathcal F;\{K_i\}_{i=1}^n)

nodes.name: Conclude from definition of alpha^*
nodes.statement_short: Use the definition of alpha^* and cofinal intersections.
nodes.statement: This is clear from the definition of $\alpha^\ast$ and from Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal}.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves, then the induced map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X,\mathcal G^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
conclusions: the induced map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X,\mathcal G^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism
nodes.label: qicech

nodes.name: Proof that Cech cohomology preserves quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: There is clearly a long exact sequence: \begin{equation} \cdots\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}])\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\cdots \end{equation} Hence it suffices to show that if $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is acyclic then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$. This is true because then each \v Cech complex has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: Mapping cone long exact sequence reduces to acyclic complexes, whose Cech complexes have acyclic finite filtrations.

nodes.name: Mapping cone long exact sequence
nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence for the mapping cone.

nodes.name: Mapping cone long exact sequence on Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: \cdots\to\check H^{\bullet-1}(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}])\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)\to\cdots
nodes.label: cechmappingconeles

nodes.name: Acyclic complexes have vanishing Cech cohomology
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to acyclic F; finite filtration argument.
nodes.statement: Hence it suffices to show that if $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is acyclic then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$.  This is true because then each \v Cech complex has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic.

nodes.name: Hypercohomology spectral sequence
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves. Then there is a convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=\check H^q(X;\mathcal F^p)\Rightarrow\check H^{p+q}(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a bounded below complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
conclusions: there is a convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=\check H^q(X;\mathcal F^p)\Rightarrow\check H^{p+q}(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$
nodes.label: hypercohomologyss

nodes.name: Proof of hypercohomology spectral sequence
nodes.statement: This is just the spectral sequence of the \v Cech double complex.
nodes.statement_short: Spectral sequence of the Cech double complex.

nodes.name: A homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^\bullet$
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfies \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, then the canonical map $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfies \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic} and \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}
conclusions: the canonical map $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism
nodes.label: homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism

nodes.name: Proof that homotopy K-sheaves compute their own Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: We prove that $\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,\ldots,K_n)$ (the right hand side denotes \v Cech complex for the finite compact cover $X=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_n$) is a quasi-isomorphism by induction on $n$. The base case $n=1$ is obvious since $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;X)=\mathcal F^\bullet(X)$ by definition. For the inductive step, it suffices to show that the natural map $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1\cup K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. We will show that the mapping cone is acyclic; to see this, let us filter it according to how many of the $K_3,\ldots,K_n$ are chosen among $i_0,\ldots,i_p$. This is a finite filtration, so it suffices to show that the associated graded is acyclic. The associated graded is a direct sum of complexes of the form $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K)]$ (which is obviously acyclic) and $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap(K_1\cup K_2))\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K\cap K_1\cap K_2)]$ (which is acyclic by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}). The above argument works when $X\ne\varnothing$; if $X=\varnothing$, use \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of sets in a finite compact cover. The inductive step filters the mapping cone of merging K_1 and K_2 and uses the homotopy Mayer-Vietoris axiom.

nodes.name: Induction on number of compact sets
nodes.statement_short: Prove the comparison map to Cech complexes is a quasi-isomorphism by induction on n.
nodes.statement: We prove that $\mathcal F^\bullet(X)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,\ldots,K_n)$ (the right hand side denotes \v Cech complex for the finite compact cover $X=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_n$) is a quasi-isomorphism by induction on $n$.  The base case $n=1$ is obvious since $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;X)=\mathcal F^\bullet(X)$ by definition.  For the inductive step, it suffices to show that the natural map $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1\cup K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.  We will show that the mapping cone is acyclic; to see this, let us filter it according to how many of the $K_3,\ldots,K_n$ are chosen among $i_0,\ldots,i_p$.  This is a finite filtration, so it suffices to show that the associated graded is acyclic.  The associated graded is a direct sum of complexes of the form $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K)]$ (which is obviously acyclic) and $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap(K_1\cup K_2))\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K\cap K_1\cap K_2)]$ (which is acyclic by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}).

nodes.name: Base case n=1
nodes.statement_short: Base case holds by definition.
nodes.statement: The base case $n=1$ is obvious since $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;X)=\mathcal F^\bullet(X)$ by definition.

nodes.name: Inductive step: filter the mapping cone
nodes.statement_short: Merge K_1 and K_2; filter the mapping cone finitely.
nodes.statement: For the inductive step, it suffices to show that the natural map $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1\cup K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet;K_1,K_2,K_3,\ldots,K_n)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.  We will show that the mapping cone is acyclic; to see this, let us filter it according to how many of the $K_3,\ldots,K_n$ are chosen among $i_0,\ldots,i_p$.  This is a finite filtration, so it suffices to show that the associated graded is acyclic.

nodes.name: Associated graded acyclic
nodes.statement_short: Graded pieces are acyclic by the homotopy Mayer-Vietoris axiom.
nodes.statement: The associated graded is a direct sum of complexes of the form $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K)]$ (which is obviously acyclic) and $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap(K_1\cup K_2))\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_1)\oplus\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap K_2)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-2}(K\cap K_1\cap K_2)]$ (which is acyclic by \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}).

nodes.name: Empty space case
nodes.statement_short: Handle X empty by the acyclicity axiom.
nodes.statement: The above argument works when $X\ne\varnothing$; if $X=\varnothing$, use \eqref{homotopysheafacyclic}.

nodes.name: A $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^0$
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F$ satisfies \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}, then the canonical map $\mathcal F(X)\to\check H^0(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism.
assumptions: $\mathcal F$ satisfies \eqref{sheafvanishing} and \eqref{sheafproperty}
conclusions: the canonical map $\mathcal F(X)\to\check H^0(X;\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism
nodes.label: sheafcechHzero

nodes.name: Proof for K-sheaves H^0
nodes.statement: Use induction as in the proof of Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction as in the homotopy K-sheaf case.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks I
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. If the stalks of $\mathcal F$ vanish, then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=0$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}
the stalks of $\mathcal F$ vanish
conclusions: $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=0$
nodes.label: localvanishingcechzero

nodes.name: Proof of vanishing from vanishing stalks
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all $\alpha\in\mathcal F(K)$, there exists a finite compact cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i$ such that $\mathcal F(K)\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal F(K\cap K_i)$ annihilates $\alpha$. We consider the commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq U}\mathcal F(\overline U)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(\overline U)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \mathcal F(K)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\mathcal F_p \end{CD} \end{equation} where the vertical maps are both isomorphisms. Now the vanishing of $\mathcal F_p$ and a compactness argument shows that there are finitely many open sets $U_i\subseteq X$ covering $K$ such that $\alpha$ vanishes in $\mathcal F(K\cap\overline{U_i})$ for all $i$. Thus the compact cover $X=(X\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^nU_i)\cup\overline{U_1}\cup\cdots\cup\overline{U_n}$ has the desired properties.
nodes.statement_short: Each section is killed on a finite compact cover, found by a compactness argument from vanishing stalks and continuity.

nodes.name: Reduce to killing sections on a cover
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to annihilate each section on a finite compact cover.
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for all $\alpha\in\mathcal F(K)$, there exists a finite compact cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nK_i$ such that $\mathcal F(K)\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal F(K\cap K_i)$ annihilates $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Diagram comparing with stalks
nodes.statement_short: Commutative diagram with isomorphic vertical maps.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \varinjlim_{K\subseteq U}\mathcal F(\overline U)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\varinjlim_{p\in U}\mathcal F(\overline U)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \mathcal F(K)@>>>\prod_{p\in K}\mathcal F_p \end{CD}

nodes.name: Compactness gives the cover
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing stalks and compactness give the cover.
nodes.statement: Now the vanishing of $\mathcal F_p$ and a compactness argument shows that there are finitely many open sets $U_i\subseteq X$ covering $K$ such that $\alpha$ vanishes in $\mathcal F(K\cap\overline{U_i})$ for all $i$.  Thus the compact cover $X=(X\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^nU_i)\cup\overline{U_1}\cup\cdots\cup\overline{U_n}$ has the desired properties.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks II
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. If $\mathcal F^\bullet$ has acyclic stalks, then $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ has acyclic stalks
conclusions: $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$
nodes.label: cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex

nodes.name: Proof of vanishing for complexes with acyclic stalks
nodes.statement: We show that for all $i$, the map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism (this is sufficient since $\check H^j(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$ for $j<i$). We proceed by induction on $i$. Since $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$, we have that $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for $i<<0$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}). Thus we have the base case of the induction. For the inductive step, it suffices to show that $\check H^\bullet(X;H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$. This follows from Lemma \ref{localvanishingcechzero}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on truncation degree i: base case by quasi-isomorphism invariance, inductive step by the vanishing lemma for sheaves with zero stalks.

nodes.name: Reduce to truncations; induction on i
nodes.statement_short: Show the map to truncations is an isomorphism by induction on i.
nodes.statement: We show that for all $i$, the map $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism (this is sufficient since $\check H^j(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$ for $j<i$).  We proceed by induction on $i$.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement_short: For i very negative the truncation map is a quasi-isomorphism.
nodes.statement: Since $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$, we have that $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\tau_{\geq i}\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for $i<<0$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}).  Thus we have the base case of the induction.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing for H^{i-1} by the stalk lemma.
nodes.statement: For the inductive step, it suffices to show that $\check H^\bullet(X;H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet)=0$.  This follows from Lemma \ref{localvanishingcechzero}.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ is determined by stalks III
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet,\mathcal G^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. If $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on stalks, then it induces an isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet,\mathcal G^\bullet$ satisfy \eqref{homotopysheafcontinuity} and $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$
$\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on stalks
conclusions: it induces an isomorphism $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal G^\bullet)$
nodes.label: cechdeterminedbystalks

nodes.name: Proof via mapping cone
nodes.statement: Recall the long exact sequence \eqref{cechmappingconeles} and apply Lemma \ref{cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex} to the mapping cone $[\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^{\bullet-1}]$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the acyclic-stalks vanishing lemma to the mapping cone and use the long exact sequence.

nodes.name: A map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves being a quasi-isomorphism can be checked on stalks
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ be a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves which satisfy $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. Then $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p\in X$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ be a map of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves which satisfy $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=H^i\mathcal G^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$
conclusions: $\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism iff $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p\in X$
equivalent_conditions: $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism for all $p\in X$
nodes.label: homotopysheafcheckqionstalks

nodes.name: Proof that quasi-isomorphism is checked on stalks
nodes.statement: For any $K\subseteq X$, we have a commutative diagram: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal F^\bullet)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr H^\bullet\mathcal G^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal G^\bullet) \end{CD} \end{equation} The rows are isomorphisms by Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}. If $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then the right vertical map is a quasi-isomorphism by Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare sections with Cech cohomology on each compact K; Cech cohomology is determined by stalks.

nodes.name: Rows are isomorphisms
nodes.statement_short: Sections compute Cech cohomology for homotopy K-sheaves.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal F^\bullet)\cr @VVV@VVV\cr H^\bullet\mathcal G^\bullet(K)@>\sim>>\check H^\bullet(K;\mathcal G^\bullet) \end{CD}

nodes.name: Right map is an isomorphism
nodes.statement_short: Cech cohomology determined by stalks.
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal F^\bullet_p\to\mathcal G^\bullet_p$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then the right vertical map is a quasi-isomorphism by Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence for $\check H^\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}. If $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to 0$ is exact on stalks, then it induces a long exact sequence on $\check H^\bullet$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F,\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ satisfy \eqref{sheafcontinuity}
$0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal H\to 0$ is exact on stalks
conclusions: it induces a long exact sequence on $\check H^\bullet$
nodes.label: cechles

nodes.name: Proof of long exact sequence
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{cechlocalglobalvanishingcomplex}, we have $\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F\to\mathcal G[-1]\to\mathcal H[-2]])=0$. Now inspection of the hypercohomology spectral sequence (Lemma \ref{hypercohomologyss}) gives the desired long exact sequence.
nodes.statement_short: The total complex has vanishing Cech cohomology by the stalk lemma; read off the long exact sequence from the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Pullback on $\check H^\bullet$
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of compact spaces. A finite compact cover of $Y$ pulls back to give a finite compact cover of $X$, and this gives an identification of the \v Cech complex for the cover of $Y$ with coefficients in $f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ with the \v Cech complex for the cover of $X$ with coefficients in $\mathcal F^\bullet$. Hence we get a natural map: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check H^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ for $\mathcal F^i\in\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} X$. \end{rlist}
nodes.definiendum: pullback $f^\ast$ on $\check H^\bullet$ of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
nodes.label: pullbackcHKprshv

nodes.name: Pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.statement: We say that a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X$ is \emph{pure} iff: \begin{rlist} \item(Stalk cohomology) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0$ for $i\ne 0$ and all $p\in X$. \item(Weak vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$ locally on $X$ (meaning that for all $p\in X$, there exists an open set $U\subseteq X$ containing $p$ and an integer $N>-\infty$ such that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K)=0$ for all $K\subseteq U$ and $i\leq N$). \end{rlist}
nodes.statement_short: A homotopy K-sheaf is pure if its stalk cohomology is concentrated in degree 0 and its cohomology vanishes in very negative degrees locally.
nodes.label: purehomotopyKsheaf

nodes.name: Does stalk cohomology vanishing imply weak vanishing?
nodes.statement: It would be nice to know whether the stalk cohomology condition implies the weak vanishing condition in general (it would be much easier to check purity).

nodes.name: Strong vanishing and $H^0$ of a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then: \begin{rlist} \item(Strong vanishing) $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<0$. \item$H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. \end{rlist}
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<0$
$H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.label: cechsimplebasic

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.5.57
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, strong vanishing implies that $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Now let us prove strong vanishing. By restricting to a compact subset, it suffices to treat the case when the underlying space is compact. Now from \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, compactness, and weak vanishing, it follows that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$. Now let us prove strong vanishing by induction on $i<0$ (we have just proven the base case). For the inductive step, observe that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a sheaf by the induction hypothesis ($H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$) and Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, and thus $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0\implies H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii) follows from Lemma lowervanishingimpliessheaf once strong vanishing holds; strong vanishing is proved on compact sets by induction on $i<0$.

nodes.name: Strong vanishing gives sheaf property
nodes.statement_short: Strong vanishing implies $H^0$ is a K-sheaf by Lemma lowervanishingimpliessheaf.
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, strong vanishing implies that $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a $\mathcal K$-sheaf.

nodes.name: Reduce to compact space
nodes.statement_short: Reduce strong vanishing to the compact case.
nodes.statement: Now let us prove strong vanishing.  By restricting to a compact subset, it suffices to treat the case when the underlying space is compact.

nodes.name: Base case: vanishing for very negative degrees
nodes.statement_short: Compactness plus weak vanishing give vanishing for $i<<0$ (base case).
nodes.statement: Now from \eqref{homotopysheafproperty}, compactness, and weak vanishing, it follows that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$ for $i<<0$.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement_short: Induct on $i<0$: $H^i$ is a sheaf with zero stalks, hence zero.
nodes.statement: Now let us prove strong vanishing by induction on $i<0$ (we have just proven the base case).  For the inductive step, observe that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a sheaf by the induction hypothesis ($H^{i-1}\mathcal F^\bullet=0$) and Lemma \ref{lowervanishingimpliessheaf}, and thus $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_p=0\implies H^i\mathcal F^\bullet=0$.

nodes.name: $\check H^\bullet$ of a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet) \end{equation} More generally, let $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}_1\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves where each $\mathcal F^\bullet_i$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]]) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The hypercohomology of a pure homotopy K-sheaf (or a finite complex of them) is the Čech cohomology of its $H^0$ sheaf(s).
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
each $\mathcal F^\bullet_i$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet)
H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]])

assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet)

assumptions: each $\mathcal F^\bullet_i$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
conclusions: H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]])

nodes.label: cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X)=\check H^\bullet(X;H^0\mathcal F^\bullet)

nodes.name: Equation cechsimplecanonicaliso
nodes.statement: H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]=\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to(H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_n)[-n]])
nodes.label: cechsimplecanonicaliso

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.5.58
nodes.statement: The isomorphism \eqref{cechsimplecanonicaliso} is defined as the composition of the following isomorphisms: \begin{equation} \begin{matrix} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\tau_{\geq 0}\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\tau_{\geq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \uparrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to H^n\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]) \end{matrix} \end{equation} The maps are isomorphisms for the following reasons. Map one: $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}), and a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}). Map two: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism (Lemma \ref{cechsimplebasic}) and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}). Map three: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (by purity), and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}).
nodes.statement_short: Compose three isomorphisms: homotopy K-sheaf computes its own Čech cohomology, truncation is a quasi-isomorphism, and purity gives stalkwise quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.name: Define the isomorphism as a composite
nodes.statement_short: Define the isomorphism as a composition of three maps.
nodes.statement:
The isomorphism \eqref{cechsimplecanonicaliso} is defined as the composition of the following isomorphisms:
\begin{equation} \begin{matrix}
H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]\cr
\downarrow\cr
\check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr
\downarrow\cr
\check H^\bullet(X;[\tau_{\geq 0}\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\tau_{\geq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr
\uparrow\cr
\check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to H^n\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])
\end{matrix}
\end{equation}
The maps are isomorphisms for the following reasons.

nodes.name: Equation isosforpurehtpysheafcech
nodes.statement: \begin{matrix} H^\bullet[\mathcal F^\bullet_0(X)\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n(X)]\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \downarrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[\tau_{\geq 0}\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\tau_{\geq n}\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n])\cr \uparrow\cr \check H^\bullet(X;[H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to H^n\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]) \end{matrix}
nodes.label: isosforpurehtpysheafcech

nodes.name: Map one
nodes.statement_short: Map one is an isomorphism since homotopy K-sheaves compute their own Čech cohomology.
nodes.statement: Map one: $[\mathcal F^\bullet_0\to\cdots\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-n}_n]$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf (Lemma \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}), and a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf calculates its own $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{homotopysheafcechquasiisomorphism}).

nodes.name: Map two
nodes.statement_short: Map two is an isomorphism by strong vanishing and Lemma qicech.
nodes.statement: Map two: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism (Lemma \ref{cechsimplebasic}) and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Lemma \ref{qicech}).

nodes.name: Map three
nodes.statement_short: Map three is an isomorphism by purity and Proposition cechdeterminedbystalks.
nodes.statement: Map three: the map of coefficient $\mathcal K$-presheaves is a quasi-isomorphism on stalks (by purity), and thus induces an isomorphism on $\check H^\bullet$ (Proposition \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}).

nodes.name: Checking purity on a cover
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Write $X=U\cup Z$ with $U$ open and $Z$ closed, and suppose that $i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ and $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ are both pure ($i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$). Then $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure.
assumptions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf
$X=U\cup Z$ with $U$ open and $Z$ closed
$i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ and $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$ are both pure
conclusions: $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure
nodes.label: openclosedpurity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.5.59
nodes.statement: It suffices to show the weak vanishing property for $\mathcal F^\bullet$. Let $\alpha\in H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K)$ be arbitrary with $i<0$. By Remark \ref{nbhdintersectiongood} and Lemma \ref{anycompactintersectionworks}, the following is a quasi-isomorphism: \begin{equation} \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}Z\subseteq V\cr V\textrm{ open}\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)\to\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap Z) \end{equation} Since $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap Z)=0$ by strong vanishing for $i^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$, we see that the image of $\alpha$ in $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)$ vanishes for some open $V\supseteq Z$. Now applying \eqref{homotopysheafproperty} to $K=(K\cap\overline V)\cup(K\setminus V)$, we see that the vanishing of the image of $\alpha$ in $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet(K\cap\overline V)$ implies that $\alpha$ ``comes from'' the cohomology of $[\mathcal F^\bullet(K\setminus V)\to\mathcal F^{\bullet-1}(K\cap\overline V\cap(K\setminus V))$]. On the other hand, this latter group vanishes in degrees $i<0$ by strong vanishing for $j^\ast\mathcal F^\bullet$. Thus $\alpha=0$, so we have even shown strong vanishing for $\mathcal F^\bullet$.

nodes.name: Orientation sheaf of manifold
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold. We let $\mathfrak o_M$ denote the \emph{orientation sheaf}\footnote{Note that the fundamental class lies in homology twisted by $\mathfrak o_M^\vee$.} of $M$ (the corresponding $\mathcal K$-sheaf is defined by $\mathfrak o_M(K):=H_{\dim M}(M,M\setminus K)$); it is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$ (and following Convention \ref{signconventions}, it has parity $\dim M\in\mathbb Z/2$). Now let $M$ be a topological manifold with boundary, and define orientation sheaves on $M$: \begin{align} \mathfrak o_M&:=j_*\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M}\\ \mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}&:=j_!\mathfrak o_{M\setminus\partial M} \end{align} where $j:M\setminus\partial M\hookrightarrow M$. Then $\mathfrak o_M$ is locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbb Z}$, and there is a sequence of sheaves which is exact on stalks: \begin{equation} 0\to\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}\to\mathfrak o_M\to i_\ast\mathfrak o_{\partial M}\to 0 \end{equation} where $i:\partial M\hookrightarrow M$, and the second map comes from the boundary map in the long exact sequence of the pair $(M,\partial M)$.
nodes.statement_short: Orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_M$ of a topological manifold, and for manifolds with boundary the sheaves $\mathfrak o_M$, $\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial}$ with their short exact sequence.
also_stated_at: For a topological manifold $M$, let $\mathfrak o_M$ denote its orientation sheaf (whose fiber at a point $p\in M$ is canonically $H_{\dim M}(M,M\setminus p;\mathbb Z)$).

nodes.name: Homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf axioms for singular chains
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a topological space. Then we have: \begin{rlist} \item$C_\bullet(X,X)$ is acyclic. \itemLet $A,B\subseteq X$ be closed. Then the complex: \begin{equation*} \bigl[C_\bullet(X,X\setminus(A\cup B))\to C_{\bullet+1}(X,X\setminus A)\oplus C_{\bullet+1}(X,X\setminus B)\to C_{\bullet+2}(X,X\setminus(A\cap B))\bigr] \end{equation*} is acyclic. \itemLet $K=\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}K_\alpha$ where $\{K_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in A}$ is a family of closed subsets of $X$ which is \emph{filtered} in the sense that for all $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in A$, there exists $\beta\in A$ with $K_\beta\subseteq K_{\alpha_1}\cap K_{\alpha_2}$. Then $\varinjlim_{\alpha\in A}C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K_\alpha)\to C_\bullet(X,X\setminus K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. \end{rlist}
assumptions: $X$ be a topological space
conclusions: $C_\bullet(X,X)$ is acyclic.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.6.62
nodes.statement: Statement (\ref{scacyc}) is obvious. Statement (\ref{scpatch}) can be deduced from Mayer--Vietoris using a form of the nine lemma as we now explain. Let us write $U:=X\setminus A$ and $V:=X\setminus B$. Now consider the following total complex: \begin{equation} \begin{CD} C_\bullet(U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+1}(U)\oplus C_{\bullet+1}(V)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(U\cup V)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+1}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+2}(X)\oplus C_{\bullet+2}(X)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X)\cr @VVV@VVV@VVV\cr C_{\bullet+2}(X,U\cap V)@>>>C_{\bullet+3}(X,U)\oplus C_{\bullet+3}(X,V)@>>>C_{\bullet+4}(X,U\cup V)\cr \end{CD} \end{equation} The columns are acyclic (by definition of relative chains), and hence the total complex is acyclic as well. The first row is acyclic by Mayer--Vietoris, and the second row is obviously acyclic. Thus the third row is acyclic, as needed. Statement (\ref{sccont}) is true because the map is in fact an isomorphism on the chain level. It is clearly surjective; to show injectivity we must show that a singular chain on $X$ which is disjoint from $K$ is in fact disjoint from $K_\alpha$ for some $\alpha\in A$. This follows because the standard $n$-simplex is compact.
nodes.statement_short: (i) trivial; (ii) nine-lemma argument on a grid of Mayer–Vietoris sequences; (iii) chain-level isomorphism by compactness of simplices.

nodes.name: Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a topological manifold of dimension $n$ with boundary. Let $i:X\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed subset. Let $N\subseteq\partial M$ (closed) be a tamely embedded codimension zero submanifold with boundary.\footnote{In other words, $N\subseteq\partial M$ is a closed subset which locally looks like either $\varnothing\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$, $\mathbb R_{\geq 0}\times\mathbb R^{n-2}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$, or $\mathbb R^{n-1}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-1}$.} Then there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus X)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)]=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M) \end{equation} where $j:M^\circ\cup N^\circ\hookrightarrow M$. In particular, specializing to $N=\varnothing$, there is a canonical isomorphism: \begin{equation} H_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus X)=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast\mathfrak o_{M\operatorname{rel}\partial M}) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality
nodes.statement: Let $X^+$ be the one-point compactification of $X$. Define a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves $\mathcal F^\bullet$ on $X^+$: \begin{equation} \mathcal F^\bullet(K):=[C_{n-1-\bullet}(N,N\setminus K)\to C_{n-\bullet}(M,M\setminus K)] \end{equation} (where on the right hand side by $K$ we really mean $K\cap X$). Applying Lemmas \ref{singularchainshomotopyKsheaf} and \ref{associatedgradedhomotopysheaf}, we see that $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. We claim that $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. Certainly the homology of $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is bounded below, because the singular chain complex of a topological manifold has homology bounded above and $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is built out of these. Now, it is easy to calculate: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z&p\in M^\circ\cup N^\circ\cr 0&p\notin M^\circ\cup N^\circ\end{cases} \end{equation} concentrated in degree zero (see \cite[p231 \S3.3]{hatcher} for the special case $N=\partial M=\varnothing$). Hence $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf. In fact, it is not hard to see (using the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^\ast$) that \eqref{stalkhomologyofPDpure} lifts to an isomorphism of sheaves $f_!i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M\to H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ where $f:X\hookrightarrow X^+$. Now we conclude: \begin{equation*} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X^+)\overset{\text{Prop \ref{cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf}}}=\check H^\bullet(X^+;f_!i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M)\overset{\text{Lem \ref{cptcechembeddingproperty}}}=\check H^\bullet_c(X;i^\ast j_!j^\ast\mathfrak o_M) \end{equation*} Now observe that $H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet(X^+)$ is the left hand side of \eqref{poincaredualitygoal}.
nodes.statement_short: Show the relative chain complex is a pure homotopy K-sheaf on $X^+$ with $H^0$ the orientation sheaf, then apply Proposition cechcohomologypurehomotopysheaf and Lemma cptcechembeddingproperty.

nodes.name: Why homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves instead of homotopy sheaves?
nodes.statement: The naive modification of \eqref{purehomotopyKsheafinPD} substituting open $U\subseteq X$ in place of compact $K\subseteq X$ does not yield a homotopy sheaf. To get a homotopy sheaf, one could apply the proposed functor $R\alpha_\ast:\operatorname{hShv}_{\mathcal K} X\to\operatorname{hShv} X$ from Remark \ref{homotopyKnotsheavesequivalencermk} to the homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf \eqref{purehomotopyKsheafinPD}. It is somewhat easier, though, to just work directly in the setting of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves (which has some advantages, for example stalks of $\mathcal K$-presheaves are easier to define/understand). It is for this reason that throughout this paper we work with homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves instead of homotopy sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Explains why the paper works with homotopy K-sheaves (compact sets) rather than homotopy sheaves (open sets).

nodes.name: Homotopy diagram
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset. A \emph{homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S$} is a collection of complexes $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ equipped with compatible maps $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$ (meaning that $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s'',\mathfrak t''}$ and $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s'',\mathfrak t''}$ agree).
differentia: equipped with compatible maps $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s',\mathfrak t'}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\preceq\mathfrak t'\preceq\mathfrak t$
nodes.statement_short: A homotopy diagram over a finite poset: complexes indexed by pairs $s\preceq t$ with compatible maps for nested intervals.

nodes.name: Homotopy colimit
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S$. We define the \emph{homotopy colimit}: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}:=\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\mathfrak s_0\prec\cdots\prec\mathfrak s_p\in\mathcal S}A^{\bullet+p}_{\mathfrak s_0,\mathfrak s_p} \end{equation} with differential (decreasing $p$) given by the alternating sum over forgetting one of the $\mathfrak s_i$ (plus the internal differential).\footnote{This can be interpreted as the complex of simplicial chains on the nerve of $\mathcal S$ using a coefficient system determined by $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}$.} Loosely speaking, we are ``gluing together'' the $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s}\}_{\mathfrak s\in\mathcal S}$ along the ``morphisms'' $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s}\leftarrow A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t}$ for $\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t$.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy colimit of a homotopy diagram: direct sum over chains $s_0\prec\cdots\prec s_p$ with the simplicial differential.
nodes.label: homotopycolimit

Then the natural inclusion $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}},\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.7.67
nodes.statement: We filter $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ by the number of $\mathfrak s_0,\ldots,\mathfrak s_p$ which are not equal to $\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}$. The zeroth associated graded piece is the subcomplex $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}},\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}$, so it suffices to show that all the other associated graded pieces are acyclic. Each of these is a direct sum of mapping cones $[A^{\bullet+1}_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s^{\mathrm{top}}}\to A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}]$, which are acyclic by assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Filter by the number of chain elements different from the top element; the higher graded pieces are sums of acyclic mapping cones.

nodes.name: $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Fix a finite poset $\mathcal S$ and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ and $\{B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S$. Suppose that there are compatible quasi-isomorphisms $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$. Then the induced map $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
assumptions: $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ and $\{B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S$
there are compatible quasi-isomorphisms $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\to B^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$

nodes.statement: Since the functor $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ commutes with the formation of mapping cones, it suffices to show that if each $A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is acyclic, then so is $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$. This holds since in this case it has a finite filtration whose associated graded is acyclic.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to mapping cones and use a finite filtration with acyclic associated graded.

nodes.name: Tensor product of homotopy diagrams
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ be two finite posets, and let $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\}$ and $\{B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\}$ be homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ respectively. Their tensor product $\{A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\}$ is naturally a homotopy diagram over $\mathcal S\times\mathcal T$. Now there is a natural morphism: \begin{equation} \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal T}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\times\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak s'\times\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal S\times\mathcal T}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'} \end{equation} To define this morphism, we simply observe that the nerve of $\mathcal S\times\mathcal T$ is the standard simplicial subdivision of the product of the nerves of $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$, and this is covered by a morphism of coefficient systems.\footnote{In fact, from this perspective one easily sees that \eqref{tensorproductdirectlimitmorphism} is always a quasi-isomorphism.}
nodes.statement_short: Tensor product of homotopy diagrams over $\mathcal S\times\mathcal T$ and the natural map from the tensor product of homotopy colimits.
nodes.label: simplicialproduct

nodes.name: Equation tensorproductdirectlimitmorphism
nodes.statement: \operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak s'\in\mathcal S}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal T}B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}\to\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\times\mathfrak t\preceq\mathfrak s'\times\mathfrak t'\in\mathcal S\times\mathcal T}A^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'}\otimes B^\bullet_{\mathfrak t,\mathfrak t'}
nodes.label: tensorproductdirectlimitmorphism

nodes.name: $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}$ preserves homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite poset and let $\{\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}\}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}$ be a homotopy diagram of homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves. Then $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{\mathfrak s\preceq\mathfrak t\in\mathcal S}\mathcal F^\bullet_{\mathfrak s,\mathfrak t}$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf.

nodes.name: Gluing pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a finite set. Let $\{U_I\}_{I\subseteq A}$ be an open cover of a space $X$ satisfying: \begin{rlist} \item$U_I\cap U_K\subseteq U_J$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$. \item$U_I\cap U_{I'}\subseteq U_{I\cup I'}$ for $I,I'\subseteq A$. \end{rlist} Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $X$ and let $\mathcal G_{IJ}:=(j_{IJ})_!(j_{IJ})^\ast\mathcal G$ where $j_{IJ}:U_I\cap U_J\hookrightarrow X$. By property (\ref{nestedintersectionOK}), this gives rise to a homotopy diagram $\{\mathcal G_{IJ}\}_{I\subseteq A}$ over $2^A$ of sheaves on $X$. Let $\{\mathcal F_{IJ}^\bullet\}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}$ be a homotopy diagram over $2^A$ of pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaves on $X$, and suppose we give a compatible system of isomorphisms $\mathcal G_{IJ}\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$. Then $\mathcal F^\bullet:=\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$ is a pure homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf and there is a canonical induced isomorphism $\mathcal G\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.8.71
nodes.statement: Certainly $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a homotopy $\mathcal K$-sheaf by Lemma \ref{pihomotopysheaf}. Since $A$ is finite, it is easy to see that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ}$ being bounded below implies that $H^i\mathcal F^\bullet$ is bounded below. Now let us calculate $\mathcal F^\bullet_p$ using the spectral sequence associated to the $p$-filtration. The $E_1$ term is concentrated along the $q=0$ row since $(H^q\mathcal F^\bullet_{IJ})_p$ is concentrated in degree zero; thus there are no further differentials after the $E_1$ page. On the $E_1$ page the differentials coincide precisely with the differentials in the definition of $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p$ (regarding $\mathcal G_{IJ}$ as complexes concentrated in degree zero). Hence we have an isomorphism: \begin{equation} H^\bullet\mathcal F^\bullet_p=H^\bullet\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p \end{equation} To calculate the right hand side of \eqref{FGiso}, let us start with the trivial observation that: \begin{equation} (\mathcal G_{IJ})_p=\begin{cases}\mathcal G_p&p\in U_I\cap U_J\cr 0&p\notin U_I\cap U_J\end{cases} \end{equation} Now consider $(2^A)_p:=\{I\subseteq A:p\in U_I\}$, which satisfies the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$(2^A)_p$ has a maximal element (restatement of (\ref{nonnestedintersectionbig})). \item$I,K\in(2^A)_p$ implies $J\in(2^A)_p$ for $I\subseteq J\subseteq K$ (restatement of (\ref{nestedintersectionOK})). \end{rlist} These two properties imply that $\operatornamewithlimits{hocolim}_{I\subseteq J\subseteq A}(\mathcal G_{IJ})_p$ is simply $\mathcal G_p$ tensored with the simplicial chain complex of the nerve of $(2^A)_p$ (which is contractible). Hence \eqref{FGiso} gives a canonical isomorphism of stalks $H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_p=\mathcal G_p$ (and thus in particular $\mathcal F^\bullet$ is pure). Now it remains to construct a canonical isomorphism of sheaves $\mathcal G\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$. Over the open set $U_I$, we define this isomorphism to be the composition $\mathcal G_{II}\xrightarrow\sim H^0\mathcal F_{II}^\bullet\to H^0\mathcal F^\bullet$ (the second map being the inclusion of a $p=0$ subcomplex in the homotopy colimit). At any point $p\in U_I$, this specializes to the isomorphism of stalks $\mathcal G_p=H^0\mathcal F^\bullet_p$ defined earlier. Hence since $\{U_I\}_{I\subseteq A}$ is an open cover of $X$, these isomorphisms patch together to give the desired global isomorphism.

nodes.name: Rigid open cover
nodes.statement: A \emph{rigid open cover} of a compact space $X$ consists of open sets $\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}$ such that $x\in U_x$, $\overline{\{x:U_x=U\}}\subseteq U$, and $\#\{U:U=U_x\text{ for some }x\}<\infty$. Warning: even if $U_x=U_y$ for some $x\ne y$, they are still different elements of the cover; in particular, the nerve of a rigid cover is always infinite unless $X$ is finite.

nodes.name: Rigid covers form a convenient indexing category
nodes.statement_short: Rigid covers form a set and any two have at most one refinement morphism, so they index Čech complexes conveniently.
nodes.statement: For doing \v Cech theory, the category of rigid open covers is technically more convenient than the usual cateory of open covers (c.f.\ Remark \ref{coveringscategoryrmk}).  Specifically, the collection of rigid covers forms a set, and there is at most one morphism between any pair of rigid covers (we only consider refinements which act as the identity on the index set $X$).

nodes.name: Čech cochains $\check C^\bullet$ and $\check C^\bullet_c$ of sheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf. We define the \v Cech cochains: \begin{equation} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p] \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential. For any compact $K\subseteq X$, define $\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cochains with supports in $K$) via \eqref{cechcomplexIderived} except replacing every instance of $\mathcal F(U)$ with $\ker[\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U\setminus K)]$. We let $\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{K\subseteq X}\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$ (\v Cech cochains with compact supports). Clearly the homology of $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ (resp.\ $\check C^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$, $\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$) is $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ (resp.\ $\check H^\bullet_K(X;\mathcal F)$, $\check H^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$).
nodes.statement_short: Čech cochains of a sheaf as a direct limit over rigid open covers, with versions supported in $K$ and with compact support.

nodes.name: Equation cechcomplexIderived
nodes.statement: \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]

nodes.name: Čech cochains of complexes of $\mathcal K$-presheaves
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal K$-presheaves on a compact space $X$. We define: \begin{equation} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet):=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\bullet-p}\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}\overline{U_x}\Bigr) \end{equation} with the standard \v Cech differential (plus the internal differential of $\mathcal F^\bullet$). We also define $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for any $\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F$ by viewing it as a complex concentrated in degree zero. The homology of $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ is $\check H^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$, as can be seen by applying the arguments from the proof of Lemma \ref{cHsameforopencompactcovers}. Note that for a sheaf $\mathcal F$, the complexes \eqref{cechcomplexIderived} and \eqref{cechcomplexIIderived} are canonically isomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Čech cochains of a complex of K-presheaves via closures of rigid covers; computes $\check H^\bullet$.

nodes.name: Pullback on Čech cochains
nodes.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a map of spaces. A rigid open cover $\{U_y\}_{y\in X}$ pulls back to a rigid open cover $\{f^{-1}(U_{f(x)})\}_{x\in X}$, and this gives natural maps: \begin{rlist} \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Prshv} X$. \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet_c(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F)\to\check C^\bullet_c(X;\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Shv} X$ (if $f$ is proper). \item$f^\ast:\check C^\bullet(Y;f_\ast\mathcal F^\bullet)\to\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F^\bullet)$ for $\mathcal F^i\in\operatorname{Prshv}_{\mathcal K} X$. \end{rlist} whose action on homology coincide with the maps $f^\ast$ defined earlier.
nodes.statement_short: Pulling back rigid covers along $f$ gives chain-level pullback maps on Čech cochains lifting the earlier $f^*$.

nodes.name: Derived inverse limit
nodes.statement: Let $\{C^\bullet_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be an inverse system of complexes. We define: \begin{equation} \mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}C^\bullet_\lambda:=\prod_{q\geq 0}\prod_{\lambda_0\leq\ldots\leq\lambda_q}C^{\bullet-q}_{\lambda_0} \end{equation} with differential obtained by viewing this as cochains on the nerve of $\Lambda$ with a particular coefficient system. See Marde\v si\'c \cite[\S 17]{mardesic} for more details on and basic properties of $\mathop{R\varprojlim}$.

nodes.name: Derived functors of inverse limit
nodes.statement: Let $\{A_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ be an inverse system of abelian groups. We define: \begin{equation} \mathop{\textstyle\varprojlim^i}\limits_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda:=H^i\Bigl[\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A_\lambda\Bigr] \end{equation} (viewing $A_\lambda$ as an inverse system of complex concentrated in degree zero). The inverse limit functor $\varprojlim$ from inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by $\Lambda$ to abelian groups is left exact, and $\varprojlim^i$ are its right derived functors (see Marde\v si\'c \cite[Corollary 11.47]{mardesic}). See Marde\v si\'c \cite[\S\S 11--15]{mardesic} for more details on and basic properties of $\varprojlim^i$.

nodes.name: Partitions and their nerves (Chogoshvili)
nodes.statement: A partition $X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i$ shall mean an \emph{unordered} partition into finitely many disjoint nonempty subsets $E_1,\ldots,E_n\subseteq X$; there is an associated finite closed covering $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^n\overline{E_i}$, whose nerve is denoted $N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}_{i=1}^n)$ (the simplicial complex with vertices $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ where $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ spans a simplex iff $\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing$). A partition $\{F_j\}_{j=1}^m$ refines $\{E_i\}_{i=1}^n$ iff for all $j$, there exists a (necessarily unique) $i$ with $F_j\subseteq E_i$. For a refinement $\{E_i\}_{i=1}^n\to\{F_j\}_{j=1}^m$, there is an associated map of nerves $N(X;\{\overline{F_j}\})\to N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Unordered finite partitions of $X$, the nerves of their closure covers, and refinement with induced maps of nerves.

nodes.name: Properties of Chogoshvili partitions
nodes.statement_short: The poset of partitions is a cofinite set with unique refinements, finite nerves, surjective transition maps, common refinements and pullbacks.
nodes.statement: For doing \v Cech theory, Chogoshvili's construction has exceptionally nice properties.  The collection of partitions is a set, and there is at most one morphism between any pair of partitions.  The poset of partitions is cofinite (a given partition refines only finitely many other partitions).  Each nerve $N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ is a finite simplicial complex, and the transition maps $N(X;\{\overline{F_j}\})\to N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ are all surjective.  Also, any pair of partitions has a minimal common refinement.  Given a map $f:X\to Y$, a partition $\{E_i\}$ of $Y$ pulls back to a partition $\{f^{-1}(E_i)\}$ of $X$, and there is an associated map on nerves $N(X;\{\overline{f^{-1}(E_i)}\})\to N(Y,\{\overline{E_i}\})$.

nodes.name: Inverse limit of Chogoshvili nerves has the Čech cohomology of $X$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be compact. There is a natural map: \begin{equation} \varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})\to X \end{equation} which induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
assumptions: $X$ be compact
conclusions: which induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
nodes.label: inverselimithassamecech

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.9.81
nodes.statement: There is a natural correspondence $C\subseteq X\times N(X;\{\overline E_i\})$, whose fiber over $x\in X$ is the complete simplex on $\{i:x\in\overline{E_i}\}$. Now it is not hard to check that the inverse limit of these correspondences maps bijectively (and thus homeomorphically) to $\varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$, thus giving rise to the desired map \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison}. Now the inverse image of $p\in X$ under \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} is an inverse limit of complete simplices with surjective transition maps (``the complete simplex on a profinite set''), and this has the \v Cech cohomology of a point. Indeed, for any inverse system of compact spaces $\{X_\alpha\}$, the natural map $\varinjlim_\alpha\check H^\bullet(X_\alpha)\to\check H^\bullet(\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism (since open covers of $\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha$ pulled back from some $X_\alpha$ are cofinal among all open covers). Thus it follows from the Leray spectral sequence that \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} induces an isomorphism on \v Cech cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: Build the map from the inverse limit of correspondences; fibers are complete simplices on profinite sets, Čech-acyclic, so Leray gives the isomorphism.

nodes.statement: There is a natural correspondence $C\subseteq X\times N(X;\{\overline E_i\})$, whose fiber over $x\in X$ is the complete simplex on $\{i:x\in\overline{E_i}\}$. nodes.statement: Now the inverse image of $p\in X$ under \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} is an inverse limit of complete simplices with surjective transition maps (``the complete simplex on a profinite set''), and this has the \v Cech cohomology of a point.  Indeed, for any inverse system of compact spaces $\{X_\alpha\}$, the natural map $\varinjlim_\alpha\check H^\bullet(X_\alpha)\to\check H^\bullet(\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism (since open covers of $\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha$ pulled back from some $X_\alpha$ are cofinal among all open covers).
