nodes.name: Steenrod chains and homology
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be compact. We define: \begin{equation} \overline C_\bullet(X):=\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\cr\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z[-p] \end{equation} For a map $f:X\to Y$, there is an induced pushforward map $f_\ast:\overline C_\bullet(X)\to\overline C_\bullet(Y)$. We denote by $\overline H_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ the homology of $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$, and we define relative homology $\overline H_\bullet(X,Y;\mathcal F)$ as the homology of the relevant mapping cone. More generally, let $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf of abelian groups on $X$. Fix a partition $X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i^0$ and trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i^0}}$. This gives rise to a local system $\mathcal F$ on $N(\{\overline{E_i}\}_{i=1}^n)$ for any partition $\{E_i\}$ refining $\{E_i^0\}$. We now define $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ as in \eqref{steenrodchainsRlimeqn}, restricted to partitions refining $\{E_i^0\}$ and using the coefficient system on the nerve induced by $\mathcal F$ and the fixed trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i^0}}$. Since any two choices of trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i}}$ become isomorphic (in the sense that that their sets of ``constant sections'' coincide) after pulling back to some common refinement, it follows that $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ is well-defined up to essentially unique quasi-isomorphism (by Lemma \ref{cofinalityforRlim}). For a map $f:X\to Y$ and $\mathcal F\to f^\ast\mathcal G$, there is a pushforward map $\overline C_\bullet(X;\mathcal F)\to\overline C_\bullet(Y;\mathcal G)$.
nodes.statement_short: Steenrod chains as the derived inverse limit over Chogoshvili partitions of simplicial chains on nerves, with local-system coefficients.
nodes.label: steenrodhomdef

nodes.name: Equation steenrodchainsRlimeqn
nodes.statement: \overline C_\bullet(X):=\mathop{R\varprojlim}_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\cr\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\ne\varnothing\end{smallmatrix}}\mathbb Z[-p]
nodes.label: steenrodchainsRlimeqn

nodes.name: Steenrod homology agrees with Mardešić's strong homology
nodes.statement_short: Definition steenrodhomdef agrees with Mardešić's (strong) Steenrod homology for constant coefficients.
nodes.statement: Although not logically necessary for our purposes, we now argue that Steenrod homology as given in Definition \ref{steenrodhomdef} coincides with the definition from Marde\v si\'c \cite{mardesic} (at least for constant coefficient systems).

nodes.name: Argument that Steenrod homology agrees with Mardešić's
nodes.statement_short: Use Mardešić's description of strong homology via cofinite polyhedral resolutions, barycentric subdivision plus Lemma quasiisomorphismforRlim, and Lemma inverselimithassamecech.

nodes.name: Recall Mardešić's definition
nodes.statement_short: Recall strong homology of an inverse limit of compact polyhedra as homology of $R\varprojlim$ of chains.

nodes.name: Strong homology via derived inverse limit
nodes.statement: \overline H_\bullet(X)=H_\bullet\mathop{R\varprojlim}_\alpha C_\bullet(X_\alpha)

nodes.name: Identify with Steenrod chains of the nerve limit
nodes.statement_short: Barycentric subdivision and Lemma quasiisomorphismforRlim identify the definition with strong homology of the inverse limit of nerves.
nodes.statement: In particular, $\overline C_\bullet(X)$ as defined in \eqref{steenrodchainsRlimeqn} computes the Steenrod homology of $\varprojlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\})$ (using the morphism of inverse systems $C_\bullet^\mathrm{simp}(N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}))\to C_\bullet^\mathrm{sing}(N(X;\{\overline{E_i}\}))$ given by barycentric subdivision, which is a level-wise quasi-isomorphism and thus induces a quasi-isomorphism on derived inverse limits by Lemma \ref{quasiisomorphismforRlim}).

nodes.name: Compare with $X$
nodes.statement_short: The comparison map induces an isomorphism on strong homology.
nodes.statement: Finally, note that the map \eqref{chogoshvilinervecomparison} induces an isomorphism on strong homology by Lemma \ref{inverselimithassamecech} and \cite[p446, Theorem 21.15]{mardesic}.

nodes.name: Steenrod homology is the derived dual of \v Cech cohomology
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf whose stalks are finitely generated free $R$-modules, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then there is a natural isomorphism: \begin{equation} \overline C_\bullet(X;\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F),M) \end{equation} in the derived category $D(R)$. The same holds for relative (co)chains of a closed subspace $Y\subseteq X$, and the isomorphisms are compatible with the relevant exact triangles relating $Y$, $X$ and $(X,Y)$.
assumptions: $\mathcal F$ be a locally constant sheaf whose stalks are finitely generated free $R$-modules
$M$ be an $R$-module
conclusions: \overline C_\bullet(X;\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F),M)
The same holds for relative (co)chains of a closed subspace $Y\subseteq X$, and the isomorphisms are compatible with the relevant exact triangles relating $Y$, $X$ and $(X,Y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Steenrod chains with dual coefficients are the derived dual of Čech cochains.
nodes.label: steenrodisderiveddualofcech

nodes.name: Equation strongcechdualiso
nodes.statement: \overline C_\bullet(X;\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))=R\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F),M)
nodes.label: strongcechdualiso

nodes.name: Relation to Milnor and Mardešić
nodes.statement_short: Lemma steenrodisderiveddualofcech is close to results of Milnor and Mardešić and morally follows from a derived universal property of $R\varprojlim$.
nodes.statement: This result is very similar to Milnor \cite[p92, Definition, Lemma 5]{milnor} and Marde\v si\'c \cite[p446, Theorem 21.15]{mardesic}.  Note also that morally, the above result should be thought of as following trivially from some derived universal property of the form $\mathop{R\varprojlim} R\operatorname{Hom}(A_\alpha^\bullet,B^\bullet)=R\operatorname{Hom}(\varinjlim A_\alpha^\bullet,B^\bullet)$ (hopefully this provides some motivation for the proof below).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.9.83
nodes.statement: Let us relate $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ as defined using rigid open covers to a version using partitions. Specifically, we consider the following quasi-isomorphisms: \begin{align} \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i\cr\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}U_i\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\downarrow\cr \varinjlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}<\cdots<\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p] \end{align} The first map is induced by associating to a partition $\{E_i\}$ and $\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i$ the rigid open cover assigning $U_i$ to $x\in E_i$, and pulling back along the induced map on nerves; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by a filtration argument (basically the Leray spectral sequence). The second map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} and the definition of $\alpha^\ast$. The third map is defined as the tautological map on $q=0$ direct summands and zero for $q>0$; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by expressing the domain (resp.\ codomain) as the direct limit over partitions $\{E_i\}$ of the corresponding complex (resp.\ direct limit) restricted to partitions refined by $\{E_i\}$ and observing that for any fixed $\{E_i\}$ the map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{comboretraction}. Finally, the last pair of maps consists of the natural inclusion ($\downarrow$) and the retraction annihilating any component with $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}=\{E_i^{(j+1)}\}_{i=1}^{n_{j+1}}$ for some $j$ ($\uparrow$); one can see that both are quasi-isomorphisms by filtering by $\{E_i\}$ (as before) and then by the number of distinct $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}$. For any partition $\{E_i\}$ of $X$ and collection of trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline E_i}$, there is a sub-$\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\subseteq\mathcal F$ whose sections over $K$ are those sections of $\mathcal F$ whose restrictions to $K\cap\overline{E_i}$ are constant with respect to the specified trivializations. The complex \eqref{cechbychogoshvili} calculates \v Cech cohomology \eqref{cechcomplexII} by a cofinality argument, and the inclusion $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\to\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism on stalks and thus on \v Cech cohomology by Lemma \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}. The third map above remains a quasi-isomorphism for $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}$ (for the same reason), and furthermore we may restrict \eqref{almosthomotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} to partitions refining the fixed $\{E_i\}$ by Lemma \ref{cofinalityforRlim}. The conclusion of the above discussion is that we have thus constructed a canonical (and functorial) quasi-isomorphism between $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ and: \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i\}\leq\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p] \end{equation} (for any fixed partition $\{E_i\}$ and trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i}}$ giving rise to $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\subseteq\mathcal F$). Note that $\overline C_\bullet(X,\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))$ is precisely $\operatorname{Hom}(\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize},M)$. Thus it suffices to show that this particular $\operatorname{Hom}$ is in fact the $R\operatorname{Hom}$. Recall that $R\operatorname{Hom}$ in $D(R)$ may be computed using a K-projective resolution of the first argument (see Spaltenstein \cite{spaltenstein}), where a complex $P^\bullet$ is called K-projective iff $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P^\bullet,M^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $M^\bullet$ (note that a bounded above complex of projective modules is K-projective). Thus it suffices to show that \eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} is K-projective. We consider subsets $\wp$ of the poset of partitions of $X$ with the property that any partition refined by a partition in $\wp$ also lies in $\wp$. Since the poset of partitions is cofinite, we may use Zorn's lemma to choose a directed system $\{\wp_i\}_{i\in I}$ of such collections, indexed by a well-ordered set $I$, with the following properties: \begin{rlist} \item$\wp_0=\varnothing$, where $0\in I$ is the least element. \item$\left|\wp_i\setminus\wp_{i-1}\right|=1$ if $i\in I$ has a predecessor $i-1$. \item$\wp_i=\bigcup_{i'<i}\wp_{i'}$ if $i\in I$ has no predecessor. \end{rlist} Now for $i\in I$, let $\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i\subseteq\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}$ denote the subcomplex generated by restricting to partitions in $\wp_i$. It follows that: \begin{rlist} \item$\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_0=0$, where $0\in I$ is the least element. \item$\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_{i-1}\to\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is injective and component-wise split with K-projective cokernel if $i\in I$ has a predecessor $i-1$ (this holds since the cokernel is a bounded above complex of free modules). \item$\varinjlim_{i'<i}\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_{i'}\to\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is an isomorphism if $i\in I$ has no predecessor. \end{rlist} It follows that $\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}=\varinjlim_i\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is K-projective by Spaltenstein \cite[p131, 2.8 Corollary]{spaltenstein}. Since the construction of the isomorphism \eqref{strongcechdualiso} was given by a functorial chain-level construction, it can be checked that it is natural, applies in the relative case, and is compatibile with exact triangles.
nodes.statement_short: Replace Čech cochains by a quasi-isomorphic complex built from partitions whose Hom into $M$ is Steenrod chains, then show it is K-projective. The key step is a Zorn's-lemma filtration by down-closed sets of partitions with free cokernels.

nodes.name: Chain of comparison complexes
nodes.statement_short: Write a chain of quasi-isomorphisms relating rigid-cover Čech cochains to partition-based complexes.
nodes.statement:
Let us relate $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ as defined using rigid open covers to a version using partitions.  Specifically, we consider the following quasi-isomorphisms:
\begin{align}
\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]\\
&\quad\uparrow\cr
\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i\cr\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}U_i\Bigr)[-p]\\
&\quad\downarrow\cr \varinjlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\Bigr)[-p]\\
&\quad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}<\cdots<\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]\\
&\quad\uparrow\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
\end{align}

nodes.name: Equation cechbychogoshvili
nodes.statement: \check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)=\varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}\{U_x\subseteq X\}_{x\in X}\cr\text{rigid open cover}\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq X\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{x\in S}U_x\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \varinjlim_{\begin{smallmatrix}X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i\cr\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i\end{smallmatrix}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}U_i\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\downarrow\cr \varinjlim_{X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^nE_i}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i}\Bigr)[-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}<\cdots<\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]\\ &\quad\uparrow\downarrow\cr \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}&\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
nodes.label: cechbychogoshvili

nodes.name: First map
nodes.statement_short: The first map is a quasi-isomorphism by a filtration (Leray) argument.
nodes.statement: The first map is induced by associating to a partition $\{E_i\}$ and $\overline{E_i}\subseteq U_i$ the rigid open cover assigning $U_i$ to $x\in E_i$, and pulling back along the induced map on nerves; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by a filtration argument (basically the Leray spectral sequence).

nodes.name: Second map
nodes.statement_short: The second map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma intersectioncofinal.
nodes.statement: The second map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{intersectioncofinal} and the definition of $\alpha^\ast$.

nodes.name: Third map
nodes.statement_short: The third map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma comboretraction after restricting to refinements.
nodes.statement: The third map is defined as the tautological map on $q=0$ direct summands and zero for $q>0$; it can be seen to be a quasi-isomorphism by expressing the domain (resp.\ codomain) as the direct limit over partitions $\{E_i\}$ of the corresponding complex (resp.\ direct limit) restricted to partitions refined by $\{E_i\}$ and observing that for any fixed $\{E_i\}$ the map is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma \ref{comboretraction}.

nodes.name: Last pair of maps
nodes.statement_short: The inclusion/retraction pair are quasi-isomorphisms by a double filtration.
nodes.statement: Finally, the last pair of maps consists of the natural inclusion ($\downarrow$) and the retraction annihilating any component with $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}=\{E_i^{(j+1)}\}_{i=1}^{n_{j+1}}$ for some $j$ ($\uparrow$); one can see that both are quasi-isomorphisms by filtering by $\{E_i\}$ (as before) and then by the number of distinct $\{E_i^{(j)}\}_{i=1}^{n_j}$.

nodes.name: Constant-section subpresheaf
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}$ of sections constant w.r.t. trivializations.
nodes.statement: For any partition $\{E_i\}$ of $X$ and collection of trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline E_i}$, there is a sub-$\mathcal K$-presheaf $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\subseteq\mathcal F$ whose sections over $K$ are those sections of $\mathcal F$ whose restrictions to $K\cap\overline{E_i}$ are constant with respect to the specified trivializations.

nodes.name: Replace $\mathcal F$ by $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}$
nodes.statement_short: Cofinality and stalk comparison let one replace $\mathcal F$ by $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}$ and restrict to refinements.
nodes.statement: The complex \eqref{cechbychogoshvili} calculates \v Cech cohomology \eqref{cechcomplexII} by a cofinality argument, and the inclusion $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\to\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism on stalks and thus on \v Cech cohomology by Lemma \ref{cechdeterminedbystalks}.  The third map above remains a quasi-isomorphism for $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}$ (for the same reason), and furthermore we may restrict \eqref{almosthomotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} to partitions refining the fixed $\{E_i\}$ by Lemma \ref{cofinalityforRlim}.

nodes.name: Reduce to Hom equals RHom
nodes.statement_short: The resulting complex dualizes to Steenrod chains, so it suffices that Hom computes RHom.
nodes.statement:
The conclusion of the above discussion is that we have thus constructed a canonical (and functorial) quasi-isomorphism between $\check C^\bullet(X;\mathcal F)$ and:
\begin{equation} \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i\}\leq\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
\end{equation}
(for any fixed partition $\{E_i\}$ and trivializations of $\mathcal F|_{\overline{E_i}}$ giving rise to $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\subseteq\mathcal F$).  Note that $\overline C_\bullet(X,\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,M))$ is precisely $\operatorname{Hom}(\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize},M)$.  Thus it suffices to show that this particular $\operatorname{Hom}$ is in fact the $R\operatorname{Hom}$.

nodes.name: Equation homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize
nodes.statement: \bigoplus_{q\geq 0}\bigoplus_{\{E_i\}\leq\{E_i^{(0)}\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\leq\cdots\leq\{E_i^{(q)}\}_{i=1}^{n_q}}\bigoplus_{p\geq 0}\prod_{\begin{smallmatrix}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_0\}\cr\left|S\right|=p+1\end{smallmatrix}}\mathcal F^{\mathrm{pre}}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i\in S}\overline{E_i^{(0)}}\Bigr)[q-p]
nodes.label: homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize

nodes.name: Reduce to K-projectivity
nodes.statement_short: Recall RHom via K-projective resolutions; reduce to K-projectivity.
nodes.statement: Recall that $R\operatorname{Hom}$ in $D(R)$ may be computed using a K-projective resolution of the first argument (see Spaltenstein \cite{spaltenstein}), where a complex $P^\bullet$ is called K-projective iff $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P^\bullet,M^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $M^\bullet$ (note that a bounded above complex of projective modules is K-projective).  Thus it suffices to show that \eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize} is K-projective.

nodes.name: Zorn filtration
nodes.statement_short: Choose a well-ordered exhaustive filtration by down-closed sets of partitions via Zorn's lemma.

nodes.name: Filtration properties
nodes.statement_short: The induced subcomplexes form a continuous filtration with K-projective split cokernels.

nodes.name: K-projectivity by Spaltenstein
nodes.statement_short: Conclude K-projectivity by Spaltenstein's corollary.
nodes.statement: It follows that $\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}=\varinjlim_i\eqref{homotopycolimitofchogoshvilicoverstodualize}_i$ is K-projective by Spaltenstein \cite[p131, 2.8 Corollary]{spaltenstein}.

nodes.name: Naturality and relative case
nodes.statement_short: Functoriality of the chain-level construction gives naturality, the relative case and compatibility with triangles.
nodes.statement: Since the construction of the isomorphism \eqref{strongcechdualiso} was given by a functorial chain-level construction, it can be checked that it is natural, applies in the relative case, and is compatibile with exact triangles.

nodes.name: Almost complex manifold $(X,J)$
Equation
nodes.statement: (X,J)

nodes.name: Divisors $D,D_1,\ldots,D_r$
Equation
nodes.statement: D,D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq X

nodes.name: Base $\overline{\mathcal M}$ with étale map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$
nodes.statement: Fix a smooth manifold $\overline{\mathcal M}$ equipped with a smooth \'etale map $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$\footnote{We give $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ the standard smooth structure from its structure as a complex analytic orbifold.  Every point in a smooth orbifold $M$ is in the image of a smooth \'etale map $M'\to M$.  Indeed, $M$ is covered by open sets each diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^n/G$ for some finite group $G\to GL_n(\mathbb R)$, and the map $\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n/G\hookrightarrow M$ is smooth \'etale.} (in the orbifold sense).

nodes.name: Family of curves $\overline{\mathcal C}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$
Equation
nodes.statement: \begin{CD} \overline{\mathcal C}@>>>\overline{\mathcal C}_{g,n+\ell}\cr @VVV@VVV\cr \overline{\mathcal M}@>>>\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell} \end{CD}

nodes.name: Smooth locus $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ$
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C}$ denote the open subset where the fiber is smooth.

nodes.name: Perturbation space $E$ and map $\lambda$
nodes.statement_short: Fix a finite-dimensional space $E$ and a linear map $\lambda$ to smooth $(0,1)$-forms on fiber products of the smooth locus with values in $TX$.
nodes.statement:
Fix a finite dimensional vector space $E$ and a linear map:
\begin{equation} \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\cdots\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r\text{ times}}{}\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)
\end{equation}
Here $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}$ is the $(0,1)$-part of the complexified vertical cotangent bundle $T^\ast_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ of (the last factor of) $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\to\overline{\mathcal M}$, and $C^\infty$ means smooth sections.

nodes.name: Equation lambdafix
nodes.statement: \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\cdots\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r\text{ times}}{}\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ/\overline{\mathcal M}}\otimes_{\mathbb C} TX)
nodes.label: lambdafix

nodes.name: $\lambda$ vanishes near nodes
nodes.statement: We require that $\lambda$ be zero in a neighborhood of the nodes $\overline{\mathcal C}\setminus\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ$ of the last $\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ$ factor.

nodes.name: Normalization of a nodal curve
differentia: equipped with a map $\tilde C\to C$ which identifies points in pairs to form the nodes of $C$
nodes.statement: For a nodal curve $C$, we denote by $\tilde C$ its normalization, i.e.\ the unique smooth compact Riemann surface equipped with a map $\tilde C\to C$ which identifies points in pairs to form the nodes of $C$.

nodes.name: Smooth function on a nodal curve
nodes.statement: A function on $C$ being smooth means (by definition) that its pullback to $\tilde C$ is smooth.

nodes.name: Homology class $\beta$
nodes.statement: Fix a homology class $\beta\in H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$.

nodes.name: Moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$
nodes.statement_short: Moduli space of $(s,u,\{x_i\},e)$: maps of class $\beta$ from fibers $C_s$ with divisor constraints solving the $\lambda$-perturbed Cauchy–Riemann equation.

nodes.name: Equation Mbarfirstdef
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}s\in\overline{\mathcal M}\hfill\cr u:C_s\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_s\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_s]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\}
nodes.label: Mbarfirstdef

nodes.name: Fibers $C_s$ and marked points
nodes.statement: We let $C_s$ denote the fiber of $\overline{\mathcal C}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ over $s$, with marked points $p_1,\ldots,p_{n+\ell}\in C_s$.

nodes.name: Transversality $u\pitchfork D_i$ at $x_i$
nodes.statement: Here $u\pitchfork D_i$ at $x_i$ means (by definition) that $x_i$ is not a node of $C_s$ and the map $T_{x_i}C_s\oplus T_{u(x_i)}D_i\xrightarrow{du\oplus\operatorname{id}}T_{u(x_i)}X$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$
nodes.definiendum: topology of uniform convergence on $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$
nodes.statement: We give $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ the topology of uniform convergence (i.e.\ using the Hausdorff distance between graphs $\subseteq\overline{\mathcal C}\times X$ to compare maps $u$).

nodes.name: $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ need not be compact
nodes.statement: Note that $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is not necessarily compact, however this will be irrelevant since we are only interested in its local properties.

nodes.name: Subspace $E'$
nodes.statement: Fix a subspace $E'\subseteq E$.

nodes.name: Base point $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)$
nodes.statement: Fix $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$; we will describe when $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$.

nodes.name: Banach manifold $\mathcal B$
Equation
nodes.statement: \mathcal B:=\Bigl\{(u,e)\in W^{k,p}(C_{s_0},X)\times E\Bigm|u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\;(1\leq i\leq\ell)\Bigr\}

nodes.name: Banach bundle $\mathcal E$
nodes.statement: Over $\mathcal B$, we consider the smooth Banach bundle $\mathcal E$ whose fiber over a map $u:C_{s_0}\to X$ is $W^{k-1,p}(\tilde C_{s_0},\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_{s_0}}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TX)\oplus E/E'$.

nodes.name: Intersection point functions $x_i$
assumptions: $k$ is large
conclusions: defined in a neighborhood of $(u_0,e_0)\in\mathcal B$, which coincide with $x_i^0$ at $(u_0,e_0)$, and for which $u(x_i(u))\in D_i^\circ$
nodes.statement_short: For large $k$, the intersection points $x_i$ with the divisors $D_i$ are unique continuous functions near $(u_0,e_0)$.
nodes.statement:
Now suppose $k$ is large; then there are unique continuous functions:
\begin{equation} x_i:\mathcal B\to C_{s_0}\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
\end{equation}
defined in a neighborhood of $(u_0,e_0)\in\mathcal B$, which coincide with $x_i^0$ at $(u_0,e_0)$, and for which $u(x_i(u))\in D_i^\circ$.

nodes.name: Equation intersectionsfunction
nodes.statement: x_i:\mathcal B\to C_{s_0}\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
nodes.label: intersectionsfunction

nodes.name: Highly differentiable
nodes.statement: Moreover, \eqref{intersectionsfunction} are ``highly differentiable'', by which we mean that for all $\ell<\infty$, the function \eqref{intersectionsfunction} is of class $C^\ell$ provided $k\geq k_0(\ell)$.

nodes.name: Differentiability of $x_i$ via implicit function theorem
nodes.statement_short: Implicit function theorem plus Sobolev embedding $W^{k,p}\hookrightarrow C^\ell$.
nodes.statement: In the present situation, we can of course be more precise: $x_i$ is $C^\ell$ as a function of $u\in C^\ell$ (by the implicit function theorem), so \eqref{intersectionsfunction} is $C^\ell$ as long as $W^{k,p}\hookrightarrow C^\ell$ (which holds iff $(k-\ell)p>2$).

nodes.name: Highly differentiable $\bar\partial$-section
nodes.statement_short: The perturbed $\bar\partial$-section of $\mathcal E$ over $\mathcal B$ is highly differentiable.
nodes.statement:
It follows that:
\begin{equation} (u,e)\mapsto\left[\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\right]\oplus e
\end{equation}
is a highly differentiable section of $\mathcal E$ over $\mathcal B$ (the only nonsmoothness comes from how the $x_i$'s depend on $u$).

nodes.name: Equation firstdelbarsection
nodes.statement: (u,e)\mapsto\left[\bar\partial u+\lambda(e)(x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\right]\oplus e
nodes.label: firstdelbarsection

nodes.name: $1<p<\infty$
nodes.statement: Assume $1<p<\infty$.

nodes.name: Regular locus $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$
nodes.statement_short: A point is regular iff the perturbed $\bar\partial$-section (with $E/E'$ component) is transverse to zero there.
nodes.statement: We say $(s_0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ iff \eqref{firstdelbarsection} is transverse to the zero section at $(u_0,e_0)$.

nodes.name: Regularity is independent of $(k,p)$
nodes.statement_short: By elliptic regularity, regularity does not depend on the Sobolev exponents $(k,p)$.
nodes.statement: It is an easy exercise using elliptic regularity to see that this notion is independent of $(k,p)$ (as long as $k$ is sufficiently large so that the condition makes sense).

nodes.name: Orientation module $\mathfrak o_E$
nodes.statement: For a vector space $E$, let $\mathfrak o_E$ denote its orientation module (canonically $H_{\dim E}(E,E\setminus 0;\mathbb Z)$).

nodes.name: Gluing theorem for $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$
nodes.statement: In the above setup (from the beginning of \S\ref{setupforgluing} until here), we have: \begin{rlist} \item$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is open. \item$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle+\dim E-2\ell$. \itemThe projection $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\to E/E'$ is a topological submersion, i.e.\ locally modeled on a projection $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$. \itemThe orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$. \end{rlist}
assumptions: In the above setup (from the beginning of \S\ref{setupforgluing} until here)
conclusions: $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is open.
$\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ is a topological manifold of dimension $\dim\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}+(1-g)\dim X+2\langle c_1(X),\beta\rangle+\dim E-2\ell$.
The projection $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\to E/E'$ is a topological submersion, i.e.\ locally modeled on a projection $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$.
The orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$.
nodes.statement_short: The regular locus is open in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$, a topological manifold of the expected dimension, submersive over $E/E'$, with orientation sheaf $\mathfrak o_E$ times normal-bundle factors.
nodes.label: mainresult

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9.2.9 from Theorem B.1.1
nodes.statement_short: Locally identify the thickened Gromov–Witten moduli space with an $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ by choosing a stabilizing divisor $D$, divisors $D_\alpha$ and the combined perturbation $\lambda$, then apply Theorem mainresult. The key step is choosing $\ell$ minimal so that regular loci match.

nodes.name: Reduce to a local statement
nodes.statement_short: The proposition is local; plan to build matching setup data near a given point.
nodes.statement: Let us now explain how Theorem \ref{mainresult} implies Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}.  Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded} is a local statement, so let us prove it in a neighborhood of a specific point $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$.  We will construct data $(X,J,D,D_1,\ldots,D_r,\overline{\mathcal M},E,\lambda,E')$ as in the above setup and a point $(s,u,\{x_i\},e)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$.  It will be clear from the construction that there is a natural homeomorphism between a small neighborhood of this point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ and a small neighborhood of the given point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^\beta(X)_I$, and using this we will infer Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded} from Theorem \ref{mainresult}.

nodes.name: Claim: points of injectivity
nodes.statement_short: Each unstable component has a point where $du$ is injective, by domain stabilization or transversality to $D_\alpha$.
nodes.statement: We claim that every unstable irreducible component of $C$ has a point where $du$ is injective.  If $I=\varnothing$, this follows from the domain stabilization step Lemma \ref{everythingcanbethickened}, and if $I\ne\varnothing$, then picking any $\alpha\in I$, this follows from the fact that $u\pitchfork D_\alpha$ and adding the intersections as marked points makes $C$ stable.

nodes.name: Choose stabilizing divisor $D$ and $\ell$
nodes.statement_short: Pick $D$ transverse to $u$ and the minimal number $\ell$ of stabilizing points.
nodes.statement: It follows from the claim that we may pick $D\subseteq X$ with $u\pitchfork D$ such that adding these intersections as extra marked points makes $C$ stable, and none of these points are nodes or marked points.  We take $\ell$ to be the \emph{minimum} number of points in $u^{-1}(D)$ necessary to stabilize $C$, and we fix an ordered $\ell$-tuple of such points, adding them as new marked points $p_{n+1},\ldots,p_{n+\ell}\in C$, so now $C$ is a curve of type $(g,n+\ell)$.

nodes.name: Choose $D_i$, $x_i$, and étale chart
nodes.statement_short: Set $D_i$ from the $D_\alpha$, the $x_i$ as intersection points, and choose an étale chart and isomorphism $\iota$.
nodes.statement: Now we let $r=\sum_{\alpha\in I}r_\alpha$, we let $D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq X$ consist of $r_\alpha$ copies of $D_\alpha$ (union over $\alpha\in I$), and we let the $x_i$'s be the intersection points $u^{-1}(D_\alpha)$ (union over $\alpha\in I$).  For the purposes of the present argument, let us reindex $\{x_i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}$ as $\{x^\alpha_i\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha}$.  Now since $C$ is a curve of type $(g,n+\ell)$, it corresponds to a point in $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$.  Choose an \'etale map $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ covering this point, and choose a point $s\in\overline{\mathcal M}$ and an isomorphism $\iota:C\to C_s$.

nodes.name: Maps $\tilde\phi_\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: Construct the unique local maps $\tilde\phi_\alpha$ extending $\phi_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \tilde\phi_\alpha:\overbrace{\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\cdots\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ}^{r_\alpha\text{ times}}{}\underset{\overline{\mathcal M}}\times\overline{\mathcal C}^\circ\to\overline{\mathcal C}_\alpha

nodes.name: Define $E$ and $\lambda$
nodes.statement_short: Take $E=E_I$ and define $\lambda$ as the sum of the pulled-back $\lambda_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Local identification of moduli spaces
nodes.statement_short: Neighbourhoods in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ and the thickened moduli space coincide.
nodes.statement: Finally, we observe that with this definition, a neighborhood of $(s,u\circ\iota^{-1},\{x^\alpha_i\}_{\alpha\in I,1\leq i\leq r_\alpha},\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}e_\alpha)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ coincides with a neighborhood of $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I$ (note that the point $(C,u,\{\phi_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I},\{e_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in I})\in\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ has trivial automorphism group by definition of $\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$).

nodes.name: Openness and orientation
nodes.statement_short: For $E'=E$ regular loci correspond, giving openness and orientation parts.
nodes.statement: For $E'=E$, under this identification of a small open set in $\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I$ and a small open set in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$, we have $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}^\beta_{g,n}(X)_I^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (for this it is important that we chose $\ell$ as the \emph{minimum} number of points necessary to stabilize $C$).  It follows that Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{openness},\ref{orientation}) implies Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}(\ref{GWgluingopen},\ref{GWgluingor}) (note that over this small open set, we have an identification $\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}=\mathfrak o_{T_{p_{n+i}}C_s}$ and that the latter is canonically trivial using the complex structure on $C_s$).

nodes.name: Submersion part
nodes.statement_short: Using $J$ in place of $I$ and $E'=E_I$ gives the submersion part.
nodes.statement: Taking the above construction with $J$ in place of $I$ and setting $E':=E_I\subseteq E_J=E$, we get Proposition \ref{GWgluingneeded}(\ref{GWgluingsubmersion}) from Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{manifold},\ref{submersion}) as well.

nodes.name: Central curve $C_0$ and its number of nodes $d$
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be the number of nodes of $C_0:=C_{s_0}$.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Cylindrical ends at the nodes of $C_0$
nodes.statement:
On each side of each node of $C_0$, fix a ``cylindrical end'', that is, a map:
\begin{equation} [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_0
\end{equation}
which is a biholomorphism onto some small neighborhood $D^2\setminus 0$ of the node.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Equation cylindricalends
nodes.statement: [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_0
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: cylindricalends

nodes.name: End coordinates $(s,t)$
nodes.statement: We use coordinates $(s,t)\in[0,\infty)\times S^1$, which is given the standard holomorphic structure $z=e^{s+it}$.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Locus $\overline{\mathcal M}^d$ of curves with $d$ nodes
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathcal M}^d\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}$ denote the locus of curves with exactly $d$ nodes.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Family of almost complex structures $j_y$
nodes.statement: Pick a smooth family of smooth almost complex structures $j_y$ on $C_0$ parameterized by $y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}$, where $j_0$ is the given almost complex structure on $C_0$, which is constant over the cylindrical ends \eqref{cylindricalends}, and such that the induced map $\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\to\overline{\mathcal M}^d$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Neck from a gluing parameter
nodes.statement_short: Gluing two standard ends with parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}$: truncate at $6S$ and identify, giving a neck.
nodes.statement: Now consider the following procedure, which takes a ``gluing parameter'' $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}\in\mathbb C$ and two copies of the standard end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\sqcup[0,\infty)\times S^1$.  We first truncate both ends, leaving just the subset $[0,6S]\times S^1\sqcup[0,6S]\times S^1$.  We then identify $(s,t)$ in the first piece with $(6S-s,\theta-t)=(s',t')$ in the second piece.  We call the resulting cylinder a ``neck''.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Glued curve $C_lpha$
nodes.statement_short: Gluing $C_0$ at its nodes with parameters $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$ gives the curve $C_\alpha$ with ends and necks.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Equation Gend
nodes.statement: [0,\infty)\times S^1\to C_\alpha
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: Gend

nodes.name: Equation Gneck
nodes.statement: [0,6S_i]\times S^1\to C_\alpha
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node
nodes.label: Gneck

nodes.name: Neck coordinates $(s,t)$ and $(s',t')$
nodes.statement: In each neck, we have coordinates $(s,t)\in[0,6S_i]\times S^1$ and coordinates $(s',t')\in[0,6S_i]\times S^1$, which satisfy $s+s'=6S_i$ and $t+t'=\theta_i$.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Gluing coordinates are a local diffeomorphism
assumptions: $\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n+\ell}$ is \'etale
conclusions: which is a local diffeomorphism near zero
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}&\to\overline{\mathcal M}\\ (\alpha,y)&\mapsto(C_\alpha,j_y,p_1,\ldots,p_{n+\ell})
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Local description of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$
nodes.statement_short: In gluing coordinates, $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is the set of $(\alpha,y,u,\{x_i\},e)$ solving the perturbed $\bar\partial$-equation with incidence conditions.
nodes.section: B.2 Local model for resolution of a node

nodes.name: Equation modulispace
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathcal M}(X):=\left\{\begin{matrix}\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\hfill\cr y\in\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\hfill\cr u:C_\alpha\to X\hfill\cr x_i\in C_\alpha\quad 1\leq i\leq r\hfill\cr e\in E\hfill\end{matrix}\;\middle|\;\begin{matrix}u\text{ smooth and }u_\ast[C_\alpha]=\beta\hfill\cr u(p_{n+i})\in D^\circ\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq\ell)\cr u(x_i)\in D_i^\circ\text{ and }u\pitchfork D_i\text{ at }x_i\quad\hfill(1\leq i\leq r)\cr\bar\partial_yu+\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x_1,\ldots,x_r,\cdot,u(\cdot))=0\hfill\end{matrix}\right\}

nodes.name: Perturbation $\lambda$ in gluing coordinates
nodes.statement_short: The perturbation $\lambda$ rewritten as a function of the gluing coordinates $(\alpha,y)$.

nodes.name: Cylindrical ends avoid the support of $\lambda$
nodes.statement: We assume that the cylindrical ends were chosen disjoint from the support of $\lambda^\mathrm{old}$, so we can make sense of $\lambda^\mathrm{new}$ as giving sections on $C_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Exponential map $\exp$
nodes.statement: Let $\exp:TX\to X$ denote the exponential map of some Riemannian metric on $X$ for which $D$ is totally geodesic.

nodes.name: $J$-linear connection $\nabla$
nodes.statement:
Let $
abla$ denote any $J$-linear ootnote{Given any connection $
abla^0$, the connection $
abla_XY:= rac 12(
abla^0_XY-J(
abla^0_X(JY)))$ is $J$-linear.} connection on $TX$ (equivalently, a connection for which $
abla J=0$).

nodes.name: Parallel transport $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}:T_xX\to T_yX$ denote parallel transport via $\nabla$ along the shortest geodesic between $x$ and $y$ (we will only use this notation when it may be assumed that $x$ and $y$ are very close in $X$); note that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is $J$-linear.

nodes.name: Cutoff function $\chi$
Equation
nodes.statement: \chi(x)=\begin{cases}0&x\leq 0\cr 1&x\geq 1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Flattening $u_{0|\alpha}$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define the ``flattened'' map $u_{0|\alpha}:C_0\to X$ as follows. Away from the ends, $u_{0|\alpha}$ coincides with $u_0$. Over an end $[0,\infty)\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $n\in C_0$ denotes the corresponding node.
nodes.statement_short: Flatten $u_0$ near each node: equal to $u_0$ until $S-1$, interpolated to the constant $u_0(n)$ by $S$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: u_{0|\alpha}(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Pregluing $u_\alpha$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define the ``preglued'' map $u_\alpha:C_\alpha\to X$ as follows. Away from the necks, $u_\alpha$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} ($u_\alpha$ should be thought of as the ``descent'' of $u_{0|\alpha}$ from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: The preglued map on $C_\alpha$: $u_0$ away from the necks, cut off to the constant $u_0(n)$ in the middle of each neck.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: u_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} u_0(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}

nodes.name: Pregluing vector fields $\xi_\alpha$
nodes.statement: For $\xi\in C^\infty(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)$, we define: \begin{equation} \xi_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. Away from the necks, $\xi_\alpha$ coincides with $\xi$. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1$, we define it as follows: \begin{equation} \xi_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \xi(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \xi(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \xi(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \xi(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transfer a vector field $\xi$ on $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$ by parallel transport, interpolating to $\xi(n)$ in the necks.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \xi_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Equation kernelpregluingformula
nodes.statement: \xi_\alpha(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s,t)\to u_\alpha(s,t)}\left[\xi(s,t)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \xi(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \xi(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \xi(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(s',t')\to u_\alpha(s',t')}\left[\xi(s',t')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \xi(s',t')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases}
nodes.label: kernelpregluingformula

nodes.name: Sobolev order $k$ and weight $\delta$
nodes.statement: Fix $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 6}$ and fix $\delta\in(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev space $W^{k,2}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $W^{k,2}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)$ the space of sections of $u_\alpha^\ast TX$ over $C_\alpha$ whose pullback to $\tilde C_\alpha$ is $W^{k,2}$ (since $W^{k,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ as $k\geq 6$, this is the same as $W^{k,2}$ sections over $\tilde C_\alpha$ which coincide on each pair of points identified in $\tilde C_\alpha\to C_\alpha$, where $\tilde C_\alpha$ denotes the normalization of $C_\alpha$).

nodes.name: Sobolev space of $(0,1)$-forms $W^{k-1,2}$
nodes.statement: Similarly we denote by $W^{k-1,2}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)$ the space of sections of class $W^{k-1,2}$.

nodes.name: Local parallel-transport trivialization near a node
nodes.statement:
To make calculations in ends/necks easier, for each node $n\in C_0$ we fix the local trivialization of $TX$ given by parallel transport:
\begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(n)\to p}:T_{u_0(n)}X\to T_pX
\end{equation}
over $p$ contained in a small ball centered at $u_0(n)$.

nodes.name: Equation localPTcoords
nodes.statement: \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(n)\to p}:T_{u_0(n)}X\to T_pX
nodes.label: localPTcoords

nodes.name: Ends map into small balls
nodes.statement: We assume that the ends \eqref{cylindricalends} were chosen small enough so that $u_0$ maps each end into a compact subset of the small ball associated to the corresponding node.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX) \end{equation} using the following norm. We use the usual $(k,2)$ norm away from the ends. Over an end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$, we consider the local trivialization \eqref{localPTcoords}, in which a section of $u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX$ simply becomes a function $\xi:[0,\infty)\times S^1\to T_{u_0(n)}X$. In terms of this function, the contribution from the end to the norm squared is: \begin{equation} \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+\int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}\biggl[\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt \end{equation} The derivatives of $\xi$ are measured with respect to the standard metric on $[0,\infty)\times S^1$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any end we have a uniform bound on $\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|e^{\delta s}$ and $\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|e^{\delta s}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted Sobolev norm on $C_0$ with weight $e^{2\delta s}$ in the ends, measuring $\xi-\xi(n)$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Equation endnorm
nodes.statement: \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+\int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}\biggl[\left|\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt
nodes.label: endnorm

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} using the following norm. We use the usual $(k,2)$ norm away from the ends/necks. Over an end, the contribution to the norm squared is \eqref{endnorm}. Over a neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, we again think of a section as a function $\xi:[0,6S]\times S^1\to T_{u_0(n)}X$, and the contribution to the norm squared is: \begin{equation*} \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\biggr|^2+\int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(s,t)-\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt \end{equation*} Of course, for fixed $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, this norm is equivalent to not weighting the necks, though the two norms are not uniformly equivalent as $\alpha\to 0$. The weight in the necks is important since the key point is to establish certain estimates which are uniform as $\alpha\to 0$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any neck we have a uniform bound on $\left|\xi(s,t)-\int_{S^1}\xi(3S,t)\,dt\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ and $\left|D^j\xi(s,t)\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted norm on $C_\alpha$ with weight $e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ in the necks, relative to the average at the neck's center.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k-1,2,\delta}$ of $(0,1)$-forms
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d$, we define a weighted Sobolev space: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. We use the usual $(k-1,2)$ norm away from the ends/necks. Over an end or neck, we trivialize $(T\tilde C_\alpha,j_y)$ over $\mathbb C$ by the basis vector $\frac\partial{\partial s}$, and we trivialize $TX$ via \eqref{localPTcoords}, and hence the section is simply a function $\eta$ from the end/neck to $T_{u_0(n)}X$. In terms of this function, the contribution to the norm squared is (for end/neck respectively): \begin{align} \int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt\\ \int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt \end{align} By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, in any end (resp.\ neck) we have a uniform bound on $\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|e^{\delta s}$ (resp.\ $\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|e^{\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$) ($1\leq j\leq k-3$) linear in $\left\|\eta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weighted $(k-1,2)$ norm on $(0,1)$-forms over ends and necks.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \int_{[0,\infty)\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;ds\,dt\\ \int_{[0,6S]\times S^1}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(s,t)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;ds\,dt

nodes.name: Direct sum norm

nodes.name: Reason for the vertical inclusions
nodes.statement_short: The inclusions $W^{k,2}\hookrightarrow W^{k,2,\delta}$ hold because pulled-back norms on the end are bounded, using $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement: Let us remark on the reason for the vertical inclusions in \eqref{fredholmsquare}.  For the leftmost vertical inclusion, one just needs to check that for a function $f:D^2\to\mathbb R$, the $W^{k,2,\delta}$ norm of its pullback to $[0,\infty)\times S^1$ is bounded linearly by its $W^{k,2}$ norm on $D^2$.  For the rightmost vertical inclusion, one checks the same property for $1$-forms.  In both of these calculations we use the fact that $\delta<1$.

nodes.name: Proof (F724)
nodes.statement:
The operator $D_{\alpha,y}$ equals $(
abla\xi)^{0,1}_y$ plus compact terms (by Lemma ef{linearizedformula}), so it is equivalent to show that $\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}_y$ is Fredholm (and we may forget about $E$). Here $
abla$ is really the pullback of $
abla$ via $u_\alpha$. Thus it suffices to show that if $V$ is a smooth complex vector bundle over a nodal Riemann surface $C$ equipped with a smooth connection $
abla$, then the horizontal maps:  egin{equation}  egin{tikzcd}[column sep = large] W^{k,2,\delta}(C,V)\ar{r}{\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)\ W^{k,2}(C,V)\ar[hook]{u}\ar{r}{\xi\mapsto(
abla\xi)^{0,1}}&W^{k-1,2}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)\ar[hook]{u} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} are Fredholm. For the bottom map, the Fredholm property is standard. Indeed, $W^{k,2}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2}(	ilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and $
abla^{0,1}:W^{k,2}(	ilde C,V)	o W^{k-1,2}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)$ is Fredholm by elliptic regularity on the compact Riemann surface $	ilde C$. For the top map, the Fredholm property follows from results of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen} concerning the Fredholmness (in weighted Sobolev spaces) of elliptic operators on manifolds with cylindrical ends. Specifically, $W^{k,2,\delta}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2,\delta}(	ilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and the map $
abla^{0,1}:W^{k,2,\delta}(	ilde C,V)	o W^{k-1,2,\delta}(	ilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)$ is Fredholm by the theory of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen}. This uses the fact that the weight $\delta\in(0,1)$ is not an eigenvalue of the asymptotic linearized operator in any end (the set of eigenvalues in any end is precisely $\mathbb Z$, corresponding to the powers $\{z^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ on $D^2\setminus 0$). Let us also remark that both of these Fredholmness statements are easier at $p=2$ than for general $p\in(1,\infty)$, since for $p=2$ one can use Fourier analysis (after localizing the problem with a partition of unity). Now it remains to show that the induced maps on kernel and cokernel are isomorphisms. The map on kernels is obviously injective, and the map on cokernels is easily seen to be surjective (use the fact that the image of the top horizontal map is closed and the fact that the rightmost vertical inclusion is dense). For the surjectivity of the map on kernels and the injectivity of the map on cokernels, it suffices to show that if $D_{\alpha,y}\xi=\eta$ for $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta}$ and $\eta\in W^{k-1,2}$, then $\xi\in W^{k,2}$. To show $\xi\in W^{k,2}$, it suffices to argue locally on one side of a given node. Certainly (the vector field part of) $\xi$ extends continuously to $C_\alpha$ (by definition of $W^{k,2,\delta}$), and this continuous extension satisfies $D_{\alpha,y}\xi=\eta+\epsilon$ where $\epsilon$ is a distribution on $	ilde C_\alpha$ valued in $\Omega^{0,1}_{	ilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX$ and supported inside the (inverse images of the) nodes. By elliptic regularity, it suffices to show that $\epsilon=0$. 
ewlength\arrowwidthawesome \settowidth{\arrowwidthawesome}{$
rightarrow$} Now for smooth test functions $\varphi$ supported inside a small neighborhood of the support of $\epsilon$, we have:  egin{equation} \langle\epsilon,\varphiangle=\langle D_{\alpha,y}\xi-\eta,\varphiangle=\langle\xi,D_{\alpha,y}^\ast\varphiangle-\langle\eta,\varphiangle \end{equation} We thus obtain the bound $\left|\langle\epsilon,\varphiangleight|\leq c\left\|\varphiight\|_{1,1}$ since $D_{\alpha,y}^\ast$ is a first order operator and $\xi,\eta$ are bounded (as they are continuous). On the other hand, $\epsilon$ is supported at a finite set of points, so it is a linear combination of $\delta$-functions and their derivatives. Hence $\epsilon$ does not satisfy the bound $\left|\langle\epsilon,\varphiangleight|\leq c\left\|\varphiight\|_{1,1}$ (recall that $W^{1,1}\hookrightarrow\hspace{-\arrowwidthawesome}
rightarrow C^0$ since we are in two dimensions) unless $\epsilon=0$, as desired.

nodes.statement_short: Bottom map Fredholm by elliptic regularity
nodes.name: Bottom map Fredholm by elliptic regularity
nodes.statement: For the bottom map, the Fredholm property is standard.  Indeed, $W^{k,2}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2}(\tilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and $\nabla^{0,1}:W^{k,2}(\tilde C,V)\to W^{k-1,2}(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)$ is Fredholm by elliptic regularity on the compact Riemann surface $\tilde C$.

nodes.statement_short: Top map Fredholm by Lockhart--McOwen, as $\delta$ is not an eigenvalue
nodes.name: Top map Fredholm by Lockhart--McOwen, as $\delta$
nodes.statement: For the top map, the Fredholm property follows from results of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen} concerning the Fredholmness (in weighted Sobolev spaces) of elliptic operators on manifolds with cylindrical ends.  Specifically, $W^{k,2,\delta}(C,V)$ lies inside $W^{k,2,\delta}(\tilde C,V)$ as a closed subspace of finite codimension, and the map $\nabla^{0,1}:W^{k,2,\delta}(\tilde C,V)\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C}\otimes_{\mathbb C} V)$ is Fredholm by the theory of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen}.  This uses the fact that the weight $\delta\in(0,1)$ is not an eigenvalue of the asymptotic linearized operator in any end (the set of eigenvalues in any end is precisely $\mathbb Z$, corresponding to the powers $\{z^n\}_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ on $D^2\setminus 0$).  Let us also remark that both of these Fredholmness statements are easier at $p=2$ than for general $p\in(1,\infty)$, since for $p=2$ one can use Fourier analysis (after localizing the problem with a partition of unity).

nodes.name: Proof (F730)
nodes.statement: Away from the ends/necks of $C_\alpha$, the expression is zero when $y=0$ (since $(0,0,u_0,\{x_i^0\},e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$) and more generally it follows easily that its $j$th derivative is bounded pointwise by $c_j\left|y\right|$. In the ends of $C_\alpha$, the expression is zero. In a given neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, argue as follows. Recall that $\lambda$ vanishes in the ends/necks, so we just have to bound $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$. Now $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$ is only nonzero over $[S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1]$; by symmetry we may just work over $[S-1,S]$. Now since $u_0$ is smooth, it and all its derivatives decay exponentially in any cylindrical end $[0,\infty)\times S^1$ (since every end is holomorphically conjugate to the map $[0,\infty)\times S^1\to D^2$ given by $z=e^{-s-it}$). Precisely, we have the following pointwise bound over $[S-1,S]$: \begin{equation} \left|D^ju_0(s,t)\right|\leq c_je^{-S} \end{equation} (derivatives with respect to $s$ and $t$). It follows from the definition of $u_\alpha$ that the same bound holds for $u_\alpha$. Thus the contribution of $[S-1,S]$ to the norm of $\bar\partial_yu_\alpha$ is bounded by a constant times $e^{S\delta}e^{-S}$.

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse $T_{\alpha,y}$
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)\to W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E \end{equation} as the composition: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{id}\circ Q_{0,0}\circ I_y\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ\operatorname{break} \end{equation} of maps in the following diagram, to be defined below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar{r}{D_{0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_0^\ast TX)\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{I_y}\\ W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}{\operatorname{id}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_0^\ast TX) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} ($D_{0|\alpha,y}$ denotes the linearized operator at $u_{0|\alpha}$). We fix once and for all a smooth family of $(j_0,j_y)$-linear identifications $I_y:(T\tilde C_0,j_0)\to(T\tilde C_0,j_y)$ which are the identity over the ends/necks. This gives rise to the bottom right vertical map in \eqref{biginversediagram}. We define the middle vertical maps in \eqref{biginversediagram} using parallel transport (equivalently, using the local trivializations defined by \eqref{localPTcoords}). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX) \end{equation} as follows. Fix a smooth function $\bar\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ such that: \begin{equation} \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1 \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TX)$. Away from the ends with $\alpha\ne 0$, $\operatorname{break}(\eta)$ is simply $\eta$. In any particular end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ with $\alpha\ne 0$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{break}(\eta)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \eta(s,t)&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot\eta(s,t)&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D \end{equation} Let $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TX)_D$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\xi)$ is simply $\xi$. In any particular neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding ends $(s,t)\in[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ and $(s',t')\in[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$). Note that the cutoff of $\xi(s,t)$ occurs around $4S\in[0,6S]$, where the weight $e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}$ is much smaller than the weight $e^{2\delta s}$ at $4S\in[0,\infty)$. We will see in the proof of Lemma \ref{approxtop} that this makes it easy to derive the desired estimates on $\bar\partial\mathrm{glue}(\xi)$. This trick was explained to us by Abouzaid and attributed to Fukaya--Oh--Ohta--Ono \cite{foootechnicaldetails}.

nodes.name: Neumann series right inverse
nodes.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, let $D:X\to Y$ and $T:Y\to X$ be bounded, and suppose $\epsilon:=\left\|DT-\mathbf 1_Y\right\|<1$. Then: \begin{equation} Q:=T\cdot\sum_{n\geq 0}(\mathbf 1_Y-DT)^n \end{equation} converges and satisfies $DQ=\mathbf 1_Y$. In addition, we have the following estimates: \begin{equation} \left\|Q\right\|\leq\frac 1{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\|\qquad \left\|Q-T\right\|\leq\frac\epsilon{1-\epsilon}\left\|T\right\| \end{equation}

Then for all $\delta>0$ there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(n,c,\delta)>0$ such that if for all $1<i\leq n$: \begin{equation} D_i\xi=B_{i-1}\eta\implies\left\|D_{i-1}G_{i-1}\xi-\eta\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|\xi\right\| \end{equation} then we have: \begin{equation} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\delta \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof (F772)
nodes.statement: We work by induction on $n$. The case $n=1$ is clear: $\epsilon(1,c,\delta)=\infty$. Now assume $n\geq 2$. Let us also assume without loss of generality that $c\geq 1$. Applying \eqref{keytocheckforARI} to $i=n$ and $\xi=Q_nB_{n-1}\eta$, we see that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{n-1}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}\right\|\leq\epsilon\cdot\left\|Q_n\right\|\left\|B_{n-1}\right\|\leq\epsilon c^2 \end{equation} Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 12c^{-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12$. Then by Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} applied to $T=G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}$, we see that there exists $Q_{n-1}$ with $D_{n-1}Q_{n-1}=\mathbf 1_{Y_{n-1}}$ and: \begin{equation} \left\|Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2c^3\qquad\left\|Q_{n-1}-G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^5 \end{equation} Now we see that: \begin{multline} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1\right\|\\ \leq c^{2n-3}\left\|G_{n-1}Q_nB_{n-1}-Q_{n-1}\right\|\leq 2\epsilon c^{2n+2} \end{multline} Let us require that $\epsilon\leq\frac 14\delta c^{-2n-2}$, so the above bound is $\leq\frac 12\delta$. Let us also require that $\epsilon\leq\epsilon(n-1,2c^3,\frac 12\delta)$ (which exists by the induction hypothesis), so that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_1G_1\cdots G_{n-2}Q_{n-1}B_{n-2}\cdots B_1-\mathbf 1_{Y_1}\right\|\leq\frac 12\delta \end{equation} Combining \eqref{approxclosetogiven} and \eqref{inductionbound}, we get the desired bound \eqref{approxbootstrappingworks}.

nodes.name: Proof (F788)
nodes.statement: This is similar to McDuff--Salamon \cite[p68, Proposition 3.5.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. We have already remarked that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}\xi$ is defined for $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Let $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}$ at $\zeta$ applied to $\xi$. So, for instance, $D_{\alpha,y}(\xi):=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)$. It suffices to show that: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,\xi)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ uniformly as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ (one recovers \eqref{quadestgoal} by integrating $\int_{\xi_1}^{\xi_2}\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(0,d\zeta)-\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,d\zeta)$). For $\zeta\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$, let: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C}(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the $\bar\partial$-section based at $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta:C_\alpha\to X$ and $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$ (so, for example, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}:=\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,0}$). Let: \begin{equation} D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX)_D\oplus E\to W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C}(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta)^\ast TX) \end{equation} denote the derivative of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ at zero. Of course, $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be calculated as in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and the result is the same (i.e.\ we just substitute $(\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta,e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)$ in place of $(u_\alpha,e_0)$). Now the first step in proving \eqref{derivislip} is to express $\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)$ in terms of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$. To do this, we observe that: \begin{equation} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(a)=\left[\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\right]\left[\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Bigl((\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a)\oplus(\operatorname{proj}_Ea-\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta)\Bigr)\right] \end{equation} We now differentiate with respect to $a$ and evaluate at $a=\zeta$ and $\dot a=\xi$. We find: \begin{multline} \mathcal F_{\alpha,y}'(\zeta,\xi)=\Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y,\zeta}(0)\bigr)\\ +\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{proj}_E\xi\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{multline} We rewrite the first term: \begin{equation} \Biggl[\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}a\to u_\alpha}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to\exp_{u_\alpha}a}\Bigr)\Biggr]\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\bigl(\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\bigr) \end{equation} We know that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$ (Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmall} implies that $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(0)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ is bounded as $(\alpha,y)\to 0$, and from this one may derive a bound on $\left\|\mathcal F_{\alpha,y}(\zeta)\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ in terms of $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$). The operator $[\frac d{da}(\mathsf{PT}\circ\mathsf{PT})]\mathsf{PT}$ in front is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to\operatorname{End}(TX)$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Since $H$ satisfies $H(0,\cdot)=H(\cdot,0)=0$, it follows that $\left\|H(\zeta,\xi)\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$ for $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta},\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$. Hence the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$-norm of the first term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$, so for the purposes of proving \eqref{derivislip} it may be ignored. The second term in \eqref{changebasisderivative} is approximated by $\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\left[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\left(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi\right)\right]$ with error: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\biggl[\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\xi-\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} which we may write as: \begin{equation} \mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\Biggl[D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\Biggl(\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\biggl[\xi-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u_\alpha}\frac d{da}\biggr|_{\begin{smallmatrix}a=\zeta\cr\dot a=\xi\end{smallmatrix}}\Bigl(\exp_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}^{-1}\exp_{u_\alpha}a\Bigr)\biggr]\oplus 0\Biggr)\Biggr] \end{equation} Now the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k-1,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of the outer $\mathsf{PT}$ is bounded uniformly for $(\alpha,y)\to 0$ and $\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\leq c'$, as is the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}$ norm of $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ and the $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k,2,\delta)}$ norm of the following $\mathsf{PT}$. The difference $\xi-\mathsf{PT}\frac d{da}()$ is of the form $H(\zeta,\xi)$ for a smooth (non-linear) bundle map $H:TX\oplus TX\to TX$ (defined in a neighborhood of $\zeta=\xi=0$). Hence the error \eqref{errorexpression} has $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta}$ bounded by $c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta}$. Thus we have reduced the estimate \eqref{derivislip} to proving: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,y}-\mathsf{PT}_{\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta\to u}\circ D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}\circ\mathsf{PT}_{u_\alpha\to\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta}\right\|_{(k,2,\delta)\to(k-1,2,\delta)}\leq c\cdot\left\|\zeta\right\|_{k,2,\delta} \end{equation} We calculated $D_{\alpha,y}$ in Lemma \ref{linearizedformula}, and $D_{\alpha,y,\zeta}$ may be expressed in exactly the same way (specifically, it is obtained by taking the expression for $D_{\alpha,y}$ and replacing every occurence of $u_\alpha$ with $\exp_{u_\alpha}\zeta$ and $e_0$ by $e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\zeta$). nodes.name: Proof (F816)
nodes.statement: Suppose that: \begin{equation} (\alpha,y,u_{\alpha,y,\kappa},e_{\alpha,y,\kappa})=(\alpha',y',u_{\alpha',y',\kappa'},e_{\alpha',y',\kappa'}) \end{equation} We see immediately that $(\alpha,y)=(\alpha',y')$. Now we see that: \begin{align} \exp_{u_\alpha}\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\exp_{u_\alpha}(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}\\ \operatorname{proj}_E\kappa_{\alpha,y}&=\operatorname{proj}_E(\kappa')_{\alpha,y} \end{align} Since the norms of $\kappa_{\alpha,y}$ and $\kappa_{\alpha,y}'$ go to zero as $(\alpha,y,\kappa,\kappa')\to 0$ (in $W^{k,2,\delta}$, and hence in $C^0$) and the injectivity radius of the exponential map is fixed, we see that $\kappa_{\alpha,y}=(\kappa')_{\alpha,y}$. nodes.name: A priori estimate on long pseudo-holomorphic necks
nodes.statement: For all $\mu<1$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ with the following property. Let $J$ be a smooth almost complex structure on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ satisfying $\left\|J-J_{\mathrm{std}}\right\|_{C^2}\leq\epsilon$ (measured with respect to $g_{\mathrm{std}}$). There exists $c_k<\infty$ depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^k}$ with the following property. Let $u:[-R,R]\times S^1\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic. If: \begin{equation} \int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt<\epsilon \end{equation} Then: \begin{equation} \left|(D^ku)(s,t)\right|\leq c_k\cdot e^{\mu\cdot(\left|s\right|-R)}\left(\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2} \end{equation} for $\left|s\right|\leq R-1$.
