nodes.name: $W^{1,2}$ norm decays exponentially
nodes.statement: For all $\mu<1$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ with the following property. Let $u:[-R,R]\times S^1\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ satisfying $\left\|J-J_{\mathrm{std}}\right\|\leq\epsilon$ (measured with respect to $g_{\mathrm{std}}$). Then: \begin{equation*} \left(\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt\right)^{1/2}\leq c\cdot e^{\mu\cdot(r-R)}\left(\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt\right)^{1/2} \end{equation*} for $0\leq r\leq R$.
nodes.statement_short: On a long holomorphic cylinder the $W^{1,2}$ energy decays exponentially away from the boundary.
assumptions: Let $u:[-R,R]\times S^1\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.11.29
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p99, Lemma 4.7.3]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{std}}:=\frac 12\sum_jx_j\,dy_j-y_j\,dx_j$. Note the identity: \begin{equation} \sum_jz_j\,d\bar z_j=\frac 12\sum_jd\left|z_j\right|^2-2i\lambda_{\mathrm{std}} \end{equation} Let $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ be a smooth loop. Write the Fourier series $\gamma(t)=\sum_ka_ke^{ikt}\in\mathbb C^n$ where $a_k\in\mathbb C^n$. Now using \eqref{zdzbaridentity}, we see that: \begin{equation*} \int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_{\mathrm{std}}=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_j\gamma^\ast(z_j\,d\bar z_j)=\frac i2\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=\pi\sum_kk\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation*} We may also calculate: \begin{equation} \int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt=\int_{S^1}\sum_{k,\ell}a_k\bar a_\ell(ik)(-i\ell)e^{i(k-\ell)t}\,dt=2\pi\sum_kk^2\left|a_k\right|^2 \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \left|\int_{S^1}\gamma^\ast\lambda_{\mathrm{std}}\right|\leq\frac 12\int_{S^1}\Bigl|\frac{d\gamma}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} Let: \begin{equation} E(r):=\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,ds\,dt\approx\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\omega_{\mathrm{std}}=\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}u^\ast\lambda_{\mathrm{std}} \end{equation} ($\approx$ means equality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). Applying \eqref{sympisoperimetric}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim\frac 12\int_{\partial[-r,r]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} ($\lesssim$ means inequality up to a factor which can be made arbitrarily close to $1$ by taking $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small). The right hand side above equals $\frac 12E'(r)$, so we have $E'(r)\gtrsim 2E(r)$, and hence $E'(r)\geq 2\mu E(r)$ (for $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small), from which we conclude that $E(r)\leq e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}E(R)$. Using \eqref{boundonenergyfromboundary} to bound $E(R)$, we see that: \begin{equation} E(r)\lesssim e^{2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\frac 12\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} We have: \begin{equation} E(r)\approx\frac 12\int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt \end{equation} Hence we conclude that: \begin{equation} \int_{[-r,r]\times S^1}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{ds}\Bigr|^2+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\biggr]\,ds\,dt\lesssim e^{ 2\mu\cdot(r-R)}\int_{\partial[-R,R]\times S^1}\Bigl|\frac{du}{dt}\Bigr|^2\,dt \end{equation} which is the desired estimate.
nodes.statement_short: Symplectic isoperimetric inequality via Fourier series yields $E'(r)\geq 2\mu E(r)$, which integrates to exponential decay.

nodes.name: $W^{1,2}$ controls $W^{1,\infty}$
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be an almost complex structure on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$; there exist $\epsilon>0$ and $c<\infty$, depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$ (measured with respect to $g_{\mathrm{std}}$) with the following property. nodes.statement_short: Small energy on a square bounds the derivative at the center by the energy (mean value inequality).
assumptions: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.11.30
nodes.statement: This proof is essentially lifted from McDuff--Salamon \cite[p80, Lemma 4.3.1]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. Let $w:=\frac 12u_x^2+\frac 12u_y^2$ (using the standard inner product $g_{\mathrm{std}}$), so $w:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$. Now we calculate: \begin{equation} w_{xx}+w_{yy}=\Bigl[u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2\Bigr]+\Bigl[u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\Bigr] \end{equation} Now differentiating \eqref{formulaforDeltau} yields: \begin{align*} u_{xxx}+u_{xyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xx}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_x)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xx})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{xy}\\ u_{xxy}+u_{yyy}=&\ddot J(u,u_y,u_y)\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_{yy})\circ u_x+\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_{xy}\\ &-\ddot J(u,u_x,u_y)\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_{xy})\circ u_y-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_{yy} \end{align*} Now we conclude that: \begin{align*} \bigl|u_x\cdot(u_{xxx}&+u_{xyy})+u_y\cdot(u_{xxy}+u_{yyy})\bigr|\\ &\leq 2\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^3\left|u_y\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|^3)\\ &\qquad+2\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}\cdot(\left|u_x\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_y\right|^2\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_x\right|\left|u_y\right|\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}w\cdot(\left|u_{xx}\right|+\left|u_{xy}\right|+\left|u_{yy}\right|)\\ &\leq c\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}w^2+c\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2w^2+\frac 1{100}(u_{xx}^2+2u_{xy}^2+u_{yy}^2) \end{align*} Plugging this into \eqref{formulaforDeltaw}, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta w=w_{xx}+w_{yy}\geq -c\cdot (\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}+\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}^2)w^2 \end{equation} Now we may apply a mean value inequality McDuff--Salamon \cite[p81, Lemma 4.3.2]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp} or Wehrheim \cite[p306, Theorem 1.1]{wehrheimmeanvalue} to see that there exist $\epsilon>0$ and $c<\infty$ such that if $\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy<\epsilon$, then $w(\frac 12,\frac 12)\leq c\cdot\int_{[0,1]^2}w\,dx\,dy$. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\Delta w\geq -c w^2$ for the energy density $w$ and apply a mean value inequality.

nodes.name: $W^{1,\infty}$ controls $W^{k,p}$
nodes.statement: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$. For all $k\geq 1$, there exists $c_k<\infty$ depending only on $\left\|J\right\|_{C^k}$ such that if: \begin{equation} \sup_{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|\biggr]\leq 1 \end{equation} then: \begin{equation} \left|(D^ku)({\textstyle\frac 12},{\textstyle\frac 12})\right|\leq c_k\cdot\sup_{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2}\biggl[\Bigl|\frac{du}{dx}\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{du}{dy}\Bigr|\biggr] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic regularity: a $W^{1,\infty}$ bound on a holomorphic map controls all higher derivatives at the center.
assumptions: Let $u:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to B^{2n}(1)$ be $J$-holomorphic for an almost complex structure $J$ on $B^{2n}(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$.
nodes.label: Woneinftycontrolsall

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.11.31
nodes.statement: For more details see McDuff--Salamon \cite[p533, \S B.4]{mcduffsalamonJholsymp}. The $\bar\partial$-equation for $u$ may be written as: \begin{equation} u_y=J(u)\circ u_x \end{equation} Differentiating with respect to $x$ and to $y$, we conclude that: \begin{align} u_{xy}&=\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xx}\\ u_{xx}&=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xy} \end{align} Combining these and using the fact that $\dot J$ and $J$ anticommute, we conclude that: \begin{equation} \Delta u=u_{xx}+u_{yy}=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x-\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_y \end{equation} Now a standard elliptic bootstrapping argument based on \eqref{formulaforDeltau} gives the desired result. By hypothesis, we have an $L^\infty$ bound in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau}, which gives a $W^{2,p}$ bound ($2<p<\infty$) on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$. Now we have a $W^{1,p}$ bound on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau} in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$, which gives a $W^{3,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$. Iterating, we get a $W^{k,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^{k-1}}$, which is enough. There is no need to worry about elliptic regularity estimates near the boundary since we can shrink the domain slightly after each iteration.
nodes.statement_short: Elliptic bootstrapping from the formula for $\Delta u$, gaining one derivative per iteration.

nodes.statement: u_{xy}&=\dot J(u,u_x)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xx}\\ u_{xx}&=\dot J(u,u_y)\circ u_x+J(u)\circ u_{xy}

nodes.statement_short: Iterate $W^{k,p}$ estimates.
nodes.statement: Now a standard elliptic bootstrapping argument based on \eqref{formulaforDeltau} gives the desired result.  By hypothesis, we have an $L^\infty$ bound in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$ on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau}, which gives a $W^{2,p}$ bound ($2<p<\infty$) on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^1}$.  Now we have a $W^{1,p}$ bound on the right hand side of \eqref{formulaforDeltau} in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$, which gives a $W^{3,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^2}$.  Iterating, we get a $W^{k,p}$ bound on $u$ in terms of $\left\|J\right\|_{C^{k-1}}$, which is enough.  There is no need to worry about elliptic regularity estimates near the boundary since we can shrink the domain slightly after each iteration.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the gluing map (Gromov--Witten)
nodes.statement: The restriction of \eqref{gluingmap} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,u_0,e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map near zero covers a neighborhood of the basepoint in the moduli space.
conclusions: The restriction of \eqref{gluingmap} to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $(0,0,u_0,e_0)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$.
nodes.label: gluingsurjective

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition B.11.32 (surjectivity of gluing)
nodes.statement: Let $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)\in\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ be a sequence converging to $(0,0,u_0,\{x^0_j\},e_0)$. We must show that for $i$ sufficiently large, $(\alpha_i,y_i,u_i,\{x^i_j\},e_i)$ is contained in the image of the map \eqref{gluingmap}. We may restrict to sequences rather than nets since the topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is first countable (recall the definition of the topology following \eqref{Mbarfirstdef}; it is even a metric topology). This is convenient when we apply Arzel\`a--Ascoli. Let us define $\xi_i\in C^\infty(C_{\alpha_i},u_{\alpha_i}^\ast TX)_D\oplus E$ by the property: \begin{align} u_i&=\exp_{u_{\alpha_i}}\xi_i\\ e_i&=e_0+\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i \end{align} (and the exponential follows the shortest geodesic). Obviously $\operatorname{proj}_E\xi_i\to 0$ and $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_\infty\to 0$. Now we claim that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes, or equivalently, that $\xi_i\to 0$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes of $C_0$. To see this argue as follows. The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$. Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$). Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes. Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes. Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$. This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes. It follows that in fact $u_i$ itself converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes. In the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, note that $u_i$ is genuinely $J$-holomorphic (the $\lambda$ term vanishes), so we may apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate} to conclude that $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ (here using the fact that $\delta<1$). We should remark that to apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate}, we need to be able to choose some $M<\infty$ such that for any neck $[0,6S]\times S^2\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$, the derivatives of $u_i$ restricted to $\partial[M,6S-M]\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$ are bounded by $\delta$ (the constant in Proposition \ref{neckestimate}). Such an $M$ exists because of our earlier observation that $u_i\to u$ in $C^\infty$ on compact sets away from the nodes, and we can certainly choose a large $M$ such that the derivatives of $u$ over $\{M\}\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ (any end) are arbitrarily small. Let us define $\kappa_i\in K$ by the property that $\xi_i\in(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i}+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$. Now since $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ and the norms on the left and right of \eqref{QKtoall} are uniformly commensurable, we see that $\kappa_i\to 0$. Now the uniqueness in Proposition \ref{newtoniteration} shows that $\xi_i=(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ for $i$ sufficiently large. Thus we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Take a convergent sequence; Gromov--Schwarz, bootstrapping and Arzela--Ascoli give $C^\infty_{loc}$ convergence, the neck estimate gives weighted convergence. Newton--Picard uniqueness then puts the sequence in the image of the gluing map.

nodes.name: Claim: $C^\infty$ convergence away from nodes
nodes.statement_short: Prove $u_i\to u$ in $C^\infty_{loc}$ away from nodes.
nodes.statement: Now we claim that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes, or equivalently, that $\xi_i\to 0$ in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes of $C_0$.  To see this argue as follows.  The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$.  Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$).  Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes.  Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes.  Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$.  This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.  It follows that in fact $u_i$ itself converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.

nodes.name: Graph trick
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite thickened equation as honest holomorphic equation for the graph.
nodes.statement: To see this argue as follows.  The thickened holomorphic curve equation from \eqref{modulispace} is equivalent to an honest holomorphic curve equation for the graph $u:C\to C\times X$ where the almost complex structure on $C\times X$ is defined in terms of $\lambda(e)$.

nodes.name: Gromov--Schwarz
nodes.statement_short: Uniform derivative bounds away from nodes.
nodes.statement: Hence the Gromov--Schwarz Lemma (see \cite[p316, 1.3.A]{gromov} or \cite[p223, Corollary 4.1.4]{muller}) applies and we conclude that $\left\|du_i\right\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, on compact sets away from the nodes (equivalently, the same for $\left\|d\xi_i\right\|_\infty$).

nodes.name: Bootstrapping
nodes.statement_short: All derivatives bounded.
nodes.statement: Now elliptic bootstrapping (as in the proof of Lemma \ref{Woneinftycontrolsall}) implies that all derivatives are bounded uniformly on compact sets away from the nodes.

nodes.name: Arzela--Ascoli
nodes.statement_short: Extract a convergent subsequence with limit $u$.
nodes.statement: Using Arzel\`a--Ascoli and diagonalization, we conclude that there exists a subsequence of $u_i$ which is convergent in the $C^\infty$ topology away from the nodes.  Since we know that $u_i\to u$ in the $C^0$ topology, the limit of this $C^\infty$ convergent subsequence must be $u$.

nodes.name: Subsequence argument
nodes.statement_short: Every subsequence has a convergent subsequence, so the sequence converges.
nodes.statement: This argument can be applied to any subsequence of $u_i$, so we conclude that every subsequence of $u_i$ has a subsequence which converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.  It follows that in fact $u_i$ itself converges to $u$ in $C^\infty$ away from the nodes.

nodes.name: Neck estimate
nodes.statement_short: Proposition B.11.28 gives weighted convergence in the necks.
nodes.statement: In the ends/necks of $C_{\alpha_i}$, note that $u_i$ is genuinely $J$-holomorphic (the $\lambda$ term vanishes), so we may apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate} to conclude that $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ (here using the fact that $\delta<1$).  We should remark that to apply Proposition \ref{neckestimate}, we need to be able to choose some $M<\infty$ such that for any neck $[0,6S]\times S^2\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$, the derivatives of $u_i$ restricted to $\partial[M,6S-M]\subseteq C_{\alpha_i}$ are bounded by $\delta$ (the constant in Proposition \ref{neckestimate}).  Such an $M$ exists because of our earlier observation that $u_i\to u$ in $C^\infty$ on compact sets away from the nodes, and we can certainly choose a large $M$ such that the derivatives of $u$ over $\{M\}\times S^1\subseteq[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ (any end) are arbitrarily small.

nodes.name: Newton--Picard uniqueness
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\xi_i$ via $K$ and $\operatorname{im}Q$; uniqueness shows it lies in the image.
nodes.statement: Let us define $\kappa_i\in K$ by the property that $\xi_i\in(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i}+\operatorname{im} Q_{\alpha_i,y_i}$.  Now since $\left\|\xi_i\right\|_{k,2,\delta}\to 0$ and the norms on the left and right of \eqref{QKtoall} are uniformly commensurable, we see that $\kappa_i\to 0$.  Now the uniqueness in Proposition \ref{newtoniteration} shows that $\xi_i=(\kappa_i)_{\alpha_i,y_i}$ for $i$ sufficiently large.  Thus we are done.

nodes.name: Injective locally surjective continuous map into a Hausdorff space is a local homeomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological space and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ be continuous. Suppose that: \begin{rlist} \item$f$ is injective. \item The restriction of $f$ to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $f(0)$. \end{rlist} Then there is an open set $0\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ such that $f(U)\subseteq X$ is open and $f:U\xrightarrow\sim f(U)$ is a homeomorphism.
assumptions: Let $X$ be a Hausdorff topological space and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ be continuous.
$f$ is injective.
The restriction of $f$ to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of $f(0)$.
conclusions: there is an open set $0\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ such that $f(U)\subseteq X$ is open and $f:U\xrightarrow\sim f(U)$ is a homeomorphism.
nodes.label: injectiveHdorffhomeo

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.12.33
nodes.statement: Let $B(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ denote the closed unit ball and $B(1)^\circ$ its interior. We know that $f(B(1))$ is compact (since $f$ is continuous) and Hausdorff (since $X$ is Hausdorff). We know that $f:B(1)\to f(B(1))$ is bijective (since $f$ is injective), so it is in fact a homeomorphism. Now choose an open subset $V\subseteq X$ with $f(0)\in V\subseteq f(B(1)^\circ)$ (which exists by assumption). Set $U=f^{-1}(V)\cap B(1)^\circ$, which is clearly open. Now $f:U\to f(U)$ is a homeomorphism onto its image (since $U\subseteq B(1)$), and $f(U)=V$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: A continuous bijection from a compact ball onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism; restrict to a small open set.

nodes.name: Compact ball embeds homeomorphically
nodes.statement_short: $f$ restricted to the closed ball is a homeomorphism onto its image.
nodes.statement: Let $B(1)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ denote the closed unit ball and $B(1)^\circ$ its interior.  We know that $f(B(1))$ is compact (since $f$ is continuous) and Hausdorff (since $X$ is Hausdorff).  We know that $f:B(1)\to f(B(1))$ is bijective (since $f$ is injective), so it is in fact a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Choose $U$
nodes.statement_short: Take $U=f^{-1}(V)\cap B(1)^\circ$.
nodes.statement: Now choose an open subset $V\subseteq X$ with $f(0)\in V\subseteq f(B(1)^\circ)$ (which exists by assumption).  Set $U=f^{-1}(V)\cap B(1)^\circ$, which is clearly open.  Now $f:U\to f(U)$ is a homeomorphism onto its image (since $U\subseteq B(1)$), and $f(U)=V$ is open.

nodes.name: Proof of the Gromov--Witten gluing theorem (openness, manifold, submersion)
nodes.statement: We have shown that the map $g:=$\eqref{gluingmap} is continuous, injective, and that its restriction to any neighborhood of zero is surjective onto a neighborhood of the image of zero. The target $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)$ is Hausdorff, and thus it follows from Lemma \ref{injectiveHdorffhomeo} that for some open neighborhood of zero $U\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R^{\dim\overline{\mathcal M}^d}\times K$, we have $g(U)$ is open and $g:U\xrightarrow\sim g(U)$ is a homeomorphism. Since $g$ respects the projection map from both sides to $\overline{\mathcal M}\times E/E'$, we obtain the desired conclusions (\ref{openness}), (\ref{manifold}), and (\ref{submersion}).
nodes.statement_short: The gluing map is continuous, injective and locally surjective, so Lemma B.12.33 makes it a local homeomorphism respecting projections.

nodes.name: Conclude parts

nodes.name: Proof of the orientation part of the Gromov--Witten gluing theorem
nodes.statement_short: Orient fibers of the submersion to $\overline{\mathcal M}$ via the kernel $K$; agreement on overlaps holds off the codimension-two nodal locus, so the identification extends.
nodes.statement:
To show Theorem \ref{mainresult}(\ref{orientation}) (the statement about orientations), observe that since $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ is a submersion, and $\overline{\mathcal M}$ is canonically oriented as a complex manifold, it follows that $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ is canonically identified with the orientation sheaf of the fibers of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}\to\overline{\mathcal M}$.  Now orienting a fiber is the same as orienting the kernel $K$.  It is standard to see that $\mathfrak o_K=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$.

This argument gives an identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ at every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$.  Via the gluing map, we get an identification of $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}$ with $\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ over a small neighborhood of every point in $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$.  It is probably straightforward to check that these identifications agree on overlaps (this is a concrete question about whether the projection map $K\to K_\alpha\to\ker D_{\alpha,y}$ is orientation preserving; a similar question is dealt with in Floer--Hofer \cite{floerhoferorientations}).

This is the best way to prove the desired result, but we can actually get away with a less technical argument.  Namely, it is easy to see that the identifications induced by points with smooth domain curve agree on overlaps (since then there is no gluing and we have a nice smooth Banach bundle picture).  Since the nodal locus is codimension two inside $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (this follows from the gluing map constructed previously), the identification $\mathfrak o_{\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}}=\mathfrak o_E\otimes\bigotimes_{i=1}^\ell\mathfrak o_{u(p_{n+i})^\ast N_{D/X}}^\vee$ away from the nodal locus extends uniquely to all of $\overline{\mathcal M}(X)^{\mathrm{reg}}$.

Note that $A_0$ is holomorphic even when $e_0\ne 0$, since $\lambda_\beta$ lands in $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM$ (as opposed to $\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_{\mathbb R} T(M\times S^1\times\mathbb R)$).

conclusions: every unstable bubble component of $C_0$ has a point where $du_0$ is injective

nodes.name: Proof of injective points on bubble components
nodes.statement_short: Case split: nonconstant holomorphic spheres have injective points; stabilized bubbles get one from transverse intersection with $D_\beta$.
nodes.statement: Indeed, on any unstable bubble component which is not contained in $(C_0)_\beta$ for any $\beta\in I$, the map $u_0$ is a (nonconstant!) $J(\ell_0(A_0(\cdot)))$-holomorphic sphere in $M$, and thus has such a point of injectivity.  Any unstable bubble component contained in $(C_0)_\beta$ for some $\beta\in I$ is stabilized by its intersections with the corresponding $D_\beta$.  Since these intersections are transverse (and $A_0$ is constant on the bubble), it follows that $du_0$ has a point of injectivity on such bubble components as well.  Hence the claim is valid.

u}	imes\prod_{ egin{smallmatrix}	ext{main components}\cr	ext{with $\ell_0$ non-constant}\end{smallmatrix}}(S^1	imes\mathbb R)^
u	imes\prod_{ egin{smallmatrix}	ext{main components}\cr	ext{with $\ell_0$ constant}\cr	ext{and $
u\geq 1$}\end{smallmatrix}}(S^1	imes\mathbb R)^
u\!/\mathbb R
\end{equation*}
be a diffeomorphism onto its image (in particular, this determines $\ast\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}$).  We fix, once and for all, a family $(j_y,A_y)_{y\in\mathbb R^\ast}$ satisfying the above properties (such a family always exists).

nodes.name: Equation Aymaps
nodes.statement: A_y^i:C^{(i)}_0\setminus\{q_{i-1},q_i\}\to S^1\times\mathbb R
nodes.label: Aymaps

nodes.name: Glued curve $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement_short: Glue $C_0$ at bubble and main nodes by truncating ends to length $6S$ and identifying them, with $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}$.
nodes.statement: Given a set of gluing parameters\footnote{We only care about what happens for gluing parameters $\alpha$ in a neighborhood of zero, and many constructions will only make sense (and many statements will only be true) for sufficiently small gluing parameters $\alpha$, even though this assumption is not always explicitly stated.  The same goes for the parameters $w$ (introduced below) and $y$.} $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ (where $d$ is the number of bubble nodes of $C_0$), we may glue $C_0$ to obtain a curve $C_\alpha$ as follows.  At a bubble node with gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S+i\theta}\in\mathbb C$, we truncate both bubble ends \eqref{bubbleends} from $S^1\times[0,\infty)$ to $S^1\times[0,6S]$, and we identify them via the map $s'=6S-s$ and $t'=\theta-t$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing).  At each main node $q_i$ with gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S}\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$, we truncate the main ends $S^1\times[N,\infty)\subseteq C_0^{(i)}$ and $S^1\times(-\infty,-N]\subseteq C_0^{(i+1)}$ incident at $q_i$ to $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$ and $S^1\times[-6S+N,-N]$, and we identify them via $s'=s-6S$ and $t'=t$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing).

nodes.name: Ends and necks of $C_\alpha$
nodes.statement: The curve $C_\alpha$ now has \emph{main ends} and \emph{bubble ends} (those where no gluing was performed), as well as \emph{bubble necks} $S^1\times[0,6S]$ and \emph{main necks} $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$.

nodes.name: Glued lines $(\coprod\mathbb R)_\alpha$
nodes.statement: We perform a similar gluing operation to $\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$, and we denote the result by $(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha$.  Namely, for the gluing parameter $\alpha=e^{-6S}\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ associated to $q_i$, we truncate the $i$th copy of $\mathbb R$ to $(-\infty,6S]$, we truncate the $(i+1)$st copy of $\mathbb R$ to $[-6S,\infty)$, and we identify $[0,6S]$ in the $i$th copy with $[-6S,0]$ in the $(i+1)$st copy via $s'=s-6S$ (if $\alpha=0$, then we do nothing).

nodes.name: Induced maps $A_y$ on $C_\alpha$
Equation
nodes.statement: A_y:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to S^1\times\Bigl(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\Bigr)_\alpha

nodes.name: Stratum-adapted gluing parameters
nodes.statement: Eventually, only a subset of $\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ will be relevant for us, namely the subset $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$ cut out by the requirement that if the break in the trajectory at $(v_i,\gamma_i)$ is dictated by the stratum $\mathfrak s$, then the gluing parameter at $q_i$ is zero.

nodes.name: Hypersurfaces $H^i$
nodes.statement: For every nonconstant $\ell_0^i$, choose a local hypersurface $H^i\subseteq\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}$ transverse to $\ell_0^i$ at $\ell_0^i(0)$.

nodes.name: Varied flow lines $\ell_w$
nodes.statement: For $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$ (where $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}$ denotes the product over those $i$ for which $\ell_0^i$ is nonconstant), let $\ell_w:\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R\to\Delta^n$ denote the unique trajectory satisfying $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_w^i(0)=w$ and broken at the same sequence of vertices $0=v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_k=n$.

nodes.name: Origin of $\prod H^i$
nodes.statement: We let $0:=\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_0^i(0)\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, so in this notation $\ell_w=\ell_0$ for $w=0$.

nodes.name: Thickened hypersurfaces $\bar H^i$
nodes.statement: Now choose a neighborhood parameterization $\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}\times[0,\epsilon)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{v_{i-1},\ldots,v_i\}}\to\Delta^n$, and define a local hypersurface $\bar H^i:=H^i\times[0,\epsilon)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{v_{i-1},\ldots,v_i\}}\subseteq\Delta^n$ and a projection map $\bar H^i\to H^i$.

nodes.name: Glued flow lines $\ell_{\alpha,w}$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, let $\ell_{\alpha,w}:(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha\to\Delta^n$ denote the trajectory characterized uniquely by the property that $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\ell_{\alpha,w}(0_i)\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}\bar H^i$ projects to $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, where $0_i\in(\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R)_\alpha$ denotes the image of $0$ in the $i$th copy of $\mathbb R$.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$
assumptions: for $(\alpha,w)$ close to $(0,0)$
conclusions: The existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$
nodes.statement: The existence and uniqueness of $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ for $(\alpha,w)$ close to $(0,0)$ follows simply by explicitly integrating the Morse flow on $\Delta^n$ from Definition \ref{simplexflows}.

nodes.name: Stratum-adapted hypersurfaces $(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$
nodes.statement: Eventually, only a subset of $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$ will be relevant for us, namely the subset $\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}H^i$, where $(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\subseteq H^i$ is the intersection of $H^i$ with $\Delta^{[i_0\ldots i_m]}\cap\Delta^{[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}=\Delta^{[i_0\ldots i_m]\cap[v_{i-1}\ldots v_i]}$, where $(\sigma|[i_0\ldots i_m],\gamma_a,\gamma_b)$ is the part of the stratum $\mathfrak s$ containing $\ell^i_0$.

nodes.name: Equation
nodes.statement: \lambda_\beta:E_\beta\to C^\infty(\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}\times M,\Omega^{0,1}_{\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}/\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,2+r_\beta}}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM)

nodes.name: Repackaged linear map $\lambda$
Equation
nodes.statement: \lambda:E\to C^\infty(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times C_0^r\times C_0\times M,\Omega^1_{C_0}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM)

nodes.name: Construction of $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$
nodes.statement_short: Pull back each $\lambda_\beta$ along the induced map $\phi^\beta$ from the subcurve $(C_\alpha)_\beta$, lift to $C_0$ and sum over $\beta$.
nodes.statement: Suppose we are given $e\in E=\bigoplus_{\beta\in I}E_\beta$, $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and $y\in\mathbb R^\ast$, along with points $x^1,\ldots,x^r\in C_0$, each in a small neighborhood of the corresponding $x_0^i$; let us define $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$ as a section $C_0\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM\subseteq\Omega^1_{C_0}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM$.  Consider the glued curve $C_\alpha$ equipped with the almost complex structure $j_y$ and the marked points $x^1,\ldots,x^r\in C_\alpha$ (descended from $C_0$).  Since $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, there is a subcurve $(C_\alpha)_\beta\subseteq C_\alpha$ corresponding to any given $\beta\in I$.  If we equip it with the $r_\beta$ marked points from $x^1,\ldots,x^r$ corresponding to $\beta$ (with respect to the reindexing from \S\ref{reindexingsec}), then this induces a unique map $\phi^\beta:(C_\alpha)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ (isomorphism onto a fiber) which is close to the given map $\phi_0^\beta:(C_0)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ (this assumes we are in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingneeded}; in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}, we instead have a map $\phi^\beta:((C_\alpha)_\beta)^{\mathrm{st}}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ close to the given map $\phi_0^\beta:((C_0)_\beta)^{\mathrm{st}}\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$, where $(C_\alpha)_\beta\to((C_\alpha)_\beta)^{\mathrm{st}}$ contracts those components all of whose constituent components of $(C_0)_\beta$ were contracted by $(C_0)_\beta\to((C_0)_\beta)^{\mathrm{st}}$).  Now the pullback of $\lambda_\beta(\operatorname{proj}_{E_\beta}e)$ under $\phi^\beta$ gives us a section $C_\alpha\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM$ (defined to be zero at those points not contained in $(C_\alpha)_\beta$).  We may assume without loss of generality that the ends of $C_0$ were chosen small enough so that this section vanishes over the ends/necks of $C_\alpha$, and hence gives rise to a well-defined lift to a section $C_0\times M\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb R} TM$.  We declare $\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,\cdot)$ to be the sum of these sections over all $\beta\in I$.  This defines the function $\lambda$, which is indeed of class $C^\infty$ since the partially defined composition $C_0\to C_\alpha\to(C_\alpha)_\beta\to\overline{\mathcal C}_{0,2+r_\beta}$ depends smoothly on $\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r$.

nodes.name: Moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.statement_short: Tuples $(\alpha,w,y,u,e,\{x^i\})$ with $u$ on $C_\alpha$ solving the thickened Floer equation and marked points hitting the $D_i$.
nodes.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ denote the moduli space of tuples $(\alpha,w,y,u,e,\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})$, where:
\begin{rlist}
\item$\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$.
\item$w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$.
\item$y\in\mathbb R^\ast$.
\item$u:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to M$ is smooth with finite energy, is asymptotic to $\gamma_i$ at $q_i\in C_\alpha$ (whenever the gluing parameter $\alpha$ at $q_i\in C_0$ is zero), and $u(p_i)\in D^\circ$ ($1\leq i\leq L$) and $u(p_i')\in H^\circ$ ($1\leq i\leq L'$).
\item$e\in E$.
\item$x^i\in C_\alpha$ (not nodes) satisfy $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell_{\alpha,w})((u\times A_y)(x^i))\in D_i$ with transverse intersection ($1\leq i\leq r$).
\item We require that:
\begin{multline} \Bigl(du+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}\\
+\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}=0
\end{multline}
\end{rlist}
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Equation finalHFdelbareqn
nodes.statement: \Bigl(du+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_y)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))}\\ +\lambda(e)(\alpha,y,x^1,\ldots,x^r,\cdot,u(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_y,J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}=0
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.label: finalHFdelbareqn

nodes.name: Topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$
nodes.statement: We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the topology of uniform convergence.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Base $\overline{\mathcal M}$ and bundle $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$$
nodes.statement: More precisely, let $\overline{\mathcal M}:=\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, and let $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$\to\overline{\mathcal M}$ be the bundle whose fiber over $\alpha$ is $C_\alpha^\$$, obtained from $C_\alpha$ by replacing each $q_i$ ($0\leq i\leq k$) with a copy of $S^1$ (thus $u$ as above extends continuously to $C_\alpha^\$$ and equals $\gamma_i(t)$ on the $S^1$ over $q_i$ whenever the corresponding $\alpha$ is zero).
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Topology on $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ (precise)
nodes.statement: We equip $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the obvious topology on $w\in\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}$, $y\in\mathbb R^\ast$, $e\in E$, $\{x^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r}\in\overline{\mathcal C}{}^r$, and the Hausdorff topology on the graph of $u$ inside $\overline{\mathcal C}{}^\$\times M$.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is a local model of the thickened moduli space
assumptions: as long as the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ has trivial automorphism group
conclusions: a neighborhood of this basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is canonically homeomorphic to a neighborhood of the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$
nodes.statement: Note that there is a distinguished basepoint $(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$.  Furthermore, a neighborhood of this basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ is canonically homeomorphic to a neighborhood of the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ (as long as the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ has trivial automorphism group).
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Justification of the local model in the $S^1$ setting
nodes.statement_short: In the $S^1$-equivariant setting appeal to Lemma morseistransverse.
nodes.statement: Note that to justify this statement in the setting of Proposition \ref{HFgluingSS}, we must appeal to Lemma \ref{morseistransverse}.
nodes.section: C.1.5 A new moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$

nodes.name: Sobolev parameters $k$ and $\delta$
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 6}$ (not to be confused with the number $k$ of main components of $C_0$) and a small real number $\delta\in(0,1)$ (we will be precise about how small $\delta$ must be shortly).

nodes.name: Weighted Banach manifold $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$
nodes.statement:
Let $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$ denote the smooth Banach manifold consisting of maps $u:C_\alpha\setminus\{q_0,\ldots,q_k\}\to M$ which are of locally of class $W^{k,2}$ such that for all positive main ends of $C_\alpha$ with corresponding node $q_i$, we have:
\begin{equation} \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\bigl[\exp^{-1}_{\gamma_i(t)}u(t,s)\bigr]\right|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
\end{equation}
for sufficiently large $N'<\infty$ (along with the analogous condition over negative main ends); this definition is independent of the choice of metric and connection used in \eqref{deltaweightedend}.

nodes.name: Equation deltaweightedend
nodes.statement: \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\bigl[\exp^{-1}_{\gamma_i(t)}u(t,s)\bigr]\right|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
nodes.label: deltaweightedend

nodes.name: Banach bundle $\mathcal E$
nodes.statement:
Over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$, we consider the smooth Banach bundle $\mathcal E$ whose fiber over $u:C_\alpha\to M$ is $W^{k-1,2,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$, namely the space of sections $\eta:\tilde C_\alpha\to\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$ which are locally of class $W^{k-1,2}$ and which satisfy:
\begin{equation} \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\Bigl|D^j\bigl[\mathsf{PT}_{u(t,s)\to\gamma_i(t)}\eta(t,s)\bigr]\Bigr|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
\end{equation}
over positive main ends (along with the analogous condition over negative main ends); this definition is independent of the choice of metric and connection used in \eqref{deltaweightedendII}.

nodes.name: Equation deltaweightedendII
nodes.statement: \int_{S^1\times[N',\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\Bigl|D^j\bigl[\mathsf{PT}_{u(t,s)\to\gamma_i(t)}\eta(t,s)\bigr]\Bigr|^2e^{2s\delta}\;dt\,ds<\infty
nodes.label: deltaweightedendII

nodes.name: Exponential decay at non-degenerate periodic orbits
assumptions: for every non-degenerate periodic orbit $\gamma$ of a smooth Hamiltonian $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ and every smooth $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure $J$ on $M$
conclusions: all derivatives of $u$ decay like $e^{-\delta s}$ for any $\delta<\delta_{H,J,\gamma}$
nodes.statement: It is well-known (see Proposition \ref{neckestimateHF} below) that for every non-degenerate periodic orbit $\gamma$ of a smooth Hamiltonian $H:M\times S^1\to\mathbb R$ and every smooth $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure $J$ on $M$, there exists $\delta_{H,J,\gamma}>0$ such that for every $u:S^1\times[0,\infty)\to M$ (resp.\ $u:S^1\times(-\infty,0]\to M$) of finite energy satisfying $(du+2dt\otimes X_H)^{0,1}_J=0$ and asymptotic to $u(t,\infty)=\gamma(t)$ (resp.\ $u(t,-\infty)=\gamma(t)$), all derivatives of $u$ decay like $e^{-\delta s}$ for any $\delta<\delta_{H,J,\gamma}$ (precisely, $\delta_{H,J,\gamma}$ is the smallest magnitude of any eigenvalue of the asymptotic linearized operator, which depends only on $\omega$, $H$, $J$, and $\gamma$).

nodes.name: Decay rates $\delta_i$
nodes.statement: In particular, for $0\leq i\leq k$, there is a corresponding $\delta_i:=\delta_{H(v_i),J(v_i),\gamma_i}>0$.

nodes.name: Choice of weight $\delta$
nodes.statement: We fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ with $\delta<\delta_i$ for all $i$; thus $u_1\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$.

nodes.name: Intersection functions $x^i(u)$
assumptions: since $k\geq 6$
conclusions: there are unique continuous functions:
nodes.statement:
Now since $k\geq 6$, there are unique continuous functions:
\begin{equation} x^i:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\to C_\alpha\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
\end{equation}
defined for $u$ in a neighborhood of $u_1\in W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)$, coinciding with the given $x^i_1\in C_\alpha$ at $u_1$, and which satisfy $(\operatorname{id}_{M\times S^1}\times\ell_{\alpha,y})((u\times A_y)(x^i(u)))\in D^i$ (the intersection is automatically transverse for $u$ close to $u_1$).

nodes.name: Equation intersectionsfunctionHF
nodes.statement: x^i:W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\to C_\alpha\quad(1\leq i\leq r)
nodes.label: intersectionsfunctionHF

nodes.name: Regularity of $x^i(u)$
conclusions: \eqref{intersectionsfunctionHF} are of class $C^{k-2}$
nodes.statement: Moreover, \eqref{intersectionsfunctionHF} are of class $C^{k-2}$ (see the discussion following \eqref{intersectionsfunction}).

nodes.name: Thickened Floer equation is a $C^{k-2}$ section
conclusions: the left hand side of \eqref{finalHFdelbareqn} is a $C^{k-2}$ section of $\mathcal E$ over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\times E$
nodes.statement: It follows that the left hand side of \eqref{finalHFdelbareqn} is a $C^{k-2}$ section of $\mathcal E$ over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)\times E$.

nodes.name: Fredholm property (Lockhart--McOwen)
assumptions: for $\delta>0$ as above
conclusions: this section is Fredholm
nodes.statement: By results of Lockhart--McOwen \cite{lockhartmcowen}, this section is Fredholm for $\delta>0$ as above (note that over each end, the almost complex structure on $M$ is constant and $\omega$-compatible).

nodes.name: Constrained subspace $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}$
nodes.statement: Let $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}$ denote the subspace cut out by the requirements $u(p_i)\in D$ and $u(p_i')\in H$.

nodes.name: Regular locus $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$
nodes.statement_short: A point is regular iff the thickened Floer section plus projection to $E/E'$ is transverse to zero there.
nodes.statement: We say that the given point $(\alpha,w,y,u_1,e_1,\{x^i_1\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\in\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ iff the section $(u,e)\mapsto\eqref{finalHFdelbareqn}\oplus e$ of $\mathcal E\oplus E/E'$ over $W^{k,2,\delta}(C_\alpha,M)_{D,H}\times E$ is transverse to the zero section at $(u_1,e_1)$ (it follows from elliptic regularity theory that this condition is independent of the choice of $k,\delta$ as above).

nodes.name: Regular loci correspond
assumptions: Now suppose that we take $E':=E_{I'}$ for $I'\subseteq I$
conclusions: the basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$
nodes.statement: Now suppose that we take $E':=E_{I'}$ for $I'\subseteq I$ and that the given basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$ was chosen inside the inverse image of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_{I'}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^{\mathrm{reg}}$.  Then, the basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ (this uses the fact that $L,L'$ were chosen to be minimal), and furthermore $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}\cap\operatorname{proj}_{E/E'}^{-1}(0)$ is contained inside the inverse image of $(\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_{I'}^{\leq\mathfrak s})^{\mathrm{reg}}$.

nodes.name: Basepoint is regular
nodes.statement: We henceforth assume that the basepoint in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ lies in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$.
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.name: Hamiltonian Floer gluing chart (goal)
nodes.statement_short: There is a germ of local chart from gluing parameters times the kernel $K$ into $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$, compatible with projections and landing in the regular locus.
conclusions: which respects the natural projection from both sides
nodes.statement:
The remainder of this appendix is devoted to the construction of a germ of a local chart:
\begin{equation} \Bigl(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K,(0,0,0,0)\Bigr)\to\Bigl(\overline{\mathcal M}(M),(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\Bigr)
\end{equation}
which respects the natural projection from both sides to $\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times E/E'$ and whose image is contained in $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)^{\mathrm{reg}}$ ($K$ denotes the kernel of the linearization of \eqref{finalHFdelbareqn} at the distinguished basepoint of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$; see \eqref{definitionofkernel}).
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.name: Equation HFgluinggoal
nodes.statement: \Bigl(\mathbb C^d\times(\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1})^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times\mathbb R^\ast\times\prod_{i=1}^{k\prime}(H^i)^{\leq\mathfrak s}\times K,(0,0,0,0)\Bigr)\to\Bigl(\overline{\mathcal M}(M),(0,0,0,u_0,e_0,\{x_0^i\}_{1\leq i\leq r})\Bigr)
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map
nodes.label: HFgluinggoal

nodes.name: Reduction of Propositions 10.3.10 and 10.6.21 to the gluing chart
nodes.statement_short: The local chart plus the identification of $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ with the thickened moduli space gives openness and submersion.
nodes.statement: Propositions \ref{HFgluingneeded} and \ref{HFgluingSS} follow from the existence of such a chart \eqref{HFgluinggoal} and our earlier observations relating $\overline{\mathcal M}(M)$ to $\overline{\mathcal M}(\sigma,\gamma^-,\gamma^+)_I^{\leq\mathfrak s}$.
nodes.section: C.2 Our goal: the gluing map

nodes.name: Exponential map with $D$, $H$ totally geodesic
nodes.statement: Let $\exp:TM\to M$ denote the exponential map of some Riemannian metric on $M$ for which $D$ and $H$ are totally geodesic (such a metric exists since $D$ and $H$ are disjoint).

nodes.name: Family of $J$-linear connections $\nabla$
nodes.statement:
Let $
abla$ denote a smooth family of $J$-linear connections on $M$ parameterized by $\Delta^n$ which is constant near the vertices (for instance, we could take $
abla_XY:= rac 12(
abla^0_XY-J(

nodes.name: Parallel transport $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}:T_xM\to T_yM$ denote parallel transport via $\nabla$ along the shortest geodesic between $x$ and $y$ (we will only use this notation when it may be assumed that $x$ and $y$ are very close in $M$); note that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is $J$-linear, and that $\mathsf{PT}_{x\to y}$ is a \emph{family} of maps parameterized by $\Delta^n$.

nodes.name: Cutoff function $\chi$
Equation
nodes.statement: \chi(x)=\begin{cases}0&x\leq 0\cr 1&x\geq 1\end{cases}

nodes.name: Flattening
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, we define the ``flattened'' map $u_{0|\alpha}:C_0\to M$ as follows. Away from the ends, $u_{0|\alpha}$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a bubble end $S^1\times[0,\infty)$, we define $u_{0|\alpha}$ as follows: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $n\in C_0$ denotes the corresponding node. Over a positive main end $S^1\times[N,\infty)$, we define $u_{0|\alpha}$ as: \begin{equation} u_{0|\alpha}(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\gamma(t)=u_0(t,\infty)$ denotes the corresponding periodic orbit; an analogous definition applies over the negative main ends.
nodes.statement_short: Cut $u_0$ off to the node value or the periodic orbit on each end, using a cutoff $\chi$.

nodes.name: Pregluing
nodes.statement: For $\alpha\in\mathbb C^d\times\mathbb R_{\geq 0}^{k-1}$, we define the ``preglued'' map $u_\alpha:C_\alpha\to M$ as follows. Away from the necks, $u_\alpha$ coincides with $u_0$. Over a bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]$, we define $u_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr u_0(n)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{u_0(n)}\left[\chi(S-s')\cdot\exp_{u_0(n)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} and over a main neck $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$, we define $u_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} u_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} u_0(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S-s)\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \gamma(t)&S\leq s\leq 5S\cr \exp_{\gamma(t)}\left[\chi(S+s')\cdot\exp_{\gamma(t)}^{-1}u_0(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr u_0(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} ($u_\alpha$ should be thought of as the ``descent'' of $u_{0|\alpha}$ from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$).
nodes.statement_short: Preglued map on $C_\alpha$: flatten $u_0$ near both ends of each neck and patch.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$
nodes.statement: We define the weighted Sobolev space $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ using the usual $(k,2)$-norm away from the ends/necks, and using the following weighted $(k,2)$-norms over the bubble ends/necks and main ends/necks respectively (we will write the contribution to the norm squared): \begin{align} \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}\biggl[\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\biggr|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(t,s)-\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta(s-N)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,6S-N]}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s-N,6S-N-s)}\;dt\,ds \end{align} These are to be interpreted as follows. For each bubble node $n\in C_0$, we fix, once and for all, a small trivialization of $TM$ in a neighborhood of $u_0(n)$; this allows us to view $\xi$ as a function (rather than a section) for the purposes of the integrals over the bubble ends/necks. For each $i=0,\ldots,k$, we fix, once and for all, a smooth family of trivializations of $TM$ near $\gamma_i(t)$ (parameterized by $t\in S^1$); this allows us to view $\xi$ as a section of $\gamma_i^\ast TM$ for the purposes of the integrals over the main ends/necks. We also fix, once and for all, a connection on each such bundle $\gamma_i^\ast TM$ over $S^1$. The derivatives in the integrals above are measured with respect to the standard metric on $S^1\times\mathbb R$. The case of negative main ends is completely analogous to that of positive main ends. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, we get uniform bounds linear in $\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ on $\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|e^{\delta s}$ in the bubble ends, $\left|\xi(t,s)\right|e^{\delta s}$ in the main ends, and $\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|e^{\delta s}$ ($1\leq j\leq k-2$) in all ends (as well as similar estimates in the necks). We will occasionally use other very similar weighted Sobolev spaces (e.g.\ $W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)$), and we leave it to the reader to make the necessary adjustments to the definition (which is essentially identical to the above).
nodes.statement_short: Sobolev norm with exponential weights over all ends and necks, measuring deviation from the node value on bubble ends/necks.
nodes.label: weightedonespace

nodes.name: Equation endnormHFbubble
nodes.statement: \left|\xi(n)\right|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}\biggl[\left|\xi(t,s)-\xi(n)\right|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds

nodes.name: Equation necknormHFbubble
nodes.statement: \biggl|\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\biggr|^2+&\int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}\biggl[\Bigl|\xi(t,s)-\int_{S^1}\xi(t,3S)\,dt\Bigr|^2+\sum_{j=1}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2\biggr]e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,\infty)}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta(s-N)}\;dt\,ds\\ &\int_{S^1\times[N,6S-N]}\sum_{j=0}^k\left|D^j\xi(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s-N,6S-N-s)}\;dt\,ds

nodes.name: Independence of the weighted norm from trivializations
nodes.statement: The particular choice of trivializations and connections in the definition above is not crucial: any other (fixed) choice would lead to a uniformly commensurable norm (this holds because $u_0$ satisfies the exponential decay estimates \eqref{uzerobubble}, \eqref{uzeromain}, and because $\delta<1$ and $\delta<\delta_i$).
nodes.statement_short: Different trivializations/connections give uniformly commensurable norms.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ for one-forms
nodes.statement: We define the weighted Sobolev space $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,T^\ast\tilde C_\alpha\otimes_{\mathbb R} u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ using the usual $(k-1,2)$-norm away from the ends/necks, and using the following weighted $(k-1,2)$-norms over the bubble ends/necks (we will write the contribution to the norm squared): \begin{align} \int_{S^1\times[0,\infty)}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta s}\;dt\,ds\\ \int_{S^1\times[0,6S]}&\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\left|D^j\eta(t,s)\right|^2e^{2\delta\min(s,6S-s)}\;dt\,ds \end{align} (for the main ends/necks, simply make the obvious replacement of $[0,\infty)$ with $[N,\infty)$ and $e^{2\delta s}$ with $e^{2\delta(s-N)}$, etc.). These are to be interpreted as follows. We trivialize $T\tilde C_\alpha$ over any end/neck with the basis vectors $\frac\partial{\partial t},\frac\partial{\partial s}$. We trivialize $TM$ as in Definition \ref{weightedonespace}, and hence the section $\eta$ is simply a pair of functions $\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_2)$. By Sobolev embedding $W^{2,2}\hookrightarrow C^0$ in two dimensions, we get uniform exponential decay bounds on $\eta$ up to $k-3$ derivatives in any end/neck, linear in $\left\|\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$. We are actually interested in certain closed subspaces of $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,T^\ast\tilde C_\alpha\otimes_{\mathbb R} u_\alpha^\ast TM)$, e.g.\ $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_J)$ for certain almost complex structures $j,J$ on $C_\alpha,M$ respectively, which we equip with the restriction of the norm defined above. We will occasionally use other very similar weighted Sobolev spaces, and we leave it to the reader to make the necessary adjustments to the definition (which is essentially identical to the above).
nodes.statement_short: Exponentially weighted $(k-1,2)$-norm for $TM$-valued one-forms on $\tilde C_\alpha$.

nodes.statement: For $\kappa\in K\subseteq C^\infty(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)$, we define $\kappa_\alpha\in C^\infty(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)$ as follows. Away from the necks, $\kappa_\alpha$ coincides with $\kappa$. Over a bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]$, we define $\kappa_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} \kappa_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} \kappa(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))+\chi(s-S)\cdot \kappa(n)&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr \kappa(n)&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s'-S))+\chi(s'-S)\cdot \kappa(n)&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \kappa(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} and over a main neck $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$, we define $\kappa_\alpha$ as: \begin{equation} \kappa_\alpha(t,s):=\begin{cases} \kappa(t,s)&s\leq S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]&S-1\leq s\leq S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t,s)\to u_\alpha(t,s)}\left[\kappa(t,s)\right]\cdot(1-\chi(s-S))&S\leq s\leq S+1\cr 0&S+1\leq s\leq 5S-1\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]\cdot(1-\chi(-s'-S))&5S-1\leq s\leq 5S\cr \mathsf{PT}_{u_0(t',s')\to u_\alpha(t',s')}\left[\kappa(t',s')\right]&5S\leq s\leq 5S+1\cr \kappa(t',s')&5S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.6.8
nodes.statement: Recall that: \begin{equation} \Bigl(du_0+2d(\operatorname{proj}_{S^1}A_0)\otimes X_{H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))}(u_0) +\lambda(e_0)(0,0,x_0^1,\ldots,x_0^r,\cdot,u_0(\cdot))\Bigr)^{0,1}_{j_0,J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}=0 \end{equation} We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the main ends/necks. Note that over this region, the $\lambda$ term vanishes, $j_y=j_0$, $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))=J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$, and $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))=H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. Now due to \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF}, it follows that in this region, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is supported inside the subsets $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$ of the main necks $S^1\times[N,6S-N]$. The contribution of such a region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded above by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$, as follows from the estimate \eqref{uzeromain} on the derivatives of $u_0$ and the fact that $\delta<\delta_i$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ away from the ends/necks. Note that $\ell_{\alpha,w}$ is close to $\ell_{0,0}$, in the sense that they differ over $\coprod_{i=1}^k[-N,N]$ (which may be viewed as a subset of $\coprod_{i=1}^k\mathbb R$ and of $(\coprod_{i=1}^k)_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$ in $C^\ell$ for some fixed $\epsilon>0$ (depending on the flow on $\Delta^n$ from Definition \ref{simplexflows}) and any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that away from the ends/necks, the $C^\ell$ distance between $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ on $C_\alpha$ and $J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))$ on $C_0$ is bounded by a constant (depending on $\ell$) times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$, where we identify $C_0$ and $C_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks in the canonical way (any $\ell<\infty$). The same holds for $H((\ell_{\alpha,w}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_y(\cdot)))$ and $H((\ell_{0,0}\times\operatorname{id}_{S^1})(A_0(\cdot)))$. It also follows that the distance between $x^i\in C_\alpha$ and (the image in $C_\alpha$ of) $x^i_0\in C_0$ is bounded by a constant times $|\alpha|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|$. Hence we conclude that away from the ends/necks, $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ differs from the left hand side of \eqref{delbareqnforuzeroHF} in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. It follows that the contribution of this region to the norm of $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble ends. The reasoning above applies as written to imply that $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ (with respect to the usual metric on $\tilde C_\alpha$) by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$. Since $\delta<1$, the weighted Sobolev norm over the bubble ends is also bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. We estimate $\mathcal F_{\alpha,w,y}(0)$ over the bubble necks $S^1\times[0,6S]$. The argument for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$ is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S]\cup[5S,5S+1])$, we bound the expression termwise: both $u_\alpha$ and $A_y$ are $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, so the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$. Over $S^1\times[S,5S]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and since $A_y=O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives, its contribution to the norm is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ since $\delta<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Region-by-region estimate (main ends/necks, interior, bubble ends, bubble necks) using exponential decay of $u_0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.6.9
nodes.statement: Recall that $D_{0,0,0}\kappa=0$; we will use this to estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ via the explicit expression for $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF}. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks. Over this region, the $\lambda$ terms vanish, and $J,H$ are the same for $(\alpha,w,y)$ as they are for $(0,0,0)$. Thus $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ is supported inside $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$ in the main necks, and vanishes in the main ends. From the exponential decay estimates \eqref{uzeromain}--\eqref{kappamain}, we obtain that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the main ends/necks is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ away from the ends/necks. As in the proof of Lemma \ref{mappregluingissmallHF}, the difference between $J,H$ for $(\alpha,w,y)$ and for $(0,0,0)$ is bounded in $C^\ell$ by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|$ for any $\ell<\infty$; similarly for the distance between $x^i$ and $x^i_0$. It thus follows from the explicit form in Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over this region is bounded by a constant times $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|+\left|y\right|)\left\|\kappa\right\|$. Over the bubble ends, the same reasoning applies, and we obtain the desired bound since $\delta<1$. We estimate $D_{\alpha,w,y}\kappa_\alpha$ over the bubble necks. Outside $S^1\times[S-1,5S+1]$, the reasoning for the bubble ends applies to show that the contribution is bounded as desired. Over $S^1\times([S-1,S+1]\cup[5S-1,5S+1])$, the exponential decay estimates on $u_0$ and $\kappa$, along with similar estimates on $A_y$, show that the contribution of this region is bounded by $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ for some $\epsilon>0$ since $\delta<1$. Over $S^1\times[S+1,5S-1]$, only the term involving $X_H$ is nonzero, and its contribution is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon\left\|\kappa\right\|$ since $\delta<1$ and $A_y$ decays like $O(e^{-s})$ in all derivatives.

nodes.name: Approximate right inverse $T_{\alpha,w,y}$ (HF)
nodes.statement: We define a map: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,w,y}:W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\to W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E \end{equation} as the composition: \begin{equation} T_{\alpha,w,y}:={\operatorname{glue}}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break} \end{equation} of maps in the following diagram, to be defined below: \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{r}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar{d}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{u}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[equals]{u}\ar{r}{D_{0|\alpha,0,0}}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))})\ar[leftrightarrow]{d}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[swap]{u}{{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast}\otimes{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_0^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar[leftrightarrow]{u}{\mathsf{PT}}\ar[yshift=0.5ex]{r}{D_{0,0,0}}&\ar[yshift=-0.5ex]{l}{Q_{0,0,0}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_0}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_0^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot)))}) \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} The top and bottom horizontal maps $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ and $D_{0,0,0}$ are the linearized operators defined earlier. The third horizontal map $D_{0|\alpha,0,0}$ is the linearized operator at the flattened map $u_{0|\alpha}$ (its definition is identical to that of $D_{0,0,0}$ except for using $u_{0|\alpha}$ in place of $u_0$). Similarly, the second horizontal map $D_{0|\alpha,0,y}$ is the linearized operator at the flattened map $u_{0|\alpha}$, using $(j_y,A_y)$ in place of $(j_0,A_0)$. The vertical maps $\mathsf{PT}$ are simply parallel transport $\mathsf{PT}^{\ell_{0,0}(A_0(\cdot))}$; this is valid since $\mathsf{PT}$ is $J$-linear. The vertical map $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast\otimes\operatorname{id}^{1,0}$ denotes the tensor product of $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:TM_{J(a)}\to TM_{J(b)}$ (the $(1,0)$-component of the identity map) and $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}_\ast:\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_0}\to\Omega^{0,1}_{C_0,j_y}$ (the map induced by $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:(TC_0,j_0)\to(TC_0,j_y)$). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H} \end{equation} Let $\xi\in W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\xi)$ is simply $\xi$. In any particular bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\xi)(s,t):=\begin{cases} \xi(s,t)&s\leq 2S\cr \xi(n)+\chi(4S-s)\cdot[\xi(s,t)-\xi(n)]+\chi(4S-s')\cdot[\xi(s',t')-\xi(n)]&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \xi(s',t')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding ends $(t,s)\in S^1\times[0,\infty)\subseteq C_0$ and $(t',s')\in S^1\times[0,\infty)\subseteq C_0$); this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment (and no $\xi(n)$ terms). We define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{break}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation} as follows. Fix a smooth function $\bar\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ such that: \begin{equation} \bar\chi(x)=\begin{cases}1&x\leq-1\cr0&x\geq+1\end{cases}\qquad\bar\chi(x)+\bar\chi(-x)=1 \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the ends with $\alpha\ne 0$, $\operatorname{break}(\eta)$ is given by $(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta)$, where $\operatorname{id}^{1,0}:TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))}\to TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$ denotes the $(1,0)$-component of the identity map. In any particular bubble end $[0,\infty)\times S^1\subseteq C_0$ with $\alpha\ne 0$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{break}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} (\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&s\leq 3S-1\cr \bar\chi(s-3S)\cdot(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}(\eta(t,s))&3S-1\leq s\leq 3S+1\cr 0&3S+1\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (noting the corresponding neck $[0,6S]\times S^1\subseteq C_\alpha$); this definition also applies over the main ends, with the obvious adjustment for negative main ends.
nodes.statement_short: $T_{\alpha,w,y}=\mathrm{glue}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ Q_{0,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\circ(\mathrm{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\mathrm{break}$, with glue and break maps defined via cutoffs.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.7.11
nodes.statement: In simpler terms, we bound the operator norm of the difference between the two diagonal compositions: \begin{equation} \left\|\mathsf{PT}\circ D_{0,0,0}-D_{0|\alpha,0,0}\circ\mathsf{PT}\right\|\leq c\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon \end{equation} (this trivially implies the claimed statement). To show \eqref{betterPTcommutingoperatornormboundHF}, observe that the two operators only differ over the $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ subset of each end. Now it follows from Lemma \ref{linearizedformulaHF} that the contribution to the operator norm over $S^1\times[S-1,\infty)$ is bounded by a constant times the $C^k$-distance between $u_0$ and $u_{0|\alpha}$ over $S^1\times[0,\infty)$. The estimates \eqref{uzerobubble}, \eqref{uzeromain} imply that this distance is bounded by a constant times $\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon$ (to be precise, the bubble ends contribute $\left|\alpha\right|^{1/6-\rho}$ and each main end contributes $\left|\alpha\right|^{\delta_i/6-\rho}$ for any $\rho>0$).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.7.13
nodes.statement: We consider the following diagram, which is a copy of the top square in \eqref{biginversediagramHF} with one extra vector space and some extra maps (to be defined below). \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[row sep = tiny] {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{\mathrm{break}'}\ar[rounded corners,to path={(\tikztostart) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztostart.east) -- ([xshift=2ex]\tikztotarget.east) \tikztonodes -- (\tikztotarget)}]{dddd}{\mathrm{break}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_\alpha,u_\alpha^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar[shift left=0.5ex]{dd}{(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}}\\ W^{k,2,\delta,\delta}(C_0,u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM)_{D,H}\oplus E\ar{uu}{\mathrm{glue}}\ar{rd}{D_{0|\alpha,0,y}}\ar{ru}{D_{\alpha,w,y}}\\ {}&W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{0,0}(A_y(\cdot)))})\ar[shift right=-0.5ex]{uu}{\operatorname{id}^{1,0}} \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} Since the almost complex structure $J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))$ is a function of a point in $C_\alpha$, we should remark immediately on what we mean by $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the ends, the curve $C_0$ is identified canonically with $C_\alpha$, and this identification extends holomorphically to a (non-injective) map from $C_0$ to $C_\alpha$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends. Thus there is a well-defined such $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections on $C_0$ defined outside the $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ subsets of the ends, valued in $\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}$. Now, for instance, the middle horizontal map $D_{\alpha,w,y}$ can be seen as giving a section in this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$. In the proof below, it is convenient to use this $W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}$ space of sections defined outside $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$, though we must be careful that the expressions we write are well-defined. Let us define the rest of the maps in \eqref{topdiagrambigger}. The vertical map $\operatorname{break}$ has been factored as $(\operatorname{id}^{1,0})^{-1}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ in the obvious way. Finally, let us define the map: \begin{equation} W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{glue}}W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_\alpha,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_\alpha,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_\alpha^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))}) \end{equation} Let $\eta\in W^{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}(\tilde C_0,\Omega^{0,1}_{\tilde C_0,j_y}\otimes_{\mathbb C} u_{0|\alpha}^\ast TM_{J(\ell_{\alpha,w}(A_y(\cdot)))})$. Away from the necks of $C_\alpha$, $\operatorname{glue}(\eta)$ is simply $\eta$. In any particular bubble neck $S^1\times[0,6S]\subseteq C_\alpha$, we define: \begin{equation} \operatorname{glue}(\eta)(t,s):=\begin{cases} \eta(t,s)&s\leq 2S\cr \chi(4S-s)\eta(t,s)+\chi(4S-s')\eta(t',s')&2S\leq s\leq 4S\cr \eta(t',s')&4S\leq s \end{cases} \end{equation} (this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment). Note that $\operatorname{glue}\circ\operatorname{break}'$ is the identity map. Now suppose that $D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi=\operatorname{break}(\eta)$; we must show that: \begin{equation} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|_{k-1,2,\delta,\delta}\leq c\cdot\bigl(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|\bigr)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta} \end{equation} Using the triangle inequality and the fact that $\eta=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{break}'(\eta))=\operatorname{glue}(\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi))$, we conclude that $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\eta\right\|$ is bounded above by: \begin{equation*} \left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|+\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}(\xi))\right]\right\| \end{equation*} We now estimate each term separately. To estimate $\left\|D_{\alpha,w,y}(\operatorname{glue}(\xi))-\operatorname{glue}(D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi))\right\|$, argue as follows. The difference is only nonzero over the regions $S^1\times([2S,2S+1]\cup[4S-1,4S])$ of each neck. Now the norm is bounded by $\left\|\xi\right\|e^{-2S\delta}$ (calculation left to the reader), where the factor of $e^{-2S\delta}$ comes as the ratio of the weight given to $S^1\times[4S-1,4S]$ inside a neck vs inside an end; this gives the desired bound since $\delta>0$. To estimate $\left\|\operatorname{glue}\left[D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)\right]\right\|$, argue as follows. This is bounded by a constant times the $(k-1,2,\delta,\delta)$-norm of $D_{\alpha,w,y}(\xi)-\operatorname{id}^{1,0}(D_{0|\alpha,0,y}\xi)$ over the complement of the subsets $S^1\times[4S,\infty)$ of the ends. Now this is bounded by $(\left|\alpha\right|^\epsilon+\left|w\right|)\left\|\xi\right\|_{k,2,\delta,\delta}$ using the reasoning from Lemma \ref{approxmiddleHF}.

nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{bootstrapinverse} and Proposition \ref{approxworksHF}.
